                                                                Projection--Reduction Gluing for Maximum Parents

                                                                Name: Projection--Reduction Gluing for Maximum Parents

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Maximum-Generated Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Peripheral Expansion
                                                                • Universal Projection

                                                                Result Type: Construction

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For nonempty maximum-generated $H\subseteq\{0,1\}^{X\sqcup D}$, put $U=\pi_XH$ and $I=\partial_DH$. Then $(U\times\{0\})\cup(I\times\{1\})$ is maximum-generated. If a supplied parent has rank $r$, marked auxiliary set $T$, $k=|D|$, $N=|X|+|T|$, and $0\le r-k<\min(r,N)$, a parent of rank $\min(r,N)$ retains the original mark and uses exactly $\min(r,N)-(r-k)-1\le k-1$ new auxiliaries.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Successively reduce the parent on an initial part of $D$ and project the rest. The resulting nested classes on $X\sqcup T$ pass through consecutive maximum ranks from the full projection to the full reduction. Extend them to a maximum sequence. A delayed one-coordinate maximum sequence has entry levels zero and the rank gap at its two visible values; the disjoint level sum is a maximum parent whose marked section is exactly the two-shore gluing. Empty and equal endpoints reduce to constant-coordinate and product closure.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                CompressionSchemes:maximum_parent_methods.tex?#thm:block-gluing

                                                                Convex Sign Classes Have Maximum Parents

                                                                Name: Convex Sign Classes Have Maximum Parents

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Maximum-Generated Classes

                                                                Result Type: Construction

                                                                Statement:

                                                                If a nonempty binary class is the set of coordinate orthants meeting an open convex set in $\mathbb R^n$, then it is maximum-generated. More quantitatively, if a bounded full-dimensional polytope uses $q$ nonconstant inequalities plus $2n$ box inequalities, contains an interior witness in every allowed orthant, and misses every forbidden closed orthant, then the class has a rank-$n$ maximum parent with at most $q+2n$ auxiliaries. The analogous statement for $n$ affine visible forms in $\mathbb R^d$ gives rank $d$ and $q+2d$ auxiliaries.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Use the visible hyperplanes and the oriented polytope facets as auxiliary hyperplanes. Small generic perturbations preserve all chosen witnesses; the box inequalities uniformly bound possible witnesses, so compactness prevents a forbidden sign region from appearing. Perturb into affine general position. The region class of the arrangement has the Sauer number and VC dimension equal to the ambient dimension, hence is maximum, and fixing the auxiliary facet signs recovers the original class. An arbitrary open convex realization is reduced to the bounded case by taking the convex hull of small boxes around one witness per allowed orthant.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                CompressionSchemes:maximum_parent_methods.tex?#lem:strict-realization; CompressionSchemes:maximum_parent_methods.tex?#cor:convex-realization

                                                                Exact Maximum-Parent Parameters for Two Monotone Shores

                                                                Name: Exact Maximum-Parent Parameters for Two Monotone Shores

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Maximum-Generated Classes

                                                                Result Type: Construction

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $C=(A\times\{0\})\cup(B\times\{1\})$ be nonempty and proper, where after common coordinate reflections $A,B$ are upsets. Then $C$ is ample. If $d=\operatorname{VC}(C)$ and $s$ is the least support size of a minimally missing pattern, a rank-$r$ maximum parent with exactly $m$ auxiliary coordinates exists exactly when $r\ge d$ and $m\ge r+1-s$. Thus the simultaneous minima are rank $d$ and $d+1-s$ auxiliaries. This includes every proper nonempty downset and daisy cube.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Upset projections supply positioned cubes for every shattered support. Necessity follows because sections cannot raise VC dimension and a missing pattern of size $s$ needs $r+1-s$ auxiliary coordinates in any rank-$r$ parent witness. For sufficiency, mark $m$ zero auxiliaries and choose on every $(r+1)$-support the lexicographically first pattern absent from the marked target. Monotonicity makes these patterns zero or singleton patterns and makes every agreement graph connected. The resulting avoiding class is maximum of rank $r$, and padding each minimal missing pattern with auxiliaries proves that its marked section is exactly $C$.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                CompressionSchemes:maximum_parent_methods.tex?#thm:monotone-parameters

                                                                Witnesses:

                                                                • Downset with Simultaneously Optimal Parent Parameters

                                                                Maximum Parents of Learning Spaces

                                                                Name: Maximum Parents of Learning Spaces

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Learning-Space Graphs
                                                                • Maximum-Generated Classes

                                                                Result Type: Construction

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Every finite learning space is maximum-generated. On $n\ge1$ coordinates, if it has $q$ inclusion-minimal missing consistent patterns, it has a coordinate-hyperplane convex realization in $\mathbb R^n$ and a rank-$n$ maximum parent with at most $q+2n$ auxiliary coordinates. The zero-coordinate learning space needs none.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Union closure makes every minimal missing pattern have exactly one positive literal, say $a=1$ with prerequisites $A$ fixed to zero. Accessibility orders every feasible state by feasible prefixes. Give earlier learned elements geometrically larger positive coordinates, absent elements value $-1$, and use the inequalities $x_a<(n+1)^{-1}\sum_{b\in A}x_b$. Every feasible state satisfies them strictly and every forbidden orthant violates one. Adding a bounding box and applying the strict-realization construction gives the stated parent bound.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                CompressionSchemes:maximum_parent_methods.tex?#thm:learning-maxmin

                                                                Finite Auxiliary Bounds at a Prescribed Parent Rank

                                                                Name: Finite Auxiliary Bounds at a Prescribed Parent Rank

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Maximum-Generated Classes

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Maximum-Parent Profile

                                                                Result Type: Algorithm

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $\varnothing\ne C\subsetneq\{0,1\}^X$ and fix $r\ge0$. If a minimally missing pattern has support larger than $r+1$, no rank-$r$ maximum parent exists. Otherwise put $B_r(C)=\sum_{p\in\mathcal M(C)}(r+1-|\operatorname{supp}p|)$ and $D_r(C)=(r+1)|\{0,1\}^X\setminus C|-e_\partial(C)$. If a rank-$r$ parent exists then $D_r(C)\ge0$, and some rank-$r$ parent with the same visible labels and section uses at most $\min(B_r(C),D_r(C))$ auxiliaries. Consequently existence at any specified rank is decidable by finite enumeration.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Every minimal missing visible pattern extends, together with part of the auxiliary mark, to the unique missing pattern on an $(r+1)$-support of the maximum parent. Retaining the union of these auxiliary supports preserves every forbidden visible word and hence the exact section, giving $B_r$. Alternatively choose one parent witness per absent full word. Every boundary coordinate toward $C$ must occur visibly in that witness, leaving at most $r+1-d_C(x)$ auxiliary entries; summing gives $D_r$. These finite bounds reduce rank-$r$ existence to enumerating finitely many marked maximum classes.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                CompressionSchemes:maximum_parent_methods.tex?#thm:bound; CompressionSchemes:maximum_parent_methods.tex?#cor:decision

                                                                Witnesses:

                                                                • Two Missing Patterns Sharing One Parent Witness Coordinate

It therefore computes the least parent rank, least complementary rank, and least auxiliary count.

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The profile is upward closed by nested maximum lifts, and its minimal points form a finite antichain. Use the fixed-rank auxiliary bound to decide and find the least feasible point in every row $r

                                                                Maximum-Parent Profiles under Constant Coordinates

                                                                Name: Maximum-Parent Profiles under Constant Coordinates

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Maximum-Generated Classes

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Maximum-Parent Profile
                                                                • Minimum Maximum-Parent Auxiliary Count

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For nonempty proper $C\subsetneq\{0,1\}^X$, $|X|=n$, and $t\ge1$, one has $\mathcal F(C\times\{0\}^t)=\{(r,s):s\ge n+t-1,\ (r,s-t)\in\mathcal F(C)\}$. Its minimal frontier is obtained from $(r,u)$ by $(r,\max(u+t,n+t-1))$ and deleting dominated points. Moreover $a(C\times\{0\}^t)=\min_{(r,u)\in\mathcal F(C)}\max\{r,r+u+1-n\}$, independent of positive $t$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Projecting constant visible coordinates from a parent gives necessity, while the complementary target contains an $(n+t-1)$-cube. Conversely, after raising the complementary rank if needed, use face avoidance to choose a rank-one-lower maximum subclass avoiding the mark and lift it beneath the parent at the new constant coordinate. This preserves rank and auxiliary count while raising complementary rank by one; iterate and translate the frontier formula.

                                                                Maximum-Parent Profile Bounds under Free Coordinates

                                                                Name: Maximum-Parent Profile Bounds under Free Coordinates

                                                                For $D_t=C\times\{0,1\}^t$, $\mathcal F(C)+(t,t)\subseteq\mathcal F(D_t)\subseteq\bigcap_{u=0}^t(\mathcal F(C)+(u,t-u))$. Hence $h(D_t)=h(C)+t$, $h(D_t^c)=h(C^c)+t$, and $a(C)\le a(D_t)\le a(C)+t$. If $\mathcal F(C)$ has one minimal point, the first inclusion is equality and $a(D_t)=a(C)+t$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                A two-control lift from a predecessor-parent-successor triple adds one free visible coordinate and one auxiliary while raising both parent ranks. Conversely, from any parent of $D_t$, fully reduce any $u$ free coordinates and project the other $t-u$; the resulting parent of $C$ has profile shifted by $(u,t-u)$. The exact least-rank and auxiliary bounds follow. A unique minimal original profile forces the translated quadrant.

                                                                A parent can be symmetrized without changing parameters exactly when it arises from a nested chain of consecutive-rank maximum parents with one common marked section; numerical profile feasibility alone does not supply that chain.

                                                                Optimal Fixed-Rank Parent after Deleting a Minimum Section

                                                                Name: Optimal Fixed-Rank Parent after Deleting a Minimum Section

                                                                • Maximum-Generated Classes

                                                                Result Type: Construction

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $M$ be maximum of rank $r$, let $J$ have size $q$ with $1\le q\le r$, and suppose the section $S=M[p]$ is contained in every other $J$-section, equivalently $S=\partial_JM$. Deleting all words of $M$ with $J$-pattern $p$ yields a class with a rank-$r$ maximum parent using exactly $r+1-q$ auxiliaries, and no rank-$r$ parent retaining the original visible coordinates uses fewer.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Choose a decreasing maximum sequence inside the minimum section. At each step construct a rank-$(r-1)$ maximum subclass of the current parent whose marked $J$-section is the next sequence level, then exchange the removed layer between two heights of one new auxiliary. The union and intersection of the shores have ranks $r$ and $r-1$, and a missing-trace argument gives the VC bound. After $r-q+1$ steps the marked section is empty. Conversely the absent pattern consisting of $p$ and the auxiliary mark needs at least $r+1$ coordinates in a rank-$r$ maximum class, so at least $r+1-q$ auxiliaries are necessary.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                CompressionSchemes:maximum_parent_methods.tex?#thm:minimum-section-deletion

                                                                Witnesses:

                                                                • Minimum-Section Deletion from a Rank-Three Hamming Ball

                                                                Exact Parent Criterion for One Missing Shattering Block

                                                                Name: Exact Parent Criterion for One Missing Shattering Block

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Maximum-Generated Classes

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Suppose ample $C\subseteq\{0,1\}^X$ has $\operatorname{Sh}(C)=\{T:|T|\le r,\ J\nsubseteq T\}$ for $1\le|J|=q\le r<|X|$. There is one absent $J$-pattern $p$. With $I=\bigcap_{t\ne p}C[t]$, the following are equivalent: $C$ has a rank-$r$ maximum parent; $C$ lies in a rank-$r$ maximum class on $X$; and $I$ contains a maximum rank-$(r-q)$ class. Every envelope is $C\cup(S\times\{p\})$ for such an $S$. When these hold, the least parent rank is $r$ and the least auxiliary count is $r+1-q$, even allowing larger ranks.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Projection after deleting any coordinate of $J$ is already maximum, forcing every new envelope word to occur at the single missing pattern $p$ and its private part to lie in $I$. Shattered supports containing $J$ are then exactly $J\cup T$ with $T$ shattered by the added section. The envelope is maximum precisely when that section is maximum of rank $r-q$. Minimum-section deletion supplies a parent, while VC dimension and the missing-pattern witness bound prove simultaneous optimality.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                CompressionSchemes:maximum_parent_methods.tex?#thm:one-missing-block

                                                                Deleting Compatible Minimum Sections

                                                                Name: Deleting Compatible Minimum Sections

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Maximum-Generated Classes

                                                                Result Type: Construction

                                                                Statement:

                                                                In a supplied rank-$r$ maximum class, let $M[b_i]=\partial_{B_i}M$ be designated minimum sections whose patterns agree on every overlap. Deleting all words matching any designated pattern has a rank-$r$ maximum parent using at most $\sum_i\max(r+1-|B_i|,0)$ auxiliaries. Blocks may be processed in any order; unprocessed minimum properties and any disjoint old mark are preserved.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Compatibility gives a common pattern and nonemptiness of the residual class. Inductively choose a maximum predecessor that retains all protected minimum properties. The one-section deletion lift then lowers the target marked section by one rank while keeping every compatible protected minimum at both heights. Repeating empties one designated section in $r+1-|B_i|$ steps and leaves the remaining hypotheses intact.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                CompressionSchemes:maximum_parent_methods.tex?#thm:compatible-minimum-deletion

                                                                Deleting a Forest of Minimum Sections

                                                                Name: Deleting a Forest of Minimum Sections

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Maximum-Generated Classes

                                                                Result Type: Construction

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $M\subsetneq\{0,1\}^X$ be maximum of rank $r$ and let $M[p_i]=\partial_{B_i}M$ be minimum sections. After deleting every word matching some $p_i$, the residual $C$ is nonempty and ample with $\operatorname{Sh}(C)=\{T:|T|\le r,\ B_i\nsubseteq T\text{ for all }i\}$. Join two patterns when they disagree on their overlap. If this disagreement graph is a forest, $C$ has a rank-$r$ parent with at most $\sum_i\max(r+1-|B_i|,0)$ auxiliaries, preserving any disjoint old mark.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Incompatible minimum patterns have union support at least $r+2$ and their deleted sections are disjoint. Inclusion--exclusion matches the residual word count with the displayed support family, so the sandwich theorem gives ampleness and exact shattering. For the parent, repeatedly choose a leaf of the disagreement forest. A modified predecessor construction preserves all compatible minima and the leaf's sole possible incompatible neighbor. The single-section lift deletes the leaf in the stated number of steps without changing the disagreement graph; induction over leaves completes the construction.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                CompressionSchemes:maximum_parent_methods.tex?#thm:forest-minimum-deletion

                                                                Witnesses:

                                                                • Three-Section Forest Deletion in the Seven-Cube

                                                                Comments:

                                                                The shattering formula does not require the forest hypothesis. Cyclic disagreement families are not covered by the parent construction. Properness of the supplied maximum class is essential.

                                                                Rank-Preserving Downset Filtering

                                                                Name: Rank-Preserving Downset Filtering

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Maximum-Generated Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Downset Filter

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                If nonempty $C$ is downward closed in $U$ and $D\subseteq\{0,1\}^U$ is a nonempty downset, then $F=C|_D$ is nonempty and $\operatorname{Sh}(F)=\{T\in\operatorname{Sh}(C):T\cap U\in D\}$. Ampleness is preserved. If $C$ has a rank-$r$ parent with $m$ auxiliaries, then $F$ has one of rank $r$ with at most $m+\sum_{J\in\mathcal N(D)}\max(0,r+1-|J|)$ auxiliaries; in particular the least parent rank cannot increase.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Downward closure identifies the section at the characteristic word of $B\subseteq U$ with the private shattering data over $B$, giving the exact support formula and, by counting ample sections, ampleness. Standardize the supplied parent in all constrained coordinates so every minimal forbidden support of $D$ becomes a compatible all-one minimum section. Compatible minimum-section deletion removes those patterns while retaining the old mark, rank, and stated auxiliary bound.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                CompressionSchemes:maximum_parent_methods.tex?#thm:monotone-filter

                                                                Quantitative Maximum-Parent Product Bounds

                                                                Name: Quantitative Maximum-Parent Product Bounds

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Maximum-Generated Classes

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Maximum-Parent Profile
                                                                • Minimum Maximum-Parent Auxiliary Count
                                                                • Maximum Subclass Rank
                                                                • Constant-Stabilized Maximum-Parent Auxiliary Count

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Cartesian Product

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let nonempty proper $C_i\subsetneq\{0,1\}^{X_i}$ have disjoint grounds of sizes $n_i$. Then $m(C_1\times C_2)=\min\{m(C_1),m(C_2)\}$. If $(r_i,s_i)\in\mathcal F(C_i)$, then $(r_1+r_2,\max\{s_1,n_1-1\}+\max\{s_2,n_2-1\}+1)\in\mathcal F(C_1\times C_2)$. Consequently $b(C_1\times C_2)\le b(C_1)+b(C_2)$ and $a(C)\le b(C)\le a(C)+m(C)$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                A same-ground maximum subclass of a proper product projects to maximum subclasses in both factors, which bounds its rank by both core ranks. Maximum sequences through largest cores give the reverse inequality at their minimum rank. For the parent bound, pad each supplied parent until its auxiliary count is at least its rank, choose a predecessor avoiding the marked face, and take the level sum of the two maximum sequences. The marked section is exactly the product and has the displayed profile. Minimizing first for $b$ gives subadditivity. Projection gives $a\le b$, while the parent-core inequality gives $b\le a+m$.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                CompressionSchemes:maximum_parent_methods.tex?#prop:product-profiles

                                                                Comments:

                                                                The construction controls the maximum-parent profile and auxiliary count; it does not preserve an arbitrary parent-decomposition level.

                                                                Auxiliary Cost of Cartesian Powers

                                                                Name: Auxiliary Cost of Cartesian Powers

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Maximum-Generated Classes
                                                                • Maximum Classes

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Asymptotic Maximum-Parent Auxiliary Rate
                                                                • Minimum Maximum-Parent Auxiliary Count
                                                                • Constant-Stabilized Maximum-Parent Auxiliary Count
                                                                • Maximum Subclass Rank

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Cartesian Product

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For every nonempty proper maximum-generated $C$, the limit $\gamma(C)=\lim_{k\to\infty}a(C^k)/k=\inf_{k\ge1}b(C^k)/k$ exists and $\operatorname{VC}(C)\le\gamma(C)\le b(C)$. Visible constant coordinates do not change $\gamma$. If $d=\operatorname{VC}(C)$ and $C$ has a rank-$d$ parent with at most $d$ auxiliaries, then $b(C^k)=kd$, $kd-m(C)\le a(C^k)\le kd$, and $\gamma(C)=d$. In particular a proper rank-$d$ maximum class satisfies $(k-1)d\le a(M^k)\le kd$ and $b(M^k)=kd$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The sequence $b(C^k)$ is subadditive, so the elementary subadditive-limit argument gives its normalized limit and infimum formula. Product cores satisfy $m(C^k)=m(C)$ and $0\le b(C^k)-a(C^k)\le m(C)$, hence the normalized $a$-sequence has the same limit. Parent rank is at least $k\operatorname{VC}(C)$, yielding the lower bound; subadditivity yields the upper bound. Under the stated certificate, both bounds force $b(C^k)=kd$. Constant invariance follows because $(C\times\{0\}^t)^k$ is a constant extension of $C^k$.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                CompressionSchemes:maximum_parent_methods.tex?#thm:auxiliary-rate

                                                                Parent Costs for Products of Maximum Factors

                                                                Name: Parent Costs for Products of Maximum Factors

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Maximum Classes
                                                                • Maximum-Generated Classes

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Minimum Maximum-Parent Rank
                                                                • Minimum Maximum-Parent Auxiliary Count
                                                                • Constant-Stabilized Maximum-Parent Auxiliary Count
                                                                • Maximum Subclass Rank

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Cartesian Product

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $M_1,\ldots,M_\ell$ be nonempty proper maximum classes of ranks $d_1,\ldots,d_\ell$, let $D=\prod_iM_i$, and put $R=\sum_i d_i$. Then $h(D)=b(D)=R$, $m(D)=\min_i d_i$, and $R-\min_i d_i\le a(D)\le R$. Adjoining one or more visible constant coordinates makes the auxiliary count exactly $R$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Each factor has a rank-$d_i$ zero-auxiliary parent and $b(M_i)=d_i$. Repeated product subadditivity gives $b(D)\le R$, while VC additivity forces every parent rank, and hence $h(D)$ and $b(D)$, to be at least $R$. The product-core formula gives $m(D)=\min_i d_i$, and $0\le b(D)-a(D)\le m(D)$ gives the displayed interval. The definition of $b$ gives the constant-extension assertion.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                CompressionSchemes:maximum_parent_methods.tex?#thm:auxiliary-rate

                                                                Comments:

                                                                The factors need not be geometrically realizable.

                                                                Operation Laws for the Asymptotic Parent Rate

                                                                Name: Operation Laws for the Asymptotic Parent Rate

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Maximum-Generated Classes

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Asymptotic Maximum-Parent Auxiliary Rate

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Cartesian Product
                                                                • Coordinate Projection
                                                                • Full Reduction
                                                                • Partial-Trace Expansion

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For nonempty proper represented classes on disjoint grounds, $\gamma(C\times D)\le\gamma(C)+\gamma(D)$. Projection and full reduction do not increase $\gamma$ when their outputs remain nonempty and proper. For $t\ge0$, $\max\{\gamma(C),\operatorname{VC}(C)+t\}\le\gamma(C\times\{0,1\}^t)\le\gamma(C)+t$. If $C$ has $n$ coordinates, then its partial-trace expansion satisfies $\gamma(T(C))\le\gamma(C)+n$. Thus $\gamma=\operatorname{VC}$ is preserved by products of equality cases, visible free or constant coordinates, partial traces, and VC-preserving proper projections.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Regroup $(C\times D)^k$ as $C^k\times D^k$, apply subadditivity of $b$, divide by $k$, and pass to the limit. Apply projection or full reduction independently in every factor for monotonicity. The finite free-coordinate profile construction adds at most $tk$ auxiliaries to $C^k$, while projection and VC dimension give the two lower bounds. Partial trace commutes with products and its finite construction adds at most $nk$ auxiliaries. Combining these inequalities with VC additivity proves preservation of equality.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                CompressionSchemes:maximum_parent_methods.tex?#prop:auxiliary-rate-operations

                                                                Finite Parent-Rank Lower Bound for Cartesian Powers

                                                                Name: Finite Parent-Rank Lower Bound for Cartesian Powers

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Maximum-Generated Classes

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Minimum Maximum-Parent Rank

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Cartesian Product
                                                                • Full Reduction
                                                                • Coordinate Conditioning

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For every nonempty proper maximum-generated class $C$ and every $k\ge1$, $h(C^k)\ge h(C)+(k-1)\operatorname{VC}(C)$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Choose a positioned cube of dimension $\operatorname{VC}(C)$ in each of the first $k-1$ factors. Fully reduce those cube coordinates and fix all remaining visible coordinates in those factors. Any rank-$h(C^k)$ parent of $C^k$ then yields a parent of the last copy of $C$ whose rank is lower by $(k-1)\operatorname{VC}(C)$. Its rank is at least $h(C)$, giving the inequality.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                CompressionSchemes:maximum_parent_methods.tex?#subsec:products-and-asymptotic-auxiliary-cost

                                                                Comments:

                                                                A fixed one-copy excess in $h(C)$ does not by itself imply an asymptotic excess in $\gamma(C)$.

                                                                Exact Marked Maximum-Parent Recognition

                                                                Name: Exact Marked Maximum-Parent Recognition

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Maximum Classes
                                                                • Maximum-Generated Classes

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $C$ be a nonempty proper class on visible coordinates $X$, fix an auxiliary mark $\tau$ on $A$, and choose one pattern $f_T$ on every $(r+1)$-support of $X\sqcup A$. Call $f_T$ active when its auxiliary restriction agrees with $\tau$. The avoider $M_f$ is a rank-$r$ maximum parent with section $M_f[\tau]=C$ exactly when: every local agreement graph is connected; every active pattern's visible restriction contains a minimally missing pattern of $C$; and every minimally missing pattern of $C$ occurs as the visible restriction of an active selected pattern.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Local connectivity is exactly maximumity. In a maximum class the selected patterns are all minimally missing. If the marked section is $C$, every active restriction is missing from $C$, hence contains a minimal missing pattern; minimizing a missing extension of each pattern of $C$ gives an active selected pattern with exactly that visible restriction. Conversely, the containment condition keeps every word of $C$ in the marked section, while coverage of every minimal missing pattern excludes every visible word outside $C$.

                                                                References:

                                                                [AlmousaVandeBogert22]

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                CompressionSchemes:maximum_parent_methods.tex?#cor:exact-section

                                                                Witnesses:

                                                                • Connected and Disconnected Signed Pattern Triples

                                                                Signed Ideal of a Downset Filter

                                                                Name: Signed Ideal of a Downset Filter

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Maximum-Generated Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Downset Filter

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                If $C$ is downward closed in a coordinate block $U$, $D\subseteq\{0,1\}^U$ is a nonempty downset with minimal nonfaces $\mathcal N(D)$, and $F=\{x\in C:x|_U\in D\}$, then $Q_F=Q_C+(\prod_{j\in J}x_{j,1}:J\in\mathcal N(D))$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                A consistent partial pattern missing from $F$ either was already missing from $C$, or has a witness in $C$. Lower every unspecified coordinate of $U$ in that witness to zero. Downward closure retains membership in $C$ and the prescribed pattern. Since the resulting word is not in $F$, its prescribed one-set in $U$ contains a minimal nonface of $D$. This proves both generator containments; minimal consistent generators suffice for the monomial-ideal equality.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                CompressionSchemes:maximum_parent_methods.tex?#eq:filter-ideal

                                                                Comments:

                                                                This identity retains literal signs and is stronger than the corresponding unsigned shattered-support formula.

                                                                Signed-Ideal Colon Identity for Sections

                                                                Name: Signed-Ideal Colon Identity for Sections

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Partial Cubes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Coordinate Conditioning

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For any finite class $M$ with nonempty marked section $C=M[\tau]$ on visible coordinates $X$, if $m_\tau$ is the product of the marked auxiliary literals, then $Q_C=(Q_M:m_\tau)\cap S_X$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The contracted colon is generated by visible restrictions of missing parent patterns whose auxiliary signs agree with the mark, so every generator is missing from the section. Conversely, extend a minimally missing pattern of $C$ by the mark and minimize it inside $M$; the resulting active parent generator has visible restriction dividing the original pattern. These containments prove equality for every monomial.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                CompressionSchemes:maximum_parent_methods.tex?#prop:colon

                                                                Yang Complex of a Marked Section

                                                                Name: Yang Complex of a Marked Section

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Partial Cubes
                                                                • Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Coordinate Conditioning

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For a class $M$ on visible and auxiliary coordinates and a realized auxiliary mark $\tau$, the Yang complex of the section is the link $\Delta_{M[\tau]}=\operatorname{lk}_{\Delta_M}(\sigma_\tau)$ on the remaining literal pairs, after discarding opposite auxiliary ghost vertices.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                A visible literal face lies in the link exactly when adjoining all marked auxiliary literals yields a face of $\Delta_M$. This is equivalent to extension by a word of $M$ with auxiliary restriction $\tau$, hence to membership in the Yang complex of the marked section.

                                                                References:

                                                                [BousquetAmpleCM26]

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                CompressionSchemes:maximum_parent_methods.tex?#eq:link

                                                                Relative Initial-Ideal Maximum-Parent Criterion

                                                                Name: Relative Initial-Ideal Maximum-Parent Criterion

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Maximum Classes
                                                                • Maximum-Generated Classes

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Fix visible class $C$, auxiliary mark $\tau$, total coordinate set of size $N$, and rank $r$. A coordinate-multigraded ideal $F$ with the maximum-class Hilbert series $\mathcal H_{N,r}$ and exact marked colon $(F:m_\tau)\cap S_X=Q_C$ exists exactly when $C$ has a rank-$r$ maximum parent at that mark. For a block term order placing every opposite auxiliary literal before all monomials without one, $\operatorname{in}(F)=Q_M$ for such a parent and its marked colon remains $Q_C$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The prescribed Hilbert series forces the initial ideal to contain no monomial on at most $r$ colors and exactly one signed squarefree monomial on each $(r+1)$-support. Full-word counting gives the Sauer cardinality and the selected patterns bound VC dimension, so their avoider is rank-$r$ maximum. Homogeneous polarization then gives equality of the whole initial ideal with its signed ideal. Under the elimination block order, a leading monomial compatible with the mark comes from a polynomial containing no opposite auxiliary literal; coordinate homogeneity factors its marked auxiliary part, and the prescribed colon forces the visible leading factor into $Q_C$. This preserves the exact marked colon. The converse takes $F=Q_M$.

                                                                References:

                                                                [ConcaDeNegriGorla20]

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                CompressionSchemes:maximum_parent_methods.tex?#thm:relative-initial

                                                                Witnesses:

                                                                • Marked Section Depends on the Initial Term Order

                                                                Maximum Sequences, Level Sums, and Delays

                                                                Name: Maximum Sequences, Level Sums, and Delays

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Maximum Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Cartesian Product

                                                                Result Type: Construction

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Every maximum class on $n$ coordinates, and every nested maximum pair of consecutive ranks, extends to a chain $A_0\subseteq\cdots\subseteq A_n=\{0,1\}^n$ with $A_i$ maximum of rank $i$. If $\rho,\sigma$ are entry-level functions of two such chains on disjoint grounds, then $\{(x,y):\rho(x)+\sigma(y)\le R\}$ is maximum of rank $R$. For any threshold $h$, one new coordinate can delay precisely the levels above $h$ by one on its zero shore; $q$ iterations add $q\mathbf1_{\rho>h}$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Face avoidance supplies a maximum predecessor of one lower rank and cube addition supplies a maximum successor of one higher rank, so iteration completes the chain. Vandermonde's identity gives the Sauer cardinality of a level sum; missing traces in the two blocks prevent shattering a support of size $R+1$. For delay, put the two consecutive levels on opposite shores below and above the threshold. Pascal's identity gives the correct size, the nested shores give the VC bound, and the resulting chains remain nested across the threshold.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                CompressionSchemes:maximum_parent_methods.tex?#lem:sequences

                                                                Shattering and Signed Ideals under Boolean Substitution

                                                                Name: Shattering and Signed Ideals under Boolean Substitution

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Boolean Substitution

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For $D=(C_0\times T)\cup(C_1\times T^c)$, put $P=C_0\cup C_1$ and $J=C_0\cap C_1$. If the outer class and test are ample, then $\operatorname{Sh}(D)=(\operatorname{Sh}(J)\times2^Y)\cup(\operatorname{Sh}(C_0)\times\operatorname{Sh}(T))\cup(\operatorname{Sh}(C_1)\times\operatorname{Sh}(T^c))$. Without ampleness, the signed missing-pattern ideals satisfy $Q_D=Q_P+Q_{C_0}Q_{T^c}+Q_{C_1}Q_T$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                A support shattered in the outer projection lies in one or both shores. If it lies in both, ampleness supplies a positioned cube in their intersection and any test support is possible. If it lies only in one shore, a trace absent from the other forces the corresponding test side, giving the displayed union. For signed ideals, split a missing partial pattern into outer and test blocks. It is absent exactly when its outer part misses both shores, or it misses one shore while its test part misses the side paired with that shore. These three alternatives are precisely the three ideal summands.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                CompressionSchemes:maximum_parent_methods.tex?#thm:substitution

                                                                Factor Restriction on a Minimal Non-Maximum-Generated Class

                                                                Name: Factor Restriction on a Minimal Non-Maximum-Generated Class

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Convex-Treelike Partial Cubes
                                                                • Maximum-Generated Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Boolean Substitution
                                                                • Peripheral Expansion

                                                                Result Type: Implication

                                                                Statement:

                                                                If an ample class outside $\mathsf{MaxMin}$ has the least possible number of coordinates, it cannot have the form $(B\times T)\cup(S\times\{0,1\}^Y)$ with $\varnothing\ne S\subsetneq B$, nonempty proper $T$, $|X|\ge1$, and $|Y|\ge2$. The same holds for a least-coordinate member of $\mathcal R_{\mathrm{per}}$ outside $\mathsf{MaxMin}$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The class is the substitution of the smaller peripheral expansion $E(B,S)$ by the smaller test $T$. Both recovered factors belong to the same ambient family and have fewer coordinates. Minimality therefore places both in $\mathsf{MaxMin}$, and the nested-section substitution theorem constructs a maximum parent of the original class, a contradiction.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                CompressionSchemes:maximum_parent_methods.tex?#cor:substitution-factor

                                                                Comments:

                                                                The conclusion uses a parent of the joint expansion $E(B,S)$; separate parents of $B$ and $S$ do not suffice.

                                                                Exact Equal-Cardinality Fiber Replacement Criterion

                                                                Name: Exact Equal-Cardinality Fiber Replacement Criterion

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Maximum Classes

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let maximum sequences $(A_i)$ on $U$ and $(B_j)$ on $Y$ define a rank-$R=k+s$ level sum. Replace the rank-$s$ fiber $B_s$ over every $x\in A_k\setminus A_{k-1}$ by a set $F_x$ of the same Sauer cardinality. Form $G_k$ by joining two level-$k$ words when they agree with a missing pattern of $A_{k-1}$ on a $k$-support. The modified class remains maximum exactly when every $F_x$ is maximum of rank $s$, the fibers are constant on each component of $G_k$, every $F_x\subseteq B_{s+1}$ when $k>0$, and every $F_x\supseteq B_{s-1}$ when $k<|U|$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                If a replacement has excessive rank, adjacent vertices have unequal fibers, or either neighboring-level containment fails, combine the offending control trace with a missing old trace to shatter $R+1$ coordinates. Conversely, consider a candidate support of size $R+1$ and split by whether its control part has at most $s$, exactly $s+1$, or at least $s+2$ coordinates. A missing trace from the appropriate old level, component constancy at the middle case, and the two containment conditions respectively supply a missing combined trace. Cardinality is unchanged, so the modified class is maximum.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                CompressionSchemes:maximum_parent_methods.tex?#thm:fibers

                                                                Witnesses:

                                                                • Maximum Level Sum with Distinct Nonsingleton Fibers

                                                                Combinatorial and Parent-Rank Laws for Partial Traces

                                                                Name: Combinatorial and Parent-Rank Laws for Partial Traces

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Maximum-Generated Classes

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • VC Dimension
                                                                • Minimum Maximum-Parent Rank

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Partial-Trace Expansion
                                                                • Full Reduction

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For nonempty $C\subseteq\{0,1\}^X$, with one mask coordinate $a_i$ for each $i\in X$, put $D(U)=\{i:i,a_i\in U\}$. Then $\operatorname{Sh}(T(C))=\{U:D(U)\in\operatorname{Sh}(C)\}$, the zero-mask section and full mask reduction both equal $C$, $\operatorname{VC}(T(C))=|X|+\operatorname{VC}(C)$, and $h(T(C))=h(C)+|X|$, including the value $+\infty$. A rank-$r$ parent with $m$ auxiliaries yields a rank-$(r+|X|)$ parent with at most $m+|X|$ auxiliaries while retaining the original mark.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                A trace on $U$ is realizable precisely when the old class can realize the coordinates whose value and mask are both prescribed with mask zero; this proves the shattering formula and VC shift. Membership is increasing in the masks, so the zero section equals the full reduction and is $C$. For one coordinate, the fiber theorem replaces the rank-one control fiber according to the unique old height and constructs a parent one rank higher with one new auxiliary. Iterate for the upper bound. Full reduction of any parent in all mask coordinates lowers rank by $|X|$ and leaves a parent of $C$, proving equality.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                CompressionSchemes:maximum_parent_methods.tex?#thm:partial-traces

                                                                Witnesses:

                                                                • Partial-Trace Path and Star Calibrations

                                                                Disjoint Auxiliary-Witness Normal Form

                                                                Name: Disjoint Auxiliary-Witness Normal Form

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Maximum-Generated Classes

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Maximum-Parent Profile

                                                                Result Type: Construction

                                                                Statement:

                                                                If nonempty proper $C$ has a rank-$r$ maximum parent, then it has one on $X\sqcup B$ with $B=\bigsqcup_{p\in\operatorname{Patt}(C)}B_p$, $|B_p|=r+1-|\operatorname{supp}p|$, whose zero section is $C$ and whose unique missing pattern on $\operatorname{supp}p\sqcup B_p$ is $p\cup0_{B_p}$. Thus the selected witness blocks are pairwise disjoint and $|B|=\sum_p(r+1-|\operatorname{supp}p|)$. The construction may preserve the visible projection of any supplied parent.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Extract one active rank-$(r+1)$ missing pattern above each minimally missing pattern of $C$. Whenever an auxiliary coordinate is shared by several selected patterns, replace it by a maximum path with one coordinate per occurrence. The singleton-fiber case of the replacement theorem preserves rank, the zero-marked section, every selected pattern avoiding that coordinate, and the projection onto any one copy. Repeat for all shared auxiliaries and project away unused old coordinates. Each outside visible word realizes one retained selected pattern, so the final zero section is exactly $C$.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                CompressionSchemes:maximum_parent_methods.tex?#thm:disjoint-witnesses

                                                                Comments:

                                                                Only the selected witnesses are disjoint; their coordinates may occur in other parent missing patterns. This normalizes an existing parent and is not an independent existence criterion.

                                                                Complementary Fiber Replacement Obstruction

                                                                Name: Complementary Fiber Replacement Obstruction

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Maximum Classes

                                                                Result Type: Implication

                                                                Statement:

                                                                In a nontrivial old maximum sequence, if the control dimension is $m=2s+1$ with $s\ge1$, replacing even one middle fiber $B_s$ by its cube complement while keeping every other level unchanged cannot produce a maximum class.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The complement has the correct cardinality and rank, but it cannot contain the nonempty lower neighbor $B_{s-1}\subseteq B_s$, and it cannot lie in the proper upper neighbor $B_{s+1}\supseteq B_s$, since then $B_s$ together with its complement would force the full control cube into $B_{s+1}$. At least one containment condition of the exact fiber criterion applies.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                CompressionSchemes:maximum_parent_methods.tex?#cor:complement-fiber

                                                                Comments:

                                                                This only obstructs a single-level equal-cardinality replacement inside the level-sum construction; it does not disprove general maximum-generated substitution.

                                                                Let a Boolean formula use binary AND and OR, possibly negated literals, with every leaf coordinate occurring exactly once.                                                                 Proof:

                                                                Coordinate reflections implement literal negations and turn disjunction into conjunction by De Morgan duality. Expand the read-once tree from its root and apply the one-gate conjunction construction at each binary gate. Disjoint subtrees ensure that no coordinate identification is needed, and each step adds one to both rank and the auxiliary upper bound.

                                                                Statement:

Given this interval and a proper rank-$r$ parent of the outer class with $m$ auxiliaries, substitution has a rank-$(r+s)$ parent with the old auxiliaries plus those of the interval.

                                                                Projecting and fully reducing a parent of the three-section class in its two controls extracts the four consecutive maximum classes and their marked sections. Conversely, extend one nested side of the interval and the projection/reduction pair of the outer parent to maximum sequences. A level sum followed by componentwise replacement of the middle fiber by $N_0$ or $N_1$ gives the required maximum parent and retains both marks.

                                                                Statement:

Consequently every realizable ample test is universal. If $k=|Y|$ and $q_0,q_1$ count the minimal signed missing patterns of $T,T^{\mathrm c}$, respectively, $H_T$ has a rank-$(k+1)$ parent with at most $q_0+q_1+2k+2$ auxiliaries.

                                                                A realization of $H_T$ restricts to its control sections and realizes $T$. Conversely, take independent strict signed separators for $T$ and its complement. Couple the first system to the upper control and the second to the lower control, together with an inequality excluding control word $10$.                                                                 For nested shores $S\subseteq B$, write the outer signed separators independent of the replaced coordinate as $h_\ell(x)<0$ and the remaining ones as $a_p(x)+b_pz<0$ with $b_p>0$. If $\alpha_q(y)<0$ are signed separators for the inner test, then the inequalities $h_\ell(x)<0$ and $a_p(x)/b_p+\alpha_q(y)<0$ realize the substituted class $(B\times T)\cup(S\times Q^Y)$.

                                                                Proof:

                                                                A word of $B\times T$ uses an outer witness at replaced value zero and a test witness; scaling the test block makes all sums negative. A word of $S\times Q^Y$ uses an outer witness at value one, so every normalized outer term is negative; scaling the outer block dominates any chosen test signs. A forbidden outer word violates an independent separator, while a word in $(B\setminus S)\times T^{\mathrm c}$ makes one normalized outer term and one test separator nonnegative.

                                                                Rooted-Union Test for Learning-Space Roots

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $\mathcal H\subseteq2^X$ be finite, nonempty, and well graded, and let $R\in\mathcal H$. Then $R$ is a valid learning-space root exactly when $\mathcal H\triangle R$ is union closed, equivalently when $B\sqcup_R C\in\mathcal H$ for every $B,C\in\mathcal H$, where rooted union takes coordinatewise maximum outside $R$ and minimum on $R$. Every convex restriction containing a valid parent root is again a learning-space graph.

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Symmetric difference by $R$ is a cube isometry sending $R$ to the empty state and transporting ordinary union to rooted union.                                                                 Defect-Hitting Criterion for Convex Learning-Space Restrictions

                                                                Name: Defect-Hitting Criterion for Convex Learning-Space Restrictions

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Learning-Space Graphs
                                                                • Partial Cubes

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For a finite partial cube $G$, a vertex $r$, and a convex subgraph $C$ containing $r$, the vertex $r$ is a valid root of $C$ exactly when $C$ contains no complete fork of an $r$-defect of $G$. Consequently $C$ is a learning-space graph exactly when it contains a $C$-antipodal pair $r,\bar r$ and every $r$-defect fork loses a vertex outside $C$. For a semicube, every retained defect centered inside must use the boundary $\Theta$-class.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Orient every coordinate away from $r$. A failure of closedness is exactly a pair of outgoing incident edges without their square. Convexity ensures that any parent square whose fork remains in $C$ also remains entirely in $C$. A valid root supplies an opposite state by taking the union of states containing every active coordinate after translating the root to empty.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/learning-spaces/sections/convex_restrictions.tex?#prop:learning-space-defect-hitting

                                                                Two-Link Recursion for Learning-Space Families

                                                                Name: Two-Link Recursion for Learning-Space Families

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Learning-Space Graphs

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For $\mathcal H=\mathcal H_0\cup\{A\cup\{e\}:A\in\mathcal H_1\}$ with nonempty links on $Y$, union closure is equivalent to union closure of both links plus $\mathcal H_0\vee\mathcal H_1\subseteq\mathcal H_1$. Well-gradedness is equivalent to well-gradedness of both links plus $\mathcal H_0\cap\mathcal H_1\cap[A,B]_\square\ne\varnothing$ for every cross pair. Translating the links gives exact lower- and upper-root tests; with all coordinates active, an antipodal pair exists exactly when some $A\in\mathcal H_0$ has $Y\setminus A\in\mathcal H_1$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Within-side unions and tight paths reduce to the corresponding link. A cross union must land in the upper link. A cross geodesic changes $e$ exactly once at a shared state in the Boolean interval, and conversely such a state concatenates two tight link paths. The root clauses follow by translating and applying the rooted-union test.

                                                                Root Holes, Contraction Repair, and Punctured Subcubes

                                                                Name: Root Holes, Contraction Repair, and Punctured Subcubes

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For a finite well-graded family and present state $R$, deletion of coordinate $e$ makes the projected state a valid root exactly when every missing rooted union has its $e$-neighbor present. If the family is also union closed and a missing state $W$ has present neighbors in every coordinate of $C$, then the entire coordinate $C$-subcube through $W$, except $W$ itself, is present; hence the family has at least $2^{|C|}-1$ states.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Rooted union commutes with coordinate deletion, while a missing state appears after deletion precisely when its coordinate neighbor is present. Pairwise neighbor states force all two-coordinate flips by well-gradedness, and union closure then generates every nonempty flip set.

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The base combines a maximal chain with a singly punctured full fiber and an optional state; direct union and accessibility checks make it a learning space.                                                                 Two PC-Minimal Nonlearning Graphs Do Not Form a Forbidden Basis

                                                                Name: Two PC-Minimal Nonlearning Graphs Do Not Form a Forbidden Basis

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Learning-Space Graphs

                                                                Result Type: Other

                                                                Statement:

                                                                The three-leaf star $K_{1,3}$ and the six-cycle $C_6$ are pc-minor-minimal partial cubes that are not learning-space graphs. They cannot form forbidden pc-minors for the class because learning-space graphs are not pc-minor closed and can contain $K_{1,3}$ as a pc-minor.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Every proper pc-minor of the star is a path. Every one-step restriction of $C_6$ is a path and every contraction is $C_4$. All are learning-space graphs. The catalogued conditioning construction realizes the star inside a learning-space graph.
