                                                                Connected Minimal-Non-Ample Structure Theorem

                                                                Name: Connected Minimal-Non-Ample Structure Theorem

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Connected Conditioning-Minimal Non-Ample Classes

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For a conditioning-minimal non-ample class, connectedness, having at least three concepts, having an irredundant isometric one-inclusion embedding, and being the tope set of a non-free simple uniform oriented matroid are equivalent. Every proper convex antipodal subgraph of its one-inclusion graph is a hypercube, and the oriented-matroid rank equals its VC dimension.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Ample conditionings supply ambient geodesics between non-antipodal pairs. A third concept splices such geodesics between antipodes, proving isometry. Proper convex antipodal subgraphs lie in an ample conditioning and are cubes; global nonampleness then forces antipodality. Uniform-oriented-matroid tope recognition gives the classification and its converse.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                YangDim:minimal_nonample_classes.tex?#prop:partial-cube; YangDim:minimal_nonample_classes.tex?#lem:proper-antipodal; YangDim:minimal_nonample_classes.tex?#thm:antipodality; YangDim:minimal_nonample_classes.tex?#thm:mna-uom

                                                                Terminal States and Square Budget in Learning Spaces

                                                                Name: Terminal States and Square Budget in Learning Spaces

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Learning-Space Graphs

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $\mathcal H\subseteq2^X$ be finite, irredundant, well graded, and union closed, with $d=|X|$. For a state $A$, let $p(A)$ count its one-element supersets in $\mathcal H$; let $m$ and $q$ be the numbers of edges and squares, and let $m_i$ count edges in coordinate $i$. Then at least $d$ states have $p(A)=1$, $q=\sum_A\binom{p(A)}2$, each coordinate's edges form a connected graph under opposite-edge adjacency in squares, and $m-d=\sum_i(m_i-1)\le2q$. If every $p(A)\le2$, then the positive-outdegree profile is $n_0=1$, $n_1=d$, and $|\mathcal H|=1+d+n_2$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                For each coordinate $i$, the union of all states omitting $i$ is a distinct state with exactly one upward edge. Union closure completes every pair of upward edges at a state to a unique square. Tight monotone paths to unions connect all edges of a fixed coordinate through squares, giving the budget inequality after summing over coordinates. Under outdegree at most two, the edge and square counts force $n_1=d$; the full state is the unique state of outdegree zero.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/survey/main.tex?#prop:learning-space-terminal-square-budget

                                                                Crossed-Subcube Critical-Pendant Obstructions

                                                                Name: Crossed-Subcube Critical-Pendant Obstructions

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Learning-Space Graphs
                                                                • Partial Cubes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Coordinate Projection

                                                                Result Type: Construction

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $X=\{a,b,p,q\}\mathbin{\dot\cup}U\mathbin{\dot\cup}V$ have size $d\ge4$, and choose $\alpha,\beta\in\{0,1\}$. Delete from $2^X$ the two crossed wings based at $a$ and $b$, together with the optional $p$- and $q$-half-wings specified by $\alpha$ and $\beta$. The remaining family $\mathcal K_d^{\bowtie,\alpha,\beta}$ is a learning space with complementary invalid roots $R=\{b,p\}\cup V$ and $\bar R=\{a,q\}\cup U$ whose contraction-repair sets cover $X$. Its pendant extension $\mathcal Y_{d+1}^{\alpha,\beta}$ is therefore a contraction-minimal nonlearning partial cube of order $2^d-(2+\alpha)2^{|U|}-(2+\beta)2^{|V|}+2$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The deleted wings are downward closed relative to their anchor coordinates, so no union of retained states enters a wing; a direct deletion argument gives accessibility. Translating at either displayed root identifies its rooted-union holes with the opposite wing except for the shared state. The neighbor test gives two explicit repair sets whose union is every coordinate, and the critical-pair pendant theorem gives contraction minimality. Inclusion-exclusion over the wings yields the order formula.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/survey/main.tex?#prop:learning-space-crossed-subcube-pendant-obstructions

                                                                Comments:

                                                                When $U=V=\varnothing$, the three values of $\alpha+\beta$ supply the order-13, order-12, and order-11 pointed base types not represented by the chain-and-punctured-fiber family.

                                                                UOM Fibers Are Proper Conditionings of Minimal-Non-Ample Parents

                                                                Name: UOM Fibers Are Proper Conditionings of Minimal-Non-Ample Parents

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Uniform-Oriented-Matroid Fiber Classes
                                                                • Connected Conditioning-Minimal Non-Ample Classes
                                                                • Conditioning-Minimal Non-Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Coordinate Conditioning

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                UOMFib consists exactly of the finite cubes and, after fixed coordinates are suppressed, the nonempty classes obtained by fixing at least one coordinate of a conditioning-minimal non-ample parent. Apart from the parallel rank-one case, those parents are precisely the connected conditioning-minimal non-ample classes, equivalently the full tope sets of non-free simple uniform oriented matroids.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The minimal-non-ample classification identifies every nontrivial simple parent with a non-free uniform-oriented-matroid tope set, and its proper conditionings are exactly its nonempty topal fibers. Conversely, a noncube UOM fiber comes from a non-free uniform oriented matroid of rank at least two, whose full tope set is such a parent. Rank-one fibers are singletons and the definition includes all cubes separately.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                CompressionSchemes:partitionable_yang_complexes.tex?#prop:uom-fibers-minimal-nonample-conditioning-closure; YangDim:minimal_nonample_classes.tex?#thm:mna-uom

                                                                Comments:

                                                                This is a parent-to-fiber construction, not a class inclusion: the full connected parents are non-ample, whereas every UOMFib member is ample.

                                                                Exact Operation Profile of Minimal Non-Ample Classes

                                                                Name: Exact Operation Profile of Minimal Non-Ample Classes

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Conditioning-Minimal Non-Ample Classes
                                                                • Connected Conditioning-Minimal Non-Ample Classes
                                                                • Uniform-Oriented-Matroid Fiber Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Coordinate Projection
                                                                • Coordinate Conditioning
                                                                • Partial-Cube Minor

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For a conditioning-minimal non-ample class of VC dimension $k$, projection to $Z$ gives a cube for $|Z|\le k$, an antipodally punctured $(k+1)$-cube for $|Z|=k+1$, and another minimal non-ample class for $|Z|>k+1$. Every nonempty proper conditioning is a UOM fiber; consequently every nonempty pc-minor lies in either the minimal-non-ample layer or UOMFib. For a connected parent, every noncube projection in this profile remains connected.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The uniform-oriented-matroid classification turns projection into deletion of a uniform matroid, giving the three projection cases. Conditioning fixes tope signs and therefore gives a topal fiber. Once a pc-minor sequence enters UOMFib it stays there by pc-minor closure; otherwise its projection steps remain in the minimal-non-ample layer. The connected qualification follows from the non-free simple UOM recognition theorem.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                YangDim:minimal_nonample_classes.tex?#thm:structure; CompressionSchemes:partitionable_yang_complexes.tex?#prop:uom-fibers-minimal-nonample-conditioning-closure; CompressionSchemes:partitionable_yang_complexes.tex?#prop:uniform-oriented-matroid-fibers-pc-minor-closed

The complementary endpoints $R=\{b,p\}\cup V$ and $\bar R=\{a,q\}\cup U$ are invalid roots with repair sets $\{a\}\cup V\cup(\{q\} ext{ if }\epsilon=0)$ and $\{b,p,q\}\cup U$. Their pendant extension is contraction-minimal nonlearning of order $2^d-4\cdot2^{|U|}-2\cdot2^{|V|}+2$.

                                                                For the zero cap, the deleted first wing and cap form one anchored subcube, making union closure and accessibility direct; the one cap is handled after translation. Exact rooted-union witnesses determine both hole sets, the neighbor test gives the displayed repair sets, and their union is all of $X$. Inclusion-exclusion gives the order.

                                                                Learning-Space Graphs Have Infinitely Many Contraction-Minimal Obstructions

                                                                Name: Learning-Space Graphs Have Infinitely Many Contraction-Minimal Obstructions

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Learning-Space Graphs
                                                                • Partial Cubes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Coordinate Projection

                                                                Result Type: Construction

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For every $d\ge3$, the truncated cube $\mathcal T_d$ and every distant two-vertex-deleted cube $\mathcal S_{d,t}$, $3\le t\le d$, are contraction-minimal nonlearning partial cubes. For every $d\ge4$ and $0\le r\le d$, the antipode-neighborhood-deleted cube $\mathcal U_{d,r}$ is also contraction-minimal nonlearning. Hence the contraction-minimal obstruction family for learning-space graphs is infinite and has unbounded isometric dimension.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Each displayed set family is well graded. The rooted-union test excludes every possible root: translated missing sets contain a present partition witnessing failure of union closure. A contraction of $\mathcal T_d$ is a one-vertex-deleted cube; every contraction of $\mathcal S_{d,t}$ is a cube; and a contraction of $\mathcal U_{d,r}$ is either a cube or a one-vertex-deleted cube. These images are learning-space graphs, proving contraction-minimality.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/survey/main.tex?#prop:learning-space-infinite-contraction-obstructions

                                                                Antipodal Pairs Do Not Certify a Safe Convex Restriction

                                                                Name: Antipodal Pairs Do Not Certify a Safe Convex Restriction

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Learning-Space Graphs
                                                                • Partial Cubes

                                                                Result Type: Construction

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For every $d\ge4$ there is a learning space $\mathcal P_d$ of isometric dimension $d+1$ whose positive semicube in a coordinate $e$ induces a nonlearning partial cube $\mathcal F_d$ of isometric dimension $d$, even though $\mathcal F_d$ contains the antipodal pairs $\{i\},X\setminus\{i\}$ for every $i\ne a$. Thus antipodality alone does not make a convex restriction of a learning-space graph safe.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The restriction $\mathcal F_d$ is a translate of $\mathcal T_d$, so it is well graded, union closed in its displayed orientation, and has no valid root. Adding the empty state produces a union-closed well-graded family $\mathcal B_d$. Stacking $\mathcal B_d$ below a positive $e$-fiber equal to $\mathcal F_d$ gives the union-closed well-graded parent $\mathcal P_d$. The stated complementary pairs avoid all deleted states of $\mathcal F_d$.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/survey/main.tex?#prop:learning-space-antipodal-restriction-counterexamples

                                                                Low-Dimensional Antipodal Criterion for Learning-Space Graphs

                                                                Name: Low-Dimensional Antipodal Criterion for Learning-Space Graphs

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Learning-Space Graphs
                                                                • Partial Cubes

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $G$ be a finite partial cube of isometric dimension at most three whose medium admits a closed orientation. Then $G$ is a learning-space graph if and only if $G$ contains an antipodal pair. Consequently, a finite convex subgraph $C$ of a learning-space graph with $\operatorname{idim}(C)\le3$ is a learning-space graph exactly when it contains a $C$-antipodal pair. The dimension bound is sharp: the semicube $\mathcal F_4\subseteq\mathcal P_4$ is a dimension-four counterexample.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                A learning-space graph has an antipodal pair by the defect-hitting theorem. Conversely, a closed orientation gives a well-graded union-closed positive-content family. In dimensions at most three, an antipodal pair forces either the empty state to be present or a translation by one member to be union closed; the rooted-union criterion then supplies a valid root. Convex restrictions inherit a closed parent orientation, while $\mathcal F_4$ proves sharpness.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/survey/main.tex?#prop:learning-space-low-dimensional-antipodes

                                                                Dimension-Four Antipodal Trichotomy

                                                                Name: Dimension-Four Antipodal Trichotomy

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Learning-Space Graphs
                                                                • Partial Cubes

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $G$ be a finite partial cube of isometric dimension four whose medium admits a closed orientation. If $G$ has an antipodal pair but is not a learning-space graph, then $G$ is isomorphic to exactly one of $\mathcal V_4$, $\mathcal Z_4$, and $\mathcal T_4$. Equivalently, a convex subgraph $C$ of a learning-space graph with $\operatorname{idim}(C)\le4$ is learning exactly when it has a $C$-antipodal pair and is not one of these three exceptions. The six possible closed oriented normal forms collapse to those three underlying graphs.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                A closed orientation gives a well-graded union-closed positive-content family without the empty state. Classifying it by the number of present singletons leaves six rootless oriented normal forms. Coordinate translations and permutations identify three with $\mathcal V_4$, two with $\mathcal T_4$, and one with $\mathcal Z_4$; all other cases admit an explicit translated root. Convex restrictions inherit the closed orientation.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/survey/main.tex?#prop:learning-space-dimension-four-antipodes

                                                                Eleven-State Contraction Reduction

                                                                Name: Eleven-State Contraction Reduction

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Learning-Space Graphs
                                                                • Partial Cubes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Coordinate Projection

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $G$ be a closed-orientable, five-dimensional partial cube with an antipodal pair, no learning-space root, and at most eleven vertices. If some $\Theta$-class contraction is nonlearning, then $G$ has eleven vertices and is exactly one of three graphs: $\mathcal V_4$ with a pendant at an antipodal endpoint, or $\mathcal Z_4$ with a pendant at a degree-two or degree-three antipodal endpoint. Conversely, all three graphs satisfy these properties.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The contracted antipodal graph is one of $\mathcal V_4,\mathcal Z_4,\mathcal T_4$ by the dimension-four trichotomy. Vertex counting excludes $\mathcal T_4$ and forces a singleton contracted edge class over a ten-vertex core. Since both remaining cores are 2-connected, the inverse expansion must attach a pendant at an antipodal endpoint. Their automorphism orbits give exactly the three stated types; the pendant-antipode construction proves the converse.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/survey/main.tex?#prop:learning-space-eleven-state-contraction-reduction

                                                                Sharp Endpoint-Root Bound in Four Coordinates

                                                                Name: Sharp Endpoint-Root Bound in Four Coordinates

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Learning-Space Graphs

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $\mathcal H\subseteq2^X$ be well graded, let its graph be a learning-space graph, and suppose $|X|=4$ and $A,X\setminus A\in\mathcal H$. If $|\mathcal H|\le10$, then at least one endpoint of this complementary pair is a valid learning-space root. The bound is sharp: the eleven-state learning space $\mathcal L_{11}$ contains the antipodal pair $1,234$, neither of whose endpoints is valid.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Translate by an arbitrary valid root to obtain an accessible union-closed family. If neither complementary endpoint is valid, each has a rooted square defect. Separating complementary pair sizes $(1,3)$ and $(2,2)$ and counting the states forced by accessibility and union closure gives at least eleven states. Direct defects at roots $1$ and $234$ verify sharpness for $\mathcal L_{11}$.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                Name: Five-Coordinate Endpoint-Cover Reformulation

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Learning-Space Graphs
                                                                • Partial Cubes

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $\mathcal H\subseteq2^X$ be irredundant, well graded, and union closed, with $|X|=5$, $|\mathcal H|\le11$, and complementary members $A,X\setminus A$. For each coordinate $e$, the contraction $\pi_e(\mathcal H)$ is a learning-space graph exactly when one projected endpoint is a valid root. Therefore all five contractions are learning exactly when the two endpoint repair sets satisfy $\mathcal C_A(\mathcal H)\cup\mathcal C_{X\setminus A}(\mathcal H)=X$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Each contraction has at most ten states and retains a complementary pair on four coordinates. The sharp endpoint-root bound makes learning equivalent to validity of a projected endpoint. Applying the root-hole contraction-repair criterion coordinate by coordinate turns these alternatives into the displayed union of repair sets.

                                                                Two-by-Three Endpoint-Cover Obstruction

                                                                Name: Two-by-Three Endpoint-Cover Obstruction

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Partial Cubes

                                                                Result Type: Other

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $X=P\mathbin{\dot\cup}Q$ with $|P|=2$ and $|Q|=3$, and let $\mathcal H\subseteq2^X$ be union closed and well graded, with at most eleven states, no empty state, and a complementary pair $A,B$. There cannot simultaneously be an absent state whose two $P$-neighbors are present and lie in the required $A$-outward directions, and an absent state whose three $Q$-neighbors are present and has at least two required $B$-outward directions.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The two holes force punctured coordinate subcubes inside $\mathcal H$. Union closure, the endpoint directions, absence of the two holes, and the order bound reduce the possibilities to fourteen symmetry orbits. Ten order-eleven cases violate well-gradedness directly. In each of the four order-ten cases, no single additional state can repair all missing tight paths.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/survey/main.tex?#lem:learning-space-two-three-endpoint-cover

                                                                Small Contraction Descent and the Eleven-State Minimum

                                                                Name: Small Contraction Descent and the Eleven-State Minimum

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Learning-Space Graphs
                                                                • Partial Cubes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Coordinate Projection

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $G$ be a closed-orientable, five-dimensional partial cube containing an antipodal pair. If $G$ is nonlearning and has at most eleven vertices, then some $\Theta$-class contraction remains nonlearning. Consequently $G$ has exactly eleven vertices and is one of the three pendant extensions of $\mathcal V_4$ or $\mathcal Z_4$ described by the contraction-reduction theorem. The bound is sharp: the twelve-state obstruction $\mathcal H_\star$ has all five contractions learning.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                If all contractions were learning, the endpoint-cover theorem would make the two repair sets cover five directions. Repair sets of size at least four force too many states; the $(3,3)$ pattern forces at least twelve; and the remaining disjoint $(2,3)$ pattern is excluded by the two-by-three endpoint-cover lemma. The eleven-state contraction reduction then yields the three types, while $\mathcal H_\star$ proves sharpness.

Hence each family is contraction minimal.

                                                                Representation-Sensitive Recognition and Completion for Learning Spaces

                                                                Name: Representation-Sensitive Recognition and Completion for Learning Spaces

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Learning-Space Graphs

                                                                Result Type: Algorithm

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For an explicit medium with $n$ states, $m$ transitions, and $\tau$ token pairs, a given orientation can be tested for closedness in $O(m\log n)$ time with a violating state and token pair, and a closed orientation can be found or ruled out in $O(m\tau)$ time. For a listed candidate base $\mathcal B$, with $b=|\mathcal B|$ and total member size $s$, one can decide in $O(bs)$ time whether it is the base of a learning space: exactly when $\varnothing\in\mathcal B$ and every nonempty member has exactly one endpoint. A minimal well-graded extension of an arbitrary listed family is constructible in polynomial time, while deciding whether all listed input members can remain base members of some learning space is NP-complete.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                These are the cited medium-orientation, base-recognition, and extension theorems. Trying each of the $n$ states as a root and testing the induced orientation yields the derived $O(nm\log n)$ recognition bound for learning-space graphs represented as explicit finite media. Minimal extension means inclusion-minimal, not minimum cardinality.

                                                                References:

                                                                [EppsteinFalmagne08media] [EppsteinFalmagneUzun09]

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                Sandwich and Sauer--Shelah Bounds

                                                                Name: Sandwich and Sauer--Shelah Bounds

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • VC Dimension

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For every finite Boolean class $H\subseteq\{0,1\}^X$, the strongly shattered and shattered complexes satisfy $|\operatorname{sstr}(H)|\le|H|\le|\operatorname{str}(H)|$. Equality in either sandwich inequality holds exactly when $H$ is ample. Consequently, if $|X|=n$ and $\operatorname{VCdim}(H)=d$, then $|H|\le\sum_{i=0}^d\binom ni$. The cardinality bound is sharp, attained by $\binom{X}{\le d}$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The Sandwich inequalities compare a family with the supports of its contained cubes and with all supports whose traces are complete. Equality forces the two support families to coincide, which is precisely ampleness; conversely ampleness makes both inequalities equalities. Bounding the shattered complex by all subsets of size at most the VC dimension gives the Sauer--Shelah estimate.

                                                                References:

                                                                [Bollobas89] [Bollobas95] [Anstee2002] [BandeltCDK06] [Moran2012] [Sauer1972Density]

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/vc-littlestone/main.tex?#thm:vc-bounds; PartialCubes:papers/ample-corners/main.tex?#thm:sandwich

                                                                Down-Shifts Do Not Create Shattered Coordinate Sets

                                                                Name: Down-Shifts Do Not Create Shattered Coordinate Sets

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • VC Dimension

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Elementary Down-Shift

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For every Boolean class $H$ and coordinate $x$, elementary down-shifting satisfies $\operatorname{str}(D_xH)\subseteq\operatorname{str}(H)$. In particular $\operatorname{VCdim}(D_xH)\le\operatorname{VCdim}(H)$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                A shattered set omitting $x$ has the same trace before and after the shift. If a shifted class shatters a set containing $x$, each upper-fiber concept realizing a trace survived only because its matching lower concept was present before shifting; the surviving concepts and their lower mates already realize every trace in the original class.

                                                                Shattered coordinate patterns and shattered labeled trees after projection or conditioning lift to the original class.                                                                 Minimal-Pattern Coefficient Bound

                                                                Name: Minimal-Pattern Coefficient Bound

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Separation Margin

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                In a separation-margin $t$-certificate, if $p$ is a minimal missing pattern with support $P$, then every normalized row coefficient satisfies $a_{p,i}\ge2t/(1+t)$ and $t\le1/(2|P|-1)$. Hence every row coefficient is strictly positive whenever $t>0$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Minimality supplies a concept agreeing with $p$ outside each chosen coordinate $i$ and having the opposite sign at $i$. Evaluating the row at that witness gives $t(1-a_{p,i})-a_{p,i}\le-t$, which yields the coefficient bound. Summing it over the normalized row yields the margin bound.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                Name: Prescribed Coefficient Rows on a Join Tree

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Separator Coefficient Space

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Suppose the maximal local coefficient systems admit a join tree, so the systems containing each row form a connected subtree. Root the tree at $r$. If the positive-front reduction clears every child-parent row intersection at the child concept, then every feasible coefficient family on the root system extends globally. In particular the full coefficient space is nonempty, with rational extension from rational data.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Strip nonroot leaves. Rows outside the parent intersection occur only at that leaf and can be projected away; the residual intersection clears by hypothesis. Repeating leaves only the protected root system, and exact shared-row reduction extends every feasible root assignment.

                                                                Two-Coefficient-Row Feasibility Criterion

                                                                Name: Two-Coefficient-Row Feasibility Criterion

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Separator Coefficient Space

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For a blocked pair of positive normalized rows $p,q$ at concept $c$, let $I=I_c(p)$ and $J=I_c(q)$. A positive witness exists exactly when $\max_{i\in I}a_{p,i}/a_{q,i}>\min_{j\in J}a_{p,j}/a_{q,j}$, equivalently when $a_{p,i}a_{q,j}>a_{q,i}a_{p,j}$ for some $i\in I,j\in J$. Rational feasible rows admit an explicit rational witness.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                If the maximum ratio does not exceed the minimum, chaining the two strict row inequalities gives a contradiction. Conversely, choose a strict determinant pair, put positive weight one on its first coordinate, choose the second weight strictly between the two ratios, and give all remaining coordinates sufficiently small positive rational weights.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/coefficient-topology/coefficient_spaces.tex?#lem:two-row-criterion

                                                                Two-Row Recognition and Coefficient-Space Nerve

                                                                Name: Two-Row Recognition and Coefficient-Space Nerve

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Separator Coefficient Space

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                When every terminal local system in exact coefficient reduction has at most two rows, positive logarithmic compatibility margin is equivalent to nonempty coefficient space, and $\mathcal A(C)$ is homotopy equivalent to the finite nerve of its feasible strict logarithmic cones. A collection of selections is a nerve face exactly when zero is outside the convex hull of its pooled inequality vectors, giving an exact rational linear-feasibility test. Singleton-disagreement terminal pairs, and empty terminal families, give contractible coefficient spaces whenever feasible.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The two-row determinant criterion converts each terminal relation into a finite union of strict homogeneous linear systems in logarithmic coefficients. Exact reduction identifies their union with the coefficient space up to homotopy. All nonempty cone intersections are convex; the good-cover nerve theorem gives the homotopy equivalence, while strict separation of zero from the pooled convex hull gives the exact face test.

                                                                Minimal Missing Patterns Have Strictly Positive Separators

                                                                Name: Minimal Missing Patterns Have Strictly Positive Separators

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Realizable Ample Classes

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Separator Coefficient Space

                                                                Result Type: Implication

                                                                Statement:

                                                                If a nonempty complete sign class has an affine-convex realization and $p$ is a minimal missing sign pattern on support $P$, then there are strictly positive coefficients $\lambda_e$ such that $\sum_{e\in P}\lambda_e\epsilon_e f_e(z)\le0$ throughout the realizing convex domain.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Separate the affine image of the realizing domain from the disjoint open orthant cylinder specified by the missing pattern. Free coordinates force the separating functional to be supported on $P$, and unbounded signed directions make its coefficients nonnegative. If a coefficient vanished, minimality would supply a strict witness for the proper positive-support subpattern, contradicting separation; hence all coefficients are positive.

                                                                Root Faces and Canonical Cube Factors of Daisy Cubes

                                                                Name: Root Faces and Canonical Cube Factors of Daisy Cubes

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Daisy Cubes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Cartesian Product

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                If $K\subseteq2^E$ is a nonempty down-set, then its roots are exactly $2^{\operatorname{Free}(K)}$. Hence two reoriented nonempty down-sets $K$ and $\delta\triangle L$ admit a common root exactly when $\delta\subseteq\operatorname{Free}(K)\cup\operatorname{Free}(L)$. More generally, every nonempty daisy representation $D$ has a unique root $r_0$ disjoint from $F=\operatorname{Free}(D)$ and a unique nonempty single-root down-set $U$ on $E\setminus F$ such that $D=r_0\triangle(2^F\times U)$; its full root set is $r_0\triangle2^F$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Toggling a free coordinate preserves a down-set. Conversely, if a coordinate belongs to a translating root, downward closure before and after translation forces both values to occur together, so that coordinate is free. The common-root condition is intersection of the two Boolean root faces. Factoring membership over all free coordinates yields $2^F\times U$; removing the free part from any root gives the unique distinguished root and leaves $U$ with no free coordinate and only the empty root.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/daisy-cubes/sections/daisy_pc_minors_body.tex?#lem:root-face; PartialCubes:papers/daisy-cubes/sections/daisy_pc_minors_body.tex?#cor:root-factor-decomposition

                                                                Name: Elementary Minors of a Peripheral Daisy Expansion

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Daisy Cubes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Peripheral Expansion
                                                                • Coordinate Projection
                                                                • Coordinate Conditioning

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For nonempty down-sets $K,L\subseteq2^E$ with $\delta\triangle L\subseteq K$, the peripheral expansion $C(K,L,\delta)$ is a daisy cube exactly when $\delta\subseteq\operatorname{Free}(K)\cup\operatorname{Free}(L)$. Restriction in an old coordinate $i$ gives $C(K_i^b,L_i^{b\oplus\mathbf1_{i\in\delta}},\delta\setminus\{i\})$, contraction gives $C(K_i^0,L_i^0,\delta\setminus\{i\})$, and the new-coordinate restrictions and contraction are respectively $K$, $\delta\triangle L$, and $K$ after suppressing constants.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The expansion is daisy precisely when one reorientation makes both layers down-sets, which is the common-root criterion. Taking an old-coordinate section tracks whether its bit is flipped by $\delta$; projection of a down-set equals its zero section because its one section is contained there. The new-coordinate formulas follow directly from the two-layer construction.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/daisy-cubes/sections/daisy_pc_minors_body.tex?#lem:expansion-minors

                                                                Antipodal Rigidity from Daisy Restrictions

                                                                Name: Antipodal Rigidity from Daisy Restrictions

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Daisy Cubes
                                                                • Partial Cubes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Coordinate Conditioning

                                                                Result Type: Implication

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $X\subseteq2^E$ be an irredundant partial-cube representation. If every elementary coordinate restriction is a daisy cube and no coordinate of $X$ is peripheral, then $X$ is invariant under the global cube antipode $x\mapsto E\setminus x$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                For each coordinate, choose boundary vertices on both sides. Any agreement in another coordinate would survive in a restriction having two-sided boundary, impossible for a daisy cube, so the boundary vertices are antipodal and unique. Membership changes across an edge exactly when it changes across the antipodal edge. The xor of membership at antipodal vertices is therefore constant on the connected ambient cube, and the selected antipodal pair makes it zero.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/daisy-cubes/sections/daisy_pc_minors_body.tex?#lem:antipodal-rigidity

                                                                Common Deletion--Link Form of a Peripheral Daisy Obstruction

                                                                Name: Common Deletion--Link Form of a Peripheral Daisy Obstruction

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Daisy Cubes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Peripheral Expansion
                                                                • Partial-Cube Minor

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                In a reduced-root peripheral obstruction $C(K,L,P)$, put $N=E\setminus P$. There is one set $A\subseteq N$ such that for every $p\in P$, the deletion--link differences are singletons $\Delta_p(K)=\{(P\setminus\{p\})\cup A\}$ and $\Delta_p(L)=\{(P\setminus\{p\})\cup(N\setminus A)\}$. Thus every incompatible root coordinate sees the same complementary outside part.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Minimality makes every old-coordinate restriction and contraction root-compatible. For each $p$, these constraints fix every other coordinate on both nonempty deletion--link differences, with all other root coordinates equal to one and the outside coordinates complementary, so both differences are singletons. Comparing the top $P$-sections of the down-set $K$ then forces the outside singleton part to be independent of $p$.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/daisy-cubes/sections/daisy_pc_minors_body.tex?#lem:common-form

                                                                Intrinsic Antipodal-Deletion Basis for Daisy Cubes

                                                                Name: Intrinsic Antipodal-Deletion Basis for Daisy Cubes

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Daisy Cubes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Concept Deletion
                                                                • Partial-Cube Minor

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $D$ be an irredundant daisy cube of isometric dimension at least three with at least two roots. If ambient-antipodal vertices $x,y$ are each maximal from some root, then $D\setminus\{x,y\}$ is pc-minimal outside the daisy cubes. Conversely, every forbidden pc-minor for daisy cubes arises this way. The witnessing roots are unique and differ exactly on $\operatorname{Free}(D)$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Use the canonical factorization $D=2^F\times U$ with $U$ single-root. Maximality from a root makes the $F$-part of each deleted vertex opposite that root and makes their complementary $U$-parts maximal. If $U$ is trivial the deletion is $Q_{|F|}^{--}$; otherwise it is the peripheral normal form. The complete coordinate basis gives the converse, and the factor calculation yields the two unique opposite roots.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/daisy-cubes/sections/daisy_pc_minors_body.tex?#thm:intrinsic-antipodal-deletion

                                                                Ample and Nonample Daisy Obstructions

                                                                Name: Ample and Nonample Daisy Obstructions

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Daisy Cubes
                                                                • Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Partial-Cube Minor

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                A forbidden pc-minor for daisy cubes is nonample exactly when it is an antipodally punctured hypercube $Q_n^{--}$ for some $n\ge3$. Every obstruction in the peripheral coordinate normal form is ample.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The $Q_n^{--}$ are precisely the forbidden pc-minors for ampleness. If a daisy obstruction were nonample, it would contain some $Q_n^{--}$ as a pc-minor; since that minor is itself nondaisy, pc-minimality forces equality with the whole obstruction. All remaining members of the complete daisy basis are therefore ample.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/daisy-cubes/sections/daisy_pc_minors_body.tex?#cor:ample-daisy-obstructions

                                                                Facet-Cube Structure of Ample Classes

                                                                Name: Facet-Cube Structure of Ample Classes

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Cornerless Ample Classes

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Every facet of the shattered complex of a nonempty ample class supports exactly one contained cube. These facet cubes are exactly the maximal cubes, their union is the class, and a vertex is a corner exactly when it lies in one facet cube. Consequently the class is cornerless exactly when every vertex lies in at least two facet cubes. Conversely, choosing one placed cube for each facet of a down-set $\Sigma$ produces an ample class with shattered complex $\Sigma$ whenever their union shatters no support outside $\Sigma$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                For a facet $S$, the reduction $C^S$ is ample and has only the empty strongly shattered support, so Sandwich equality makes it a singleton and gives the unique placement. A maximal cube has an isolated placement in its reduction; connectedness of nonempty ample reductions forces that reduction to be a singleton, so its support is a facet. Every vertex lies in a maximal cube, giving the corner criterion. In the converse direction, the chosen cubes give $\Sigma\subseteq\operatorname{sstr}(U)$ while the hypothesis gives $\operatorname{str}(U)\subseteq\Sigma$; the Sandwich inequalities force equality throughout.

                                                                References:

                                                                [BandeltCDK06] [ChalopiChepoiMoran22]

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/ample-corners/main.tex?#lem:facet-cubes; PartialCubes:papers/ample-corners/main.tex?#cor:cornerless-cover

                                                                Witnesses:

                                                                • Vertex-Deleted Three-Cube
                                                                • A Non-Ample Union of Chosen Facet Edges

                                                                Local Corner Criterion

                                                                Name: Local Corner Criterion

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Cornerless Ample Classes

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For any Boolean class $C$ and vertex $v\in C$, let $I_C(v)$ be the coordinates of the neighbours of $v$ in $C$. Then $v$ is a corner exactly when the cube spanned by $v$ in all directions $I_C(v)$ is contained in $C$. If a corner belongs to a coordinate face, it remains a corner in the induced section on that face.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Every cube through $v$ uses only incident directions. If their full span is present, it contains every cube through $v$ and is the unique maximal one. Conversely, when $v$ has a unique maximal cube, every incident edge extends into that cube, so its support contains every incident direction and it equals the full span.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/ample-corners/main.tex?#lem:local-corner; PartialCubes:papers/gluing/main.tex?#lem:corner

                                                                Dimension Bounds for Cornerless Ample Classes

                                                                Name: Dimension Bounds for Cornerless Ample Classes

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Cornerless Ample Classes
                                                                • Maximum Classes

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • VC Dimension

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                If a nonempty cornerless ample class has VC dimension $d$ and $n$ active coordinates, then $3\le d\le n-1$. If it is maximum, then $3\le d\le n-2$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Ample classes of VC dimension at most two are corner peelable and therefore have a corner. At $d=n$, ampleness forces the full cube, whose vertices are corners. A maximum class with $d=n-1$ has $2^n-1$ vertices and is a cube with one vertex deleted; its corners are the neighbours of the missing vertex.

                                                                References:

                                                                \cite[Proposition~4.11]{ChalopiChepoiMoran22}

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/ample-corners/main.tex?#lem:small-vc

                                                                Cornerlessness Descends through Peripheral Coordinates

                                                                Name: Cornerlessness Descends through Peripheral Coordinates

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Cornerless Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Full Reduction

                                                                Result Type: Implication

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Write an ample class with an active peripheral coordinate as $C=(B\times\{0\})\cup(S\times\{1\})$ with $\varnothing\ne S\subseteq B$. Then $S$ is ample, and $(s,1)$ is a corner of $C$ exactly when $s$ is a corner of $S$. In particular, a cornerless $C$ has a nonempty cornerless ample reduction $S$ on one fewer coordinate.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The site $S$ is the full reduction in the peripheral coordinate and is ample. Every cube through $(s,1)$ extends across that coordinate because its lower copy lies in $B$. Thus the maximal cubes through $(s,1)$ are precisely $Q\times\{0,1\}$ for maximal cubes $Q$ of $S$ through $s$, preserving their number and hence the corner condition.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/ample-corners/main.tex?#lem:peripheral

                                                                Corners Factor through Cartesian Products

                                                                Name: Corners Factor through Cartesian Products

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Cornerless Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Cartesian Product

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For nonempty Boolean classes $A$ and $B$ on disjoint coordinate sets, the maximal cubes of $A\times B$ are exactly the products of maximal cubes of the factors. A vertex $(a,b)$ is a corner exactly when both $a$ and $b$ are corners. Hence a cornerless product has a cornerless factor; for ample factors that factor is again ample.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Every cube in the product factors uniquely over the two coordinate blocks, and it is maximal exactly when both factor cubes are maximal. The number of maximal cubes through $(a,b)$ is therefore the product of the corresponding two counts, which equals one exactly when both counts equal one. Ampleness also factors through Cartesian products.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/ample-corners/main.tex?#lem:products

                                                                Cornerless Minimum Equals the Dismantlable-Ample Obstruction Minimum

                                                                Name: Cornerless Minimum Equals the Dismantlable-Ample Obstruction Minimum

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Cornerless Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Partial-Cube Minor

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                The least order $c_{\min}$ of a nonempty cornerless ample class equals the least order $m_{\mathrm{amp}}$ of an ample forbidden pc-minor for the dismantlable ample classes. More precisely, every such forbidden pc-minor contains a nonempty cornerless ample subclass, and every nonempty cornerless ample class has such a forbidden pc-minor of order at most its own.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Starting from an ample forbidden pc-minor, repeatedly delete corners. Corner deletion preserves ampleness, and the process cannot empty the class because that would be a corner peeling; it therefore ends in a nonempty cornerless ample subclass. Conversely, a cornerless ample class is not dismantlable. Choose a smallest pc-minor of it that is still not dismantlable. Every proper pc-minor has fewer vertices and is dismantlable by minimality, while ample pc-minor closure keeps the chosen class ample, so it is a forbidden pc-minor of no larger order.

                                                                References:

                                                                [ChalopiChepoiMoran22] [BousquetDampReader]

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/ample-corners/main.tex?#prop:cmin-equals-mamp

                                                                • The 267-Concept Cornerless Ample Class

                                                                Exact Facet-Cube SAT Encodings

                                                                Name: Exact Facet-Cube SAT Encodings

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Maximum Classes
                                                                • Cornerless Ample Classes

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                The formula $F_{n,d}$ is satisfiable exactly when there is a nonempty cornerless ample class on $n$ active coordinates with VC dimension $d$; its variables recover the shattered complex, the unique facet cubes, and the vertex set. When the complex is fixed to all supports of size at most $d$, the reduced formula $M_{n,d}$ is satisfiable exactly when there is a cornerless maximum class of VC dimension $d$ on $[n]$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                A model chooses a down-set, exactly one placed cube for each facet, and their covered union. Missing-trace clauses prevent the union from shattering anything outside the down-set, so the facet-cube converse theorem makes it ample with the selected shattered complex. Double-coverage clauses are exactly cornerlessness. Conversely, the shattered complex, unique facet cubes, vertex set, and one absent trace for every unshattered support of any admissible class satisfy all clauses. Fixing the down-set to all supports of size at most $d$ gives the maximum specialization.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/ample-corners/main.tex?#thm:encoding; PartialCubes:papers/ample-corners/main.tex?#prop:maximum-encoding

                                                                Name: Exact Encoding of Bounded Cornerless Lifts

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Cornerless Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Coordinate Projection

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For a fixed Boolean class $B$, a new coordinate $z$, and an integer $N$, the formula $L_{B,N}$ is satisfiable exactly when $B$ has a cornerless ample lift $Y\subseteq B\times\{0,1\}$ of order at most $N$, with all old coordinates and $z$ active and with projection along $z$ equal to $B$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Restricting the general facet-cube encoding to vertices and cubes inside $B\times\{0,1\}$ preserves exactness because every facet cube of a lift lies there. Requiring at least one copy of every $b\in B$ makes the projection contain $B$, while the ambient restriction gives the reverse inclusion. A totalizer imposes the order bound, and the remaining clauses retain exact ampleness, activity, and cornerlessness.

                                                                Cube-Symmetry Lex Leaders Preserve SAT Satisfiability

                                                                Name: Cube-Symmetry Lex Leaders Preserve SAT Satisfiability

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Maximum Classes
                                                                • Cornerless Ample Classes

                                                                Result Type: Algorithm

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Adding lexicographic leader constraints for adjacent coordinate transpositions and single-coordinate reflections to $F_{n,d}$ or $M_{n,d}$ preserves satisfiability.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Cube automorphisms preserve every encoded property and permute the facet-cube indicator vector equivariantly. In the finite orbit of any admissible class, choose the class with lexicographically least indicator vector.                                                                 Small Ample Classes Have Corners

                                                                Name: Small Ample Classes Have Corners

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Maximum Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes
                                                                • Cornerless Ample Classes

                                                                Result Type: Implication

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Every nonempty ample class on at most seven coordinates has a corner and therefore has a complete corner peeling. Every maximum class on at most eight coordinates has a corner. Consequently, a cornerless ample class on eight active coordinates has no peripheral coordinate and no nontrivial Cartesian product decomposition.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The exact formulas $F_{n,d}$ with lex leaders are certified unsatisfiable for all 15 cases $3\le d\le n\le7$; the structural dimension bound handles smaller VC dimensions. Repeated corner deletion preserves ampleness, giving a complete peeling. For maximum classes on eight coordinates, the four possible cornerless dimensions $3\le d\le6$ are excluded by checked $M_{8,d}$ certificates. Peripheral or product descent from a cornerless eight-coordinate class would produce a cornerless ample class on at most seven coordinates, contradicting the first result.

                                                                Shattered Complex of the 267-Concept Cornerless Class

                                                                Name: Shattered Complex of the 267-Concept Cornerless Class

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Cornerless Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Coordinate Projection

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Partition the twelve coordinates of $Y_{267}$ into three consecutive groups of four, each split into two labelled pairs. Its shattered supports are the empty set, all singletons and pairs, and exactly the 188 triples that are not transversals meeting every group once with even label parity. These triples are its facet supports, every coordinate contraction has 208 concepts, and its cube-automorphism group is trivial.
