                                                                Composition Law for Simplicial Shelling Records

                                                                Name: Composition Law for Simplicial Shelling Records

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Common-Section Gluing

                                                                Result Type: Construction

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For pure simplicial pieces over a common pure base $\Gamma$, with pairwise disjoint private vertices and one distinguished facet over each base facet, a global shelling record $(\pi,S)$ exists exactly when every piece has a local record $(\pi,S_i)$ with the same distinguished-facet order and the active sets $S_i$ are pairwise disjoint; then $S=\bigcup_iS_i$. Any chosen compatible local shellings can be interleaved while preserving every local order. When the base has one empty facet, this says that the polyhedral-join assembly is shellable exactly when every factor is shellable and all but at most one can start at its chosen facet.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                For compatible records, interleave local blocks between successive distinguished facets. Any earlier facet from another piece has its intersection with the current facet covered by an already inserted distinguished facet; simultaneous activity would be the only obstruction. Conversely, links in the fixed private blocks recover all local shellings. If two pieces were active at one base facet, a codimension-two link in the prefix would be a disconnected union of two stars, contradicting shellability. The one-facet base specializes activity to whether the chosen facet occurs first.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/gluing/main.tex?#thm:simplicial-composition; PartialCubes:papers/gluing/main.tex?#cor:prescribed-first-facet

                                                                Witnesses:

                                                                • Two-Path Shelling Compatibility Conflict
                                                                • Tetrahedral-Boundary Shelling Composition

                                                                Attachment Test for Relative Shellability

                                                                Name: Attachment Test for Relative Shellability

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Common-Section Gluing

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $\Delta$ be a finite pure complex of nonnegative dimension in which every ridge belongs to at most two facets, and let $\Gamma$ be a nonempty facet-generated subcomplex. If $\Lambda$ is pure and shellable but no shelling starts at a chosen facet $\rho$, then $\Theta=(\Delta*\langle\rho\rangle)\cup(\Gamma*\Lambda)$ is shellable exactly when $\Gamma$ is shellable and $(\Delta,\Gamma)$ is relatively shellable.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Shellings of $\Gamma$, $\Lambda$, and the relative pair concatenate to give sufficiency. Conversely, the links of $\rho$ and of any other facet of $\Lambda$ recover shellings of $\Delta$ and $\Gamma$. Because $\rho$ cannot start a shelling of $\Lambda$, every $\Gamma$ facet precedes each ridge-adjacent outside facet: otherwise a codimension-two prefix link is disconnected, with the missing mixed edge as its only possible bridge. Non-ridge-sharing consecutive facets commute, so all $\Gamma$ facets can be moved first; the remaining order is relative.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/gluing/main.tex?#thm:shelling-attachment

                                                                Composition Law for Corner-Peeling Records

                                                                Name: Composition Law for Corner-Peeling Records

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Common-Section Gluing

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For arbitrary Boolean pieces over a common section $D$, record a complete corner peeling by its induced order $\pi$ on $D$ and by the common vertices that still have a private neighbour when deleted. A global peeling has record $(\pi,S)$ exactly when every piece has a record $(\pi,S_i)$ with pairwise disjoint active sets, in which case $S=\bigcup_iS_i$. Thus the union peels exactly when compatible local records exist; ampleness is not required.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Restricting a global peeling to each coordinate section gives local peelings with one common order. Two pieces cannot both be active at a common vertex because their private directions would require an absent mixed square in its incident corner cube. Conversely, synchronize compatible local peelings at successive common vertices. Private deletions see only their local piece, and at a common deletion all private incident directions occur in at most one local state, whose corner cube certifies the global deletion.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/gluing/main.tex?#thm:composition

                                                                Witnesses:

                                                                • Two Squares Glued along a Common Edge

                                                                Relative Shelling--Corner Peeling Dictionary

                                                                Name: Relative Shelling--Corner Peeling Dictionary

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For nonempty ample families $K\subseteq A\subseteq Q_E$, $A$ corner-peels down to $K$ exactly when the signed-facet pair $(\mathcal S_E(A),\mathcal S_E(K))$ is relatively shellable. The orders correspond by reversal.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                In a relative shelling, the ridge criterion for adding the signed facet of $v$ says that for every old vertex $b$, some old neighbour $u$ of $v$ begins a Hamming geodesic to $b$. Isometry of the ample old family makes the enlarged family isometric, hence ample, and $v$ is a corner. Induction gives a reversed peeling. Conversely, corner deletion preserves ampleness; shortest paths from the restored corner to every old vertex begin with a neighbour satisfying the ridge criterion.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/gluing/main.tex?#prop:relative-shelling-dictionary

                                                                Empty Active Records Characterize Relative Peeling

                                                                Name: Empty Active Records Characterize Relative Peeling

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $A$ be a piece over a peelable common section $D$. Then $A$ corner-peels down to $D$ if and only if its record set contains $(\pi,\varnothing)$ for some complete peeling order $\pi$ of $D$, and this is equivalent to containing $(\pi,\varnothing)$ for every such order.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                A relative peeling followed by any peeling of $D$ gives every empty-active record. Conversely, start from a complete peeling with empty active set, retain the common vertices, and execute only its outside deletions. A retained common vertex had no private neighbor when originally deleted, so restoring it introduces no neighbor at any later outside deletion. Each original corner cube therefore remains valid, and the retained family is exactly $D$.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/gluing/main.tex?#lem:relative

                                                                Product Attachments Test Relative Peeling

                                                                Name: Product Attachments Test Relative Peeling

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Cartesian Product
                                                                • Common-Section Gluing

                                                                Result Type: Construction

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Fix a finite ample family $R\subseteq Q_F$ containing $0_F$ that peels but has no peeling ending at $0_F$. For nonempty ample $K\subseteq A\subseteq Q_E$, set $P_R(A,K)=(A\times\{0_F\})\cup(K\times R)$. Then $P_R(A,K)$ is ample, has $|A|+(|R|-1)|K|$ vertices, and peels if and only if $K$ peels and $A$ peels down to $K$. A fixed 289-vertex choice of $R$ therefore reduces relative peeling to ordinary peeling with constant-factor growth.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                If a shattered support uses a new coordinate, its old part is shattered by $K$ and its new part by $R$, so the product of witnessing cubes lies in $K\times R$; supports using only old coordinates are witnessed in $A$. For necessity, every root $(k,0)$ must retain a private neighbor when deleted, or the induced peeling of $R$ could end at its root. The missing mixed square then prevents a simultaneous neighbor in $A\setminus K$, and retaining all of $K$ yields a relative peeling of $A$; a nonroot layer restricts to a peeling of $K$. Conversely, peel $A$ to $K$ and then peel the product $K\times R$ layer by layer.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/gluing/main.tex?#thm:attachment; PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#thm:damp-relative-attachment-test

                                                                Witnesses:

                                                                • Rooted 289-Vertex Peeling Factor

                                                                Exact Records of Product-Attachment Test Pieces

                                                                Name: Exact Records of Product-Attachment Test Pieces

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Common-Section Gluing

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $D$ be a nonempty ample common section, let nonempty ample $K\subseteq D$, and put $C_K=P_R(D,K)$ using the rooted attachment factor. Then $\operatorname{Tr}_D(C_K)$ consists exactly of the pairs $(\pi,K)$ such that every edge $xy$ with $x\in K$ and $y\in D\setminus K$ has $y$ before $x$ in $\pi$. If $K$ peels, then for every ample piece $A$ over $D$, the gluing $A\oplus_D C_K$ peels if and only if $A$ peels down to $K$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Restriction to each $R$-fiber forces every vertex of $K$ to be active, while vertices outside $K$ have no private neighbors. Missing mixed squares force the displayed edge precedences. Conversely, the precedences let one commute nonadjacent deletions until $D\setminus K$ precedes $K$; a peeling of $R$ can then be executed layer by layer around the prescribed order. The testing equivalence is the product-attachment theorem applied to $P_R(A,K)$.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/gluing/main.tex?#prop:context-records

                                                                Witnesses:

                                                                • Rooted 289-Vertex Peeling Factor

                                                                Relative Peeling Failures Transfer to Forbidden PC-Minors

                                                                Name: Relative Peeling Failures Transfer to Forbidden PC-Minors

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Common-Section Gluing
                                                                • Partial-Cube Minor

                                                                Result Type: Construction

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let rooted ample $R$ peel but not to its root, and suppose every elementary root-preserving restriction or contraction of $R$ peels to its induced root. Let nonempty ample peelable $K\subseteq A\subseteq Q_E$ have all coordinates active, and assume the same for $R$. Then $P_R(A,K)$ is a forbidden pc-minor for corner-peelable ample families exactly when $A$ does not peel down to $K$, while $\mu A$ peels down to $\mu K$ for every elementary restriction or contraction $\mu$ on an old coordinate for which $\mu K$ is nonempty.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                An old-coordinate operation commutes with the attachment: $\mu P_R(A,K)=P_R(\mu A,\mu K)$. On a new coordinate, root-preserving restriction and contraction replace $R$ by the corresponding rooted image, while the opposite restriction is a product over $K$; all three peel by hypothesis. If an old-coordinate image of $K$ is empty, the image is merely $\mu A$. Otherwise the attachment theorem says it peels exactly when $\mu A$ peels down to $\mu K$. The same theorem detects nonpeelability of the original attachment, giving both directions.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/gluing/main.tex?#thm:minor-transfer; PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#thm:damp-relative-attachment-minimality

                                                                Finite Gluing-Behavior Monoid and Relative-Peeling Nilpotence

                                                                Name: Finite Gluing-Behavior Monoid and Relative-Peeling Nilpotence

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Common-Section Gluing

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Fix a nonempty peelable ample common section $D$ of order $N$. Declare two ample pieces interchangeable when gluing either to any ample test piece gives the same peelability answer. Equal record sets imply interchangeability; there are at most $2^{|\operatorname{Ord}(D)|2^N}$ classes, and gluing makes them a commutative monoid with identity $[D]$. A piece represents the identity exactly when it peels down to $D$. The union of $N+1$ pieces that each fail to peel to $D$ is nonpeelable; $N+1$ copies of $A$ peel exactly when $A$ peels to $D$, equivalently when every positive number of copies peels; and $A\oplus_D B$ peels to $D$ exactly when both factors do. Consequently, if the monoid is nontrivial, all nonpeelable pieces form one absorbing zero class, the nonidentity classes form an ideal, and every product of $N+1$ nonidentity elements is zero.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The record composition law proves sufficiency of record equality and compatibility of interchangeability with gluing; counting record subsets gives the finite bound. Empty-active records characterize relative peeling and compose with every test record, which identifies the identity class. Every piece failing to peel to $D$ has only nonempty active sets, and $N+1$ such sets cannot be pairwise disjoint in an $N$-vertex section. This proves the repeated-gluing statements. Restricting a relative peeling to either factor proves necessity for a two-factor union, while concatenating the two relative peelings proves sufficiency. Coordinate-section inheritance makes every union containing a nonpeelable piece nonpeelable, yielding the zero and ideal laws.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/gluing/main.tex?#prop:finite; PartialCubes:papers/gluing/main.tex?#thm:structure

                                                                Witnesses:

                                                                • Singleton--Edge Record Coarsening

                                                                Fully Active Records Determine One Gluing-Behavior Class

                                                                Name: Fully Active Records Determine One Gluing-Behavior Class

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Common-Section Gluing

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For a nonempty peelable ample common section $D$ and the rooted attachment factor $R$, the product piece $\Omega_D=D\times R$ has record set $\{(\pi,D):\pi\in\operatorname{Ord}(D)\}$. Every peelable piece all of whose records have active set $D$ is interchangeable with $\Omega_D$: its union with a test piece $C$ peels exactly when $C$ peels down to $D$. Moreover, every peelable piece failing to peel down to $D$ can be extended by at most $|D|-1$ further such failing pieces to a peelable piece in this fully active class.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The exact context-record formula with attachment site $K=D$ gives the records of $\Omega_D$. Compatibility with a fully active record requires the test piece to have an empty-active record, which is equivalent to peeling down to $D$ and then holds for every order. Starting from any peelable nonidentity piece, repeatedly glue a test piece that distinguishes its class from the fully active class. Each added piece also fails to peel to $D$, while the union remains peelable. The $|D|+1$-factor nilpotence bound forces this process to stop after at most $|D|-1$ additions.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/gluing/main.tex?#prop:fully-active

                                                                Witnesses:

                                                                • Opposite Fully-Active Edge Records with Identical Gluing Behavior

                                                                Bounded Path-Interval Families Are Cover-Recursive

                                                                Name: Bounded Path-Interval Families Are Cover-Recursive

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Convex-Treelike Partial Cubes

                                                                Result Type: Construction

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For $m\ge0$, let $\mathcal J_m$ consist of the empty set and every interval of length at most three in the path on $[m]$. Then $\mathcal J_m$ is cover-recursively peripheral.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Induct on $m$. The concepts containing the last coordinate $m$ become $\varnothing$, $\{m-1\}$, and $\{m-2,m-1\}$ after deleting it, when defined, and all lie in the zero section. Thus the one-semicube is peripheral. Its contraction base is $\mathcal J_{m-1}$ and its duplicated site is a path on at most three vertices; both belong to the class.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/cover-recursive/main.tex?#lem:path-intervals

                                                                Exact Parameters and Minimality of Cyclic-Arc Obstructions

                                                                Name: Exact Parameters and Minimality of Cyclic-Arc Obstructions

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes
                                                                • Convex-Treelike Partial Cubes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Partial-Cube Minor

                                                                Result Type: Construction

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For every $n\ge5$, $\mathcal A_n$ is an ample partial cube with $3n+1$ vertices, VC dimension two, and isometric dimension $n$. It is periphery-free, while every proper pc-minor is cover-recursively peripheral. Hence $\mathcal A_n$ is an ample forbidden pc-minor for the cover-recursively peripheral class; $\mathcal A_5=\mathcal P_5$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The shattered supports are the empty set, all $n$ singletons, and exactly the $2n$ coordinate pairs at cyclic distance one or two; explicit edges and squares strongly shatter all of them, while no triple is shattered. Opposing witnesses make the two projected sections incomparable in every coordinate. A zero section is the path-interval family $\mathcal J_{n-1}$; a one section peels by two pendant deletions to a square; and the contraction has a peripheral step with path site and base $\mathcal J_{n-2}$. Rotation handles every coordinate, proving pc-minimality.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/cover-recursive/main.tex?#thm:cyclic-arcs

                                                                Deletion Rule for Short and Long Cyclic Sets

                                                                Name: Deletion Rule for Short and Long Cyclic Sets

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $n\ge9$, $S\in\mathcal F_n$, and $x\in S$. Then $S\setminus\{x\}$ remains in $\mathcal F_n$ unless $S$ is long and $x$ is its midpoint. In that exceptional case the deletion is outside $\mathcal F_n$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Every nonempty subset of a short set is short. A long set has compulsory points $a,a+2,a+4$: deleting an optional point leaves it long, and deleting either endpoint leaves at most three points in an arc of length four. Deleting the midpoint leaves both endpoints but omits the midpoint; its unique arc of length five shows it is neither short nor long.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/cover-recursive/main.tex?#lem:step-two-deletion

                                                                Exact Parameters and Minimality of Step-Two Obstructions

                                                                Name: Exact Parameters and Minimality of Step-Two Obstructions

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes
                                                                • Convex-Treelike Partial Cubes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Partial-Cube Minor

                                                                Result Type: Construction

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For every odd $n\ge9$, $\mathcal F_n$ is an ample partial cube with $10n+1$ vertices, VC dimension three, and isometric dimension $n$. It is periphery-free, while every proper pc-minor is cover-recursively peripheral. In each coordinate one oriented section defect consists of three vertices inducing a path.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The shattered complex contains the empty set, $n$ singletons, $4n$ pair orbits, and $5n$ triple orbits, all with explicit positioned cubes; the forbidden alternating triple prevents higher shattering, so the count equals $10n+1$. The deletion rule makes the one-sided defect exactly a three-vertex path and a distant singleton witnesses the opposite noncontainment. For an elementary minor, a fixed 27-vertex one-section has a recursive peripheral decomposition. The zero section and contraction peel coordinates in the order $2,4,6,\ldots$ with duplicated sites that are pc-minors of that one-section. Oddness makes step two traverse every remaining coordinate; rotation handles all starting coordinates.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                Name: Sharpness of the Cover-Recursive Position Bounds

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Tree-Like Partial Cubes
                                                                • Proper Semi-Median Partial Cubes
                                                                • Almost-Median Partial Cubes

                                                                Result Type: Implication

                                                                Statement:

                                                                The cover-recursively peripheral class is a strict subclass both of the intersection of tree-like and proper semi-median partial cubes and of the intersection of tree-like, almost-median, ample, and corner-peelable partial cubes.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Expand $Q_5$ peripherally along the pentagonal obstruction $\mathcal P_5$. The output is tree-like; the isometric ample site and cube base make it almost-median, ample, corner-peelable, and proper semi-median. Its copied site is a convex semicube isomorphic to $\mathcal P_5$. Convex heredity would force this obstruction into the cover-recursive class if the expanded graph belonged to it, so it witnesses both strict containments.

                                                                Structure of Partial Cubes with At Most Two Excess Vertices

                                                                Name: Structure of Partial Cubes with At Most Two Excess Vertices

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Partial Cubes
                                                                • Trees

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                A connected partial cube of isometric dimension $d$ has at least $d+1$ vertices. Equality holds exactly in the tree case. If it has $d+2$ vertices, it is unicyclic and its unique cycle is a square. Consequently every nontrivial partial cube with at most $d+2$ vertices has a peripheral coordinate.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Reverse a complete sequence of $d$ coordinate contractions and let $s_i$ be the order of the site duplicated by expansion $i$. Then $|V|=1+\sum_i s_i$ and the excess over $d+1$ is $\sum_i(s_i-1)$. Zero excess makes every new coordinate a bridge and yields a tree. Excess one permits exactly one two-vertex site; it is an edge in the preceding tree, its duplication creates one square, and all later singleton-site expansions attach bridges. A leaf edge is peripheral, while every coordinate of a bare square is peripheral.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/cover-recursive/main.tex?#lem:low-excess; PartialCubes:papers/survey/main.tex?#lem:low-excess-partial-cubes

                                                                Gated-Amalgam Closure Reduces to Prime Obstructions

                                                                Name: Gated-Amalgam Closure Reduces to Prime Obstructions

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Convex-Treelike Partial Cubes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Gated Amalgam
                                                                • Partial-Cube Minor

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                The cover-recursively peripheral class is closed under gated amalgamation if and only if every one of its forbidden pc-minors is gated-prime. Every antipodally punctured cube $Q_n^{--}$ is gated-prime. Exact coordinate-face audits also make the pentagonal obstruction $\mathcal P_5$ and Hall-derived obstruction $\mathcal H_{22}$ gated-prime.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                A proper gated decomposition of a minimal obstruction has both pieces as proper convex pc-minors in the class, contradicting closure. Conversely, track the two gated pieces through a descent to a minimal forbidden pc-minor: nonempty restrictions and contractions preserve gatedness, intersection, properness, and membership of both images, producing a forbidden gated decomposition. For $Q_n^{--}$, two proper Boolean faces cannot cover all but two cube vertices; the finite claims follow from exhaustive gated coordinate-face audits.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/cover-recursive/main.tex?#prop:gated-reduction; PartialCubes:papers/survey/main.tex?#prop:cover-recursive-peripheral-gated-reduction

                                                                Root-Avoiding Decompositions and Convex Root Tests

                                                                Name: Root-Avoiding Decompositions and Convex Root Tests

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Convex-Treelike Partial Cubes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Coordinate Projection
                                                                • Coordinate Conditioning

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                A pointed cover-recursively peripheral partial cube $(A,a)$ has a root-avoiding peripheral decomposition exactly when every nontrivial convex subgraph containing $a$ has a peripheral semicube omitting $a$. This pointed class is closed under coordinate contractions and restrictions to semicubes containing the root. Its pointed-minor-minimal nonmembers are exactly the root-critical pairs: root-locked pairs whose root-side restriction and contraction in every coordinate have root-avoiding decompositions.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Root-preserving minors commute past the first root-avoiding peripheral step; induction preserves the rooted contraction base and uses ordinary pc-minor closure for the duplicated site. Hence every convex subgraph containing the root inherits an avoiding periphery. Conversely, choose such a periphery in the original graph. Its opposite side is the rooted contraction base and inherits the convex test, while the duplicated site is a convex member of the unpointed class; induction reconstructs a root-avoiding decomposition. Pointed minimality is then equivalent to root-locking plus repair of every immediate rooted minor.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/cover-recursive/main.tex?#thm:rooted-wedge; PartialCubes:papers/cover-recursive/main.tex?#cor:rooted-convex; PartialCubes:papers/survey/main.tex?#thm:cover-recursive-peripheral-rooted-wedge-characterization

                                                                Witnesses:

                                                                • Root-Avoiding Three-Vertex Path

                                                                Rooted-Wedge Membership and Forbidden-Minor Classification

                                                                Name: Rooted-Wedge Membership and Forbidden-Minor Classification

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Convex-Treelike Partial Cubes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • One-Point Amalgam
                                                                • Partial-Cube Minor

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $(A,a)$ and $(B,b)$ be pointed cover-recursively peripheral partial cubes. Their one-point amalgam $A\vee B$ belongs to the class exactly when at least one factor has a root-avoiding decomposition. If both factors are nontrivial, the wedge is periphery-free exactly when both roots are locked, and it is a forbidden pc-minor exactly when both pointed factors are root-critical. Consequently the one-vertex-decomposable forbidden pc-minors are precisely the wedges of two nontrivial root-critical pointed members.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                A root-avoiding decomposition peels its factor inside the wedge because every removed side omits the attachment vertex. Conversely, the first peripheral coordinate of a recursive wedge decomposition lies in one factor and its peripheral side must avoid the common root; induction either completes a root-avoiding decomposition of that factor or supplies one in the other. The same section calculation makes wedge peripherality equivalent to an avoiding periphery in a factor. Root-criticality repairs every root-side restriction and contraction, so all elementary wedge minors return to the class; minimality of a forbidden wedge forces the converse conditions on both factors.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/cover-recursive/main.tex?#lem:rooted-amalgam; PartialCubes:papers/cover-recursive/main.tex?#thm:rooted-wedge; PartialCubes:papers/cover-recursive/main.tex?#cor:wedge-classification; PartialCubes:papers/survey/main.tex?#lem:cover-recursive-peripheral-rooted-wedge; PartialCubes:papers/survey/main.tex?#thm:cover-recursive-peripheral-rooted-wedge-characterization

                                                                Witnesses:

                                                                • Rooted-Wedge Obstruction

                                                                Pointed Construction Separating Convex- and Faithful-Treelike Graphs

                                                                Name: Pointed Construction Separating Convex- and Faithful-Treelike Graphs

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Convex-Treelike Partial Cubes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • One-Point Amalgam
                                                                • Partial-Cube Minor

                                                                Result Type: Construction

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For nontrivial root-locked pointed members $(A,0^d)$ and $(B,0^e)$, put $P(A)=(Q_d\times\{0\})\cup(A\times\{1\})$ and similarly for $P(B)$, and wedge their bottom origins to form $G$. Then $G$ is cover-recursively peripheral. The induced subgraph $F$ on the two top layers and the common bottom root is faithful and periphery-free, has convex hull $G$, and contracts along its two root edges to $A\vee B$. This quotient is a forbidden pc-minor exactly when both pointed factors are root-critical.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Each $P(A)$ has a root-avoiding decomposition beginning with its top layer, so the wedge theorem places $G$ in the class. The two top layers are isometric and median-stable: a majority of two vertices in one layer remains there, while a mixed triple with the common root has that root as majority. Root-locking supplies witnesses against peripheral old coordinates in $F$, and neither one-edge layer coordinate is peripheral. Contracting those layer coordinates gives the pointed wedge, whose minimality is the rooted-wedge criterion.

                                                                [Polat12treelike]

                                                                Root-Critical Wedges Are Corner-Peelable

                                                                Name: Root-Critical Wedges Are Corner-Peelable

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes
                                                                • Convex-Treelike Partial Cubes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • One-Point Amalgam

                                                                Result Type: Implication

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Every root-critical pointed cover-recursively peripheral partial cube has a corner peeling ending at its root. Therefore every one-vertex-decomposable forbidden pc-minor for the cover-recursively peripheral class is corner-peelable.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                First induct through a root-avoiding decomposition to build an isometric-prefix order beginning at the root: order the contraction-base layer first and append an isometric-prefix order of the duplicated site. For a root-critical pair, a peripheral coordinate has both its root-side restriction and contraction root-avoidable; interleave their root-first orders across the two layers to obtain an isometric-prefix order of the whole factor. For a wedge, list the common root, then one factor, then the other; distances between factors add through the root. Reversing these orders gives the required peelings.

                                                                Deletion Normal Form for Cover-Recursive Obstructions

                                                                Name: Deletion Normal Form for Cover-Recursive Obstructions

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Convex-Treelike Partial Cubes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Peripheral Expansion
                                                                • Partial-Cube Minor

                                                                Result Type: Construction

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $O$ be a forbidden pc-minor for the cover-recursively peripheral class, let $e$ be a coordinate, orient it by $b$, and put $D=O_e^b\setminus O_e^{1-b}$. Add to the opposite semicube the missing mates $\{(x,1-b):x\in D\}$ to obtain $G$. Then $G$ is a cover-recursively peripheral expansion of $O/e$ along $O_e^b$, coordinate $e$ is peripheral in $G$, and $O$ is recovered by deleting exactly those added vertices, each of which has its $e$-neighbor in $G$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The completed opposite section is $O_e^{1-b}\cup D=O_e^0\cup O_e^1=O/e$, while the unchanged $b$-section is $O_e^b\subseteq O/e$. Hence $G=((O/e)\times\{1-b\})\cup(O_e^b\times\{b\})$. The base and site are proper pc-minors of $O$, so both belong to the cover-recursive class; their permitted peripheral expansion is $G$. Deleting the newly supplied mates returns $O$.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/cover-recursive/sections/cover_recursive_peripheral_basis.tex?#prop:deletion-normal-form

                                                                Exact Two-Layer Periphery Criterion

                                                                Name: Exact Two-Layer Periphery Criterion

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Partial Cubes
                                                                • Periphery-Free Partial Cubes

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $O=\Lambda(A,B)=(A\times\{0\})\cup(B\times\{1\})$ be an irredundant partial cube with layer coordinates $E$. For a family $X$, define $\mathcal D_X(p,b)=X_p^{1-b}\setminus X_p^b$. Then $O$ is periphery-free exactly when $A$ and $B$ are incomparable and $\mathcal D_A(p,b)\cup\mathcal D_B(p,b)$ is nonempty for every $p\in E$ and both $b\in\{0,1\}$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The outer coordinate is peripheral in one orientation exactly when one layer contains the other. For a layer coordinate $p$, an oriented section containment holds in the complete lift exactly when it holds in both layers, which is equivalent to both corresponding defect sets being empty. These exhaust all coordinates and orientations.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/cover-recursive/sections/cover_recursive_peripheral_repair.tex?#lem:two-layer-periphery

                                                                Complete Two-Layer Basis for Cover-Recursive Peripheral Partial Cubes

                                                                Name: Complete Two-Layer Basis for Cover-Recursive Peripheral Partial Cubes

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Convex-Treelike Partial Cubes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Coordinate Projection
                                                                • Coordinate Conditioning
                                                                • Partial-Cube Minor

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                An irredundant ample two-layer partial cube $O=\Lambda(A,B)$ is a forbidden pc-minor for the cover-recursively peripheral class exactly when: $A$, $B$, and $A\cup B$ belong to that class; the layers are incomparable and together witness both orientations of every surviving layer coordinate; and no proper simultaneous descendant of $(A,B)$ obtained by common layer-coordinate restrictions and contractions retains those two nonperipherality conditions. Together with the antipodally punctured cubes $Q_n^{--}$, these lifts form the complete forbidden pc-minor basis. Every coordinate of an ample obstruction may serve as the outer coordinate.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                For an ample obstruction, the two sections and contraction at any chosen coordinate are proper pc-minors and lie in the class, while periphery-freeness gives the two-layer defect conditions. Every proper simultaneous descendant is another proper minor and must expose a periphery. Conversely, operations using the outer coordinate land in a minor of $A$, $B$, or $A\cup B$. A descendant retaining the outer coordinate either has an empty or nested layer, giving an immediate recursive construction, or condition three supplies a peripheral layer coordinate; induction on the surviving coordinates puts both children in the class. Thus every proper minor lies in the class while the original lift does not.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/cover-recursive/sections/cover_recursive_peripheral_repair.tex?#thm:complete-rper-basis

                                                                Static Repair-Antichain Formula

                                                                Name: Static Repair-Antichain Formula

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Partial Cubes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Coordinate Projection
                                                                • Coordinate Conditioning

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For an oriented defect $u\in\mathcal D_O(p,b)$, let $\mathcal H_O(p,b;u)$ be the antichain of inclusion-minimal difference supports between $u$ and possible mates in the base section. Under a layer minor state $\sigma$, the projected defect survives exactly when it matches every fixed coordinate and no repair support in $\mathcal H_O(p,b;u)$ is contained in the contracted coordinates. Hence $\sigma$ preserves nonperipherality of every displayed coordinate in both orientations exactly when each such orientation has a surviving original defect. A proper simultaneous descendant remains periphery-free exactly when a non-all-retained state with this property exists.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                A surviving defect cannot acquire a projected mate: such a mate would differ only in contracted coordinates and contain a minimal repair support there. Conversely, if the projected section has a defect, any preimage survives the fixed coordinates, and a repair support contained in the contractions would project a mate, a contradiction. Apply this equivalence to both orientations of the outer coordinate and every retained layer coordinate. Commutation of distinct-coordinate operations identifies the normalized simultaneous descendants with these states, after redundant constant coordinates are contracted.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/cover-recursive/sections/cover_recursive_peripheral_repair.tex?#lem:static-repair-formula

                                                                Witnesses:

                                                                • Repair Hypergraph of a Six-Cycle Containment

                                                                Static Repair Basis for Ample Cover-Recursive Obstructions

                                                                Name: Static Repair Basis for Ample Cover-Recursive Obstructions

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Convex-Treelike Partial Cubes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Coordinate Projection
                                                                • Coordinate Conditioning
                                                                • Partial-Cube Minor

                                                                Result Type: Algorithm

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Up to partial-cube isomorphism, the ample forbidden pc-minors for the cover-recursively peripheral class are exactly the lifts $O=\Lambda(A,B)$ such that $O$ is ample, $A$, $B$, and $A\cup B$ belong to the class, and the all-retained layer state is the unique state preserving an original defect in both orientations of every displayed coordinate. Every coordinate of an ample obstruction can be chosen as the outer coordinate. Adding the antipodally punctured cubes gives the complete basis.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The all-retained state has surviving defects in every orientation exactly when $O$ is periphery-free. By the static repair formula, uniqueness of this state is equivalent to the absence of a proper simultaneous descendant satisfying the two-layer nonperipherality criterion. The three displayed conditions are therefore precisely the conditions of the complete two-layer basis theorem.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/cover-recursive/sections/cover_recursive_peripheral_repair.tex?#thm:static-repair-basis

                                                                Prescribed-Prefix Attachment Bound

                                                                Name: Prescribed-Prefix Attachment Bound

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Ordering Width
                                                                • Prescribed-Subset Ordering Width

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For $\emptyset\ne I\subseteq C$, put $\rho(C,I)=\max(\{q(c,I):c\in C\setminus I\}\cup\{0\})$. Then $\max\{\sigma(C),\sigma(I)\}\leq\sigma(C;I)\leq\max\{\sigma(C),\sigma(I),\rho(C,I)\}$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The lower bounds follow by forgetting the prefix constraint and by restricting an admissible order to its initial segment. For the upper bound, take an optimal order of $C$, move $I$ to the front in an optimal internal order, and retain the relative order outside $I$. A minimal disagreement against the enlarged predecessor family $P\cup I$ is minimal against $P$ or against $I$, so its excess is bounded by the corresponding old step or by $q(c,I)$.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/structural-invariants/sections/prescribed_extensions.tex?#lem:prefix

                                                                Reverse Zero-Width Orders Fill the Complement at Zero Cost

                                                                Name: Reverse Zero-Width Orders Fill the Complement at Zero Cost

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Ordering Width
                                                                • Prescribed-Subset Ordering Width

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Cube Complement

                                                                Result Type: Algorithm

                                                                Statement:

                                                                If $(f_1,\ldots,f_m)$ is a zero-width order of a nonempty $F\subseteq\{0,1\}^Y$, then, starting from $F^{\mathrm c}$ and adding $f_m,\ldots,f_1$, every addition has step cost zero with the whole initial complement counted as predecessors.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                After adding $f_j$, the current class is the complement of the remaining prefix $\{f_1,\ldots,f_{j-1}\}$. Zero-width prefixes are ample, and cube complementation preserves ampleness, so the current class is ample. Its isometry supplies, toward every predecessor, an already present neighbor of $f_j$ whose singleton disagreement lies in the predecessor disagreement; this is exactly the zero-cost condition.

                                                                References:

                                                                [ChalopiChepoiMoran22] [Lawrence1983]

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/structural-invariants/sections/prescribed_extensions.tex?#lem:complement-fill

                                                                Cube-Completion Width Laws

                                                                Name: Cube-Completion Width Laws

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Ordering Width
                                                                • Prescribed-Subset Ordering Width
                                                                • Cube-Completion Width

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Coordinate Projection
                                                                • Coordinate Conditioning
                                                                • Partial-Cube Minor
                                                                • Cartesian Product
                                                                • Cube Complement

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For every nonempty $C\subseteq\{0,1\}^X$, $\sigma_{\square}(C)\geq\sigma(C)$, and $\sigma_{\square}(C)=0$ exactly when both $C$ and its cube complement are dismantlable ample (the empty complement is allowed). Nonempty pc-minors cannot increase $\sigma_{\square}$; on disjoint coordinate sets, $\sigma_{\square}(C\times D)=\max\{\sigma_{\square}(C),\sigma_{\square}(D)\}$. Cube symmetries and constant coordinates preserve the value. If $C^{\mathrm c}$ is dismantlable ample, then $\sigma_{\square}(C)=\sigma(C)$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The prescribed initial segment gives the first inequality. A zero-width full-cube order makes $C$ dismantlable; reading the suffix backwards gives a zero-width order of the complement because complements of ample prefixes are ample. Conversely, append the reverse of a zero-width complement order to an optimal order of $C$. The pc-minor and product laws follow by applying the paired prescribed-width laws to $(\{0,1\}^X,C)$, while a constant coordinate is a product with a singleton.

                                                                References:

                                                                [ChalopiChepoiMoran22] [Lawrence1983]

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/structural-invariants/sections/prescribed_extensions.tex?#prop:cube-width

                                                                Cubical Bound for Prescribed Extensions

                                                                Name: Cubical Bound for Prescribed Extensions

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Ordering Width
                                                                • Prescribed-Subset Ordering Width
                                                                • Cube-Completion Width
                                                                • Coordinate-Cube Dimension

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $\emptyset\ne F\subsetneq\{0,1\}^X$ and $F\subseteq G\subseteq\{0,1\}^X$. After any initial order of $F$, every ordering of $G\setminus F$ has added-step cost at most $d_{\square}(F^{\mathrm c})$. Consequently $\sigma(G;F)\leq\max\{\sigma(F),d_{\square}(F^{\mathrm c})\}$ and $\sigma_{\square}(F)\leq\max\{\sigma(F),d_{\square}(F^{\mathrm c})\}$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                At a newly added word $a$, let $S$ be an inclusion-minimal predecessor disagreement. No word obtained from $a$ by flipping a proper subset of $S$ can be a predecessor. After choosing $j\in S$, the coordinate cube based at $a$ and free on $S\setminus\{j\}$ therefore lies in $F^{\mathrm c}$. Hence $|S|-1\leq d_{\square}(F^{\mathrm c})$ for every added step; optimizing the initial order gives both inequalities.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/structural-invariants/sections/prescribed_extensions.tex?#thm:cubical-extension

                                                                Comments:

                                                                The bound for a general target is sharp: if $F=\{0^n\}$ and $G=\{0^n,1^n\}$ with $n\geq2$, both sides equal $n-1$. This does not make the full-cube completion bound sharp for that $F$, since a cube has a zero-width order starting at $0^n$.

                                                                Filtration-Width Splicing and Functoriality

                                                                Name: Filtration-Width Splicing and Functoriality

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Ordering Width
                                                                • Prescribed-Subset Ordering Width
                                                                • Filtration Width

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Coordinate Projection
                                                                • Coordinate Conditioning
                                                                • Partial-Cube Minor
                                                                • Cartesian Product

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For every nonempty filtration $C_0\subseteq\cdots\subseteq C_m$, $w(C_0,\ldots,C_m)=\max(\{\sigma(C_0)\}\cup\{\sigma(C_j;C_{j-1}):1\leq j\leq m\})$. Deleting prescribed stages cannot increase the width. Applying one pc-minor to every stage cannot increase it when the first resulting stage is nonempty. For equal-length filtrations on disjoint coordinates, synchronized products satisfy $w(C_0\times D_0,\ldots,C_m\times D_m)=\max\{w(C_0,\ldots,C_m),w(D_0,\ldots,D_m)\}$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Every admissible order restricts at stage $j$ to a $C_{j-1}$-first order of $C_j$, giving all lower bounds. Conversely, start with an optimal order of $C_0$ and at each stage append the new concepts in their order from an optimal $C_{j-1}$-first order of $C_j$; all of $C_{j-1}$ is already present, so the previous internal order is irrelevant to new step costs. Stage deletion relaxes constraints, and the minor and synchronized-product formulas follow termwise from the paired-width laws.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/structural-invariants/sections/prescribed_extensions.tex?#prop:filtration-width

                                                                Exact Width of Rectangular Filtrations

                                                                Name: Exact Width of Rectangular Filtrations

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Ordering Width
                                                                • Prescribed-Subset Ordering Width
                                                                • Filtration Width

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Coordinate Conditioning
                                                                • Cartesian Product

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $A_0\supseteq\cdots\supseteq A_m$ and $F_0\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq F_m$ be nonempty classes on disjoint coordinate sets, and put $D_j=\bigcup_{i=0}^j(A_i\times F_i)$. Then $w(D_0,\ldots,D_m)=\max(\{\sigma(A_j):0\leq j\leq m\}\cup\{w(F_0,\ldots,F_m)\})$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                For the upper bound, fill each new inner fiber completely while visiting outer concepts in an optimal order of $A_j$. An old-stage predecessor is replaced inside the current fiber, while a predecessor in an earlier new fiber is replaced at the same inner word using the outer order; the step cost is at most $\max\{\sigma(A_j),\sigma(F_j;F_{j-1})\}$. For the reverse bounds, conditioning $D_j$ at a new inner word recovers $A_j$, and conditioning the pair $(D_j,D_{j-1})$ at any $x\in A_j$ recovers $(F_j,F_{j-1})$.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/structural-invariants/sections/prescribed_extensions.tex?#thm:rectangular-filtration

                                                                Comments:

                                                                For one extension, with $\emptyset\ne B\subseteq A$ and $\emptyset\ne F\subsetneq G$, this specializes to $\sigma((A\times F)\cup(B\times G);A\times F)=\max\{\sigma(A),\sigma(B),\sigma(G;F)\}$. If $F=G$, the output is $A\times F$ and the $\sigma(B)$ term is omitted; an empty $B$ likewise reduces to a product.

                                                                Constrained Width of Level-Sum Maximum Sequences

                                                                Name: Constrained Width of Level-Sum Maximum Sequences

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Maximum Classes

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Ordering Width
                                                                • Filtration Width

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Cartesian Product

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $A_0\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq A_n=\{0,1\}^X$ and $B_0\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq B_m=\{0,1\}^Y$ be maximum sequences whose indices are their ranks. For $L_R=\{(x,y):\rho(x)+\lambda(y)\leq R\}$, put $j_0=\max\{0,R-n\}$ and $j_1=\min\{m,R\}$. Then $L_R=\bigcup_{j=j_0}^{j_1}A_{R-j}\times B_j$ is maximum, and the minimum width of an order that introduces these rectangles successively is $\max(\{\sigma(A_{R-j}):j_0\leq j\leq j_1\}\cup\{w(B_{j_0},\ldots,B_{j_1})\})$. In particular this quantity bounds $\sigma(L_R)$ from above; swapping the factors gives a second bound.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The level-sum maximum theorem gives the displayed class and its rectangular decomposition. The outer classes $A_{R-j}$ decrease as the inner classes $B_j$ increase, so the exact rectangular-filtration formula applies directly. Dropping the rectangle-prefix constraints can only decrease ordering width, yielding the absolute-width bound; symmetry gives the factor-swapped version.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/structural-invariants/sections/prescribed_extensions.tex?#eq:level-sum-width

                                                                Comments:

                                                                Dismantlability of the individual levels removes their absolute-width terms but does not by itself provide a zero-width order compatible with every inclusion in either maximum sequence.

                                                                Geometric Characterizations of Substitution Crossing Width

                                                                Name: Geometric Characterizations of Substitution Crossing Width

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Minimum Teaching Size
                                                                • Substitution Crossing Width

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For a proper nonempty test $T\subsetneq\{0,1\}^Y$, $g(T)$ is both the largest dimension of a coordinate face meeting one of $T,T^{\mathrm c}$ in exactly one concept and the largest size of an inclusion-minimal disagreement from a concept on one side to the other. Hence $1\leq g(T)\leq|Y|$. For every opposite-side pair $y,z$, there is a word $u$ on the side of $z$ with $\operatorname{diff}(y,u)\subseteq\operatorname{diff}(y,z)$ and $d_H(y,u)\leq g(T)$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                A teaching set of size $s$ isolates its concept on a face of dimension $|Y|-s$, and every isolating face gives such a teaching set. A minimal crossing disagreement spans a face with a unique concept on one side; conversely, the antipode of the unique concept in a positive-dimensional isolating face lies on the other side and gives a minimal crossing. A crossing edge supplies the lower bound. Finally, minimize a crossing disagreement inside the support of any specified opposite-side pair.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/structural-invariants/sections/boolean_substitution.tex?#lem:substitution-crossing

                                                                Sensitivity and Affine Laws for Substitution Crossing Width
