                                                                Name: Sensitivity and Affine Laws for Substitution Crossing Width

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Ordering Width
                                                                • Substitution Crossing Width
                                                                • Boolean Sensitivity

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Boolean Substitution
                                                                • Coordinate Projection

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Every proper nonempty test satisfies $g(T)\leq s(1_T)$. Equality holds when both $T$ and $T^{\mathrm c}$ are well graded, hence in particular when $T$ is ample. Moreover $g(T)=1$ exactly when $1_T$ is a nonconstant affine Boolean function. For such an affine test and an outer class with both exclusive sections nonempty, $\sigma(C\circ_iT)=\max\{\sigma(C),\sigma(T),\sigma(T^{\mathrm c})\}$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Every free direction of an isolating face is sensitive at its unique concept, proving $g\leq s$. In a well-graded side, the neighbor directions at a concept form a minimum teaching set because a geodesic toward any other concept begins in one of them; taking both sides gives equality. The condition $g=1$ says every square meets the test in zero, two, or four vertices, so parallel edges have equal indicator increments and the indicator is affine over $\mathbb F_2$; the converse is immediate from an active coordinate in every crossing support. The exact ordering-width law then combines the general upper bound with minor-recovery lower bounds.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/structural-invariants/sections/boolean_substitution.tex?#eq:substitution-sensitivity

                                                                Comments:

                                                                The parameter $g$ is not pc-minor monotone: deleting zero from the even-parity class in dimension $n\geq3$ gives $g=2$, while projecting one coordinate gives the punctured cube $\{0,1\}^{n-1}\setminus\{0\}$ with $g=n-1$.

                                                                Ordering Width under Boolean Substitution

                                                                Name: Ordering Width under Boolean Substitution

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Ordering Width
                                                                • Substitution Crossing Width

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Boolean Substitution

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For every nonempty outer class $C$ and proper nonempty test $T$, $\sigma(C\circ_iT)\leq\max\{\sigma(T),\sigma(T^{\mathrm c}),\sigma(C)+g(T)-1\}$. If both exclusive outer sections are nonempty, then $\sigma(C\circ_iT)\geq\max\{\sigma(C),\sigma(T),\sigma(T^{\mathrm c})\}$. No ampleness hypothesis is required.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Order optimal test-side blocks along an optimal outer order. A predecessor in the current block has an inner witness of size at most $\sigma(T)+1$ or $\sigma(T^{\mathrm c})+1$. For a completed block, an outer witness that stays on the same side keeps the inner word; one that crosses the distinguished coordinate uses a contained crossing disagreement of size at most $g(T)$. Because the outer support then spends one coordinate on the split, the combined size is at most $\sigma(C)+g(T)$. Conditioning a crossing test edge and exclusive outside words recovers the three inputs, proving the lower bound.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/structural-invariants/sections/boolean_substitution.tex?#thm:substitution-width

                                                                Comments:

                                                                For an empty or full test, every nonempty output is one outer section times the inner cube and has that section's width.

                                                                Exact Common-Section-First Substitution Width

                                                                Name: Exact Common-Section-First Substitution Width

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Ordering Width
                                                                • Prescribed-Subset Ordering Width

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Boolean Substitution

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $H=C_0\cap C_1$ be nonempty and meet every coordinate interval $[x,z]$ with $x\in C_0$ and $z\in C_1$. For $F_0=T$, $F_1=T^{\mathrm c}$, $D=C\circ_iT$, and $I=H\times\{0,1\}^Y$, one has $\sigma(D;I)=\max(\{\sigma(C_0;H),\sigma(C_1;H)\}\cup\{\sigma(F_b):C_b\setminus H\ne\emptyset\})$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Order the whole common fiber first, then the exclusive fibers on each side using optimal $H$-first outer orders and optimal inner orders. Same-fiber predecessors use inner witnesses and same-side predecessors use outer witnesses in completed fibers. For an opposite-side predecessor, the interval hypothesis supplies a point of $H$ between the two outside words, and the outer order gives a contained witness toward it without any inner-coordinate cost. Conditioning an inner word recovers each pair $(C_b,H)$, while conditioning an exclusive outside word recovers the relevant test side, giving all reverse bounds.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/structural-invariants/sections/boolean_substitution.tex?#thm:prescribed-substitution

                                                                Fixed Partial-Cube Substitution Has Uniform Width Bound

                                                                Name: Fixed Partial-Cube Substitution Has Uniform Width Bound

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Partial Cubes

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Ordering Width

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Boolean Substitution

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                If an isometric outer class $C$ is displayed on $N\geq1$ coordinates and meets both halfspaces of the substituted coordinate, then $\sigma(C\circ_iT)\leq\max\{\max\{N-2,0\},\sigma(T),\sigma(T^{\mathrm c})\}$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Isometry makes the common section meet every interval between opposite outer sides. Each section lies on $N-1$ coordinates, so every section order, including one beginning with the common part, has width at most $\max\{N-2,0\}$. Apply the exact common-section-first formula and then forget the prefix constraint.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/structural-invariants/sections/boolean_substitution.tex?#cor:fixed-outer-substitution

                                                                Comments:

                                                                Thus enlarging a test whose two sides are dismantlable cannot create unbounded width in one substitution into a fixed partial cube. This does not bound iterated constructions whose outer dimension grows.

                                                                Exact Substitution Width for the Six-Cycle

                                                                Name: Exact Substitution Width for the Six-Cycle

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Even Cycles
                                                                • Partial Cubes

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Ordering Width

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Boolean Substitution

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For $C=\{000,001,011,111,110,100\}$ with its middle coordinate substituted and every proper nonempty test $T$, $\sigma(C\circ_iT)=\max\{1,\sigma(T),\sigma(T^{\mathrm c})\}$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The two outer sections are $\{00,01,10\}$ and $\{01,10,11\}$ with common part $\{01,10\}$; both prescribed section widths are one. The displayed cycle has width one: its cyclic order has width at most one, while shattering all supports of size at most two makes it non-ample and hence excludes width zero. The common-section formula gives the upper bound and recovery of both test sides gives equality.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/structural-invariants/sections/boolean_substitution.tex?#ex:six-cycle-substitution

                                                                Witnesses:

                                                                • Six-Cycle

                                                                Comments:

                                                                This is a positive-width isometric example; it is not an ample outer example.

                                                                Exact Width for Nested-Section Substitution

                                                                Name: Exact Width for Nested-Section Substitution

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Ordering Width
                                                                • Prescribed-Subset Ordering Width
                                                                • Cube-Completion Width

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Boolean Substitution
                                                                • Cartesian Product

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $\emptyset\ne B\subseteq A$, let $F$ be proper and nonempty, and assume $F^{\mathrm c}$ is dismantlable ample. Then $\sigma((A\times F)\cup(B\times\{0,1\}^Y);A\times F)=\max\{\sigma(A),\sigma(B),\sigma(F)\}$. If $B\subsetneq A$, the same formula holds for absolute width; if $A=B$, the output is $A\times\{0,1\}^Y$ and has width $\sigma(A)$. Consequently, substituting a test with two dismantlable sides preserves the absolute width of every outer class with nested sections.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Reverse complement filling gives $\sigma_{\square}(F)=\sigma(F)$, and the exact one-stage rectangular-extension formula gives the prescribed equality. When $B\subsetneq A$, conditioning an exclusive outer word recovers $F$, while conditioning inner words on the two test sides recovers $A$ and $B$, so the same maximum is a lower bound for absolute width. The width of the original nested two-section outer class is already $\max\{\sigma(A),\sigma(B)\}$, proving preservation when both test sides have width zero.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/structural-invariants/sections/boolean_substitution.tex?#eq:nested-substitution

                                                                Comments:

                                                                Empty smaller sections reduce to products, and reflecting the substituted bit handles the opposite nesting direction. No isometry assumption is used.

                                                                One-Side-First Substitution Bound

                                                                Name: One-Side-First Substitution Bound

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Ordering Width
                                                                • Prescribed-Subset Ordering Width
                                                                • Cube-Completion Width

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Boolean Substitution

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Under the common-section interval hypothesis, for each $b\in\{0,1\}$, $\sigma(C\circ_iT)\leq\max\{\sigma(C_b),\sigma(C_{1-b};H),\sigma_{\square}(F_b),\sigma(F_{1-b})\}$. If both test sides are dismantlable ample, this becomes $\sigma(C\circ_iT)\leq\min_b\max\{\sigma(C_b),\sigma(C_{1-b};H)\}$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                First use rectangular extension to order $(C_b\times F_b)\cup(H\times\{0,1\}^Y)$ beginning with $C_b\times F_b$. Then append the exclusive fibers of the other side in an optimal $H$-first order. Same-fiber and same-side predecessors use inner and outer witnesses. An opposite-side predecessor is replaced through a point of $H$ in its coordinate interval, giving a contained pure outer disagreement. If both test sides have width zero, their cube-completion widths equal zero, and minimizing over the first side gives the second formula.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/structural-invariants/sections/boolean_substitution.tex?#prop:one-side-substitution

                                                                Zero Width Need Not Give a Low-Width Common-Section Prefix

                                                                Name: Zero Width Need Not Give a Low-Width Common-Section Prefix

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Ordering Width
                                                                • Prescribed-Subset Ordering Width

                                                                Result Type: Construction

                                                                Statement:

                                                                There is a 579-concept dismantlable ample class $C$ on 25 coordinates with nonnested sections and intersection $H$ a coordinate edge such that $\sigma(C)=0<\min\{\sigma(C_0;H),\sigma(C_1;H)\}$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Build the two sections from disjoint copies of the rooted 289-vertex ample factor $R$: one section is $A=\{(r,0):r\in R\}$ and the other is $B=\{(0,0)\}\cup\{(e,r):r\in R\}$, meeting in $H=\{(0,0),(e,0)\}$. A block order using a zero-width order of the upper copy, then a zero-width order of the lower copy starting at $e$, then the final common vertex has width zero. The retained-edge obstruction in $R$ makes $\sigma(A;H)>0$. Conditioning the active coordinate of $e$ maps $(B,H)$ to $(R,\{0\})$, whose prescribed width is positive, and paired-minor monotonicity gives the other inequality.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/structural-invariants/sections/boolean_substitution.tex?#prop:two-section-prefix-failure

                                                                Witnesses:

                                                                • Two-Section Prefix-Failure Class
                                                                • Rooted 289-Vertex Peeling Factor

                                                                Comments:

                                                                The construction makes no minimum-cardinality claim. It limits common-section-first upper bounds but does not refute zero-width preservation under two-sided dismantlable tests.

                                                                Majority Completion of a Nested Extension

                                                                Name: Majority Completion of a Nested Extension

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Majority Completion Defect

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Majority Closure
                                                                • Peripheral Expansion

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For $\emptyset\ne S\subseteq B\subseteq\{0,1\}^n$, let $F(S)$ be the smallest ambient coordinate face containing $S$, put $E(B,S)=(B\times\{0\})\cup(S\times\{1\})$, and write $H=\operatorname{med}(B)$. Then $\operatorname{med}(E(B,S))=(H\times\{0\})\cup((H\cap F(S))\times\{1\})$, and $\delta_{\mathrm{med}}(E(B,S))=\delta_{\mathrm{med}}(B)+\delta_{\mathrm{med}}(S)+|\operatorname{med}(B)\cap F(S)|-|\operatorname{med}(S)|$. The last term is nonnegative.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The pairwise patterns on old coordinates are exactly those of $B$, forcing the old word into $H$. At new-coordinate value zero, mixed pairs impose only the unary projections of $B$; at value one, they impose the unary projections of $S$, which cut out $F(S)$. Majority terms from $S$ lie in $H$ and preserve every coordinate constant on $S$, so $\operatorname{med}(S)\subseteq H\cap F(S)$. Counting the two layers and subtracting $|B|+|S|$ gives the defect formula.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/structural-invariants/main.tex?#prop:median-extension

                                                                Comments:

                                                                If $B$ and $S$ are isometric median classes, the extension is median exactly when $S=B\cap F(S)$. The formula also applies to nonmedian and disconnected inputs.

                                                                Exact Width of a Nested One-Coordinate Extension

                                                                Name: Exact Width of a Nested One-Coordinate Extension

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Ordering Width

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Peripheral Expansion

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For $\emptyset\ne B\subseteq A\subseteq\{0,1\}^E$ and $Y=(A\times\{0\})\cup(B\times\{1\})$, one has $\sigma(Y)=\max\{\sigma(A),\sigma(B)\}$. If $B=\emptyset$, the constant-coordinate copy of $A$ has width $\sigma(A)$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Both fibers are coordinate conditionings of $Y$, giving the lower bound. Order the lower $A$ layer optimally and then the upper $B$ layer optimally. At an upper word $(b,1)$ its gate $(b,0)$ is already present, so every disagreement with the lower layer contains the singleton new-coordinate disagreement; the other minimal disagreements are precisely those from the chosen order of $B$.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/structural-invariants/main.tex?#cor:peripheral

                                                                Bounded Common-Section Composition

                                                                Name: Bounded Common-Section Composition

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Ordering Width
                                                                • Prescribed-Subset Ordering Width

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Common-Section Gluing
                                                                • Coordinate Conditioning

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For common-section pieces $A_1,\ldots,A_m$ over $D$, let $X_I=\bigcup_{i\in I}A_i$, $X_\emptyset=D$, $N=|D|$, and $r_i=\sigma(A_i;D)$. Then $\sigma(X;D)=\max_i r_i$, $\sigma(X)=\min_{|I|\leq N}\max(\{\sigma(X_I)\}\cup\{r_i:i\notin I\})$, and $\sigma(X)=\max_{|J|\leq N+1}\sigma(X_J)$. For $m$ disjoint private copies of one piece $A$, $\sigma(X^{(m)})=\sigma(A;D)$ whenever $m\geq|D|+1$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Putting $D$ first and appending optimal local outside orders proves the relative formula, because every cross-piece disagreement contains the gate disagreement. For an arbitrary global order, mark for each $d\in D$ the piece containing the first word projected to $d$; at most $|D|$ pieces are marked. In every unmarked piece, moving all of $D$ first preserves the width: a newly minimal gate support is bounded using the earlier marked word over the same projection. This proves the minimization formula. A threshold argument then shows that some subunion of at most $|D|+1$ pieces realizes the full width. Identical copies give the final identity.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/structural-invariants/main.tex?#thm:bounded-gluing

                                                                Comments:

                                                                Every threshold failure is witnessed by at most $|D|+1$ pieces of the displayed decomposition; this does not bound the cardinality of an intrinsic forbidden pc-minor. The gluing preserves ampleness and the partial-cube property when all pieces have it.

                                                                Exact Root-Gluing Width

                                                                Name: Exact Root-Gluing Width

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Ordering Width
                                                                • Prescribed-Subset Ordering Width

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Common-Section Gluing
                                                                • One-Point Amalgam

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let rooted classes $A_i\subseteq\{0,1\}^{F_i}$ contain zero on pairwise disjoint coordinate blocks and set $X=\bigcup_iA_i$. Then $\sigma(X;\{0\})=\max_i\sigma(A_i;\{0\})$ and $\sigma(X)=\min_k\max(\{\sigma(A_k)\}\cup\{\sigma(A_i;\{0\}):i\ne k\})$. In particular, two or more copies of one rooted class $A$ have width exactly $\sigma(A;\{0\})$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Apply bounded common-section composition with the singleton section $D=\{0\}$. The selected subset is empty or a singleton. The empty choice cannot improve on a singleton choice because $\sigma(A_k)\leq\sigma(A_k;\{0\})$, yielding both exact formulas.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/structural-invariants/main.tex?#thm:root-gluing

                                                                Comments:

                                                                Root doubling realizes every prescribed-root width as an absolute width with at most twice as many concepts. Since root gluings preserve ample classes and partial cubes, absolute and prescribed-root widths have the same attainable ranges within each of those two families.

                                                                Two Scalar Widths Do Not Determine Edge Gluing

                                                                Name: Two Scalar Widths Do Not Determine Edge Gluing

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes
                                                                • Ample Classes

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Ordering Width
                                                                • Prescribed-Subset Ordering Width

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Common-Section Gluing

                                                                Result Type: Construction

                                                                Statement:

                                                                There are dismantlable ample pieces $A,B_u,B_v$ over one common edge $D$ such that $\sigma(B_u)=\sigma(B_v)=0$ and $\sigma(B_u;D)=\sigma(B_v;D)=s>0$, while $\sigma(A\cup B_u)=s$ and $\sigma(A\cup B_v)=0$. Moreover $\sigma(A;D)>0$, and reflecting the shared coordinate exchanges $B_u$ and $B_v$ while preserving $D$ setwise.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Take $A=R$, the rooted 289-vertex ample factor with only corner $u=0$ and a peeling ending at its neighbor $v=2$, and let $D=\{u,v\}$. Attach a private copy of $R$ at either endpoint to form $B_r=(D\times\{0\})\cup(\{r\}\times R)$. Both $B_r$ peel and have width zero, while paired conditioning and an explicit $D$-first order give the common positive value $\sigma(B_r;D)=s=\sigma(R;\{u\})$. Exact root gluing gives width $s$ when the second copy is attached at $u$ and width zero when it is attached at $v$.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/structural-invariants/main.tex?#prop:section-width-limit

                                                                Witnesses:

                                                                • Endpoint-Sensitive Edge Attachments
                                                                • Rooted 289-Vertex Peeling Factor

                                                                Comments:

                                                                The failure comes from the pieces' placement relative to the labelled common edge. Any quantitative composition rule for larger sections needs more information than absolute and prescribed-section widths, even after adjoining invariants unchanged by a reflection of the piece.

                                                                Hall's Complement Obstructs Zero-Width Complete Filtrations

                                                                Name: Hall's Complement Obstructs Zero-Width Complete Filtrations

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Maximum Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Ordering Width
                                                                • Cube-Completion Width
                                                                • Filtration Width

                                                                Result Type: Implication

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $H=C_H$ be Hall's 299-concept maximum class in $\{0,1\}^{12}$ and $K=H^{\mathrm c}$. Then $K$ is a dismantlable maximum class of rank eight and $1\leq\sigma_{\square}(K)\leq3$. Every nested filtration starting at $K$ and ending at the full cube has width between one and three, independently of its intermediate stages. Hence no complete maximum sequence containing $K$ admits a zero-width order compatible with all levels.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The published nonextendable shelling makes $K$ dismantlable, while its complement $H$ has no corner and is not dismantlable. The cube-completion zero criterion gives the lower bound. Since $H$ is ample of VC dimension three, its largest coordinate cube has dimension three, and the cubical extension theorem gives the upper bound. Adding intermediate prescribed stages cannot lower the requirement to complete $K$, while every continuation after an optimal order of $K$ has added-step cost at most three.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/structural-invariants/main.tex?#ex:hall-completion

                                                                Witnesses:

                                                                • Complement of Hall's Maximum Class

                                                                Comments:

                                                                Both $H$ and $K$ are already maximum, so positive completion width does not exclude membership in MaxMin. Reverse filling gives $\sigma_{\square}(H)=\sigma(H)$; this differs from the ordinary Hall-width interval $1$ through $7$.

                                                                Shattered Complexes Are Unrestricted on Daisy Cubes

                                                                Name: Shattered Complexes Are Unrestricted on Daisy Cubes

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Daisy Cubes
                                                                • Ample Classes

                                                                Result Type: Construction

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Every finite simplicial complex $\Gamma\subseteq2^{[n]}$ containing the empty set is the shattered-set complex of a daisy cube. Consequently, no invariant that factors only through $\operatorname{Sh}(C)$ can characterize, among ample classes, a proper subclass containing every daisy cube.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Regard $D=\Gamma$ itself as a down-closed concept class. Every $S\in\Gamma$ is shattered because all its subsets lie in $D$, while a shattered $S$ is contained in some $T\in D$ and hence lies in $\Gamma$ by downward closure. Thus $\operatorname{Sh}(D)=\Gamma$ and $|D|=|\operatorname{Sh}(D)|$, so $D$ is ample and daisy. For any ample class outside a proposed proper subclass, the daisy $\operatorname{Sh}(C)$ lies inside the subclass and has identical shattered-set data.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/structural-invariants/main.tex?#prop:shattering

                                                                Comments:

                                                                In particular, the canonical Artinian reduction determined by the shattered complex cannot detect dismantlability. This does not limit the full labelled Yang ring or its fully signed resolution.

                                                                Coordinate-Graded Yang Homology Depends Only on Shattering

                                                                Name: Coordinate-Graded Yang Homology Depends Only on Shattering

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Daisy Cubes
                                                                • Maximum-Generated Classes

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Coordinate-Graded Yang Tor Algebra

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For every nonempty ample $C\subseteq\{0,1\}^n$ and field $k$, $\operatorname{Tor}^{S}_*(k[\Delta_C],k)\cong\operatorname{Tor}^{T}_*(A_{\operatorname{Sh}(C)},k)$ as homological, coordinate-graded algebras, where $A_\Gamma=T/(z_i^2,z_U:U\notin\Gamma)$. Hence all coordinate-graded Betti numbers and Tor multiplication, even for every coordinate projection, cannot distinguish a hypothetical ample class outside MaxMin from all classes inside MaxMin.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The literal differences $x_{i,1}-x_{i,0}$ form a regular sequence on the ample Yang ring and quotient it to $A_{\operatorname{Sh}(C)}$. A change of Koszul generators splits the complex on all literal variables into the Koszul complex on these regular differences and the complex on one literal per coordinate. Augmenting the regular factor is a multiplicative, coordinate-graded quasi-isomorphism and leaves the Koszul complex computing the displayed Tor algebra. The daisy class $D=\operatorname{Sh}(C)$ is realizable ample and therefore in MaxMin; it and all corresponding projections have the same shattered supports as $C$.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/structural-invariants/main.tex?#prop:betti-blindness

                                                                Coordinate-Graded Betti Formula for Ample Alexander Duals

                                                                Name: Coordinate-Graded Betti Formula for Ample Alexander Duals

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Coordinate-Graded Alexander-Dual Betti Table

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                If $C$ is ample and $U\subseteq[n]$, then $\beta^S_{p,\mathbf1+\mathbf1_U}(J_C)=|\{V\in\operatorname{Sh}(C):U\subseteq V\}|$ for $p=|U|$ and is zero otherwise; all other coordinate-graded Betti numbers vanish. Consequently $\beta_p(J_C)=\sum_{V\in\operatorname{Sh}(C)}\binom{|V|}{p}$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The linear cellular resolution of the Alexander-dual ideal of an ample class has one step-$p$ basis element for each contained $p$-cube. A cube with direction set $U$ has coordinate degree $\mathbf1+\mathbf1_U$. Iterated two-section counting shows that the number of contained cubes in directions $U$ equals the number of shattered supports containing $U$: ampleness and the Sandwich theorem identify the shattered complex of each section intersection. Summing the multigraded formula over $U$ yields the total Betti number.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/structural-invariants/main.tex?#cor:dual-betti-blindness

                                                                Comments:

                                                                Thus the ordinary Betti table, projective dimension, and regularity also depend only on the shattered complex. The conclusion does not cover the fully signed literal grading or maps among conditioned classes.

                                                                Signed Missing-Pattern Polarization Characterizes Ampleness

                                                                Name: Signed Missing-Pattern Polarization Characterizes Ampleness

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Maximum-Generated Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Coordinate Projection
                                                                • Coordinate Conditioning

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For a nonempty binary class $C$ over any field, ampleness is equivalent to the paired differences $x_{i,1}-x_{i,0}$ forming a regular sequence on the signed minimally-missing-pattern ring $S/Q_C$ in some coordinate order, and equivalently in every order. In that case $Q_C$ is a two-fold polarization of the Stanley--Reisner ideal of $\operatorname{Sh}(C)$. The condition is preserved by projection and nonempty conditioning and cannot separate ample classes from maximum sections.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                For an ample class, after any earlier pair identifications a monomial annihilated by the next paired difference would encode a shattered set in a nonempty conditioning but forbid both values of the next coordinate. A contained cube for that shattered set fixes one of those values and contradicts the annihilation, proving regularity in every order. Conversely, identifying all pairs sends $Q_C$ to the Stanley--Reisner ideal of $\operatorname{Sh}(C)$. The multigraded Hilbert-series identity for a regular sequence equates the coefficient of $t_1\cdots t_n$ on the two sides; those coefficients are $|C|$ and $|\operatorname{Sh}(C)|$. Equality is ampleness by the Sandwich theorem.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/structural-invariants/main.tex?#thm:missing-polarization

                                                                Comments:

                                                                The homogeneous differences differ from the affine forms $x_{i,0}+x_{i,1}-1$, which are regular for every neural ideal. The theorem does not claim that $S/Q_C$ is Cohen--Macaulay. The same Koszul reduction makes the coordinate-graded Tor algebra of $S/Q_C$ depend only on the shattered complex.

                                                                Normal Form for pc-Minors

                                                                Name: Normal Form for pc-Minors

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Coordinate Projection
                                                                • Coordinate Conditioning
                                                                • Partial-Cube Minor

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Every nonempty pc-minor of $C\subseteq\{0,1\}^E$ is $C[T;S=s]=\{x|_T:x\in C,\ x|_S=s\}$ for disjoint coordinate sets $S,T$. Coordinates outside $S\cup T$ are projected away, and projection and conditioning on distinct coordinates commute.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                In any minor sequence, a removed coordinate cannot reappear. Partition the original coordinates into those retained, fixed, and projected away. Consistency of the fixed labels follows from nonemptiness, and the displayed membership test proves both the normal form and commutation. Conversely, fixing $S$ and projecting to $T$ constructs every displayed minor.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/minor-atlas/main.tex?#prop:normal-form

                                                                Projection-Conditioning Closure Calculus

                                                                Name: Projection-Conditioning Closure Calculus

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Coordinate Projection
                                                                • Coordinate Conditioning
                                                                • Partial-Cube Minor

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For every family $\mathcal F$ in an operation-stable ambient universe, $\operatorname{Cl}_{pc}(\mathcal F)=\operatorname{Cl}_c(\operatorname{Cl}_p(\mathcal F))=\operatorname{Cl}_p(\operatorname{Cl}_c(\mathcal F))$. If $\mathcal F$ is p-closed, then $\operatorname{Cl}_{pc}(\mathcal F)=\operatorname{Cl}_c(\mathcal F)$. If it is pc-closed, then $\operatorname{Obs}_{pc}(\mathcal F)=\operatorname{Obs}_p(\mathcal F)\cap\operatorname{Obs}_c(\mathcal F)$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The pc-minor normal form permits all projected coordinates to be removed before or after all conditioned coordinates. For the obstruction identity, pc-minimality implies both restricted minimalities. Conversely, the first effective step of a proper mixed minor lies in the pc-closed family by either restricted minimality, and closure keeps every later step inside.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/minor-atlas/main.tex?#prop:operators

                                                                Source Components of a Representation USO Can Be Deleted

                                                                Name: Source Components of a Representation USO Can Be Deleted

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Representation-Map Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Concept Deletion

                                                                Result Type: Implication

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $C$ be ample, let $r$ be a representation map, and orient its one-inclusion graph by the corresponding unique-sink orientation. For every source strongly connected component $S$, the deletion $C\setminus S$ is ample and the restriction of $r$ is again a representation map.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                This is the source-component deletion theorem for representation orientations. No arc enters $S$, so restricting the map after deleting the whole component preserves the representation conditions and the unique-sink property on every remaining cube.

                                                                References:

                                                                \cite[Proposition~A.2]{ChalopiChepoiMoran22}

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/minor-atlas/main.tex?#prop:source-component

                                                                USO Peeling Width Interpolates Between Dismantlability and Representation

                                                                Name: USO Peeling Width Interpolates Between Dismantlability and Representation

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes
                                                                • Representation-Map Ample Classes

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • USO Peeling Width

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For a nonempty ample class $C$, $\nu(C)=1$ exactly when $C$ is dismantlable ample, and $\nu(C)<\infty$ exactly when $C$ admits a representation map. If $\nu(C)\le k$, then repeated deletion of source components of at most $k$ concepts reduces $C$ to the empty class through represented ample intermediates.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                A unique-sink orientation is acyclic exactly when all its strongly connected components are singletons, giving the first equivalence; existence of any such orientation is the representation-map equivalence. Choose an orientation attaining $\nu(C)$ and repeatedly delete a source component. The source-component theorem preserves ampleness and the restricted representation map, while every component has at most $k$ vertices.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/minor-atlas/main.tex?#prop:peeling-width-ends

                                                                USO Peeling Width Does Not Increase under pc-Minors

                                                                Name: USO Peeling Width Does Not Increase under pc-Minors

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Representation-Map Ample Classes

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • USO Peeling Width

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Coordinate Projection
                                                                • Coordinate Conditioning
                                                                • Partial-Cube Minor

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                If $C'$ is a pc-minor of an ample class $C$, then $\nu(C')\le\nu(C)$. More precisely, conditioning restricts a representation orientation to an induced subgraph, while the canonical in-map orientation on a projection has no larger strongly connected component.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Restriction cannot enlarge a strongly connected component. For a projection, lift every projected vertex to the sink of its coordinate fiber. Each projected arc lifts to a directed path between the chosen representatives; therefore a strongly connected component downstairs injects into one strongly connected component upstairs. Iterate the two inequalities along the pc-minor sequence and minimize over orientations.

                                                                References:

                                                                \cite[Theorem~6.8 and Proposition~6.14]{ChalopiChepoiMoran22}

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/minor-atlas/main.tex?#prop:width-minor-closed

                                                                Exact Ample-Preserving Chunk Deletion Criterion

                                                                Name: Exact Ample-Preserving Chunk Deletion Criterion

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Ample Chunk-Peeling Width

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Concept Deletion

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For $T\in\operatorname{Sh}(C)$ and $a\in\{0,1\}^T$, let $F_{T,a}=\{c\in C:c|_T=a\}$ and let $L_C(S)$ be the shattered coordinate sets having some fiber contained in $S$. If $C$ is ample, then $C\setminus S$ is ample exactly when $|L_C(S)|=|S|$. In that case $S$ is a union of contained fibers, and $\chi(C)=\min_{\varnothing\ne S, |L_C(S)|=|S|}\max\{|S|,\chi(C\setminus S)\}$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Deleting concepts cannot create shattered sets, and a shattered set $T$ disappears exactly when one full fiber $F_{T,a}$ is deleted. Thus $\operatorname{Sh}(C\setminus S)=\operatorname{Sh}(C)\setminus L_C(S)$. Combine $|C|=|\operatorname{Sh}(C)|$ with the shattering inequality for the remainder to obtain $|L_C(S)|\le|S|$, with equality exactly for an ample remainder. The same inequality applied after restoring any point not covered by a contained fiber proves the union assertion. Splitting a peeling at its first deletion gives the recurrence in both directions.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/minor-atlas/main.tex?#prop:tight-sets

                                                                Witnesses:

                                                                • Chunk-Deletion Counting Pitfalls

                                                                Intermediate Decomposition Classes Form Strict pc-Closed Hierarchies

                                                                Name: Intermediate Decomposition Classes Form Strict pc-Closed Hierarchies

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Convex-Treelike Partial Cubes
                                                                • One-Decomposable Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes
                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Both-Sides Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Coordinate Projection
                                                                • Coordinate Conditioning
                                                                • Partial-Cube Minor
                                                                • Full Reduction
                                                                • Cartesian Product
                                                                • Cube Complement

                                                                Result Type: Implication

                                                                Statement:

                                                                The inclusions $\mathcal R_{\mathrm{per}}\subsetneq\mathcal D_1\subsetneq\mathcal D_{\mathrm{amp}}\subsetneq\mathcal A$ and $\mathcal R_{\mathrm{per}}\subsetneq\mathcal B\subsetneq\mathcal D_{\mathrm{amp}}$ are strict. Every ample class of VC dimension at most two belongs to $\mathcal D_1$. Every fixed decomposition level and the both-sides dismantlable class $\mathcal B$ are closed under nonempty pc-minors, full reductions, and Cartesian products; $\mathcal B$ is complement closed after adjoining the empty boundary case.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Recursive decomposition gives the inclusions, the VC-two theorem, and closure under minors, reductions, and products. The tangent-pentagon class lies in the first decomposition level and in $\mathcal B$ but is not recursively peripheral. Hall's class is ample and not dismantlable; its complement is dismantlable and belongs to $\mathcal B$ but an exhaustive one- and two-coordinate section test excludes level one. Complement-section identities exchange projection with full reduction and prove the closure assertions for $\mathcal B$.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/minor-atlas/main.tex?#prop:intermediate-inclusions

                                                                Witnesses:

                                                                • Pentagonal Obstruction
                                                                • Hall Maximum Class
                                                                • Complement of Hall's Maximum Class

                                                                Interval Families with Endpoint Cubes Are Recursively Peripheral

                                                                Name: Interval Families with Endpoint Cubes Are Recursively Peripheral

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Convex-Treelike Partial Cubes

                                                                Result Type: Construction

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $\mathcal I_L$ contain the empty set and all intervals of the linear order $[L]$. For $0\le a,b\le L$, the class $K_{L,a,b}=\mathcal I_L\cup2^{[a]}\cup2^{\{L-b+1,\ldots,L\}}$ is recursively peripheral, and its cube complement is recursively peripheral whenever nonempty.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                First inductively peel a prefix family together with its initial cube. For $K_{L,a,b}$, splitting on the first coordinate yields a smaller class of the same form and one such prefix family, with nested shores. The peripheral recursion completes the induction; complement closure gives the final statement.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/minor-atlas/main.tex?#lem:interval-endpoint-cubes

                                                                Odd Polygon Complements Separate Every Decomposition Level

                                                                Name: Odd Polygon Complements Separate Every Decomposition Level

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Realizable Ample Classes
                                                                • Maximum Classes
                                                                • Both-Sides Dismantlable Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Yang Decomposition Level

                                                                Result Type: Construction

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For every $m\ge2$, the regular $(2m+1)$-tangent sign class $H_{2m+1}$ and its complement $C_{2m+1}$ are realizable maximum classes in the both-sides dismantlable family, with $\kappa(H_{2m+1})=1$ and $\kappa(C_{2m+1})=m-1$. Hence every consecutive inclusion $\mathcal D_k\subsetneq\mathcal D_{k+1}$ is strict, realizable and both-sides dismantlable classes have unbounded decomposition level, and no $\mathcal D_k$ for $k\ge1$ is cube-complement closed.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The arrangement has the Sauer number of regions, all two-coordinate traces, and one missing trace on every triple, so it is maximum of rank two; maximum complementation and Lawrence duality handle its complement. Cyclic-interval geometry proves the dominant-shore lower bound. A sequence adjoining the length-$(m+1)$ coordinate cubes has recursively peripheral links described by endpoint-interval classes and gives the matching upper decomposition. Substituting $m=k+2$ yields every strict step, while complementing the rank-two shore proves failure of complement closure.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                Result Type: Implication

                                                                Statement:

                                                                The established chain is $\mathcal R_{\mathrm{amp}}\subsetneq\mathcal P_D\subseteq\mathcal D_{\mathrm{amp}}\cap\mathsf{MaxMin}\subsetneq\mathsf{MaxMin}\subseteq\mathsf{Ext}\subseteq\mathsf{Rep}\subseteq\mathcal A$, and $\mathcal B\subsetneq\mathsf{Ext}$. The dismantlable-parent class $\mathcal P_D$ is closed under nonempty pc-minors and full reductions but not complement; $\mathsf{Ext}$ is closed under those operations and complement after adjoining the empty boundary case.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Generic affine arrangements give dismantlable maximum parents for realizable classes, and sections of dismantlable classes stay dismantlable. A maximum parent and its complementary maximum class give representation maps on both marked shores, which is the universal-extension criterion. Hall's complement lies in $\mathcal P_D$ but is not realizable; Hall's class is maximum but not dismantlable and lies in $\mathsf{Ext}\setminus\mathcal B$. Commuting marks with projections, conditionings, and reductions proves closure for $\mathcal P_D$; forward-invariant unique-sink cube orientations prove closure for $\mathsf{Ext}$.
