                                                                Decomposition Levels Persist through Maximum Sequences

                                                                Name: Decomposition Levels Persist through Maximum Sequences

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Maximum Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Result Type: Construction

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Fix $k\ge0$. A rank-$r\ge1$ maximum class in $\mathcal D_k$ contains a rank-$(r-1)$ maximum member of $\mathcal D_k$ avoiding any prescribed face fixed on at least $r$ coordinates. A rank-$r

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Nested one-coordinate attachments preserve both maximumity and the fixed decomposition level. Induction on rank builds an avoiding predecessor from the full reduction and a lower predecessor; induction on codimension builds a successor from a projection and a larger projected successor containing the prescribed cube. Iterating downward and upward completes the sequence. A finite level containing all supplied dismantlable classes gives the dismantlable version.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/minor-atlas/main.tex?#prop:decomposable-maximum-sequences

                                                                Free Coordinates Preserve Dismantlable Maximum Parents

                                                                Name: Free Coordinates Preserve Dismantlable Maximum Parents

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Sections of Dismantlable Maximum Parents
                                                                • Maximum-Parent Decomposition-Level Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Cartesian Product

                                                                Result Type: Construction

                                                                Statement:

                                                                If $C$ has a rank-$r$ maximum parent in $\mathcal D_k$, then $C\times\{0,1\}^m$ has a rank-$(r+m)$ maximum parent in the same $\mathcal D_k$ using at most $m$ additional auxiliary coordinates. In particular, sections of dismantlable maximum parents are closed under products with full cubes.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                For one free coordinate, place a supplied maximum parent between consecutive predecessor and successor maximum classes in the same decomposition level. A two-shore construction on one new visible and one auxiliary coordinate uses the parent in the common lower auxiliary shore, the successor on one upper shore, and the predecessor on the other. Pascal counts and nestedness give a rank-one-higher maximum parent whose old mark cuts out the free-coordinate product. Iterate.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/minor-atlas/main.tex?#prop:parent-free-coordinates

                                                                Recursively Nested Maximum Sequences Give Product Parents

                                                                Name: Recursively Nested Maximum Sequences Give Product Parents

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Maximum-Parent Decomposition-Level Classes
                                                                • Sections of Dismantlable Maximum Parents

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Cartesian Product

                                                                Result Type: Construction

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Suppose $C$ has a rank-$r$ maximum parent $M\in\mathcal D_k$, while $D$ has a rank-$s$ maximum parent $N$ lying in a complete maximum sequence whose entry function has a common nested-coordinate recursion. Then $C\times D$ has a rank-$(r+s)$ maximum parent in $\mathcal D_k$ with at most $r+s$ new auxiliary coordinates beyond the supplied marks.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Extend $M$ to a complete maximum sequence in the same decomposition level. Delay its upper levels $s$ times and delay the second sequence $r$ times; delay preserves the common nested recursion. The disjoint level-sum class at rank $r+s$ is maximum. Threshold induction along the nested recursion keeps it in $\mathcal D_k$, and the zero delay face is exactly the product of the supplied parents, so their old marks recover $C\times D$.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/minor-atlas/main.tex?#prop:parent-nested-products

                                                                Tree Incidence Parities Produce Nested Maximum Sequences

                                                                Name: Tree Incidence Parities Produce Nested Maximum Sequences

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Maximum Classes

                                                                Result Type: Construction

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For a rooted tree $T=(V,E)$ with $n$ edges, put $d_v(x)=\bigoplus_{e\ni v}x_e$ for nonroot vertices, $f(x)=\sum_{v\ne o}d_v(x)$, and $B_s=\{x:f(x)\le s\}$. Then $(B_s)_{s=0}^n$ is a complete maximum sequence with a common nested-coordinate recursion. Up to coordinate reflections, every rank-one maximum class and every rank-$(n-2)$ maximum class on $n\ge2$ coordinates occurs in such a sequence.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The reduced incidence map is a bijection, giving the Sauer cardinalities. Deleting any $s+1$ tested tree edges leaves a rooted quotient in which a suitable boundary-parity assignment forces at least $s+1$ odd nonroot components, proving the VC bound. Splitting at a leaf orders the two restrictions pointwise and recursively removes that leaf, giving the common nested recursion. Single parity supports are root paths, which model every rank-one maximum tree; complementing parity gives the rank-$(n-2)$ case.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/minor-atlas/main.tex?#prop:tree-parity-flags

                                                                Maximum Projections Are Determined by the Shattered Complex

                                                                Name: Maximum Projections Are Determined by the Shattered Complex

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Maximum Classes
                                                                • One-Auxiliary Maximum Sections

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Maximum-Projection Complex

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $\Delta=\operatorname{Sh}(C)$. A coordinate set $S$ belongs to $\operatorname{MP}(C)$ exactly when $\Delta|_S$ consists of all subsets of $S$ of size at most some $d_S$. A set $S$ of size $m$ is a minimal nonface exactly when $\Delta|_S$ contains every set of size at most $m-2$ and a nonempty proper subfamily of the $(m-1)$-sets. Every corresponding bad projection needs exactly one auxiliary conditioned coordinate in a maximum parent.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Projection preserves ampleness and restricts the shattered complex, so the Sauer equality gives the skeleton criterion. Exchange-connectivity of equal-size subsets shows that a minimal nonuniform restriction can mix presence and absence only in codimension one, yielding the minimal-nonface form. Complement duality turns such a projection into a rank-one maximum coordinate tree with both active and constant coordinates. Adding one auxiliary path yields a rank-one maximum parent of the complement; complementing gives the required one-auxiliary parent, while nonmaximumity excludes zero auxiliaries.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/minor-atlas/main.tex?#prop:maximum-projection-complex

                                                                Maximum-Parent Decomposition Depth and Feasible Ranks

                                                                Name: Maximum-Parent Decomposition Depth and Feasible Ranks

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Maximum-Parent Decomposition-Level Classes
                                                                • Sections of Dismantlable Maximum Parents
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes
                                                                • Maximum-Generated Classes

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Yang Decomposition Level
                                                                • Maximum-Parent Decomposition Depth
                                                                • Level-Bounded Minimum Maximum-Parent Rank
                                                                • Minimum Maximum-Parent Rank

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Coordinate Projection
                                                                • Coordinate Conditioning
                                                                • Full Reduction
                                                                • Cube Complement

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For every $k$, the sections $\mathcal P_k$ of maximum parents in $\mathcal D_k$ satisfy $\mathcal P_k\subseteq\mathcal D_k\cap\mathsf{MaxMin}$, $\mathcal P_k\subsetneq\mathcal P_{k+1}$, and $\bigcup_k\mathcal P_k=\mathcal P_D$. They are closed under nonempty sections, projections, and full reductions and are constant-coordinate invariant. Only $\mathcal P_0$ is complement closed. Moreover $\kappa(C)\le\lambda(C)$, with equality on maximum classes. When finite, feasible parent ranks at level $k$ are exactly all ranks at least $h_k(C)$; $h_k$ decreases with $k$ and stabilizes to $h_D(C)$ by $k\ge\max\{h_D(C)-1,0\}$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Section closure of each decomposition level gives the base inclusions and intrinsic-depth inequality; maximum classes are their own parents. Odd polygon complements give every strict level. Marks commute with projection, conditioning, and reduction, while the fixed-level constant-coordinate construction preserves the parent level. Complement closure holds at level zero and fails at every higher level by the complementary polygon pair. A nested successor construction raises parent rank one step without changing its level, giving the feasible-rank ray. Every rank-$r$ dismantlable class lies in $\mathcal D_{r-1}$, which gives stabilization at a least-rank dismantlable parent.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/minor-atlas/main.tex?#prop:parent-depth-hierarchy

                                                                Witnesses:

                                                                • Odd Tangent-Polygon Classes and Complements

                                                                Face-Avoiding Maximum Predecessors Preserve Intersections

                                                                Name: Face-Avoiding Maximum Predecessors Preserve Intersections

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Maximum Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Full Reduction

                                                                Result Type: Construction

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For an ordered coordinate list $D$ and pattern $\tau$, the recursively defined face-avoidance operator $L_{D,\tau}$ satisfies $L(C)\subseteq C$, $L(C)[\tau]=\varnothing$, and $L(C\cap E)=L(C)\cap L(E)$. Hence it preserves inclusions. On a maximum class of rank $0\le r\le|D|$ it produces a maximum rank-$(r-1)$ class, allowing formal rank $-1$ for the empty output. Nonempty outputs preserve every decomposition level $\mathcal D_k$ and dismantlability.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Induction on the ordered list uses full reduction for the larger shore and recursively nests the avoiding shore. Both lifts remain in the input, the two shores avoid the target pattern in complementary ways, and full reduction commutes with intersection. Pascal's identity gives the predecessor cardinality and the two shore ranks exclude a shattered support of size $r$. Full reduction and nested expansion preserve the decomposition level.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/minor-atlas/main.tex?#prop:monotone-predecessors

                                                                Minimum-Section Deletions Have Controlled Dismantlable Parents

                                                                Name: Minimum-Section Deletions Have Controlled Dismantlable Parents

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Maximum Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes
                                                                • Sections of Dismantlable Maximum Parents

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Concept Deletion

                                                                Result Type: Construction

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $M$ be maximum of rank $r$, and let a pattern $p$ on a $q$-coordinate block, $1\le q\le r$, have the smallest section $M[p]=\partial_JM=S$. Put $C=M\setminus(S\times\{p\})$. If $M,C\in\mathcal D_k$, then $C$ has a rank-$r$ maximum parent in $\mathcal D_{\max(k,r-1)}$ with exactly $r+1-q$ auxiliaries, optimal among rank-$r$ parents. If both inputs are dismantlable, then $C$ has a dismantlable maximum parent.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Choose a compatible maximum predecessor of the minimum section and run the prescribed-section recursion, which keeps both the predecessor and its punctured form in level $\max(k,r-1)$. One auxiliary replacement lowers the marked minimum rank by one while retaining a level-bounded decomposition of both the parent and its deleted section. After $r-q+1$ repetitions the marked minimum is empty and the zero mark recovers $C$. The fixed-rank auxiliary lower bound from the minimum-section theorem proves optimality.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/minor-atlas/main.tex?#thm:dismantlable-minimum-deletion

                                                                Peripheral Classes Survive Minimum-Section Deletion

                                                                Name: Peripheral Classes Survive Minimum-Section Deletion

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Convex-Treelike Partial Cubes
                                                                • Sections of Dismantlable Maximum Parents

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Concept Deletion

                                                                Result Type: Implication

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Under the smallest-section hypotheses for a rank-$r$ maximum class and a $q$-coordinate pattern, if the maximum class is recursively peripheral then deleting that whole smallest section remains recursively peripheral. The deletion has a rank-$r$ maximum parent in $\mathcal D_{r-1}$ with the optimal $r+1-q$ auxiliaries and therefore lies in $\mathcal R_{\mathrm{per}}\cap\mathcal P_D$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Induct through a nested peripheral split. When the split coordinate lies in the deleted block, rank comparison forces the pattern into the smaller shore, where induction applies. Otherwise both shores inherit the same smallest-section identity; delete in both and retain their nesting. Apply the controlled dismantlable-parent theorem at level zero for the parent and auxiliary assertions.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/minor-atlas/main.tex?#prop:peripheral-minimum-deletion

                                                                Every Corner Deletion of a Peripheral Maximum Class Has a Peripheral Parent

                                                                Name: Every Corner Deletion of a Peripheral Maximum Class Has a Peripheral Parent

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Convex-Treelike Partial Cubes
                                                                • Maximum Classes
                                                                • Maximum-Parent Decomposition-Level Classes
                                                                • One-Auxiliary Maximum Sections

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Concept Deletion
                                                                • Coordinate Projection
                                                                • Coordinate Conditioning

                                                                Result Type: Construction

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $M$ be a recursively peripheral maximum class of positive rank $r$ and $v$ any corner. Then $M\setminus\{v\}$ is recursively peripheral and has a recursively peripheral rank-$r$ maximum parent $N$ on one auxiliary coordinate $a$, with $\pi_XN=M$ and $N[a=0]=M\setminus\{v\}$. Thus the deletion belongs to $\mathcal P_0\cap\mathcal M_1$; for proper $M$, rank $r$ and one auxiliary are optimal.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Order the corner support so the compatible face-avoiding predecessor respects a nested peripheral split of $M$. If the split coordinate is outside the corner support, apply induction in the large shore and monotonicity in the small shore. If it belongs to the support, the corner lies in the smaller shore; put that coordinate first and apply induction there. The resulting shores stay nested and peripheral. The standard one-corner parent supplies the required projection and section; nonmaximumity of a proper deletion proves optimality.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/minor-atlas/main.tex?#prop:peripheral-corner-parent

                                                                Structure of Dismantlable-Complement Ample Classes

                                                                Name: Structure of Dismantlable-Complement Ample Classes

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Dismantlable-Complement Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes
                                                                • Both-Sides Dismantlable Ample Classes
                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Maximum-Generated Classes
                                                                • Universal Cube-Extension Ample Classes
                                                                • Representation-Map Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Coordinate Projection
                                                                • Coordinate Conditioning
                                                                • Full Reduction

                                                                Result Type: Implication

                                                                Statement:

                                                                The dismantlable-complement class $\mathsf{coDamp}$ is closed under nonempty sections, projections, full reductions, and constant-coordinate changes. It is incomparable with dismantlable ample classes, while $\mathcal B\subsetneq\mathsf{coDamp}\subsetneq\mathcal A$, and $\mathsf{MaxMin}$ is not contained in their union. The open inclusions $\mathcal D_{\mathrm{amp}}\subseteq\mathsf{Ext}$ and $\mathsf{coDamp}\subseteq\mathsf{Rep}$ are equivalent; likewise $\mathcal D_{\mathrm{amp}}\subseteq\mathsf{MaxMin}$ and $\mathsf{coDamp}\subseteq\mathsf{MaxMin}$ are equivalent.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Complementation commutes with sections and exchanges projection with full reduction, so dismantlable closure laws transfer. Hall's class and its dismantlable complement witness both directions of incomparability. Their product is maximum-generated, while it and its complement each have a nondismantlable Hall section, proving the stronger noncontainment. The universal-extension complementary-shore criterion gives the first equivalence; complement closure of maximum ancestry gives the second.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/minor-atlas/main.tex?#prop:complement-dismantlable

                                                                Witnesses:

                                                                • Hall Maximum Class
                                                                • Complement of Hall's Maximum Class

                                                                Both-Sides Dismantlability Preserves a coDamp Product

                                                                Name: Both-Sides Dismantlability Preserves a coDamp Product

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Dismantlable-Complement Ample Classes
                                                                • Both-Sides Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Cartesian Product

                                                                Result Type: Implication

                                                                Statement:

                                                                If $C\in\mathsf{coDamp}$ and $D\in\mathcal B$ use disjoint coordinates, then $C\times D\in\mathsf{coDamp}$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Writing $P=C^c$ and $Q=D^c$, the product complement is $(P\times\{0,1\}^Y)\cup(\{0,1\}^X\times Q)$. Follow a corner deletion of $P$ one row at a time; within the row of its next corner, use the relative deletion from the full $Y$-cube down to $Q$ supplied by the dismantling of $D$. Each deleted vertex has the product of its two corner cubes present. The terminal class is the dismantlable product of a full cube with $Q$.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/minor-atlas/main.tex?#prop:complement-dismantlable-product

                                                                Comments:

                                                                This does not prove that the entire dismantlable-complement class is product closed; the second factor must itself and its complement be dismantlable.

                                                                Representation Criterion after Deleting a Corner

                                                                Name: Representation Criterion after Deleting a Corner

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Representation-Map Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Concept Deletion

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $E$ be ample and let $v$ be a corner whose incident directions form its support $T$. Then $E\setminus\{v\}$ has a representation map exactly when $E$ has a representation map assigning the label $T$ to $v$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Deleting the corner removes exactly $T$ from the shattered family, so a map with $r(v)=T$ restricts immediately. Conversely, extend a representation map of the deletion by $v\mapsto T$. No other concept agrees with $v$ on $T$: an isometric path to one would have to leave $v$ in a direction outside its corner support. Thus $T$ separates $v$ from every old concept and all new nonclashing conditions hold.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/minor-atlas/main.tex?#lem:corner-representation-deletion

                                                                Representation Maps Can Be Repaired at Corners of Dimension at Most Two

                                                                Name: Representation Maps Can Be Repaired at Corners of Dimension at Most Two

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Representation-Map Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Concept Deletion

                                                                Result Type: Algorithm

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $D$ be ample with a representation map and let $v$ be a corner with support $J$, $|J|\le2$. At most three adjacent label exchanges inside the corner cube produce a representation map assigning $J$ to $v$, without changing labels outside that cube. Consequently deleting $v$ preserves existence of a representation map, with no bound on the VC dimension of $D$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                A safe exchange swaps adjacent labels $A$ and $A\cup\{i\}$; the support bijection is unchanged and any supposed new clash would already have been an old clash. The owner of $J$ lies inside the corner cube, and incoming neighbors carry no directions outside $J$. For a one-edge corner one exchange suffices. For a square corner, the four possible positions and labels reduce by a case table to at most three safe exchanges. The corner-deletion representation criterion then applies.

                                                                References:

                                                                \cite[Corollary~6.7 and Theorem~6.8]{ChalopiChepoiMoran22}

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/minor-atlas/main.tex?#prop:small-corner-map-repair

                                                                Learning Spaces and Daisy Cubes Are Peripheral, Realizable, and Maximum-Generated

                                                                Name: Learning Spaces and Daisy Cubes Are Peripheral, Realizable, and Maximum-Generated

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Learning-Space Graphs
                                                                • Daisy Cubes
                                                                • Convex-Treelike Partial Cubes
                                                                • Realizable Ample Classes
                                                                • Maximum-Generated Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Coordinate Projection
                                                                • Coordinate Conditioning
                                                                • Partial-Cube Minor

                                                                Result Type: Implication

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Every finite learning-space graph and every daisy cube belongs to the intersection of recursively peripheral and realizable ample classes, hence is maximum-generated. Moreover $\operatorname{Cl}_{pc}(\mathsf{Learn})=\operatorname{Cl}_c(\mathsf{Learn})\subseteq\mathcal R_{\mathrm{per}}\cap\mathcal R_{\mathrm{amp}}$. A learning space on $n\ge1$ coordinates with $q$ inclusion-minimal missing consistent partial labelings has a rank-$n$ maximum parent with at most $q+2n$ auxiliaries; the zero-coordinate singleton needs none.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Strict coordinate inequalities realize downsets and learning spaces on an open convex domain; a bounded perturbation and generic arrangement give the quantitative maximum parent. Recursive accessibility supplies a feasible singleton whose two sections are nested learning spaces, proving peripheral membership by induction. Learning spaces are projection closed, so the pc-closure reduces to conditioning closure; minor closure of peripheral and realizable ample classes gives the containment.

                                                                Isometry in a Partial Cube and Its Ambient Hypercube Is Equivalent

                                                                Name: Isometry in a Partial Cube and Its Ambient Hypercube Is Equivalent

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Partial Cubes

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $\mathcal G$ be a partial cube embedded isometrically in $Q_X$, and let $G$ be a subgraph. Then $G$ is isometric in $\mathcal G$ exactly when it is isometric in $Q_X$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                For vertices of $G$, the ambient embedding gives $d_{\mathcal G}=d_{Q_X}$. Either of the equalities $d_G=d_{\mathcal G}$ and $d_G=d_{Q_X}$ therefore implies the other.

                                                                Reset and All-Pairs Routing Algorithms for Explicit Media

                                                                Name: Reset and All-Pairs Routing Algorithms for Explicit Media

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Partial Cubes

                                                                Result Type: Algorithm

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For an explicit adjacency-list representation of a finite medium with $n$ states and $m$ effective directed transitions, a reset message of length at most $n-1$ sending every state to one fixed state can be found in $O(m)$ time. In $O(n^2)$ time one can construct all ordered-pair distances and a first effective token on a straight path; each path is then output in time linear in its length.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                References:

                                                                \cite[Theorems~1--2]{EppsteinFalmagne08media}

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/survey/main.tex?#thm:media-algorithms

                                                                Comments:

                                                                The input includes token labels on directed transitions. The reset construction guarantees length at most $n-1$ but does not minimize reset length.

                                                                Well-Graded Incidence Duals Characterize Paths

                                                                Name: Well-Graded Incidence Duals Characterize Paths

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Partial Cubes
                                                                • Paths

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For a finite irredundant well-graded family $H\subseteq2^X$, its incidence dual $H^\star=\{\{A\in H:x\in A\}:x\in X\}$ is well graded exactly when $H$ is a full inclusion chain. Consequently, a finite partial cube admits an irredundant well-graded representation with well-graded incidence dual exactly when it is a path.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The first assertion is the essential-coordinate incidence-dual theorem for well-graded families. A full chain has a path as its one-inclusion graph, while every path admits such a chain representation when based at an endpoint.

                                                                References:

                                                                \cite[Theorem~4.12]{Mofidi20wellgraded}

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/survey/main.tex?#thm:wellgraded-incidence-dual

                                                                Comments:

                                                                The claim concerns existence of a suitable irredundant representation. Independent coordinate complementation preserves the partial cube but can destroy dual well-gradedness.

                                                                One-Step Expansion Preservation Contracts

                                                                Name: One-Step Expansion Preservation Contracts

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Partial Cubes
                                                                • Median Graphs
                                                                • Almost-Median Partial Cubes
                                                                • Semi-Median Partial Cubes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Graph Expansion

                                                                Result Type: Construction

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $H$ expand $G$ with cover $(G_1,G_2)$ and overlap $G_0$. If $G$ is a partial cube, then $H$ is a partial cube without another overlap condition. If $G$ is median and $G_0$ is convex, then $H$ is median. If $G$ and both cover members are almost-median and $G_0$ is isometric, then $H$ is almost-median; isometry alone is insufficient. If $G$ is semi-median, $G_0$ is connected, and the cover satisfies property (P), then $H$ is semi-median; connectedness alone is insufficient.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The first two clauses are the classical partial-cube and median expansion theorems. The almost-median and semi-median clauses are the exact preservation theorems for their respective cover conditions; published counterexamples show that deleting the cover-membership or property-(P) hypotheses invalidates them.

                                                                References:

                                                                [BresarImrichKlavzar03fast]

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/survey/main.tex?#prop:one-step-expansion-contracts

                                                                Gated Expansions Characterize Quasi-Median Graphs

                                                                Name: Gated Expansions Characterize Quasi-Median Graphs

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • k-Ary and Gated Expansion

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                A finite graph is a partial Hamming graph exactly when it is obtainable from $K_1$ by $k$-ary expansions. It is quasi-median exactly when it is obtainable from $K_1$ by gated expansions. The binary bipartite specialization is the median expansion theorem, but general gated expansions permit $k>2$ and cliques.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                References:

                                                                [BresarKlavzarSkrekovski03Quasi]

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/survey/main.tex?#thm:gated-expansion-scope

                                                                Comments:

                                                                Partial Hamming and quasi-median graphs are retained here as the precise ambient scope of the operation theorem; they are not promoted to nodes in the partial-cube class hierarchy.

                                                                Theta-Class Hypergraph and Theta-Graph Profile

                                                                Name: Theta-Class Hypergraph and Theta-Graph Profile

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Partial Cubes
                                                                • Median Graphs
                                                                • ACC Graphs

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Theta Graph
                                                                • Theta-Class Hypergraph

                                                                Result Type: Implication

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For an ACC graph, the 2-section of $\mathcal H_\Theta(G)$ is chordal. In a median graph every pairwise adjacent family of $\Theta$-classes has representatives with a common endpoint, so $\omega(\Theta(G))=\Delta(G)$. If $G$ is both ACC and a $p$-expansion graph, then $\mathcal H_\Theta(G)$ is conformal and $\Theta(G)$ is dually chordal. For every $p$-expansion graph, $\Theta(G)$ is chordal; hence it is doubly chordal in the ACC case.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                References:

                                                                [BresakSumenjak2014]

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/survey/main.tex?#thm:theta-hypergraph-profile

                                                                Comments:

                                                                The ACC hypothesis alone does not force conformality or dual chordality; the source supplies a counterexample.

                                                                High-Girth Partial Cubes Are Tree-Zone and Sparse

                                                                Name: High-Girth Partial Cubes Are Tree-Zone and Sparse

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Partial Cubes
                                                                • Tree-Zone Partial Cubes
                                                                • Regular Partial Cubes

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Graph Girth

                                                                Result Type: Implication

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $G$ be a finite or locally finite partial cube with $g(G)>6$. Every zone graph is a tree. If $\delta(G)\ge3$, then $G$ contains an infinite subtree of degrees two and three with degree-two vertices pairwise at distance at least two; hence $G$ is infinite and has exponential growth. A finite regular such graph is $K_1$, $K_2$, or an even cycle.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                References:

                                                                [Marc16highgirth]

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/survey/main.tex?#thm:high-girth-rigidity

                                                                Comments:

                                                                The strict girth bound is sharp: middle-levels graphs have girth six.

                                                                Tree-Like Partial Cubes Have Dismantlable Cube Graphs

                                                                Name: Tree-Like Partial Cubes Have Dismantlable Cube Graphs

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Tree-Like Partial Cubes

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Maximal-Cube Intersection Graph

                                                                Result Type: Implication

                                                                Statement:

                                                                If $G$ is a finite tree-like partial cube, then its maximal-cube intersection graph $Q(G)$ is dismantlable.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                References:

                                                                \cite[Corollary~15]{Gologranc14treehamming}

                                                                Images and Laws of Cube-Intersection Operators

                                                                Name: Images and Laws of Cube-Intersection Operators

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Median Graphs

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Maximal-Cube Intersection Graph

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Cube-Intersection Operator

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For median $G$, $Q_0(G)$ is Helly. For every $k\ge1$, the possible graphs $Q_k(G)$ are exactly the clique graphs, with $Q_1(G)=C(G^e)$. For all $k,\ell\ge0$, $Q_k(G)=Q_{k+\ell}(G\square Q_\ell)$. The possible $Q_{m2}(G)$ are exactly the diamond-free graphs, and $Q_{m2}(G\square H)=Q_{m2}(G)\square Q_{m2}(H)$; no analogous fixed-$Q_k$ product identity holds in general.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                References:

                                                                [BresarSumenjak2009]

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/survey/main.tex?#thm:cube-intersection-operators

                                                                Crossing Graph Bounds the Cube Polynomial

                                                                Name: Crossing Graph Bounds the Cube Polynomial

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Partial Cubes
                                                                • Median Graphs

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Crossing Graph
                                                                • Cube Polynomial

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For every partial cube $G\ne K_1$, $C(G,x)\le\operatorname{Cl}(G^\sharp,x+1)$ coefficientwise, with equality exactly when $G$ is median. Thus for median $G$, the coefficient of $(x+1)^k$ in $C(G,x)$ equals the number of $k$-cliques of $G^\sharp$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                References:

                                                                [XieFengXu24crossing]

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/survey/main.tex?#thm:crossing-cube-polynomial

                                                                Comments:

                                                                The identity transfers clique-polynomial phenomena to cube polynomials; in particular, median cube polynomials need not be unimodal.

                                                                Distance-Cube Polynomial Characterizes Rooted Daisy Cubes

                                                                Name: Distance-Cube Polynomial Characterizes Rooted Daisy Cubes

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Partial Cubes
                                                                • Daisy Cubes

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Cube Polynomial
                                                                • Rooted Distance-Cube Polynomial

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For a partial cube $G$ rooted at $u$, the following are equivalent: $G$ is a daisy cube rooted at $u$; $C(G,x)=W_{G,u}(x+1)$; $D_{G,u}(x,y)=W_{G,u}(x+y)$; and $D_{G,u}(x,y)=C(G,x+y-1)$. Every rooted partial cube satisfies $D_{G,u}(x,y)\le W_{G,u}(x+y)$ coefficientwise, with equality exactly in the daisy case.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                References:

                                                                \cite[Theorems~6--7]{ZhengXieXu26}

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/survey/main.tex?#thm:daisy-polynomials

                                                                Comments:

                                                                The cited source is a March 2026 arXiv preprint; that publication status is preserved.

                                                                Varchenko Matrices Multiply under Cartesian Products

                                                                Name: Varchenko Matrices Multiply under Cartesian Products

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Partial Cubes
                                                                • Arrangement-Factorizable Varchenko Partial Cubes
                                                                • Hypercubes

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Unsigned Varchenko Determinant

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Cartesian Product

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For finite partial cubes on disjoint class variables, $\mathsf V_{G\square H}=\mathsf V_G\otimes\mathsf V_H$ and $\det\mathsf V_{G\square H}=(\det\mathsf V_G)^{|V(H)|}(\det\mathsf V_H)^{|V(G)|}$. Hence arrangement-type factorization is product-closed, and $\det\mathsf V_{Q_d}=\prod_{i=1}^d(1-x_i^2)^{2^{d-1}}$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Separating classes in the product split disjointly between the two factors, so every matrix entry factors and the matrix is a Kronecker product. The determinant formula for Kronecker products gives the exponent law; iterate $Q_d=K_2^{\square d}$ for the cube formula.

                                                                References:

                                                                [HochstattlerKeipYazici25]

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/survey/main.tex?#prop:varchenko-cartesian-products

                                                                Hull Number Is Hard for Partial Cubes but Tractable for Partial-Cube Quadrangulations

                                                                Name: Hull Number Is Hard for Partial Cubes but Tractable for Partial-Cube Quadrangulations

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Partial Cubes
                                                                • Planar Partial Cubes

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Geodesic Hull Number

                                                                Result Type: Algorithm

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Given a partial cube $G$ and integer $k$, deciding whether $h(G)\le k$ is NP-complete. If a plane quadrangulation $G$ is a partial cube, then $h(G)$ is computable in polynomial time.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                For the positive case, the simple non-separating Jordan arrangement has a chordal open-interior intersection graph, and a minimum hitting set of interiors reduces to minimum clique cover. The simplicity hypothesis is essential to this reduction.

                                                                References:

                                                                [AlbenqueKnauer16hull]

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/survey/main.tex?#thm:planar-partial-cube-hull-number

                                                                Exact Tree-Product Bounds for Squaregraphs

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Cartesian Product

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Every finite squaregraph embeds isometrically into a product of five trees, and some require five. Three trees suffice when the $2\times2$ grid is absent. A finite squaregraph embeds isometrically into a product of two trees exactly when every inner vertex has even degree.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                \cite[Theorem~3]{bandelt2010combinatorics}

                                                                Squaregraphs Have Outerplanar-by-Path Semistrong Hosts

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Squaregraphs

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Semistrong Graph Product

                                                                Result Type: Construction

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Every finite squaregraph $G$ is isomorphic to a subgraph of $H\boxtimes_s P$ for some outerplanar graph $H$ and path $P$. The outerplanar factor cannot uniformly be replaced by a forest, even in a strong-product host with any fixed complete-graph factor.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                References:

                                                                \cite[Theorem~1 and Corollary~12]{HickingbothamJungeblutMerkerWood24}

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                Comments:

                                                                ACC Graphs Are Recognizable in Near-Linear Time

                                                                Name: ACC Graphs Are Recognizable in Near-Linear Time

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • ACC Graphs

                                                                Result Type: Algorithm

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Given an arbitrary graph with $n$ vertices and $m$ edges, ACC membership can be decided in $O(m\log n)$ time. The input need not be promised median or partial-cubical.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The algorithm recognizes the median structure, identifies square-generated edge classes, and maintains pendant cubes through the elimination process.

                                                                Cube-Intersection Graph Representation Classes

                                                                • Cube-Intersection Operator

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                The graphs $Q(G)$ arising from $p$-expansion graphs are exactly the chordal graphs; those from median $p$-expansion graphs are exactly the Helly chordal graphs; those from ACC graphs are exactly the dually chordal graphs; and those from ACC $p$-expansion graphs are exactly the doubly chordal graphs.

                                                                Statement:

                                                                A netlike completion $\widehat G$ is median exactly when $G$ has the median-cycle property. In that case $\widehat G$ is a minimal median graph containing $G$ isometrically. Conversely, every MCP netlike partial cube is obtained from a median graph by deleting the specified maximal finite hypercubes.

                                                                Major Partial-Cube Classes Are First-Order Definable with Betweenness

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Partial Cubes
                                                                • Median Graphs
                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Oriented-Matroid Tope Graphs
                                                                • COM Tope Graphs
                                                                • Pasch Partial Cubes
                                                                • Peano Partial Cubes
                                                                • Cellular Bipartite Partial Cubes
                                                                • Hypercellular Partial Cubes
                                                                • Almost-Median Partial Cubes
                                                                • Netlike Partial Cubes

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Each listed class is definable on finite connected graphs by a fixed first-order sentence using equality and the ternary metric-betweenness relation. Consequently every listed class has a polynomial-time recognition algorithm obtained by constructing all-pairs betweenness and evaluating its fixed sentence.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                References:

                                                                \cite[Theorem~10]{ChalopinChangatChepoiJacob24}
