                                                                Boolean Median Characterizes Flag Complexes

                                                                Name: Boolean Median Characterizes Flag Complexes

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Simplex Graphs
                                                                • Median Graphs

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Majority Closure

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For a finite abstract simplicial complex $\Delta\subseteq2^X$, the following are equivalent: $\Delta$ is flag; it is the clique complex, equivalently the independence complex, of a graph; and $\operatorname{med}(A,B,C)=(A\cap B)\cup(A\cap C)\cup(B\cap C)$ belongs to $\Delta$ for all $A,B,C\in\Delta$. Its face-poset covering graph is then a simplex graph and hence median.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                References:

                                                                \cite[Theorem~1.5]{XieXu25simplex}

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/survey/main.tex?#thm:simplex-boolean-median

                                                                Comments:

                                                                For $2^{\{1,2,3\}}\setminus\{\{1,2,3\}\}$, the three 2-faces have missing Boolean median $\{1,2,3\}$; its covering graph is $Q_3^-$ and is not simplex.

                                                                Daisy Cubes Are Recognizable with a Proper Labelling in Quadratic Time

                                                                Name: Daisy Cubes Are Recognizable with a Proper Labelling in Quadratic Time

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Daisy Cubes

                                                                Result Type: Algorithm

                                                                Statement:

                                                                An arbitrary $n$-vertex graph can be tested for being a daisy cube in $O(n^2)$ time. On acceptance, the algorithm also outputs an isometric hypercube labelling whose label family is a down-set.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                First apply the quadratic partial-cube recognition algorithm to recover the intrinsic $\Theta$-coordinates. For every $\Theta$-class, compute both semicubes and their boundaries and require one boundary to equal its semicube. Orient that peripheral semicube as the 1-side. Crossing any present 1-coordinate gives its 0-neighbor, so repeated crossings prove that the resulting labels form a down-set. The recognition and output scans remain quadratic.

                                                                References:

                                                                [taranenko2020daisy] [XieXu25simplex]

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/survey/main.tex?#cor:daisy-recognition

                                                                Local Maximal-Cube Traces Cover Every Cornerless Cube

                                                                Name: Local Maximal-Cube Traces Cover Every Cornerless Cube

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Partial Cubes
                                                                • Cornerless Ample Classes

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Maximal-Cube Intersection Graph

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $C$ be a maximal cube of a nonempty cube family $X$, and let $C_1,\ldots,C_k$ be the other maximal cubes meeting it. The corners of $X$ lying in $C$ are exactly $C\setminus\bigcup_i(C\cap C_i)$. Moreover $C_i$ meets $C_j$ exactly when their traces on $C$ meet. Thus in a cornerless family the nonempty proper traces $C\cap C_i$ cover $C$, their intersection graph is the neighbour graph of $C$, and deleting repetitions and redundant traces gives an irredundant proper-subcube cover.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                A vertex of $C$ fails to be a corner exactly when another maximal cube contains it, proving the complement formula. If two neighbouring cubes meet each other, the three pairwise-intersecting hypercube subcubes $C,C_i,C_j$ have common intersection by Helly; the reverse implication is immediate. Cornerlessness makes the traces cover, and an inclusion-minimal covering subfamily is irredundant.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#lem:damp-local-maximal-cube-trace-cover

                                                                Fibonacci-Dimension Formula, Bounds, and Product Laws

                                                                Name: Fibonacci-Dimension Formula, Bounds, and Product Laws

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Partial Cubes
                                                                • Fibonacci Cubes
                                                                • Trees

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Fibonacci Dimension
                                                                • Isometric Dimension
                                                                • Semicube Coordinating-Path Number
                                                                • Crossing Graph

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Cartesian Product

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                A connected graph has finite Fibonacci dimension exactly when it is a partial cube. For a nontrivial partial cube $G$, $\operatorname{fdim}(G)=\operatorname{idim}(G)+p(X(G))-1$ and $\operatorname{idim}(G)\le\operatorname{fdim}(G)\le2\operatorname{idim}(G)-1$; equality in the upper bound holds exactly when the crossing graph is complete. Nontrivial partial cubes satisfy $\operatorname{fdim}(G\square H)=\operatorname{fdim}(G)+\operatorname{fdim}(H)+1$, and every tree satisfies $\operatorname{fdim}(T)=|E(T)|$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                A Fibonacci-cube embedding is a hypercube embedding whose coordinate order prevents adjacent 1s. Choosing orientations and ordering the coordinates is equivalent to covering one semicube from each complementary pair by coordinating paths in $X(G)$; concatenating those paths requires one separator coordinate between consecutive paths. This gives the exact formula. The number of required paths lies between one and the isometric dimension, with the maximum characterized by complete crossing. Disjoint coordinate blocks with one separator prove the Cartesian-product law, and the tree formula follows because distinct tree edges form independent cuts.

                                                                References:

                                                                [CabelloEppsteinKlavzar11fibdim]

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/survey/main.tex?#thm:fibonacci-dimension-profile

                                                                Comments:

                                                                The cited source also gives NP-hardness and approximation results; the database record keeps the structural theorem while the survey retains the detailed algorithmic profile.

                                                                Minimum Fibonacci Dimension for Isometric Avoidance Families

                                                                Name: Minimum Fibonacci Dimension for Isometric Avoidance Families

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Isometric Word-Avoidance Cubes
                                                                • Partial Cubes

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Fibonacci Dimension
                                                                • Isometric Dimension

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $k\ge|f|$. If $|f|\ge3$ and $f$ is an isometric forbidden word, then $Q_k^{\mathrm{av}}(f)$ is a partial cube with isometric dimension $k$. If $\{11,f\}$ is isometric and $f\ne010$, then $Q_k^{\mathrm{av}}(\{11,f\})$ has both isometric and Fibonacci dimension $k$. For $f=010$ the graph is $C_4$, with dimensions two and three.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Isometricity of the forbidden language makes the induced word graph isometric in $Q_k$; when $|f|\ge3$, every coordinate remains active, so the isometric dimension is $k$. Avoiding 11 places the family inside $\Gamma_k$, giving Fibonacci dimension at most $k$, while isometric dimension gives the matching lower bound. The exceptional word 010 collapses the allowed graph to a 4-cycle, whose two dimensions are known directly.

                                                                References:

                                                                [AnselmoEtAl25fibdim]

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/survey/main.tex?#thm:avoidance-fibonacci-dimension

                                                                Partial Cubes Are Recognizable with Coordinates in Quadratic Time

                                                                Name: Partial Cubes Are Recognizable with Coordinates in Quadratic Time

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Partial Cubes

                                                                Result Type: Algorithm

                                                                Statement:

                                                                An arbitrary $n$-vertex graph can be tested for being a partial cube in $O(n^2)$ word-RAM time. On acceptance, the same algorithm outputs an isometric hypercube labelling with one coordinate for each $\Theta$-class.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Breadth-first distance data identify candidate semicube cuts and the algorithm verifies the partial-cube cut partition while incrementally assigning one bit per accepted cut. Failure of a cut or distance condition rejects the graph; when all cuts pass, Hamming distance in the constructed labels equals graph distance. The data structures and total scans take quadratic word-RAM time.

                                                                References:

                                                                \cite[Theorem~1]{Eppstein11recognizing}

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/survey/main.tex?#thm:partial-cube-recognition

                                                                Comments:

                                                                The full coordinate output can itself require quadratic size, for example on paths.

                                                                Foundational Structure of Simple COMs

                                                                • Coordinate Projection
                                                                • Coordinate Conditioning

                                                                Result Type: Other

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For a simple COM $(E,\mathcal L)$, the tope graph is a partial cube and determines the sign-vector system up to coordinate reorientation. Deletions, contractions, and fibers remain COMs, and every face becomes an oriented matroid after deleting its fixed coordinates. The system supports a contractible regular cell complex $\Delta(\mathcal L)$ whose 1-skeleton is the tope graph and whose cells are the oriented-matroid complexes carried by its faces.

                                                                [BCK2018]

                                                                Unrestricted-Rank Tope-Graph Classes Are Polynomial-Time Recognizable

                                                                Name: Unrestricted-Rank Tope-Graph Classes Are Polynomial-Time Recognizable

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • COM Tope Graphs
                                                                • Oriented-Matroid Tope Graphs
                                                                • Affine Oriented-Matroid Tope Graphs
                                                                • Ample Classes

                                                                Result Type: Algorithm

                                                                Statement:

                                                                From an arbitrary graph, membership in each unrestricted-rank tope-graph class associated with a COM, an oriented matroid, an affine oriented matroid, or a lopsided system can be decided in polynomial time.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                First recognize a partial cube and recover its $\Theta$-coordinates. The intrinsic characterizations then reduce membership to polynomially many gating tests on antipodal and, in the affine case, conformal subgraphs. The method handles the infinite obstruction families directly and does not enumerate them.

                                                                Finite Obstruction Theorems for Bounded COM Rank

                                                                Name: Finite Obstruction Theorems for Bounded COM Rank

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • COM Tope Graphs
                                                                • Oriented-Matroid Tope Graphs
                                                                • Affine Oriented-Matroid Tope Graphs
                                                                • Ample Classes

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • VC Dimension

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Partial-Cube Minor

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For $r\ge3$, COM tope graphs of rank at most $r$ are exactly $\mathcal F(\mathcal Q_r^-)$. Oriented-matroid tope graphs are the antipodal members of this class, and affine-oriented-matroid tope graphs are its affine members whose conformal subgraphs are gated. Ample or lopsided tope graphs of rank at most $r$ are exactly $\mathcal F(\mathcal Q_r^{--})$. Rank here equals VC dimension.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                References:

                                                                \cite[Corollary~7.5]{KnauerMarc20}

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/survey/main.tex?#thm:bounded-com-rank

                                                                Comments:

                                                                The finite obstruction families are recorded separately as $\mathcal Q_r^-$ and $\mathcal Q_r^{--}$; each includes $Q_{r+1}$ to enforce the rank bound.

                                                                Acycloid and Planar Rank-Three Profile of Antipodal Partial Cubes

                                                                Name: Acycloid and Planar Rank-Three Profile of Antipodal Partial Cubes

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Antipodal Partial Cubes
                                                                • Oriented-Matroid Tope Graphs
                                                                • Planar Partial Cubes
                                                                • Median Graphs
                                                                • Hypercubes

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                A finite connected graph is an antipodal partial cube exactly when it is the tope graph of a simple acycloid. It is planar and antipodal exactly when it is the tope graph of an oriented matroid of rank at most three. A graph is both median and antipodal exactly when it is a hypercube.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                [FukudaHanda1993] [KlavzarKovse09even]

                                                                Further Structure of Antipodal Partial Cubes

                                                                Name: Further Structure of Antipodal Partial Cubes

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Antipodal Partial Cubes
                                                                • Even Cycles

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Isometric Dimension
                                                                • Graph Girth

                                                                Result Type: Other

                                                                Statement:

                                                                A bipartite antipodal graph is a partial cube exactly when it is interval monotone; it suffices to test intervals of length at least $\operatorname{diam}(G)-1$. In an antipodal partial cube, an isometric cycle is principal exactly when its diameter, equivalently its isometric dimension, equals that of the graph, also exactly when its convex hull is the whole graph. For order $n$ and diameter $d$, equality $n=4d-4$ holds exactly for $C_4$ and prisms over even cycles. Every antipodal partial cube of girth greater than six is an even cycle; if a noncycle has diameter at least six, then its girth is smaller than its diameter.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                References:

                                                                [polat2020antipodal]

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/survey/main.tex?#thm:further-antipodal-structure

                                                                Low-Rank Simplicial Profile of Antipodal Partial Cubes

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Antipodal Partial Cubes

                                                                • VC Dimension
                                                                • Isometric Dimension

                                                                Result Type: Other

                                                                Statement:

                                                                If an antipodal partial cube has rank three, then every $\Theta$-class contains an edge incident with a vertex of degree three; consequently its minimum degree is at most its rank. The same degree bound has been verified computationally for every antipodal partial cube of isometric dimension at most seven.

                                                                Lawrence's Lopsided-Set Theorems

                                                                Name: Lawrence's Lopsided-Set Theorems

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Cube Complement
                                                                • Coordinate Conditioning
                                                                • Coordinate Projection
                                                                • Cartesian Product

                                                                Result Type: Other

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Closed orthants met by a convex subset of $\mathbb R^X$ form a lopsided, hence ample, sign family. Lopsided families are closed under complements, nonempty cube-face sections, coordinate projections, and Cartesian products. They are exactly the totally asymmetric sign families, and every nonempty face section has a connected induced graph.

                                                                Maximum-Class Unlabeled Compression and the Corner Boundary

                                                                Name: Maximum-Class Unlabeled Compression and the Corner Boundary

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Representation-Map Ample Classes

                                                                Result Type: Algorithm

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Every maximum class of VC dimension $d$ has a representation map and an unlabeled compression scheme of size $d$. On an ample class, representation maps are exactly the out-maps of unique-sink orientations and each yields an unlabeled scheme of size equal to the VC dimension. An ample class has a corner peeling exactly when it has an acyclic such orientation. Hall's 299-concept maximum class in dimension twelve has VC dimension three but no corner, showing that optimal unlabeled compression need not come from a corner peeling.

The same holds for every COM tope graph with a corner peeling, and hence for realizable COMs, rank-at-most-two COMs, hypercellular graphs, and cellular graphs.
