                                                                Relative Peeling Is Equivalent to an Inward USO Extension

                                                                Name: Relative Peeling Is Equivalent to an Inward USO Extension

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $T\subseteq H$ be nonempty ample classes and prescribe a unique-sink orientation $D_T$ on $T$. Then $H$ corner-peels to $T$ if and only if $D_T$ extends to a USO of $H$ whose boundary edges point into $T$ and whose orientation on $H\setminus T$ is acyclic. If $T$ is dismantlable ample, this is equivalent to an acyclic USO of $H$ with inward boundary at $T$, and every prescribed acyclic USO of $T$ extends.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Reverse a relative peeling and add each deleted corner back as a source. Its corner cube supplies the outgoing-cube condition, every old cube keeps its unique sink, and the new sources form an acyclic outside orientation with boundary directed into $T$. Conversely, repeatedly delete a source of the outside acyclic digraph. The inward boundary makes it a source of the remaining whole USO; the outgoing-cube condition makes it a corner, and the restricted representation map stays valid. Iteration deletes exactly $H\setminus T$. If the prescribed orientation of $T$ is acyclic, no directed cycle can cross the inward boundary.

                                                                References:

                                                                [ChalopiChepoiMoran22]

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#prop:damp-relative-uso-extension

                                                                Quadratic Orientation Score Detects Corner Peelings

                                                                Name: Quadratic Orientation Score Detects Corner Peelings

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Partial Cubes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Acyclic Orientation Square Defect

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For every acyclic orientation $O$ of a nonempty finite partial cube $H$, $\varepsilon_H(O)\geq0$. Equality holds exactly when every topological order of $O$ is a corner peeling; it then also follows that $H$ is ample. Thus $H$ is dismantlable ample exactly when $\mu(H)=0$, and $H$ peels to a prescribed vertex $a$ exactly when $\mu(H,a)=0$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The score is the number of outgoing edge pairs whose opposite square vertex is absent plus the number of contained squares having two sources. When it vanishes, the opposite vertex for every two-edge segment through the next vertex of a topological order survives later in the order. Replacing each such segment through the deleted vertex preserves distances, so every suffix is isometric and metric elimination yields a corner peeling and ampleness. A corner order has neither kind of defect. The rooted claim follows by requiring the last vertex to be the designated sink.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#prop:damp-quadratic-orientation-score

                                                                Protected Missing Cubes Force USO Cycles

                                                                Name: Protected Missing Cubes Force USO Cycles

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Result Type: Implication

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $H\subseteq Q_F$ be ample and $S\subseteq H$ have at least two vertices. Suppose that for every $x\in S$ there is a set $J_x\subseteq F$ such that every neighbor $x^{\{e\}}$ with $e\in J_x$ lies in $S$, while the opposite cube vertex $x^{J_x}$ is absent from $H$. Then every USO of $H$, if one exists, contains a directed cycle in $S$. Consequently $H$ is not dismantlable ample.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The outgoing-cube axiom prevents all directions in $J_x$ from pointing outward at $x$, because their joint flip is missing. Thus every vertex of the finite digraph induced by $S$ has an incoming neighbor in $S$. Following predecessors eventually repeats a vertex and produces a directed cycle. Dismantlable ampleness is equivalent to existence of an acyclic USO.

                                                                References:

                                                                [ChalopiChepoiMoran22]

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#prop:damp-protected-uso-cycle

                                                                Local Test for an Ample One-Concept Extension

                                                                Name: Local Test for an Ample One-Concept Extension

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Concept Deletion

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $S\subseteq Q_F$ be nonempty and ample, let $a\notin S$, and let $I=\{f:a^{\{f\}}\in S\}$. Then $S\cup\{a\}$ is ample exactly when $I\notin\operatorname{Sh}(S)$, equivalently when the extension is isometric, or when $\operatorname{Diff}(a,x)\cap I\ne\varnothing$ for every $x\in S$. The punctured $I$-cube around $a$ is automatically present in $S$. When the conditions hold, $a$ is a corner with unique maximal-cube support $I$, $\operatorname{Sh}(S\cup\{a\})=\operatorname{Sh}(S)\mathbin{\dot\cup}\{I\}$, and $I$ is a minimal nonface of $\operatorname{Sh}(S)$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Restrict $S$ to the face agreeing with $a$ outside $I$. Its cube complement is ample and connected, contains $a$, and contains none of its neighbors, so it is the singleton $\{a\}$; hence all other vertices of the $I$-face lie in $S$. The missing-support condition is therefore exactly the condition that every $x\in S$ has a shortest path from $a$ beginning with an $I$-edge. If the extension is ample, deleting $a$ between two ample classes makes $a$ a corner and removes exactly the shattered support $I$. Conversely the punctured cube strongly shatters $I$, so the Sandwich inequality and $|S|=|\operatorname{Sh}(S)|$ force equality for the extension. Parallel faces through neighbors of $a$ show that every proper subset of $I$ was already shattered.

                                                                References:

                                                                [ChalopiChepoiMoran22]

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#lem:damp-one-concept-extension-test

                                                                One-Concept Extensions of an Ample Forbidden Minor

                                                                Name: One-Concept Extensions of an Ample Forbidden Minor

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Concept Deletion
                                                                • Partial-Cube Minor

                                                                Result Type: Construction

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $S$ be an irredundantly embedded ample pc-minimal obstruction to dismantlable ampleness. Its ample one-concept extensions are in bijection with oriented punctured faces $(a,I)$ for which $a\notin S$, $I=I_S(a)$, every other vertex $a^U$ of that face lies in $S$, and $I\notin\operatorname{Sh}(S)$. Every such extension $E=S\cup\{a\}$ is either dismantlable ample or is itself an ample pc-minimal obstruction; the two outcomes partition the punctured-face atlas.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The local one-concept test gives the bijection and makes $a$ a corner of $E$. Under any elementary restriction or contraction, irredundancy makes the image of $S$ a proper pc-minor and hence dismantlable ample. The image of $E$ is either that same family or an ample one-concept extension of it; in the latter case the surviving new concept is a corner and may be peeled first. Thus every proper pc-minor of $E$ is dismantlable ample. If $E$ peels it is in the positive part; otherwise it is an ample pc-minimal obstruction.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#prop:damp-one-concept-atlas

                                                                Low-Support One-Concept Additions Preserve Every Relative Peeling

                                                                Name: Low-Support One-Concept Additions Preserve Every Relative Peeling

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Concept Deletion
                                                                • Full Reduction

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $S$ be nonempty and ample, and let $H=S\cup\{a\}$ be an ample one-concept extension whose acquired support $I_S(a)$ has size at most two. For every retained set $T\subseteq S$, including the empty set, $H$ corner-reduces to $T$ if and only if $S$ corner-reduces to $T$. Consequently $H$ is dismantlable ample exactly when $S$ is, and every old prescribed peeling endpoint is preserved. Any one-concept addition that makes a previously unreachable retained target reachable must acquire at least three directions.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                One direction deletes the new corner $a$ first. For the converse, take a smallest counterexample and let $z\ne a$ be the first deletion in a reduction of $H$. If $z$ is also a corner of $S$, delete it from both families and use minimality. Otherwise the unique maximal cube of $z$ in $H$ contains $a$ and equals the acquired cube. The two vertices cannot be adjacent, so the support has size two and $a,z$ are opposite vertices of a square with the same two neighbors. Swapping them is an automorphism fixing $T$ and transports the remaining reduction to one of $S$, a contradiction.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#prop:damp-rank-two-extension-invariance

                                                                Low-Degree Corners Descend within the Ample Forbidden Basis

                                                                Name: Low-Degree Corners Descend within the Ample Forbidden Basis

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Concept Deletion
                                                                • Partial-Cube Minor

                                                                Result Type: Implication

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $H$ be an irredundantly embedded ample pc-minimal obstruction to dismantlable ampleness. If $a$ is a corner of degree at most two, then $H\setminus\{a\}$ is again an irredundantly embedded ample pc-minimal obstruction. Hence, if no corner deletion remains in the ample forbidden basis, every corner has degree at least three.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Corner deletion leaves an ample family $S$, and low-support relative invariance keeps it nonpeelable. A coordinate constant on $S$ would make $S$ a proper signed restriction of $H$ and therefore peelable, so the embedding remains irredundant. Every elementary image of $H$ peels. Its corresponding image of $S$ is either identical or obtained by deleting a concept from an ample extension whose acquired support still has size at most two; low-support invariance therefore makes that image peel as well. Thus every proper pc-minor of $S$ is dismantlable ample.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#cor:damp-low-degree-corner-descent

                                                                Cut-Vertex Obstructions Are Wedges of Two Root-Critical Factors

                                                                Name: Cut-Vertex Obstructions Are Wedges of Two Root-Critical Factors

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • One-Point Amalgam
                                                                • Partial-Cube Minor

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                An ample family with a cut vertex is a pc-minimal obstruction to dismantlable ampleness exactly when it is the one-point amalgam of two rooted ample families $(A_i,a_i)$ such that each $A_i$ is dismantlable ample, does not peel to $a_i$, and every proper root-preserving pc-minor does peel to the image of $a_i$. Each factor has no cut vertex. The obstruction consequently has exactly two blocks and one cut vertex, and its rooted factors are unique up to interchange.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Isometry forces distinct components at a cut vertex to use disjoint coordinate blocks; each component together with the cut vertex is convex. Minimality puts all rooted component families in the positive class, while the exact wedge criterion requires at least two of them to fail rooted peeling. More than two components would leave a proper nonpeelable convex union, so exactly two remain. Applying any root-preserving elementary minor to one factor and keeping the other unchanged forces the changed factor to regain rooted peeling. Conversely these restoration conditions make every elementary image of the wedge peel. A further cut vertex inside a factor would split it into proper root-preserving pieces that all peel to their roots, contradicting the factor's rooted failure.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#thm:damp-cut-vertex-obstructions

                                                                Ample Assembly and USO Compatibility over a Coordinate Face

                                                                Name: Ample Assembly and USO Compatibility over a Coordinate Face

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Common-Section Gluing

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let nonempty $D\subseteq Q_E$ be the common zero section of ample pieces $A_i\subseteq Q_{E\mathbin{\dot\cup}F_i}$ with disjoint exclusive coordinate blocks, and put $X=\bigcup_iA_i$. Then $X$ is ample exactly when $\operatorname{Sh}(A_i)\cap\operatorname{Sh}(A_j)=\operatorname{Sh}(D)$ for every $i\ne j$; this is automatic when $D=Q_E$. Under this condition, USOs on the pieces glue exactly when they agree on $D$ and at every $d\in D$ at most one piece directs an edge from $d$ into its exclusive part. The glued USO is acyclic exactly when the union orientation is acyclic; acyclicity of the pieces alone suffices when $|D|\le2$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Every contained cube lies in one piece, so the strongly shattered supports of the union are the union of the piece shadows. Inclusion-exclusion and the Sandwich inequality give the exact pairwise shadow-intersection test. The same cube localization proves the unique-sink axiom piecewise. At a boundary vertex, outgoing directions in two private blocks would require a missing mixed square, while directions from at most one private block and the common face lie in one piece. A directed cycle crossing a singleton is impossible; over an edge it would combine the common directed edge with a reverse directed path inside one piece, contradicting that piece's acyclicity.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#prop:damp-uso-cube-gluing

                                                                Finite Boundary Records Decide Acyclic Gluing

                                                                Name: Finite Boundary Records Decide Acyclic Gluing

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Common-Section Gluing

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Assume the coordinate-face assembly shadow condition and let $k=|D|$. For a piece $A_i$, a boundary record consists of a total order $\sigma$ of $D$ and the set $S_i\subseteq D$ of boundary vertices having an outgoing edge into that piece's exclusive part in an acyclic USO whose topological order restricts to $\sigma$. The union is dismantlable ample exactly when the pieces admit records with one common order and pairwise disjoint outward sets. Inclusion-minimal outward sets suffice, and each piece has at most $k!2^k$ records before minimization, independently of its interior size.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Restrict an acyclic USO and one of its topological orders to every piece to obtain the common order and disjoint outward sets. Conversely, the common order makes the piece orientations agree on $D$, while disjointness supplies the USO compatibility condition. Split each piece's topological order into blocks before, between, and after successive boundary vertices, concatenate corresponding blocks across pieces, and insert each boundary vertex once; this is a topological order of the union. Replacing each outward set by a contained minimal attainable one preserves disjointness. Counting total orders and subsets gives the bound.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#cor:damp-finite-boundary-gluing

                                                                Boundary Records Have One-Sided Minor Transport

                                                                Name: Boundary Records Have One-Sided Minor Transport

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Coordinate Conditioning
                                                                • Coordinate Projection
                                                                • Common-Section Gluing

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let an ample piece $A$ over a full coordinate-face boundary $D$ have a corner order realizing boundary record $(\sigma,S)$, and let $f$ be an exclusive coordinate. Restriction to $f=0$ transports the order to a record $(\sigma,T)$ with $T\subseteq S$. Contraction in $f$, ordered by the last preimage in each fiber, gives $(\tau,T)$ with $T\subseteq S$; moreover, if $x\in D\setminus S$ precedes $y$ in $\sigma$, it still precedes $y$ in $\tau$. In particular, an empty outward set preserves the entire boundary order under contraction.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The order-level pc-minor proof transports both orders. Restriction retains boundary positions and can only remove outward edges. Under contraction, the later endpoint represents each double fiber. Any new outward boundary vertex either was already outward or used its exclusive mate as representative, which also certifies membership in $S$. For $d\notin S$, a present mate precedes $d$, so the last-preimage position remains the original position of $d$. This preserves every asserted precedence and, when $S$ is empty, all of $\sigma$.

                                                                References:

                                                                [ChalopiChepoiMoran22]

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#prop:damp-boundary-record-transport

                                                                Finite Gluing Record Algebra and Context Preorder

                                                                Name: Finite Gluing Record Algebra and Context Preorder

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Common-Section Gluing
                                                                • Coordinate Conditioning
                                                                • Coordinate Projection

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Fix a nonempty dismantlable ample boundary $D\subseteq Q_E$. A piece record stores (i) the supports in $2^E\setminus\operatorname{Sh}(D)$ additionally shattered by the piece, (ii) a corner order of $D$, and (iii) its outward boundary set. Formal record families multiply by requiring a common order and disjoint first and third coordinates, then taking their unions. This product is associative and commutative, with empty zero and the records of $D$ as identity; the record family of a gluing is the product, and the gluing is ample and dismantlable exactly when it is nonempty. Realizable record families together with zero form a finite monoid. Comparing two families by whether every realizable context compatible with the first is compatible with the second defines a product-compatible preorder; mutual comparison yields a partially ordered commutative quotient monoid of at most $2^{|\Omega_D|}$ classes. Private contractions and zero-side restrictions that preserve the marked boundary move monotonically upward in this preorder, and the move is strict modulo equivalence when it is a proper minor of a forbidden glued family.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The extra shattered-support coordinate enforces the exact ampleness criterion, while the common order and disjoint outward sets enforce the acyclic-USO gluing criterion. For three factors these are simply pairwise-disjointness conditions followed by set union, independent of parenthesization, which proves the monoid laws. The identity is realized by $D$, and gluing realizes every nonzero product, so the realized submonoid is finite. Compatibility against all realized contexts is reflexive, transitive, and preserved by multiplication. Applying a private minor inside any glued context preserves positive membership, proving monotonicity. If the original union is forbidden and the minor is proper, the unchanged opposite piece distinguishes the reverse comparison, proving strictness.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#thm:damp-finite-gluing-algebra

                                                                Piece Bound at a Separating Cube

                                                                Name: Piece Bound at a Separating Cube

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Common-Section Gluing
                                                                • Coordinate Conditioning

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let ample pieces $A_1,\ldots,A_m$ contain a common cube $D=Q_E$ and otherwise use pairwise disjoint coordinate blocks. Their union is ample. If the union is dismantlable ample, at most $|D|$ pieces fail to peel to $D$. If an ample pc-minimal obstruction has a specified separating $k$-cube $D$, the components of its complement uniquely recover pieces $A_i$ that are proper convex restrictions, are dismantlable ample, and all fail to peel to $D$; moreover $2\le m\le |D|+1=2^k+1$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Every cube of the union lies in one piece, and the piece shadows meet in the full shadow of $D$, so the Sandwich equality proves ampleness. In an acyclic USO, every piece failing to peel to $D$ needs an outward edge at some boundary vertex, while compatibility permits at most one such piece per vertex of $D$; this gives the positive bound. For a forbidden family, the components outside $D$ use disjoint coordinate blocks and adjoining $D$ gives proper convex restrictions, hence positive pieces. Each must fail relative peeling or the whole obstruction could peel. If more than $|D|+1$ pieces occurred, deleting one piece would leave a proper union with more than $|D|$ relative failures and hence a nonpeelable proper minor. The components make the decomposition unique.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#thm:damp-cube-separator-bound

                                                                Piece Bound at an Arbitrary Coordinate Face

                                                                Name: Piece Bound at an Arbitrary Coordinate Face

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Common-Section Gluing
                                                                • Coordinate Conditioning

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $X$ be ample and $D$ a nonempty coordinate-face intersection. The components $W_i$ of $X\setminus D$ use disjoint exclusive coordinate blocks, and every piece $A_i=D\cup W_i$, as well as every union of selected pieces, is a coordinate restriction of $X$. If $X$ is dismantlable ample, at most $|D|$ pieces fail to peel to $D$. If $X$ is a pc-minimal obstruction and at least two components occur, every piece is dismantlable ample, none peels to $D$, and $2\le m\le |D|+1$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                A coordinate cannot vary outside $D$ in two components: a shortest path between opposite-side witnesses would pass through $D$ and repeat that coordinate. Fixing all blocks except a selected collection to their values on $D$ gives exactly the corresponding union, proving that these are coordinate restrictions. Restrict an acyclic USO of $X$ to the pieces; each relative failure needs a distinct outward boundary vertex, giving the $|D|$ bound. In a forbidden family every proper selected union is positive. A piece that peeled to $D$ could be removed first, contradicting minimal nonpeelability, and the same deletion argument as for a cube gives the $|D|+1$ obstruction bound.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#prop:damp-face-separator-bound

                                                                Projection and Gating of Coordinate-Face Pieces

                                                                Name: Projection and Gating of Coordinate-Face Pieces

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Coordinate Projection
                                                                • Common-Section Gluing

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                In the coordinate-face decomposition of a nontrivial ample family, project onto the free coordinates $E$ of the common face $D$. If $B$ is the image of the whole family and $C_i$ the images of its pieces, then all are ample, $B=\bigcup_iC_i$, distinct $C_i$ meet exactly in $D$, and no edge joins their parts outside $D$. Thus each $C_i\setminus D$ is a union of components of $B\setminus D$. If every coordinate of $E$ varies on $D$, then $D$ is gated in the original piece $A_i$ exactly when $C_i=D$; hence the number of nongated pieces is at most the number of components of $B\setminus D$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Coordinate projections preserve ampleness and the component-block decomposition. A projected vertex outside $D$ retains a witness in one exclusive component; witnesses from two components cannot coincide or be adjacent without giving a path outside $D$ between those components. If $C_i=D$, projection of any vertex of $A_i$ lies in $D$ and is its unique metric gate. Conversely, a gate of $x$ in $D$ must equal its projection: variation of every free coordinate on $D$ would otherwise produce a route violating the gate equality in the Hamming metric. Distinct nongated pieces therefore occupy disjoint projected components.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#prop:damp-face-piece-projections

                                                                Exact Peeling Criterion for Gluing along an Edge

                                                                Name: Exact Peeling Criterion for Gluing along an Edge

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Marked-Edge Peeling Profile

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Common-Section Gluing

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let dismantlable ample pieces $A_1,\ldots,A_m$ have disjoint exclusive coordinate blocks and common edge $D$. Let $I=\{i:r_D(A_i)=0\}$ be the pieces that fail to peel to the edge. Their union is dismantlable ample exactly when either $|I|\le1$, or $I=\{i,j\}$ and the two exceptional edge profiles are endpoint-compatible: for some ordering $(s,t)$ of $D$, one piece can peel to sink $t$ and the other can first delete $s$ as a leaf, in either assignment.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Orient the common edge in an acyclic USO of the union. Each relative-failing piece needs an outgoing exclusive edge at an endpoint, and USO compatibility permits at most one such piece at each endpoint, so there are at most two. With two, the piece active at the tail must have the head as a sink, while the piece active at the head must delete the tail as a leaf, giving the profile compatibility. Conversely, pieces peeling to $D$ extend either edge orientation with inward boundary. Use the exceptional piece's orientation when there is one, or the compatible sink/leaf witnesses when there are two; the coordinate-face gluing theorem then supplies an acyclic USO of the union.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#thm:damp-edge-gluing-profile

                                                                Six Contexts Determine Every Edge-Gluing Type

                                                                Name: Six Contexts Determine Every Edge-Gluing Type

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Marked-Edge Peeling Profile

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Common-Section Gluing

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For a fixed ordered edge, context equivalence has at most eighteen types: zero for a nonpeelable piece, identity for a piece peeling to the edge, and one type $[p]$ for each realized four-bit endpoint vector $p=(t_u,t_v,\ell_u,\ell_v)$ of a peelable piece with $r_D=0$. Two pieces are context-equivalent exactly when these types agree. On realized vector types, the context preorder is coordinatewise order, with zero strictly below every vector type and identity strictly above. The product of $[p]$ and $[q]$ is the all-zero vector type when one sink entry is paired with the opposite leaf entry across the factors, and is zero otherwise; every product of three vector types is zero. The edge, the all-zero vector piece, and four unit-vector pieces distinguish all types and comparisons.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The exact edge-gluing criterion gives the Boolean product rule. A positive union of two relative-failing pieces has no attainable sink or leaf exit: either condition would force both pieces to use the other endpoint outward, violating compatibility. Hence every positive vector product is the all-zero vector, whose product with any vector is zero. Four realized unit profiles test the four dual coordinates; endpoint reversals supply all of them. The edge separates zero from positive types, while the all-zero vector piece separates identity from vector types. Coordinatewise dominance is sufficient against every context by the Boolean formula and necessary by the unit tests.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#cor:damp-edge-context-algebra

                                                                Exact Classification of Obstructions with a Separating Edge

                                                                Name: Exact Classification of Obstructions with a Separating Edge

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Marked-Edge Peeling Profile

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Common-Section Gluing
                                                                • Partial-Cube Minor

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let irredundantly embedded ample pieces with connected nonempty exclusive parts share an edge $D$, and let $X$ be their union. Then $X$ is a pc-minimal obstruction to dismantlable ampleness exactly when: (1) there are two or three pieces, every piece is dismantlable ample, and none peels to $D$; (2) two pieces are mutually incompatible, while with three pieces every pair is compatible; (3) every zero-side restriction or contraction in an exclusive coordinate either makes the changed piece peel to $D$ or, in the two-piece case, makes it compatible with the unchanged piece, whereas in the three-piece case it must peel to $D$; and (4) in each shared-coordinate restriction or contraction, at most one image fails to peel to the resulting singleton. Every obstruction with a specified separating edge arises uniquely this way, and the union is two-connected exactly when every piece is two-connected.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The separating-cube bound gives two or three positive relative-failing pieces. The edge-gluing criterion makes a two-piece obstruction incompatible, while every proper two-piece subunion of a three-piece obstruction must be compatible. Exclusive-coordinate minor minimality is exactly the stated edge-profile alternative; shared-coordinate images reduce to the one-point-amalgam criterion. Conversely these conditions make the original union nonpeelable and every elementary image peelable. Components outside the marked edge recover the pieces and their coordinate blocks. Deleting a vertex disconnects the union exactly when it disconnects one piece away from the still-shared endpoint or edge.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#thm:damp-edge-separator-obstructions

                                                                Crossing Graphs Detect and Recover Vertex and Edge Separators

                                                                Name: Crossing Graphs Detect and Recover Vertex and Edge Separators

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Partial Cubes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Crossing Graph

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Coordinate Projection

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For an irredundant partial cube $H\subseteq Q_F$ with $|F|\ge3$, $H$ has a cut vertex exactly when its crossing graph is disconnected. If $H$ is two-connected, separating edges of direction $e$ are exactly the full fibers over cut vertices of the contraction $\pi_eH$, and such an edge exists exactly when deleting $e$ disconnects the crossing graph. If that deletion has exactly two components $F_1,F_2$, there is exactly one separating $e$-edge; adjoining it to the two components of its complement yields convex coordinate restrictions with exclusive blocks $F_1,F_2$. Consequently an ample pc-minimal obstruction has neither a cut vertex nor a separating edge exactly when its crossing graph is two-connected.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The cut-vertex/crossing-graph theorem applies to $H$ and its contraction, whose crossing graph is obtained by deleting $e$. Fibers of the contraction are connected singletons or $e$-edges, every projected edge lifts, and this remains true after deleting one fiber; hence complement components correspond. Two-connectedness rules out a singleton cut fiber, proving the edge characterization. Crossing-graph components are the coordinate sets of graph blocks: blocks are convex, a coordinate cannot occur in two blocks, and coordinates in distinct blocks do not cross. Two crossing components after deleting $e$ therefore give two quotient blocks at one cut vertex and lift to one separating edge with the claimed convex pieces.

                                                                References:

                                                                [klavzar2002partial]

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#prop:damp-crossing-separator-recovery

                                                                A Two-Component Shadow Split Determines an Edge Factorization

                                                                Name: A Two-Component Shadow Split Determines an Edge Factorization

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Crossing Graph

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Common-Section Gluing
                                                                • Coordinate Projection

                                                                Result Type: Construction

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let a simplicial complex $\Sigma\subseteq2^F$ contain every singleton and have connected two-face graph. If deleting coordinate $e$ leaves exactly two graph components $F_1,F_2$, put $\Sigma_i=\Sigma\cap2^{F_i\cup\{e\}}$. Every ample realization of $\Sigma$ is obtained by choosing ample realizations of the two $\Sigma_i$, choosing and identifying oriented $e$-edges, embedding their exclusive blocks disjointly, and applying a cube translation. Every output has one separating $e$-edge, which recovers the two convex pieces up to interchange and simultaneous edge reversal. The pc-minimal obstructions among these realizations are exactly the two-piece data satisfying the separating-edge obstruction criterion.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                No face of $\Sigma$ meets both exclusive blocks, so the two subcomplexes meet only in the empty face and $\{e\}$. The edge-glued realization has shadow $\Sigma$ and cardinality $|\Sigma|$, hence is ample. Connectivity of the two subgraphs makes each piece two-connected and its complement of the chosen edge connected; crossing-graph separator recovery then makes the identified edge unique. Conversely, that theorem recovers the edge and its convex blocks from any realization. Projection onto each block plus $e$ recovers a realization of $\Sigma_i$, and normalizing the edge recovers the construction up to the stated symmetries.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                Rooted Failure Transfers to an Exact Edge Profile

                                                                Name: Rooted Failure Transfers to an Exact Edge Profile

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Marked-Edge Peeling Profile

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Coordinate Fiber Product

                                                                Result Type: Construction

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $0\in C\subseteq A,B$ be ample, with $A\cap B=C$, ample union, and $\operatorname{Sh}(A)\cap\operatorname{Sh}(B)=\operatorname{Sh}(C)$. Suppose $C$ is dismantlable ample, both wings peel to $C$, and both admit acyclic USOs with sink $0$. For a fresh coordinate, form the two-layer family $L=(A\times\{0\})\cup(B\times\{1\})$ and mark the vertical edge $D$ over $0$. Then $L$ is ample and its edge profile is $(p,1,1,p,p)$, where $p=1$ exactly when $C$ peels to $0$. Thus when rooted peeling of $C$ fails, either endpoint of $D$ is an attainable sink, but the edge cannot be retained and neither endpoint can be deleted first as a leaf.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Supports avoiding the new coordinate are counted by the ample union, while supports containing it correspond exactly to the common shadow of $A$ and $B$, proving ampleness. Clearing one wing relative to $C$, then its copy of $C$, and finishing in the other wing gives either endpoint as a sink. If $C$ peels to $0$, clear both wings and lift that rooted order to retain $D$ or exit through either leaf. Conversely, in any retention or leaf-exit peeling, record the moment when each full vertical fiber first breaks. The projected corner cubes give a corner reduction of $C$ to $0$; connectivity handles the leaf-exit terminal state. Hence each of the other three profile entries equals the rooted-peeling bit $p$.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#prop:damp-edge-boundary-transfer

                                                                Relative Peeling Obstructions at Cube Boundaries of Every Dimension

                                                                Name: Relative Peeling Obstructions at Cube Boundaries of Every Dimension

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Coordinate Fiber Product
                                                                • Coordinate Conditioning
                                                                • Coordinate Projection
                                                                • Partial-Cube Minor

                                                                Result Type: Construction

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $0\in C\subseteq A,B$ satisfy the hypotheses of the rooted-failure edge transfer: $C$ is dismantlable ample, the two ample wings peel both to $C$ and to $0$, and $A\cap B=C$ with matching shadow intersection. For a fresh $k$-set $E$, put $R_A=Q_E\setminus\{1^E\}$, $R_B=Q_E\setminus\{0^E\}$, $D_k=\{0\}\times Q_E$, and $Y_k=(C\times Q_E)\cup((A\setminus C)\times R_A)\cup((B\setminus C)\times R_B)$. Then $Y_k$ is ample and dismantlable ample. It peels to every nonempty proper face of $D_k$ and to each punctured boundary cube $\{0\}\times R_A,\{0\}\times R_B$; for $k=2$ it peels to every nonempty proper ample subfamily of $D_2$, including all four punctured squares. It peels to $D_k$ exactly when $C$ peels to $0$. If $(C,0)$ is a rooted factor using every old coordinate, every proper pc-minor of the marked pair $(Y_k,D_k)$ with nonempty target peels to its target, although the original pair does not. Certified inputs of orders $289,291,290$ yield $|Y_k|=292\cdot2^k-3$ and isometric dimension $12+k$ for every $k\ge1$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Supports using a proper subset of the new coordinates are shattered exactly according to $A\cup B$, while supports using all of $E$ are shattered exactly according to $C$. The resulting shadow count equals $(2^k-1)|A\cup B|+|C|=|Y_k|$, proving ampleness. Relative wing orders clear the two punctured-cube rows to $C\times Q_E$, so the family is peelable. A peeling retaining the whole boundary cube would record first losses of complete $E$-fibers and project to a peeling of $C$ ending at $0$; conversely such a rooted peeling lifts. Every proper face avoids one puncture, allowing one wing and then the core to be cleared to that face. To retain $R_A$, clear the opposite wing, delete the missing row copy of each core vertex in a core peeling, and finish in $A\times R_A$; symmetry gives $R_B$. When $k=2$, the two remaining punctures are handled by clearing both repairs in the punctured middle row, deleting its core, and peeling the resulting three-row path from its outer rows inward. Root-preserving old-coordinate minors make the core peel to its root, new-coordinate restrictions invoke proper-face retention, and new-coordinate contractions produce $(A\cup B)\times Q_{E\setminus\{e\}}$; these observations prove relative pc-minimality. The size formula follows by substitution.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#thm:damp-cube-boundary-retention

                                                                Rooted Failure Gives an Edge Compatibility Test and Forbidden Double

                                                                Name: Rooted Failure Gives an Edge Compatibility Test and Forbidden Double

                                                                • Ample Classes

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $L$ be the rooted-failure transfer piece with marked edge $D=\{u,v\}$ and profile $(0,1,1,0,0)$. If the core of $L$ is a rooted factor using every old coordinate, gluing two private-coordinate-disjoint copies of $L$ along $D$ produces an ample pc-minimal obstruction to dismantlable ampleness of order $2(|A|+|B|)-2$. The certified $581$-concept piece therefore gives a forbidden double of order $1160$.

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Substituting the profile of $L$ into the exact edge-gluing criterion gives the three-term compatibility test and makes two copies incompatible. A proper private-coordinate minor retaining $D$ turns the corresponding rooted core into a root-peelable minor, so that copy now peels to $D$ and the union becomes peelable. A private restriction discarding $D$ leaves a positive minor of one copy. Either shared-coordinate restriction and the shared-coordinate contraction give two pieces with an attainable common root, so the one-point-amalgam criterion makes those images peelable. Hence every proper elementary pc-minor is dismantlable ample while the original double is not.

                                                                Rooted Factors Are Exactly Minimal Zero-Context Prisms

                                                                Name: Rooted Factors Are Exactly Minimal Zero-Context Prisms

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For a dismantlable ample family $C$ with marked vertex $a$, form the prism $P=C\times Q_1$ and mark the vertical edge $D=\{a\}\times Q_1$. If $h=1$ exactly when $C$ peels to $a$, then every entry of the marked-edge profile of $P$ equals $h$. Consequently $(C,a)$ is a rooted factor exactly when $P$ has positive zero-vector context type and every proper elementary private-coordinate minor retaining $D$ peels to $D$. Conversely, restricting any witness for retention, a sink, or a leaf exit to the appropriate horizontal section gives a peeling of $C$ ending at $a$, proving the all-$h$ profile. Private minors of the prism are prisms over the corresponding rooted minors of $C$, so their retention condition is exactly rooted minimality. The fixed second piece fails edge retention but attains both endpoint sinks and becomes relatively peelable after every proper private minor. Product-attachment minimality then makes the glued family forbidden, and counting the vertices gives $581+2(|C|-1)$.

                                                                Marked-Edge Peeling Conditions Survive Edge-Retaining pc-Minors

                                                                Name: Marked-Edge Peeling Conditions Survive Edge-Retaining pc-Minors

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $D=\{u,v\}$ be an edge of an ample family. Under any coordinate-face intersection containing both endpoints, or any contraction in a coordinate other than the direction of $D$, each true entry among $r_D,t_u,t_v,\ell_u,\ell_v$ remains true for the image edge. The same holds for every sequence of such edge-retaining pc-minor operations.

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Apply the operation to all residual families of a witnessing peeling and omit repeated images. Face intersections filter the order, while contractions record a word when its last lift disappears, preserving retention and sink endpoints. For a leaf exit, a face intersection preserves the leaf directly. Under contraction, no new quotient neighbor outside the marked-edge direction can appear: otherwise a lift at distance two from the leaf would have both intermediate vertices absent, contradicting isometry of the ample residual family. The marked neighbor persists, so the image is again the first endpoint deleted as a leaf. Iteration proves the sequence form.

                                                                Exact Existence Criterion for Three-Piece Separating-Edge Obstructions

                                                                Name: Exact Existence Criterion for Three-Piece Separating-Edge Obstructions

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Marked-Edge Peeling Profile

                                                                Statement:

                                                                An ample pc-minimal obstruction to dismantlable ampleness with a separating edge whose deletion leaves exactly three connected components exists if and only if some dismantlable ample marked-edge piece $K$ satisfies $r_D(K)=0$, has at least one attainable endpoint sink, and has at least one attainable endpoint leaf exit. The sink and leaf may be witnessed by different acyclic USOs and may occur at the same or opposite endpoints; no minimality or connectivity hypothesis on $K\setminus D$ is required.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                In a three-piece obstruction, the exact separator classification gives three relative-failing pieces that are pairwise compatible. If no one piece had both a sink entry and a leaf entry, sink-only and leaf-only pieces would form two groups and three pieces could not be pairwise compatible. Conversely, take an edge-retaining minor $K_0$ minimal subject to failure of retention. Profile transport preserves the positive sink and leaf entries, and minimality makes $K_0\setminus D$ connected and every proper private minor relatively peelable. If an opposite-endpoint sink/leaf pair occurs, three copies of $K_0$ are pairwise compatible but jointly nonpeelable. For a same-endpoint pair, use $K_0$, its endpoint reversal, and the fixed $(0,1,1,0,0)$ piece. In either construction, the separator criterion and the one-point-amalgam criterion verify every private and shared-coordinate proper minor, producing the required three-component pc-minimal obstruction.

                                                                A Repair inside a Proper Face Produces a Rooted Factor or Mixed Edge Profile

                                                                Name: A Repair inside a Proper Face Produces a Rooted Factor or Mixed Edge Profile

                                                                • Ample Classes

                                                                • Coordinate Projection
                                                                • Partial-Cube Minor

                                                                Result Type: Construction

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $(C,0)$ be a rooted factor on active coordinates, with $0$ its only corner. Suppose $c\notin C$ is a one-concept ample addition whose acquired cube lies in a proper root face $Q_J(0)$ and $C\cup\{c\}$ peels to $0$. Put $B=C\cap Q_J(0)$, $T=B\cup\{c\}$, $K=(T\times\{0\})\cup(C\times\{1\})$, and mark the edge $D$ over $0$. Then $K$ is ample and dismantlable ample, with $r_D=t_v=\ell_v=0$ and $\ell_u=1$. Every proper rooted pc-minor of $(K,u)$ peels to its root, and every proper old-coordinate elementary image retaining $D$ peels to $D$. Hence either $(K,u)$ is a rooted factor or $K$ has profile $(0,1,0,1,0)$. If the chosen face omits a neighbor of $0$ in $C$, the first alternative necessarily holds. The certified $289$-concept input gives a $308$-concept rooted factor of dimension $13$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The added concept contributes exactly its acquired support beyond the shadow of $B$, while the two section shadows meet in $\operatorname{Sh}(B)$; shadow counting proves ampleness. Delete the repaired lower concept, peel the remaining lower face to its root, delete $u$ as a leaf, and peel the upper copy of $C$, proving positivity and $\ell_u=1$. Any retention, upper-end sink, or upper-end leaf witness would restrict to a forbidden rooted peeling of the upper $C$, so the other three displayed entries vanish. Rooted minimality makes both images of $C$ and $B$ peel after every proper old-coordinate operation; any surviving repair is then a corner, yielding edge retention. The new-coordinate face and contraction are respectively $T$ and $C\cup\{c\}$ and peel to the root, proving all rooted-minor tests. If the face omits a root neighbor, the first deletion in the upper shore of a hypothetical sink-$u$ order must project to the unique corner $0$, but its vertical vertex then has an incomplete incident square with that omitted neighbor. Thus $u$ is not an attainable sink and the output is rooted-critical.

                                                                A Certified Three-Piece Separating-Edge Obstruction

                                                                Name: A Certified Three-Piece Separating-Edge Obstruction

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Marked-Edge Peeling Profile

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Common-Section Gluing
                                                                • Partial-Cube Minor

                                                                Result Type: Construction

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For the fixed $289$-concept rooted factor $C$, repair $c=290$ inside the face on $J=\{1,2,5,6,7,8\}$ and form the marked two-layer piece $K$. Then $|T|=41$, $|K|=330$, $K\setminus D$ is connected, and the exact edge profile is $(0,1,0,1,0)$. Every proper old-coordinate elementary image retaining $D$ peels to $D$. Gluing $K$, an endpoint-reversed copy of $K$, and the fixed $581$-concept piece of profile $(0,1,1,0,0)$ along their common edge produces an ample pc-minimal obstruction to dismantlable ampleness with $1237$ concepts and isometric dimension $37$. Deleting the edge leaves exactly three components, and every nonempty-coordinate reduction is dismantlable ample.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The repaired-face theorem supplies ampleness, positivity, the three zero entries, $\ell_u=1$, and all private-minor retention tests. A stored complete corner order ending at $u$, independently certified by its nonclashing out-map, supplies $t_u=1$. Relative minimality forces $K\setminus D$ to be connected, since otherwise its proper convex pieces would each peel to $D$ and their orders would concatenate. The three profiles are pairwise compatible but all fail retention, so the exact three-piece separator construction gives a nonpeelable union whose every proper pc-minor peels. Counting the shared edge gives $330+330+581-4=1237$ and the disjoint private blocks give dimension $37$. Private-coordinate reductions are positive by closure; the common-edge reduction is a one-point amalgam of two rooted-positive copies of the repaired face and the positive core, so it is positive as well.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                Arbitrary Rooted Factors Occur as Peripheral Third Pieces

                                                                Name: Arbitrary Rooted Factors Occur as Peripheral Third Pieces

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Marked-Edge Peeling Profile

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Coordinate Fiber Product
                                                                • Common-Section Gluing
                                                                • Partial-Cube Minor

                                                                Result Type: Construction

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $K,L$ be the fixed $330$- and $581$-concept edge pieces and let $Y=K\cup_D L$. Then $(Y,u)$ is a $909$-concept rooted factor. For any rooted factor $(R,0)$ on active coordinates $F$ and any nonempty ample $S\subseteq R$ peeling to $0$, put $P_{R,S}=(R\times\{0\})\cup(S\times\{1\})$ and glue it to $Y$ along the edge over $0$. The result is an ample pc-minimal obstruction of order $|R|+|S|+907$ and dimension $|F|+25$. Its edge deletion has three canonical components, with $P_{R,S}$ the unique piece having nested edge sections. Every nonempty-coordinate reduction is dismantlable ample, and the result is two-connected exactly when $|S|>1$. Taking the standard $289$-concept factor and an incident edge for $S$ gives a two-connected $1198$-concept example in dimension $37$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The profiles of $K$ and $L$ are compatible, so their union is positive, while the edge-context product has all four endpoint sink and leaf entries zero and cannot peel to $u$. A private minor makes its changed piece retain $D$, after which the unchanged piece supplies a sink-$u$ order; shared-coordinate images are rooted-positive one-point amalgams. Thus every proper rooted minor peels and $(Y,u)$ is a rooted factor. Rooted two-block completion applied to $(Y,u)$, $(R,0)$ and site $S$ gives the stated forbidden family and connectivity criterion. The three private blocks are disjoint and the complements of $D$ in all three pieces are connected, so they are exactly the edge-complement components. The peripheral piece has profile $(0,0,0,0,1)$ and is the only one with nested shores. Separator descent makes every nonempty-coordinate reduction positive. The order and dimension formulas follow by subtracting the two duplicated endpoints.
