                                                                Exact Six-Component Trace Selector for the Three-Piece Obstruction

                                                                Name: Exact Six-Component Trace Selector for the Three-Piece Obstruction

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Coordinate Projection
                                                                • Coordinate Conditioning
                                                                • Coordinate Fiber Product

                                                                Result Type: Other

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For the $1237$-concept obstruction $X$, let $A=\pi_0X$ and $C=X^0$. Then $|A|=870$, $|C|=367$, both are dismantlable ample, and the six components of $A\setminus C$ have sizes $249,1,249,1,2,1$. For $t\in\{0,1\}^6$, lift component $i$ to shore $t_i$ while retaining both shores over $C$, obtaining an ample family $X_t$. The label $001100$ is dismantlable ample while $100000$ and $001000$ are not, so the positive label set is not a union of equality spaces of partitions with at most one nonsingleton block. Within this fixed pair, pc-minimal obstructions satisfy the exact selector $t_0\ne t_1$, $t_2\ne t_3$, $t_4\ne t_5$, and $t_1\ne t_3$; its four outputs are all isomorphic to $X$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The component sizes are recovered from the three edge pieces. Explicit relative orders make $001100$ a union of peripheral positive expansions. For each negative control, a protected set of $155$ vertices has the property that every member retains two neighbors while the completing square vertex is absent, so the first protected deletion could not be a corner. If either of the first two component pairs has equal labels, its $330$-piece retains the common edge; if their singleton labels agree, a proper shore contains two rooted-failing $289$-pieces. Once those pairs are mixed, equality of the last pair similarly creates a proper negative rooted shore. These arguments prove necessity of all four inequalities. The four satisfying labels arise from the original obstruction by reversing the common coordinate and exchanging its first two private blocks, proving sufficiency and isomorphism. The three exhibited labels then rule out every proposed one-block equality-space union.

                                                                Minor-Admissible Trace Positivity Is Disjunctive and Nonaffine

                                                                Name: Minor-Admissible Trace Positivity Is Disjunctive and Nonaffine

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Partial-Cube Minor
                                                                • Coordinate Fiber Product

                                                                Result Type: Other

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For the fixed six-component pair $(A,C)$ from the three-piece trace selector, let $M$ be the labels whose every elementary proper pc-minor is dismantlable ample. No affine subspace $L\subseteq\mathbb F_2^6$ satisfies $X_t\in\mathsf{Damp}$ exactly when $t\in L$ for all $t\in M$; in particular no single partition-equality condition works on this domain. Instead, for $t\in M$, positivity is exactly $(t_0=t_1)\lor(t_2=t_3)\lor(t_4=t_5)\lor(t_1=t_3)$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The positive labels $010000$, $111010$, $110000$, $000000$, and $111111$ all lie in $M$ by explicit orders and minor closure. Any affine classifier containing $000000$ is linear and, if it contains the other four, must also contain their sum $100101$, which is the original forbidden labeling and also lies in $M$. This contradiction proves nonaffinity. Every negative member of $M$ is pc-minimal by definition and minor closure, so negating the exact four-inequality forbidden selector yields the displayed four-equality disjunction.

                                                                Rooted Ample Completion Transfers Exactly between Two Blocks

                                                                Name: Rooted Ample Completion Transfers Exactly between Two Blocks

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Marked-Edge Peeling Profile

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Peripheral Expansion
                                                                • Common-Section Gluing
                                                                • Partial-Cube Minor

                                                                Result Type: Construction

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $Y\subseteq Q_F$ and $C\subseteq Q_G$ be irredundantly embedded ample families on disjoint coordinates, both containing $0$, let $v$ be a neighbor of $0$ in $Y$, and let $K\subseteq C$ be a nonempty ample subfamily containing $0$ that peels to $0$. Put $B=C\cup(v+K)$ and $X=Y\cup B$, with common edge $D=\{0,v\}$. Then $X$ is ample and is a pc-minimal obstruction to dismantlable ampleness exactly when $(Y,0)$ and $(C,0)$ are rooted factors. The parameters are uniquely recovered from $X$ by its two coordinate blocks and upper site. Under these equivalent conditions, $X$ is two-connected exactly when $|K|>1$, and $|X|=|Y|+|C|+|K|-2$. If both factors have minimum degree at least three and $K$ is a cube of dimension at least two, then $X$ also has minimum degree at least three and is its own graph three-core.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The family $B$ is the peripheral expansion of $C$ at site $K$, and an edge-amalgam shadow count proves ampleness of $X$. Clearing the upper site reduces $X$ to the one-point union $Y\vee C$, giving the exact peeling identity: $X$ peels precisely when both factors peel ordinarily and at least one peels to the root. When neither root is attainable, $B$ has profile $(0,0,0,0,1)$ and is incompatible with $Y$, proving nonpeelability. Applying each elementary pc-minor to this identity shows that forbiddenness is equivalent to rooted minimality of both inputs; opposite-side restrictions are handled by peripheral-expansion closure. The coordinate blocks and site are direct intersections of $X$, proving recovery. A singleton site leaves the common root as a cut vertex, while a larger connected upper site supplies two attachments through every deletion, proving the connectivity criterion. The degree and order formulas follow directly from the construction.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                Corner Descent Is Exact in the Cut-Vertex Obstruction Branch

                                                                Name: Corner Descent Is Exact in the Cut-Vertex Obstruction Branch

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Concept Deletion
                                                                • One-Point Amalgam
                                                                • Partial-Cube Minor

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let an ample pc-minimal obstruction with cut vertex be the one-point amalgam $X=A_1\vee A_2$ at root $a$. For any nonroot corner $x$ of one factor, $X\setminus\{x\}$ is again a pc-minimal obstruction exactly when the rooted pair $(A_i\setminus\{x\},a)$ remains a rooted factor. Consequently a cornered obstruction in this branch is terminal under obstruction-preserving corner deletion exactly when one rooted factor has a nonroot corner but none of its nonroot corner deletions remains a rooted factor.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The corners of the amalgam are exactly the nonroot corners of its two factors: the root has incident directions in both blocks without the mixed square. Deleting such a corner preserves ampleness and the cut vertex. The cut-vertex classification then makes obstruction status equivalent to the rooted-factor conditions on the changed branch; failure to peel to the root is automatic, since otherwise prefixing the deleted corner would root-peel the original factor. For terminality, one direction reads this criterion inside a terminal obstruction. Conversely, glue a rooted factor with the stated deletion property to a known rooted factor whose only corner is its root; every corner then belongs to the first branch and every deletion fails the criterion.

                                                                Every Dismantlable-Ample Obstruction Is Periphery-Free

                                                                Name: Every Dismantlable-Ample Obstruction Is Periphery-Free

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes
                                                                • Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Peripheral Expansion
                                                                • Partial-Cube Minor

                                                                Result Type: Implication

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Every pc-minimal obstruction to dismantlable ampleness has no peripheral coordinate. Consequently every such obstruction other than the nonample families $Q_n^{--}$ for $n\ge3$ is ample, periphery-free, and Cartesian-prime.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                If a coordinate were peripheral, orient it so the obstruction were $(B\times\{0\})\cup(S\times\{1\})$ with $S\subseteq B$. Its contraction base $B$ and duplicated site $S$ are proper pc-minors and hence dismantlable ample. The exact peripheral-expansion criterion would then make the whole family dismantlable ample, a contradiction. The known nonample obstruction layer and the product-prime lemma give the remaining conclusions.

                                                                Every Ample Obstruction Has a Canonical Graph Three-Core

                                                                Name: Every Ample Obstruction Has a Canonical Graph Three-Core

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Shattered Complex

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Concept Deletion
                                                                • Partial-Cube Minor

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                In an ample pc-minimal obstruction to dismantlable ampleness, every degree-two vertex is a corner. Repeatedly deleting vertices of degree below three, in any order, performs only degree-two corner deletions and ends at a nonempty ample pc-minimal obstruction $K$. This $K$ is the unique largest induced subgraph of minimum degree at least three, independent of all choices. The original family and $K$ have the same active coordinates, the same shattered supports of size at least three, and the same VC dimension. Conversely, the original family is recovered from $K$ by ample one-concept square completions, and every such sequence from any minimum-degree-three ample obstruction preserves obstruction status and has that starting family as its three-core.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                In any ample family a degree-two vertex is either a corner or a cut vertex: if its two directions realize the opposite trace, ampleness supplies the square; otherwise the two nonempty shores disconnect after deleting the vertex. A cut vertex of an obstruction belongs to two two-connected rooted factors and has degree at least four. Periphery-freeness excludes leaves, so every low-degree deletion is a degree-two corner. Low-degree corner descent preserves pc-minimal obstruction status until minimum degree three is reached. Any induced subgraph of minimum degree three survives every such process, proving uniqueness and maximality. A degree-two corner deletion removes exactly its two-support from the shadow, preserving active coordinates and all supports of size at least three; VC dimension is at least three and remains fixed. Reversing the deletions gives square completions, whose local extension and rank-two invariance theorems preserve ampleness, nonpeelability, and minor minimality.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#thm:damp-three-core

                                                                A Shattered-Support Pattern Forces Exponentially Many Corners

                                                                Name: A Shattered-Support Pattern Forces Exponentially Many Corners

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Shattered Complex

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $H\subseteq Q_F$ be ample with all coordinates active, and let the graph of shattered pairs have a partition $F=\{e\}\mathbin{\dot\cup}I\mathbin{\dot\cup}A\mathbin{\dot\cup}B$ with $I,A,B$ nonempty. Assume $P=\{e\}\cup I$ is shattered, the induced pair graphs on $A$ and $B$ are connected, no pair $\{a,i\}$ with $a\in A,i\in I$ is shattered, and no pair $\{b,e\}$ with $b\in B$ is shattered. Then the unique cube of support $P$ contains at least $2^{|I|}-1$ corners. The hypotheses depend only on the shattered complex, so the conclusion holds for every ample realization with that same complex.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The missing pairs exclude every shattered support $P\cup\{f\}$ outside $P$, making the ample $P$-cube unique. For any unshattered coordinate pair, all edges in one direction have a fixed value in the other coordinate; otherwise two such edges realize all four traces. Connectivity on $A$ makes every $A$-edge share one trace $\alpha\in Q_I$, and connectivity on $B$ makes every $B$-edge share one value $\beta$ of coordinate $e$. A vertex of the distinguished cube with $x_e\ne\beta$ and $x|_I\ne\alpha$ has no outside neighbor, so all cubes through it lie in the distinguished cube and it is a corner. Exactly $2^{|I|}-1$ cube vertices satisfy both inequalities.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#lem:damp-shadow-forced-corners

                                                                A Forbidden Three-Core Whose Shattered Complex Forces Corners

                                                                Name: A Forbidden Three-Core Whose Shattered Complex Forces Corners

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Shattered Complex

                                                                Result Type: Other

                                                                Statement:

                                                                There exists a two-connected ample pc-minimal obstruction to dismantlable ampleness with $1162$ concepts, isometric dimension $26$, and minimum degree three such that every ample family on those coordinates with the same shattered complex has at least three corners. Thus preserving the full shattered complex cannot always transform an ample forbidden three-core into a cornerless ample family, even when intermediate families need not remain pc-minimal obstructions.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                For the fixed $1162$-concept rooted-completion three-core, take $e=10$, $I=\{15,16\}$, the other first-block coordinates as $A$, and the remaining second-block coordinates as $B$. Its duplicated square supplies the cube on $\{10,15,16\}$; its shadow has no pairs between $A$ and $I$ and none between $B$ and $e$, while the pair graphs induced on $A$ and $B$ each contain a spanning star. These are properties of the shattered complex alone. The support-pattern lemma therefore applies to every ample realization with that complex and forces $2^2-1=3$ corners in the unique distinguished cube.

                                                                Small Shadow Gaps Admit Exact Relative Peelings

                                                                Name: Small Shadow Gaps Admit Exact Relative Peelings

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Shattered Complex

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Concept Deletion

                                                                Result Type: Algorithm

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $\varnothing\ne B\subseteq A\subseteq Q_F$ be ample, and suppose every support in $\operatorname{Sh}(A)\setminus\operatorname{Sh}(B)$ has size at most two. Then $A$ reduces to $B$ by deleting corners of degree at most two while retaining every concept of $B$. Equivalently, starting from $B$ and repeatedly adding an outside concept with the largest current number of neighbors always preserves ampleness and reaches $A$, acquiring a support of size at most two at each step. For every $T\subseteq B$, including $T=\varnothing$, $A$ reduces to $T$ by corner deletions exactly when $B$ does. Hence $A$ is dismantlable ample exactly when $B$ is, and $A$ peels to any $b\in B$ exactly when $B$ does. If $A$ and $B$ have the same active coordinates, every relative deletion has degree exactly two.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Every cube of $A$ of dimension at least three lies in $B$: extend it to a maximal cube, use connectedness of the corresponding reduction to see that it is the unique cube of its support, and then use ampleness of $B$ to locate that same cube there. The same uniqueness holds for maximal squares. For an ample intermediate $B\subseteq S\subsetneq A$, choose an outside concept $x$ with the most neighbors in $S$. Its punctured incident cube lies in $S$, so it has at most two directions. With two directions, maximal-square uniqueness shows the pair is not already shattered and the one-concept criterion preserves ampleness. With one direction, maximality makes $S$ locally convex and hence convex; that direction is constant on $S$, so it is again newly acquired. Iteration gives the relative order. Rank-at-most-two extension invariance preserves reduction to every retained target $T$. Equal active coordinate sets rule out a one-direction step.

                                                                References:

                                                                [@ChalopiChepoiMoran22]

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#thm:damp-relative-small-supports

                                                                Square Attachments Have a Canonical Interval Poset

                                                                Name: Square Attachments Have a Canonical Interval Poset

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Shattered Complex

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Concept Deletion

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $\varnothing\ne B\subseteq A$ be ample with the same active coordinates and with every support in $\operatorname{Sh}(A)\setminus\operatorname{Sh}(B)$ of size at most two. For $D=A\setminus B$, there is a unique acyclic orientation of all edges incident with $D$ such that boundary edges point toward $B$ and every vertex of $D$ has exactly two outgoing edges. Reachability defines a poset $P_{A,B}$ whose linear extensions are exactly the relative corner-deletion orders from $A$ to $B$. An intermediate $B\subseteq C\subseteq A$ is ample exactly when $A\setminus C$ is an order ideal of $P_{A,B}$; hence the ample intermediate families form a distributive lattice under union and intersection. Sending each $x\in D$ to the pair of its outgoing coordinate directions is a bijection from $D$ onto $\operatorname{Sh}(A)\setminus\operatorname{Sh}(B)$, independent of the deletion order.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                A relative degree-two peeling orients each edge toward its later endpoint and supplies one admissible orientation. Boundary directions and the required outdegree fix the divergence at every internal vertex; the disagreement graph of two candidate orientations would be balanced and nonempty, hence contain a directed cycle, contradicting acyclicity. Every relative peeling induces this unique orientation. Conversely, linear extensions differ by swaps of consecutive incomparable vertices, which are nonadjacent corner deletions and therefore commute. An ample intermediate concatenates relative peelings above and below it, making its removed set an order ideal; every ideal is an initial segment of a linear extension and hence leaves an ample family. Each deletion removes precisely the pair of its two outgoing directions, so these distinct pairs exhaust the shadow difference.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#thm:damp-square-interval-poset

                                                                Finite Square-Attachment Data Construct and Recover Every Three-Core Extension

                                                                Name: Finite Square-Attachment Data Construct and Recover Every Three-Core Extension

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Shattered Complex

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Concept Deletion
                                                                • Partial-Cube Minor

                                                                Result Type: Construction

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Fix a nonempty ample $K\subseteq Q_F$. Square-attachment data consist of a finite symbol set $D$ and, for each $x\in D$, a coordinate pair $I_x=\{p_x,q_x\}$ and three targets $u_x,v_x,w_x\in K\mathbin{\dot\cup}D$. They are admissible when the target-dependency digraph is acyclic, the pairs $I_x$ are distinct and absent from $\operatorname{Sh}(K)$, and the recursion $\phi(k)=k$, $\phi(x)=\phi(u_x)^{\{p_x\}}$ is injective and satisfies $\phi(v_x)=\phi(x)^{\{q_x\}}$ and $\phi(w_x)=\phi(x)^{I_x}$. Admissible data produce an ample $A=K\cup\phi(D)$ on the same active coordinates with $\operatorname{Sh}(A)=\operatorname{Sh}(K)\mathbin{\dot\cup}\{I_x:x\in D\}$. Every target-first order constructs $A$ by ample square additions. Conversely every ample $A\supseteq K$ on the same active coordinates with no new shattered support of size at least three has unique such data up to renaming $D$. Dependency reachability is the canonical interval poset and $|D|\le\binom{|F|}{2}-|\{I\in\operatorname{Sh}(K):|I|=2\}|$. If $K$ is a minimum-degree-three ample pc-minimal obstruction to dismantlable ampleness, all outputs are such obstructions with three-core $K$; every ample obstruction is recovered uniquely from its canonical three-core this way.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                In any target-first order, the three targets form the punctured $I_x$-square at the new word. Distinctness keeps $I_x$ unshattered, and an outside neighbor would force a second full $I_x$-square and contradict that fact. Thus the new word has exactly the prescribed two incident directions; the one-concept extension test preserves ampleness and adds precisely $I_x$. Conversely, orient an upper family toward $K$ by its canonical interval poset. For each outside concept, its two outgoing edge targets and the opposite square vertex supply $u_x,v_x,w_x$; the recovered arrows point forward in every relative peeling and the support pairs are distinct and absent from the base shadow. The unique orientation recovers the data up to symbol names, and diagonal-target dependencies do not enlarge its reachability order. The pair count gives the bound. The canonical three-core theorem supplies obstruction preservation and exhaustive recovery in the final clause.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#thm:damp-square-attachment-data

                                                                Peripheral Expansions, Products, and Small Additions Have Exact Endpoint Laws

                                                                Name: Peripheral Expansions, Products, and Small Additions Have Exact Endpoint Laws

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Peripheral Expansion
                                                                • Cartesian Product
                                                                • Concept Deletion

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For nonempty ample families the following endpoint laws hold. If $S\subseteq B$ and $Y=(B\times\{0\})\cup(S\times\{1\})$, then $Y$ peels to $(b,0)$ exactly when $B$ peels to $b$ and $S$ is dismantlable ample, while $Y$ peels to $(s,1)$ exactly when both $B$ and $S$ peel to $s$. A product $A\square B$ peels to $(a,b)$ exactly when its factors peel to $a$ and $b$. If $H=S\cup\{c\}$ is an ample one-concept extension whose acquired support has size at most two, then for every $r\in S$, $H$ peels to $r$ exactly when $S$ does. Consequently an ample addition that newly enables peeling to an old concept must acquire a support of size at least three.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Root-preserving contraction and face restriction prove the necessary expansion conditions. For a lower endpoint, peel the upper site first and then the base; for an upper endpoint, peel the site to its root, peel the base while retaining the matching lower vertex, and remove that lower vertex last. Product face restrictions prove necessity, while the product peeling construction with factor orders ending at the chosen roots proves sufficiency. The one-concept assertion is exactly rank-at-most-two extension invariance with the singleton target $\{r\}$.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#prop:damp-rooted-operations

                                                                Four Shadow Conditions Characterize a Marked Degree-Two Corner

                                                                Name: Four Shadow Conditions Characterize a Marked Degree-Two Corner

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Shattered Complex

                                                                Operations:

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let ample $A,D,C\subseteq Q_F$ contain $0$, put $U=A\cup D\cup C$, and set $Y=\{(0,00)\}\cup(A\times\{01\})\cup(D\times\{10\})\cup(C\times\{11\})$. Then $Y$ is ample exactly when (i) $\operatorname{Sh}(U)=\operatorname{Sh}(A)\cup\operatorname{Sh}(D)\cup\operatorname{Sh}(C)$, (ii) $\operatorname{Sh}(A\cup C)=\operatorname{Sh}(A)\cup\operatorname{Sh}(C)$, (iii) $\operatorname{Sh}(D\cup C)=\operatorname{Sh}(D)\cup\operatorname{Sh}(C)$, and (iv) $\operatorname{Sh}(A)\cap\operatorname{Sh}(D)\subseteq\operatorname{Sh}(C)$. Every ample family with a marked degree-two corner has this presentation after translating that corner to zero, uniquely up to exchanging its two directions and the side sections $A,D$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Sorting shattered supports by the two new coordinates gives $|\operatorname{Sh}(Y)|=|\operatorname{Sh}(U)|+|\operatorname{Sh}(A)\cap\operatorname{Sh}(D\cup C)|+|\operatorname{Sh}(D)\cap\operatorname{Sh}(A\cup C)|+1$. If $Y$ is ample, its two adjacent coordinate faces force conditions (ii) and (iii). Subtracting $|Y|$ then expresses the shadow excess as the sum of two nonnegative terms: the excess of $\operatorname{Sh}(U)$ over the union of the three shadows, and $|(\operatorname{Sh}(A)\cap\operatorname{Sh}(D))\setminus\operatorname{Sh}(C)|$. Equality forces (i) and (iv), and conversely the four conditions make the excess zero. For recovery, fixing both corner directions at the corner value leaves a connected ample face in which the marked vertex is isolated, so that face is a singleton; the other three sections are then uniquely determined.

                                                                Opposite Sections of a Degree-Two Corner Obey a Sharp Support Bound

                                                                Name: Opposite Sections of a Degree-Two Corner Obey a Sharp Support Bound

                                                                Classes:

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $A,B,C\subseteq\{0,1\}^n$ contain zero, with $n\le7$, and suppose $Y=\{(0,00)\}\cup(A\times\{01\})\cup(B\times\{10\})\cup(C\times\{11\})$ is ample. Put $K=A\cap C$, $\mathcal G=\operatorname{Sh}(A)\setminus\operatorname{Sh}(K)$, and let $\mathcal L$ be the supports containing no member of $\mathcal G$. Then $|B\setminus C|\le|\mathcal L\setminus\operatorname{Sh}(A)|$. If $(0,00)$ is the unique corner of $Y$, the right side is at least nine. The same conclusions hold after exchanging $A$ and $B$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Ample section-reduction identities give $\operatorname{Sh}(A\cap C)=\operatorname{Sh}(A)\cap\operatorname{Sh}(C)$ and the analogous identity for $B\cap C$. The four-section criterion gives $\operatorname{Sh}(A)\cap\operatorname{Sh}(B)\subseteq\operatorname{Sh}(C)$, so the down-set $\operatorname{Sh}(B)$ avoids every member of $\mathcal G$ and lies in $\mathcal L$. Its part outside $\operatorname{Sh}(C)$ injects into $\mathcal L\setminus\operatorname{Sh}(A)$ and has cardinality $|B\setminus C|$. If that bound were at most eight, a nonempty $B\setminus C$ would have a relative corner outside $C$; if $B\subseteq C$ and $|B|>1$, a prescribed-endpoint peeling supplies a nonzero corner; and if $B=\{0\}$, its displayed square vertex is a corner. Each case gives a second corner of $Y$, proving the lower bound nine under uniqueness.

                                                                Paired Square Sections Have Exact Root and Endpoint Transfer

                                                                Name: Paired Square Sections Have Exact Root and Endpoint Transfer

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let ample $C\subseteq A,D\subseteq Q_F$ contain $0$, with $|A\setminus C|,|D\setminus C|\le1$, $A\cap D=C$, $A\cup D$ ample, and $\operatorname{Sh}(A)\cap\operatorname{Sh}(D)=\operatorname{Sh}(C)$. For fresh $q,r$, set $Y=\{(0,00)\}\cup(A\times\{01\})\cup(D\times\{10\})\cup(C\times\{11\})$ and $a=(0,00)$. Then $Y$ is ample, $a$ is a degree-two corner, $Y$ is dismantlable ample exactly when $C$ is, and $Y$ peels to $a$ exactly when $C$ peels to $0$. If $C$ uses every old coordinate, $(Y,a)$ is a rooted factor exactly when $(C,0)$ is a rooted factor and both $A,D$ peel to $0$. When $C$ is dismantlable ample, attainable endpoints in the $01$, $10$, and $11$ sections are exactly the attainable endpoints of $A,D,C$, respectively. Thus a rooted-factor output has $a$ as its unique critical root, and its attainable sink set is nonisometric: it contains $(0,01),(0,10)$ but neither common cube neighbor $(0,00),(0,11)$. For $|C|>1$, its corners are $a$, the at most two side concepts outside $C$, and precisely those nonzero corner copies of $C$ in a side section that are not adjacent to that side's extra concept.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                A direct section count gives $\operatorname{Sh}(Y)=\operatorname{Sh}(A\cup D)\mathbin{\dot\cup}(\operatorname{Sh}(C)+q)\mathbin{\dot\cup}(\operatorname{Sh}(C)+r)\mathbin{\dot\cup}\{\{q,r\}\}$ and hence ampleness. Explicit layer orders transfer ordinary peelability and all nonroot endpoints. For the root converse, stop before the first deletion among the three nonroot copies of old zero; the surviving root square forces that copy's old section to be a singleton, and projecting the preceding broken fibers gives a peeling of $C$ to zero. Applying the same equivalence to every root-preserving old-coordinate image, and checking the two new restrictions and contractions explicitly, gives the rooted-factor criterion. Section restrictions prove necessity of the remaining endpoint formulas, while layer-by-layer constructions prove sufficiency. The unique-critical-root and nonisometric-sink conclusions follow from those formulas. Finally, inspecting which corner cubes survive across the four sections gives the stated corner list.

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Use the canonical degree-two-corner presentation $Y=\{(0,00)\}\cup(A\times\{01\})\cup(D\times\{10\})\cup(C\times\{11\})$ and its four shadow conditions. Put $R=A\cap C$ and $S=D\cap C$. Suppose $R,S$ are dismantlable ample and that $A$ and $C$ peel relatively to $R$, while $D$ and $C$ peel relatively to $S$. Then $Y$ is dismantlable ample and peels to $a=(0,00)$ exactly when either $R$ and $D$ both peel to zero or $S$ and $A$ both peel to zero. Every endpoint in another section is attainable in $Y$ exactly when it is attainable in that section. If every old coordinate is active in $A\cup D\cup C$, then $(Y,a)$ is a rooted factor exactly when $A,D$ peel to zero, neither $R$ nor $S$ peels to zero, and every root-preserving elementary old-coordinate image makes at least one of the image overlaps root-positive. The root $a$ is then the unique critical root. If $(R,0)$ and $(S,0)$ are rooted factors using all old coordinates, the last condition is automatic; no containment of $C$ in either side is required.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The four shadow conditions give ampleness. Isometry rules out words in $(A\cap D)\setminus C$ and edges between the exclusive parts of adjacent sections, so the assumed relative orders remain valid in the unions. Clearing the appropriate exclusive pieces gives relative orders to each section and proves ordinary positivity and every nonroot endpoint formula. For a root-ending order, the first deleted nonroot copy of zero and a broken-fiber projection force either $R$ or $S$ to peel to zero, while explicit section-clearing orders prove both converse alternatives. Relative orders and intersections commute with root-preserving coordinate images. Applying the endpoint equivalence to each image yields the three rooted-minimality conditions; explicit orders handle the two new-coordinate restrictions and contractions. Any other unattainable vertex already fails in its proper section, proving uniqueness of the critical root.

The adjacent vertices $r,v$ are both degree-three corners, while deleting $v$ restores the root-negative factor $K$. Degree three is therefore the least possible degree of a nonroot corner whose deletion can destroy a prescribed old endpoint. There is also a 621-concept positive partner $T=W\setminus\{z\}$ that peels to $r$ and has the same shattered complex as $K$; $K$ and $T$ form a two-square endpoint switch over a common 619-concept base.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                The two-section shadow identity shows that $W$ is ample and gains exactly one triple support. Its enlarged vertical reduction is a specified convex five-vertex face of the contraction. Lifting the contraction's acyclic USO with sink at the old root and orienting the free vertical edge toward the upper copy gives a USO of $W$ ending at $r$. The relevant eight vertices form a three-cube, so $r$ and $v$ are adjacent degree-three corners. Deleting $v$ leaves $K$, while rank-at-most-two endpoint invariance rules out any analogous repair of degree below three. A third degree-three cube corner $z$ can start the recorded endpoint order; deleting it gives $T$. The two corner deletions remove the same triple support, so $K$ and $T$ have equal shadows and differ by the two claimed square attachments over their common base.

                                                                Fix the certified 289-concept family $B$ and its path $H=a-b-c-d=2-0-4-5$. Let $P$ be any ample dismantlable family containing the edge $D=\{c,d\}$, using fresh coordinates apart from the direction of $cd$, and suppose $P$ peels to $c$. Embed $B\cap P=D$ and, for a fresh coordinate $e$, set $K(P)=(B\times\{0\})\cup((H\cup P)\times\{1\})$ with root $r=(a,1)$. Then $K(P)$ is ample and dismantlable, $r$ is a degree-two corner, and $K(P)$ peels to $r$ exactly when $P$ peels relatively to $D$. Moreover, $(K(P),r)$ is a rooted factor exactly when $P$ fails to peel to $D$ but every elementary private-coordinate restriction or contraction of $P$ that retains $D$ peels to its image of $D$. The output has $|P|+291$ concepts and $\dim(P)+12$ active coordinates. Under these minimality conditions, gluing $K(P)$ at $r$ to the fixed rooted factor $(B,b)$ gives an ample pc-minimal obstruction to dismantlable ampleness with $|P|+579$ concepts.

                                                                Status: Established

Edge gluing this orientation to one of $P$ ending at $c$ proves that the contraction $B\cup P$ and the upper section $H\cup P$ have compatible endpoint maps; their shadow intersection is exactly $\operatorname{Sh}(H)$, giving ampleness of $K(P)$ and ordinary positivity. If $P$ retains $D$, a relative clearing followed by the star-reduction endpoint theorem peels $K(P)$ to $r$. Conversely, a hypothetical root-ending USO when $P$ cannot retain $D$ forces a directed cycle through the lower path, the vertical edges at $b,d$, and an upper directed path in $P$. This proves the endpoint equivalence. Private-coordinate images remain constructions of the same form, so the equivalence gives their exact rooted-minimality condition; stored relative path orders and star reductions handle all fixed-block and new-coordinate images. The order and dimension formulas are immediate, and the cut-vertex obstruction theorem gives the final gluing claim.

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The forward implication follows from the canonical section presentation of a rooted factor. Conversely, positive contractions force both side sections to peel to zero, so all four new-coordinate rooted images are positive. Commuting operations shows that every rooted minor using a new coordinate is positive; hence any root-negative minor retains both new coordinates. Repeatedly take root-negative elementary old-coordinate images until minimal. Ordinary peelability survives, so the terminal image is a rooted factor. Old-coordinate operations preserve the singleton root section and its two incident directions. They also preserve the identity between the image of the overlap and the intersection of the image sections: a new contraction intersection would create opposite square vertices without either intermediate vertex, contradicting isometry. Endpoint minor closure preserves root positivity of the overlap.

                                                                Let $(C,0)$ be an irredundantly embedded rooted factor whose only corner is $0$. Let $A=C\cup\{\alpha\}$ and $D=C\cup\{\delta\}$ be distinct ample one-concept extensions such that $A,D,A\cup D$ are ample, both extensions peel to $0$, and their shadows intersect in $\operatorname{Sh}(C)$. The paired square construction is a rooted factor $Y$ with exactly three corners: its root and the two repair tips. Deleting either nonroot corner destroys rooted minimality. Gluing $(Y,a)$ to a disjoint copy of $(C,0)$ gives a corner-descent-terminal ample pc-minimal obstruction $X$ with a cut vertex, exactly two corners, and $|X|=4|C|+2$. It has no nontrivial replicated common-seed presentation with resolving tips.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Paired-square transfer makes $Y$ a rooted factor and gives its exact corners after any subset of the two tips is deleted. Removing either tip turns one side section back into $C$; a new-coordinate restriction followed by contraction exposes the bad rooted minor $(C,0)$, so rooted minimality fails. The cut-vertex classification makes $X=Y\vee C$ ample and pc-minimal outside dismantlable ampleness. The glued root is no longer a corner, leaving exactly the two tips. After either tip deletion, a proper minor is the nonpeelable double $C\vee C$, proving terminality. Replicated common-seed constructions with resolving tips are two-connected, while $X$ has a cut vertex.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#thm:damp-terminal-cut-vertex

                                                                Witnesses:

                                                                • Terminal Cut-Vertex Obstruction of Order 1158

                                                                Rooted Minimality Persists along Ample One-Concept Additions

                                                                Name: Rooted Minimality Persists along Ample One-Concept Additions

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Concept Deletion
                                                                • Partial-Cube Minor

                                                                Result Type: Implication

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $(H,a)$ be a rooted factor irredundantly embedded on $F$, and let $K=H\cup\{c\}\subseteq Q_F$ be ample. Then either $K$ peels to $a$, or $(K,a)$ is again a rooted factor. More generally, along any chain of ample one-concept additions on the same coordinate set starting at $H$, if the final family does not peel to $a$, every intermediate rooted family is a rooted factor.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The added concept is a corner, so $K$ is ordinarily peelable. Every elementary root-preserving image of $H$ is a proper rooted minor and peels to the root image. The corresponding image of $K$ differs by at most one concept; if present, that concept is a nonroot corner and can be deleted before the rooted order of the image of $H$. Thus all proper rooted images of $K$ are positive. If $K$ itself is root-negative, it satisfies the rooted-factor conditions. Peeling to the old root persists after an ample one-concept addition by deleting the new corner first, so root-negativity of the final chain member forces it at every intermediate stage and induction applies.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#lem:damp-rooted-ample-additions

                                                                A Forced Prefix Produces Three Rooted Inputs and Six Obstructions

                                                                Name: A Forced Prefix Produces Three Rooted Inputs and Six Obstructions

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                • Concept Deletion
                                                                • One-Point Amalgam
                                                                • Partial-Cube Minor

                                                                Result Type: Construction

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For the normalized 289-concept rooted factor $C\subseteq Q_{12}$, let $b=256$ and $H=C\setminus\{0\}$. Then $(H,b)$, $(C,0)$, and $(C,b)$ are rooted factors. The first two roots are degree-three corners and the third is a degree-four noncorner. The attainable peeling endpoints of both $C$ and $H$ are exactly $C\setminus\{0,b\}$, a set of 287 concepts. Pairwise one-point amalgams of these three rooted inputs, allowing repetition, give six pairwise nonisomorphic ample pc-minimal obstructions in dimension 24, of orders 575, 576, or 577 and with respectively 0, 0, 1, 0, 1, or 2 corners in the six unordered cases.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Direct corner calculation forces every peeling of $C$ to begin $0,b$, making $b$ the unique corner of $H$. Certificates verify an ordinary order and all 24 elementary rooted-minor orders for $(H,b)$; hence it is a rooted factor. The known $(C,0)$ factor and the ample one-concept addition lemma imply rooted minimality of $(C,b)$, since the forced prefix prevents a peeling ending at $b$. Explicit orders certify all 287 other endpoints for both families. The cut-vertex theorem then proves each amalgam forbidden and gives its order. Nonroot corners survive gluing, while the common root loses corner status; the resulting order/corner-count pairs distinguish all six outputs.

Every vertex of every nonempty proper pc-minor of $A$ is attainable as a peeling endpoint, so no proper minor is a rooted factor at any root. The double of $(A,a)$ is a cornerless ample pc-minimal obstruction of order 527 and dimension 24. More generally, the certified shrinking outputs give 24, 12, and 12 labeled rooted inputs of orders 266, 265, and 264; gluing any two roots gives a cornerless ample obstruction.

                                                                A certified ample precursor has forced first vertices $1004,748,750$; deleting the first two leaves $A$ with unique corner $a$, so it is positive but cannot peel to its root. Independent certificates give root-ending orders for all 24 elementary root-preserving images, proving rooted minimality. A stronger replay checks every one of 5,637 endpoint choices in the 36 elementary proper pc-minors; endpoint minor closure propagates this to all deeper nonempty minors and excludes every smaller rooted factor. The same certificates cover all 48 labeled inputs. The cut-vertex theorem proves every pairwise gluing forbidden. No nonroot corner exists, and the identified root is not a corner because its two coordinate blocks have no mixed square, so all outputs are cornerless.                                                                 Attainable Sink Sets Can Be Disconnected

Indeed $\operatorname{Sink}(A\times B)=\operatorname{Sink}(A)\times\operatorname{Sink}(B)$ for positive ample families $A,B$.

Their exact profiles supply compatible corner orders ending in opposite private sides, while the edge-context algebra excludes both common-edge vertices as attainable sinks; no edge joins the two private sides. Product peelings restrict to root-ending orders in both factors, and conversely fibrewise interleaving of such orders ends at any prescribed pair of attainable sinks. Hence sink sets and their component counts multiply under Cartesian products.

                                                                Corner Deletion Followed by Rooted Minor Descent

                                                                Name: Corner Deletion Followed by Rooted Minor Descent

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Concept Deletion
                                                                • Partial-Cube Minor

                                                                Result Type: Algorithm

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $(H,a)$ be a rooted factor and let $x\ne a$ be a corner such that $S=H\setminus\{x\}$ is corner-peelable. Some root-preserving pc-minor $(C,b)=(\mu S,\mu a)$ is a rooted factor with $|C|<|H|$. If $(S,a)$ is not already rooted-minimal, $\mu$ is proper and $\mu H=C\cup\{d\}$ is an ample one-concept repair peeling to $b$. If $P$ is the support of the corner cube at $x$ and a normal form for $\mu$ restricts $R$ and contracts $Q$, then $Q\cap P=\varnothing$, every restriction in $R$ keeps the root bit, the acquired support at $d$ is $P\setminus R$, and $|P\setminus R|\ge3$. Iteration ends at a rooted factor whose root is the unique source in every acyclic USO.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The deletion remains ample, fails to peel to the root, and is ordinarily peelable. Minor-minimize that rooted failure. If the chosen map is proper, its images of $H$ and $S$ differ in exactly the repair $d$. A restriction discarding $x$, or a contraction in an incident direction, would identify the images, proving the normal-form exclusions. Shattered-support transport identifies the repair support with $P\setminus R$; support at most two cannot change endpoint peelability. Cardinality decreases at every iteration. At termination no peeling can start away from the root, which is equivalent through the peeling–acyclic-USO correspondence to unique-source status in every acyclic USO.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#prop:damp-combined-rooted-descent

                                                                Joint Corner Descent for Rooted Factors and Ordinary Obstructions

                                                                Name: Joint Corner Descent for Rooted Factors and Ordinary Obstructions

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Concept Deletion
                                                                • Partial-Cube Minor

                                                                Result Type: Algorithm

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Starting from either a rooted factor or an ample pc-minimal obstruction to dismantlable ampleness, repeatedly delete a nonterminal corner and minor-minimize the residual rooted or ordinary failure. Cardinality decreases strictly, and the process ends either at a rooted factor whose root is its only geometric corner or at a cornerless ample pc-minimal obstruction. A rooted deletion with a corner-peelable remainder stays in the rooted branch; a nonpeelable remainder enters the ordinary branch, which is then permanent.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Deleting a nonroot corner from a rooted factor preserves ampleness and rooted failure. A positive remainder admits rooted minor descent; a negative remainder contains an ordinary pc-minimal obstruction. Deleting a corner from an ordinary nonpeelable ample family remains nonpeelable, since any peeling of the remainder could be prefixed by that corner, so ordinary minor-minimization can continue. Every step begins with a deletion, forcing termination with exactly the stated corner conditions.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#cor:damp-joint-rooted-ordinary-descent

                                                                Component-Label Criterion for Lifting a Repairing Addition

                                                                Name: Component-Label Criterion for Lifting a Repairing Addition

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Coordinate Fiber Product
                                                                • Peripheral Expansion

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $\varnothing\ne D\subseteq C$ be ample, let $K_1,\ldots,K_k$ be the components of $C\setminus D$, and suppose $A=C\cup\{d\}$ is ample. Lift each $K_i$ to layer $t_i$, double $D$, and lift $d$ to layer $b$. If $I(d)$ indexes the components containing a neighbour of $d$, the lift is ample exactly when $t_i=b$ for all $i\in I(d)$. Then the lifted repair is a corner with the same acquired support as $d$ over $C$. If additionally $A,D$ are corner-peelable but the ample lift is not, some untouched component $j\notin I(d)$ has label $1-b$. Thus a repair meeting every component cannot yield an ample forbidden lift when the repaired contraction and reduction are positive.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                After adjoining $d$, it merges exactly the touched components of $C\setminus D$. The component-sign parametrization of ample expansions forces, and is forced by, equality of their lift labels with the label of $d$. All old neighbours of the lifted repair then remain in its layer or lie over the doubled reduction, so its incident and acquired supports are unchanged. If no untouched opposite-layer component exists, the lift is the peripheral expansion $(A\times\{b\})\cup(D\times\{1-b\})$, which is corner-peelable when both $A$ and $D$ are.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#cor:damp-repair-lift-labels

                                                                Singleton Reductions Preserve Corner-Peelability Exactly

                                                                Name: Singleton Reductions Preserve Corner-Peelability Exactly

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Coordinate Fiber Product
                                                                • One-Point Amalgam
                                                                • Peripheral Expansion

                                                                Result Type: Implication

                                                                Statement:

                                                                If an ample one-coordinate expansion $X$ has contraction $A$ and singleton reduction $\{a\}$, then $X$ is corner-peelable if and only if $A$ is corner-peelable. Hence no active singleton-reduction expansion is an ample forbidden pc-minor. Moreover, an untouched component in the opposite layer is not sufficient for forbiddenness: a separated repair over the negative 577-concept double gives a corner-peelable 579-concept lift.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The components of $A-a$, after restoring $a$, occupy disjoint coordinate blocks and attach to the two ends of the sole new-direction edge. If $A$ peels, all component pieces peel and at most one fails to peel to $a$. Peel all other pieces to their attachment vertices, remove the resulting pendant endpoint, and peel the exceptional piece; the converse follows by contraction closure. In the explicit separated repair, peel the repaired first rooted block to zero, delete zero as a leaf across the new edge, and peel the second block.

                                                                Acyclic USOs Lift Through Convex Reductions

                                                                Name: Acyclic USOs Lift Through Convex Reductions

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Coordinate Projection
                                                                • Coordinate Fiber Product
                                                                • Partial-Cube Minor

                                                                Result Type: Implication

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $X$ be ample, let $e$ be active, and let $A=\pi_eX$ and $D=X^{\{e\}}$. If $D$ is convex in $A$, every acyclic USO of $A$ lifts to an acyclic USO of $X$ preserving every old-direction edge orientation. Consequently $X$ is corner-peelable exactly when $A$ is, and $X$ peels to $a$ exactly when $A$ peels to $\pi_ea$. Therefore no coordinate reduction of an ample pc-minimal obstruction or rooted factor is convex in its contraction; in particular no such reduction is a cube.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Convexity makes each cube intersection with $D$ a face and places the nonempty complement in one component of $A\setminus D$. Lift old edges from the given orientation and direct each vertical edge toward the component containing the outgoing neighbours at its base, choosing freely when none exist. The outgoing-cube and unique-sink conditions hold on every cube. Any directed cycle with an old edge would project to a directed closed walk in the acyclic base orientation, while vertical edges alone form a matching. Choosing the final vertical direction toward a prescribed lift proves endpoint transfer; contraction proves the reverse implications.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#thm:damp-convex-reduction-lift

                                                                Relative Face Peeling Through a Convex Reduction

                                                                Name: Relative Face Peeling Through a Convex Reduction

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Coordinate Conditioning
                                                                • Concept Deletion
                                                                • Coordinate Fiber Product

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Under the convex-reduction hypotheses, let $B$ be a nonempty coordinate-face intersection of the contraction $A$, contained in one projected section $X_t$, and put $T=B\times\{t\}$ and $C=D\cap B$. Then $X$ peels relatively to $T$ exactly when $A$ peels relatively to $B$ and $C$ is empty or corner-peelable. If $B$ is corner-peelable, the second condition follows automatically by pc-minor closure.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Contracting a relative peeling of $X$ yields one of $A$ to $B$, while restricting its residual families to the opposite target face gives a peeling of $C$. Conversely, lift the relative order on $A$ by deleting each new-coordinate fibre. Convexity makes the corner-cube intersection with the reduction a face and its complement component-monochromatic, so each fibre deletion is one or two valid corner deletions. The remainder is $(B\times\{t\})\cup(C\times\{1-t\})$; a corner order of $C$ removes the opposite layer and leaves exactly $T$.

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#prop:damp-convex-relative-face

                                                                Every Active Direction Contains a Seven-Vertex Three-Face

                                                                Name: Every Active Direction Contains a Seven-Vertex Three-Face

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Coordinate Projection
                                                                • Coordinate Conditioning

                                                                Result Type: Implication

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For every active coordinate $e$ of an ample pc-minimal obstruction to dismantlable ampleness, or of the underlying family of a rooted factor, there are coordinates $f,g$ and a coordinate three-face whose intersection with the family has exactly seven vertices. After projecting this face along $e$, exactly three vertices have both lifts. Consequently every nonempty one-coordinate reduction has at least three vertices and is not a cube.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The convex-reduction lifting theorem makes the reduction $D$ nonconvex in the contraction $A$. Both are ample and $D$ is connected and isometric. The distance-two interval criterion for convexity therefore yields a square of $A$ with exactly three vertices in $D$. Those three have both lifts in the original family and the fourth has one, producing the seven-vertex three-face and the stated reduction constraints.

                                                                Exact Criterion and Count for Horizontal USO Lifts

                                                                Name: Exact Criterion and Count for Horizontal USO Lifts

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Coordinate Fiber Product

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $X$ be ample, let $e$ be active, write $A=\pi_eX$ and $D=X^{\{e\}}$, and fix an acyclic USO $\mathcal O$ of $A$. An acyclic USO of $X$ preserving the orientation of every old-direction edge exists exactly when the induced orientation $\mathcal O|_D$ is a USO of $D$. If $s$ vertices $d\in D$ have no outgoing neighbour in $A\setminus D$, exactly $2^s$ such lifts exist. At every other $d$, the vertical edge is forced toward the lift label of its outgoing external neighbours; the remaining $s$ vertical directions are independent.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Necessity follows from the outgoing-cube condition at the source of each vertical edge and from restriction to cubes of $D$. Conversely, the complement of an ample intersection inside any cube is connected, so all external outgoing neighbours of a doubled vertex lie in one labeled component. Direct the vertical edge toward that label, with a free choice when there is no external outgoing neighbour. The outgoing-cube and unique-sink conditions then hold on every cube, and a directed cycle would project to a directed closed walk in the acyclic base orientation. Reversing any forced vertical edge creates an outgoing pair with a missing opposite lift, proving exhaustiveness and the count.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#thm:damp-horizontal-uso-lifts

                                                                A Forbidden Path Reduction Forces Every Contraction USO to Fork

                                                                Name: A Forbidden Path Reduction Forces Every Contraction USO to Fork

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Coordinate Projection
                                                                • Coordinate Fiber Product

                                                                Result Type: Implication

                                                                Statement:

                                                                If an ample pc-minimal obstruction to dismantlable ampleness has a reduction $D=\{u,c,v\}$ inducing the path $u-c-v$, every acyclic USO of its contraction directs both path edges away from $c$. Equivalently, every corner peeling of the contraction deletes $c$ before both endpoints.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The contraction is corner-peelable. On a three-vertex path the only orientation violating the outgoing-cube condition is the fork with source at its middle vertex. Every other induced orientation is a USO of the reduction and would lift by the horizontal-lift criterion, contradicting nonpeelability of the expansion. The peeling–acyclic-USO correspondence translates the orientation statement into deletion order.
