                                                                Name: Horizontal USO Preservation Is Not Necessary for Positivity

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Coordinate Fiber Product

                                                                Result Type: Construction

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Failure of the horizontal-lift criterion for a prescribed contraction USO does not imply that an ample expansion is nonpeelable: the seven-vertex peripheral expansion of a square over a three-vertex path is corner-peelable although one natural square orientation has no horizontal lift. More strongly, there is a 292-concept ample path expansion that is corner-peelable even though no acyclic USO of its contraction admits an acyclic lift preserving all horizontal directions.

                                                                Proof:

                                                                For the seven-vertex family, the displayed deletion sequence clears two square corners and a leaf before leaving a square. For the 292-concept control, the contraction has unique geometric corner zero, hence every acyclic USO has zero as its source and induces the forbidden fork orientation on the path reduction. Connectedness of the complement leaves only the two reflected peripheral expansions; deleting the two lifted path endpoints, then the lifted middle vertex, and then following the stored contraction order peels each one.

                                                                Exact Component-Label Criterion for a Three-Vertex Path Reduction

                                                                Name: Exact Component-Label Criterion for a Three-Vertex Path Reduction

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Path-Reduction Label Hypergraph

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Coordinate Fiber Product
                                                                • Concept Deletion

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $A$ be corner-peelable ample, let $D=\{u,c,v\}$ induce a path, and lift each component $K_i$ of $A\setminus D$ to layer $t_i$. The resulting ample expansion $X_t$ is corner-peelable exactly when some acyclic USO $\mathcal O$ of $A$ and some endpoint $z\in\{u,v\}$ make the labels on $N_{\mathcal O}(z)$ constant (with empty and singleton sets allowed). Equivalently, the nonpeelable labelings are precisely the proper two-colourings of every edge of $\mathcal H(A,D)$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Given such an orientation and endpoint, first delete vertices outside the set reachable from $D$; those exclusive deletions lift. All surviving external neighbours of the selected endpoint then have one label, so its opposite lift is a corner. The remaining reduction is an edge convex in the contraction and hence peels. Conversely, in any peeling of the expansion, the first deletion over $D$ must occur at an endpoint. Earlier exclusive deletions project to a contraction prefix, which can be completed to an acyclic USO; vertices reachable from $D$ survive that prefix, and the corner test forces the relevant surviving component labels to be constant.

                                                                Star Reductions Preserve Positivity and Every Attainable Endpoint

                                                                Name: Star Reductions Preserve Positivity and Every Attainable Endpoint

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes

                                                                • Coordinate Projection
                                                                • Coordinate Fiber Product
                                                                • One-Point Amalgam

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $X$ be ample with active coordinate $e$ and suppose the reduction $D=X^{\{e\}}$ has a star as its one-inclusion graph, including a singleton or edge. Then $X$ is corner-peelable exactly when $\pi_eX$ is. For every $a\in X$, $X$ peels to $a$ exactly when the contraction peels to $\pi_ea$; for every $z\in D$, $X$ peels to the whole two-point fibre over $z$ exactly when the contraction peels to $z$. Consequently a coordinate edge with an attainable endpoint that cannot be retained has at least four edges, and equality forces a four-vertex-path reduction. No active reduction of an ample pc-minimal obstruction or rooted factor is a star.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Induct on the number of star edges. Exclusive contraction corners lift directly; a leaf corner can be cleared in the layer opposite its common external-component label. If the centre appears first, its corner cube separates all remaining complement components into a core and one-vertex attachments on disjoint coordinate blocks. A USO of the core selects a leaf whose attachments peel to it, after which one lift of that leaf can be removed and induction applies. The same induction while retaining a chosen fibre proves relative transfer. Endpoint transfer follows by gluing two copies at a hypothetical failing endpoint and applying ordinary star closure after contracting one copy. The size-four conclusion uses the classification of ample families on at most four vertices.

                                                                A Radius-Two Vertex in a Tree Reduction Retains Its Fibre

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $X$ be ample and suppose an active-coordinate reduction $D$ is a tree. If every vertex of $D$ is within graph distance two of $z$, then the following are equivalent: one lift of $z$ is an attainable endpoint; $X$ peels to the entire two-point fibre over $z$; both lifts are attainable. Hence a nonretainable coordinate edge with an attainable endpoint projects to a vertex of eccentricity at least three in any tree reduction. For a four-vertex path it must project to an endpoint, and the bound is sharp.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Induct on the size of the reduction. Star reductions are the base case. In an endpoint peeling, the first deletion over the still-intact reduction projects to a tree corner and therefore to a leaf different from $z$. Removing that fibre vertex leaves an ample expansion whose reduction is the tree with this leaf deleted; distances among surviving vertices are unchanged and the endpoint-order suffix remains valid. Induction retains the whole fibre over $z$. The remaining implications and eccentricity consequence are immediate.

                                                                Attainable End Corners Force Retention in a Four-Vertex Path Reduction

                                                                Name: Attainable End Corners Force Retention in a Four-Vertex Path Reduction

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                • Coordinate Fiber Product

                                                                Result Type: Implication

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let an active-coordinate reduction be the path $a-b-c-d$, with lifts $a_0,a_1$. If some $a_i$ is both a geometric corner and an attainable endpoint, the family peels to the whole edge $\{a_0,a_1\}$. More generally, if both lifts are attainable but their edge cannot be retained, there are disjoint exclusive-prefix sets $R_0,R_1$ in components of their respective layers such that each can be deleted while retaining the path, each $A_i=A\setminus R_i$ peels to $a$, but $A_*=A\setminus(R_0\cup R_1)$ is ample with $a$ a leaf and does not peel to $a$. In such a failure neither lift is a geometric corner.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Under nonretention, any endpoint order must first break the fibre over $a$; breaking the opposite end would leave a star reduction, and an internal path vertex cannot project from the first doubled corner. Exclusive corner tests depend only on their own complement component, so the layer-specific prefixes from the two endpoint orders can be reordered, omitted, and concatenated. Each prefix removes all exterior neighbours of $a$ in its layer. A geometric attainable lift would therefore lead after the opposite prefix to a leaf contraction peeling to $a$, from which star transfer retains the edge. Combining both prefixes gives the stated ample intersection, whose failure at $a$ is necessary to avoid the same conclusion.

                                                                Canonical Free Vertical Directions Suffice for Tree-Lift Acyclicity

                                                                Name: Canonical Free Vertical Directions Suffice for Tree-Lift Acyclicity

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Coordinate Fiber Product

                                                                Result Type: Algorithm

                                                                Statement:

                                                                In the representation-map lift over a nonempty ample tree reduction $H$, fix the contraction map, component labels, a quotient sink block $K_*$, and a root $q\in K_*$. Keep forced vertical-source bits, set the free root bit to zero when applicable, and propagate each remaining free bit from its parent in the tree rooted at $q$. Some allowed free-bit assignment is acyclic exactly when this canonical assignment is. Hence at most $|K_*|$ cycle tests are needed, one per root, instead of $2^{|Z|}$. Moving a successful root along an outgoing contraction edge in $K_*$ preserves success, so only sinks of the induced orientation on $K_*$ need be tested.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                At a free nonroot vertex the only outgoing horizontal edge leads to its parent. If its bit differs from the parent, matching it to the parent cannot create a new directed cycle: replace the new two-edge vertical-then-parent segment of any alleged cycle by the old parent-then-vertical segment, producing a directed closed walk before the change. The free root edge may be normalized because its new head has no outgoing edge. Processing outward from the root yields the canonical assignment. The same cycle-splicing argument shows that moving the root along an outgoing edge inside the sink block preserves acyclicity.

Their orders are $9,10,10,10,11,11,11,12$, and at most $2,1,1,1,1,1,0,0$ pieces respectively have a nongated copy of $D$. Coordinate-face separator theory gives canonical components, positivity, disjoint coordinate blocks, and relative failure. Projection to the four face coordinates compares two nested complementary intervals, bounding nongated projected components by two, by one when the omitted interval has size at most two, and by zero in the last two stated cases.

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $(B,0)$ be a rooted factor, let $\alpha,\delta,\gamma$ be distinct ample additions with pairwise distinct acquired supports, and suppose $B\cup\{\alpha\}$ and $B\cup\{\delta\}$ peel to zero. Form the paired two-coordinate factor $S$ and add copies of $\gamma$ on an occurrence row $R\subseteq L=\{01,10,11\}$. Then $\operatorname{Sh}(S_R)=\operatorname{Sh}(S)\mathbin{\dot\cup}\{P_\gamma\cup J:J\in\operatorname{Sh}(R)\}$. The family $S_R$ is ample exactly when $R\ne\{01,10\}$. For every allowable row it is ordinarily peelable, all proper root-preserving pc-minors peel to their roots, and it peels to $(0,00)$ exactly when $|R|\ge2$ and $B\cup\{\gamma\}$ peels to zero. Otherwise it is a rooted factor; its root is always a degree-two corner.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Compatible one-concept additions give the disjoint shadow formula, and the Sandwich equality excludes only the diagonal two-point row. Empty and singleton rows cannot reach the root because their unchanged paired overlaps would force $B$ itself to peel to zero. The full row is the paired construction over $B\cup\{\gamma\}$, giving necessity and sufficiency there; an explicit layer-clearing order proves sufficiency for either incident edge row. Every allowable row lies in ample addition chains above the original rooted factor and below the full row, yielding ordinary and proper-minor positivity and the exact rooted-factor criterion.

                                                                An Antipodal New-Corner Pair Cannot Restore a Rooted Endpoint

                                                                Name: An Antipodal New-Corner Pair Cannot Restore a Rooted Endpoint

                                                                Classes:

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $(B,a)$ be a rooted factor with unique corner $a$, and let $H=B\cup\{c\}$ be an ample addition with acquired support $P$ and completed cube $Q$. Let $E$ be the old vertices $v\in Q\setminus\{a,c\}$ having no neighbour outside $Q$. Then $E$ is exactly the set of nonroot, nontip corners of $H$, every member has distance at least two from $c$, and every peeling of $H$ ending at $a$ must start in $E$. If $E$ is empty or consists only of the antipode $c^P$, then $(H,a)$ remains a rooted factor and every ordinary peeling deletes $a$ among its first two vertices. Consequently any endpoint-restoring addition has an available old corner at distance strictly between $1$ and $|P|$ from its tip.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Any old vertex newly becoming a corner must share a corner cube with the added tip, hence must lie in its completed cube and have no exterior neighbour. A neighbour of the tip cannot be such a corner, or deleting the tip would leave another corner of the unique-corner base. Root-ending peelings can start neither at the root nor at the tip, so must start in $E$. When $E$ is the singleton antipode, deleting it destroys the tip corner and exterior-neighbour witnesses exclude every other new corner; deleting the tip returns the base. Thus either first move forces the root second and the endpoint remains impossible, while ordinary peelability and proper rooted-minor positivity persist.

                                                                Signed Minimal Nonfaces Parametrize Every Fixed-Shadow Ample Family

                                                                Name: Signed Minimal Nonfaces Parametrize Every Fixed-Shadow Ample Family

                                                                • Shattered Complex

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $\Sigma\subseteq2^F$ be a simplicial complex and choose a trace $\sigma_I\in Q_I$ for every minimal nonface $I\in\mathcal N(\Sigma)$. Put $H(\Sigma,\boldsymbol\sigma)=\{x\in Q_F:x|_I\ne\sigma_I\text{ for all }I\in\mathcal N(\Sigma)\}$. The signing is admissible when $|H(\Sigma,\boldsymbol\sigma)|=|\Sigma|$. Sending an ample $H$ with $\operatorname{Sh}(H)=\Sigma$ to the unique trace omitted on every minimal nonface is a bijection onto the admissible signings, with inverse $\boldsymbol\sigma\mapsto H(\Sigma,\boldsymbol\sigma)$. Thus the signed minimal nonfaces determine the entire ample family.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Projection to a minimal nonface remains ample and has shattered complex $2^I\setminus\{I\}$, so Sandwich equality says that it omits exactly one trace. The original family lies in the avoidance family of these traces. The latter shatters no nonface of $\Sigma$, so the upper Sandwich bound gives $|H(\Sigma,\boldsymbol\sigma_H)|\le|\Sigma|=|H|$ and forces equality. Conversely an admissible avoidance family has shattered complex contained in $\Sigma$ and cardinality $|\Sigma|$; both Sandwich inequalities are equalities, proving ampleness and exact shadow.

                                                                Every Concept of a Geometrically Realizable Ample Family Is a Peeling Endpoint

                                                                Name: Every Concept of a Geometrically Realizable Ample Family Is a Peeling Endpoint

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Realizable Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Concept Deletion

                                                                Result Type: Implication

                                                                Statement:

                                                                If an ample family is the chamber-sign family of finitely many affine hyperplanes on a nonempty open convex polyhedron, then it corner-peels to every prescribed concept. Consequently no rooted factor is geometrically realizable. Geometric realizability is inherited by coordinate faces, so any family having a rooted factor as a coordinate face is nonrealizable; in particular the remote opposite-status families are all nonrealizable, including their ordinarily peelable sides.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Choose a point in the prescribed chamber and first bound the realizing polyhedron without changing its sign system. A generic affine functional close to a hyperplane separating that chamber from another chamber defines a moving halfspace that keeps the chosen point. At the first nontrivial sweep event, the Knauer--Marc corner sweep deletes one COM corner; in a lopsided system this is one ordinary corner, and the remainder is again an ample geometric realization containing the chosen point. Iteration peels to the prescribed chamber. Coordinate-face inheritance follows by intersecting with the fixed open sign halfspaces and forgetting their hyperplanes.

                                                                References:

                                                                \cite[Propositions~5.3 and~5.5]{KnauerMarc23corners}

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#prop:damp-realizable-prescribed-endpoint

                                                                Witnesses:

                                                                • Rooted 289-Vertex Peeling Factor
                                                                • Remote Forbidden-Minor Single-Clause Pivot Tower

                                                                Affine Oriented-Matroid Tope Classes Have Matroidal Shadows

                                                                Name: Affine Oriented-Matroid Tope Classes Have Matroidal Shadows

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Affine Oriented-Matroid Tope Graphs
                                                                • Ample Classes

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Shattered Complex

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                If $C$ is the projection of the $g=+$ topes of an oriented matroid $M$, then $\operatorname{Sh}(C)=\operatorname{Ind}(M/g)$. In particular its shattered complex satisfies matroid augmentation. The common shadow of the remote rooted pair violates augmentation: $\{1,2\}$ and $\{1,5,6\}$ are faces but neither $\{1,2,5\}$ nor $\{1,2,6\}$ is. Every higher paired-square level also violates augmentation. Hence none of these rooted pairs is a full affine-oriented-matroid tope class.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                A support is shattered by the full antipodal tope set exactly when it is independent in the underlying matroid. Antipodality identifies shattering of $I$ in the positive half with shattering of $I\cup\{g\}$ in the full tope set, which is equivalent to independence of $I$ in $M/g$. The displayed face pair gives an explicit augmentation failure at level zero; at higher levels the fresh root pair is a maximal two-face while adjoining either fresh coordinate to a shattered old pair gives a three-face, again violating augmentation.

                                                                References:

                                                                \cite[Claim~2.2]{Marc24compression}

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#rem:damp-affine-om-shadow

                                                                Witnesses:

                                                                • Remote Rooted Single-Clause Pivot Tower

                                                                Comments:

                                                                This excludes representation as the full positive half of one oriented matroid. It does not exclude fibers with several sign constraints or representations using auxiliary elements.

                                                                Every Single-Clause Exchange Has a Canonical Ample Completion and Outside Slice

                                                                Name: Every Single-Clause Exchange Has a Canonical Ample Completion and Outside Slice

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Shattered Complex
                                                                • Signed Minimal-Nonface Presentation

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Concept Deletion

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let ample $H_s,H_t\subseteq Q_F$ have common shadow $\Sigma$ and signed presentations differing only on a minimal nonface $I$, with omitted traces $s\ne t$. If $R$ satisfies all unchanged clauses and $R_u$ is its outside slice at $u\in Q_I$, then $R=H_s\cup H_t$ is ample, $A:=R_s=R_t=\bigcap_uR_u$ is nonempty and ample, $Q_I\times A\subseteq R$, and $H_t\setminus H_s=\{s\}\times A$, $H_s\setminus H_t=\{t\}\times A$. Moreover $\operatorname{Sh}(R)\setminus\Sigma=\{I\cup J:J\in\operatorname{Sh}(A)\}$. The admissible omitted traces are exactly $P=\{u:R_u=A\}$, and conversely every ample $R$ and nonempty $I$ with nonempty $A=\bigcap_uR_u$ and $|P|\ge2$ arises this way. For $u\in P$, deleting the slice $\{u\}\times A$ by corners is possible exactly when $A$ is dismantlable ample. If $|I|\ge2$ and some resulting $H_u$ is peelable or a forbidden pc-minor, then $A$ is automatically dismantlable ample.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Projection away from any coordinate of $I$ makes the two presentations identical. A difference vertex therefore has every one-bit neighbor in the other family; ampleness of the corresponding $I$-face forces a punctured cube, giving the common outside slice and the two difference formulas. The old shadow together with $I+\operatorname{Sh}(A)$ has cardinality $|R|$, so Sandwich equality proves that $R$ is ample with exactly this shadow. Imposing an omitted trace $u$ deletes $\{u\}\times R_u$; it has the original cardinality precisely when $R_u=A$, which is exactly admissibility. During deletion inside one minimal slice, corner tests factor as the corresponding corner tests in $A$, proving the relative-peeling equivalence. A second admissible slice exposes $A$ as a proper pc-minor when $|I|\ge2$.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#prop:damp-single-clause-completion

                                                                The Remote Clause Tower Has Exactly Four Admissible Signs

                                                                Name: The Remote Clause Tower Has Exactly Four Admissible Signs

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Shattered Complex
                                                                • Signed Minimal-Nonface Presentation

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Concept Deletion
                                                                • Partial-Cube Minor

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Fix every clause except the distinguished four-coordinate clause in the remote rooted tower at any level $j$. Exactly four signs are admissible. In coordinate order $(5,6,9,10)$ they are $0110,1001,0101,1101$, deleting respectively $604,1084,1116,1148$ in the base completion. The first class does not peel to zero and the other three do. The outside family is a translate of $\{01,11,10\}^j$, of order $3^j$, and the common ample completion has $(583\cdot3^j-3)/2$ concepts. The same four choices exhaust both ordinary remote forbidden-pivot stages; exactly the first is a forbidden pc-minor, every proper minor of all four peels, and all four square-completed classes are two-connected.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                At level zero, direct slice recovery in the common completion finds exactly four slices equal to the singleton outside family. The completion theorem makes this list exhaustive. Stored corner prefixes give root-ending orders for the last three signs, while the first is the rooted factor. Paired-square transfer multiplies the outside slice by the three-vertex path and introduces no new minimal slices, so the list and endpoint statuses persist inductively. Gluing the fixed factor and adding the common square tip occur only in a different old trace, preserving all four minimal slices; the rooted-block and block-peeling theorems then give the forbidden versus positive statuses, minor claims, and two-connectivity.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#cor:damp-four-sign-clause-family

                                                                A Cube Layer Can Switch Endpoints across Adjacent Clause Signs

                                                                Name: A Cube Layer Can Switch Endpoints across Adjacent Clause Signs

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Shattered Complex
                                                                • Signed Minimal-Nonface Presentation

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Peripheral Expansion
                                                                • Concept Deletion

                                                                Result Type: Construction

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let ample $S\subseteq Q_F$ peel to $a$, contain the coordinate cube $C=Q_I\times\{y\}$, and put $P_0=\{u\in Q_I:S_u=\{y\}\}$. For a fresh $f$, let $R=(S\times\{0\})\cup(C\times\{1\})$. Then $R$ is an ample single-clause completion on $J=I\cup\{f\}$ with outside family $\{y\}$ and admissible traces $P=(P_0\times\{0\})\cup(Q_I\times\{1\})$. All members have common shadow $\operatorname{Sh}(S)\cup\{T\cup\{f\}:T\subsetneq I\}$. Every upper omission peels to $(a,0)$; a lower omission at $u\in P_0$ peels to $(a,0)$ exactly when $S\setminus\{(u,y)\}$ peels to $a$. The root-retaining admissible-trace graph is connected, yet a corner deletion in $S$ that destroys the endpoint produces adjacent retained traces of opposite endpoint status.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The construction is the peripheral expansion of $S$ along $C$. Its outside slices are $S_u$ below and the singleton $\{y\}$ above, so the single-clause completion theorem gives exactly the displayed admissible set and shadow. A punctured cube peels by increasing distance from its missing vertex. Applying this first to the upper layer proves every upper choice positive and reduces a lower choice to the corresponding deletion in $S$; restricting any hypothetical lower-side endpoint order back to the lower face proves the converse. The intact upper trace cube connects every retained lower trace to the trace graph. A destructive corner $c=(u,y)$ has no neighbor outside $C$, so $u\in P_0$ and its two vertical choices give the adjacent opposite-status pair.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#prop:damp-adjacent-clause-endpoint-switch

                                                                Adjacent Endpoint Switches Reduce to Rooted Factors

                                                                Name: Adjacent Endpoint Switches Reduce to Rooted Factors

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Shattered Complex
                                                                • Signed Minimal-Nonface Presentation

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Partial-Cube Minor

                                                                Result Type: Implication

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let ample $H_s,H_t$ have the same shadow and differ only at one clause on $I$, with adjacent omitted traces differing at coordinate $f$. Suppose $H_s$ is dismantlable ample but does not peel to a common root $a$, while $H_t$ does, and the root-containing $f$-face of $H_s$ peels to $a$. Then a common sequence of root-preserving pc-minor operations avoiding $f$ produces a rooted factor from $H_s$ while the image of $H_t$ still peels to its root; the adjacent single-clause exchange persists on a subset of $I$, with outside family a nonempty pc-minor of the original outside family. Hence invariance under adjacent clause changes for rooted factors is equivalent to the claim that endpoint status is determined by the root-containing flipped-coordinate face; both claims are false. Such a switch is impossible for $|I|\le2$, and also for singleton outside family with $|I|\le3$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The common completion writes both sides as deletion of adjacent slices $\{s\}\times A$ and $\{t\}\times A$. Contraction inside $I$ identifies the two families; operations outside $I$ transport the same exchange through a nonempty minor of $A$; root restrictions in $I\setminus\{f\}$ either identify the sides or retain adjacency. Restriction in $f$ cannot retain failure because it commutes with the initially positive root face. Repeatedly take proper failing root-preserving images on the negative side; size decreases until rooted minimality, while the positive side and adjacent exchange persist. The small-support cases reduce both sides to the same peripheral-expansion endpoint test, and singleton outside slices with support at most three are low-support one-concept extensions with equal endpoint status.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#prop:damp-adjacent-exchange-minor-reduction

                                                                Witnesses:

                                                                • Four Root-Section Square Pivots of Order 900

                                                                Exact Root-Section Square-Row Criterion for Adjacent Endpoint Pivots

                                                                Name: Exact Root-Section Square-Row Criterion for Adjacent Endpoint Pivots

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Shattered Complex
                                                                • Signed Minimal-Nonface Presentation

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Concept Deletion
                                                                • Partial-Cube Minor

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $(B,0)$ be a rooted factor using every coordinate with unique corner zero, let $\alpha,\delta,\gamma$ be three compatible ample additions with distinct acquired supports and root-ending orders, and let a coordinate face $D$ contain zero and the punctured $\gamma$-cube while omitting a root neighbor. Form $Y_R$ over a fresh square by placing $D$ at $00$, the $\alpha$- and $\delta$-extensions at $01,10$, $B$ at $11$, and copies of $\gamma$ on row $R\subseteq Q_2$. Then $Y_R$ is ample exactly when $R$ is not a diagonal pair; for every ample row, $\operatorname{Sh}(Y_R)=\operatorname{Sh}(Y_\varnothing)\mathbin{\dot\cup}\{P_\gamma\cup J:J\in\operatorname{Sh}(R)\}$. Every such family is two-connected and ordinarily peelable, and all proper root-preserving pc-minors peel. It peels to $(0,00)$ exactly when $R$ contains $\{01,11\}$ or $\{10,11\}$. Thus eight of fourteen ample rows are rooted factors and six are endpoint-positive. For the four punctured-square rows, exactly omission $11$ is a rooted factor and the other three peel, yielding adjacent opposite-status signs with the same shadow.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Build the empty-row family from the paired rooted factor by reversing a peeling of $D$; each new support lifts through the other three core copies. Adding a row corner at $\gamma$ acquires the disjoint union of its old support and row support, giving the shadow formula; diagonal pairs create three new shattered supports with only two vertices and are nonample. Active-coordinate additions preserve ordinary peelability and positivity of proper rooted minors. If neither required row edge occurs, any first deletion from a nonroot core copy would force an old corner of $B$, hence zero, but its fresh-square and omitted-neighbor directions demand an absent $(h,00)$ vertex. If a required edge occurs, clear any $00$ tip and $D$, then apply the partial-tip endpoint theorem. Attachment degrees preserve two-connectivity. The single-clause completion theorem identifies the four punctured-square signs.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#thm:damp-root-section-square-pivots

                                                                • Four Root-Section Square Pivots of Order 900

                                                                Adjacent Clause Signs Can Change Forbidden-pc-Minor Status

                                                                Name: Adjacent Clause Signs Can Change Forbidden-pc-Minor Status

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Shattered Complex
                                                                • Signed Minimal-Nonface Presentation

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • One-Point Amalgam
                                                                • Concept Deletion
                                                                • Partial-Cube Minor

                                                                Result Type: Construction

                                                                Statement:

                                                                There are four 1188-concept ample classes in dimension twenty-six and VC dimension five with a common shadow, whose signed presentations vary over a square of adjacent signs at one clause. Exactly one is a pc-minimal obstruction to dismantlable ampleness; the other three peel, and every proper pc-minor of all four peels. Adding one common root-square concept gives four 1189-concept two-connected classes with the same conclusions.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Glue each 900-concept square pivot at its root to a fresh fixed rooted factor. The negative choice is the wedge of two rooted factors and hence forbidden; each positive choice peels its first block to the root and then clears the fixed block. All new cross-block clauses are common, so the unique varying clause persists. Completing the same root square on all four sides preserves the signs; the square-completed rooted-block theorem makes the negative member forbidden, while the common tip is a first corner on the positive sides. It also joins the two blocks after root deletion, proving two-connectivity. Forbidden minimality and positive pc-minor closure give the proper-minor claims.

                                                                Rooted Factors Are Periphery-Free, Product-Prime, and Stable under Small Corner Deletions

                                                                Name: Rooted Factors Are Periphery-Free, Product-Prime, and Stable under Small Corner Deletions

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Peripheral Expansion
                                                                • Cartesian Product
                                                                • Concept Deletion
                                                                • Partial-Cube Minor

                                                                Result Type: Implication

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Every rooted factor is periphery-free and Cartesian-prime. Deleting a nonroot corner of degree at most two preserves rooted-factor status. If two nonroot corners are adjacent and have degree three, deleting either one or both also preserves rooted-factor status. Consequently, if a rooted factor has a nonroot corner but no preserving nonroot-corner deletion, every nonroot corner has degree at least three, and a degree-three nonroot corner has no nonroot corner as a neighbor.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                A peripheral coordinate would express the family as a peripheral expansion whose contraction base and relevant section are proper rooted minors; their endpoint orders combine to reach the forbidden root. A nontrivial Cartesian product similarly combines root-ending orders of its two factor restrictions. For deletion, glue the factor to a fixed rooted factor to obtain a cut-vertex forbidden pc-minor. Low-degree corner descent, or adjacent degree-three-pair descent, preserves the obstruction; the resulting family still has the same cut vertex, so the cut-vertex classification forces the changed block to remain a rooted factor. Adjacent corners share their unique maximal cube and therefore have equal degree.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#cor:damp-rooted-irreducibility

                                                                An Adjacent Support-Four Corner Can Repair a Prescribed Endpoint

                                                                Name: An Adjacent Support-Four Corner Can Repair a Prescribed Endpoint

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                Result Type: Construction

                                                                Statement:

                                                                There is a 289-concept rooted factor $(B,29)$ and an ample one-concept extension $M=B\cup\{157\}$ acquiring four directions such that both $29$ and $157$ are adjacent corners of the completed four-cube and $M$ peels to either one, while deleting the nonroot corner $157$ returns $B$, which cannot peel to $29$. Thus even deletion of a corner adjacent to the root can destroy the prescribed endpoint; support size at most two cannot do so, while support four can.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The certified addition has acquired support $\{1,2,7,8\}$ and makes both endpoints corners joined in direction $7$. Stored corner orders end at each marked vertex. Deleting the new vertex exactly recovers the certified rooted factor, whose root-ending peeling is impossible. The low-support extension theorem supplies the contrasting impossibility through support two.

                                                                Component Labels Parametrize Ample One-Coordinate Expansions

                                                                Name: Component Labels Parametrize Ample One-Coordinate Expansions

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Shattered Complex
                                                                • Signed Minimal-Nonface Presentation

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Graph Expansion

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $\varnothing\ne C\subseteq A\subseteq Q_F$ be ample, let $e\notin F$, and let $K_1,\ldots,K_k$ be the connected components of $A\setminus C$. For $b\in\{0,1\}^k$, set $X_b=(C\times\{0,1\})\cup\bigcup_i(K_i\times\{b_i\})$. Then $X_b$ is ample and $\operatorname{Sh}(X_b)=\operatorname{Sh}(A)\cup\{T\cup\{e\}:T\in\operatorname{Sh}(C)\}$. Conversely, these are exactly the ample families with contraction $A$ and reduction $C$ in coordinate $e$, and the component labels are unique. More precisely, put $\mathcal I=\mathcal N(\operatorname{Sh}(C))\cap\operatorname{Sh}(A)$ and let $\tau_T$ be the unique trace missing from $C|_T$. The fiber $A(T,\tau_T)$ lies in a unique component $K_{i(T)}$; the new signed minimal nonfaces are exactly $(T\cup\{e\},(\tau_T,1-b_{i(T)}))$ for $T\in\mathcal I$, every component occurs, and a signing is admissible exactly when its new bits agree on equal component indices. Hence there are exactly $2^k$ expansions. If $A=C$, the unique construction is $A\times\{0,1\}$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Every cube $Q\subseteq A$ has $Q\setminus C$ connected when nonempty, because it is the complement of an ample face section inside a cube. It therefore lies in one component and survives in one layer. This proves that old-coordinate supports shattered by $X_b$ are strongly shattered. A support $T\cup\{e\}$ is shattered exactly when $T$ is shattered by $C$: if a trace is missing from $C|_T$, its nonempty connected fiber in $A$ lies in one component and occurs in only one layer. The displayed shadow formula and Sandwich equality give ampleness. Conversely, adjacent vertices of $A\setminus C$ cannot receive different lift bits, since the resulting square section would be an antipodal pair and would not be ample, so lift bits are constant on components. The minimal-nonface formula follows from the shadow identity. Every component occurs because a point outside $C$ violates a minimal signed clause of $C$; cardinality equality forces its support to lie in $\mathcal I$. Finally, the old clauses and the component-consistent new clauses force contraction and reduction into $A$ and $C$, while equal cardinality forces equality, proving sufficiency and uniqueness.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/component_expansion_signs.tex?#thm:damp-component-expansion-signs

                                                                Component Reflections Generate Every Fixed-Shadow Ample Family

                                                                Name: Component Reflections Generate Every Fixed-Shadow Ample Family

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Shattered Complex
                                                                • Signed Minimal-Nonface Presentation

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Elementary Down-Shift
                                                                • Graph Expansion

                                                                Result Type: Construction

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Fix a simplicial complex $\Sigma\subseteq2^F$ and a coordinate order $e_1,\ldots,e_n$. Starting from the down-set $D_\Sigma=\{x\in Q_F:\{f:x_f=1\}\in\Sigma\}$, reverse the coordinate down-shifts in that order: at each coordinate, independently choose a bit for every connected component outside the current reduction and apply the component-label expansion; if the reduction is empty, retain or reflect the constant coordinate. The outputs are exactly all ample families $H$ with $\operatorname{Sh}(H)=\Sigma$. For the prescribed order, every output uniquely determines all intermediate families and component choices. Consequently the graph of fixed-shadow ample realizations, with an edge for reflecting one component in one coordinate, is connected.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Moving every unique lift in coordinate $e$ to layer zero preserves ampleness and the shadow; on the signed minimal-nonface presentation it sets the $e$-bit of every clause containing $e$ to one and leaves every other bit unchanged. These normalizations commute. Applying all coordinates makes every missing trace all-one, producing exactly $D_\Sigma$. Reversing the normalizations and applying the component-label theorem reconstructs any target realization. After stage $j$, the intermediate family is $D_{e_{j+1}}\cdots D_{e_n}(H)$, so its clauses determine both the family and all recovered component labels uniquely. Reversing any realization's path to $D_\Sigma$ proves connectivity.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/component_expansion_signs.tex?#cor:damp-component-reflection-generation

                                                                Independent Repair Tips Give an Exact Component-Label Disjunction

                                                                Name: Independent Repair Tips Give an Exact Component-Label Disjunction

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Graph Expansion
                                                                • Concept Deletion
                                                                • Coordinate Conditioning

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $C\subseteq S\subseteq Q_F$ be nonempty ample families, where $C$ is corner-peelable and $S$ is not. Let $a_1,\ldots,a_r$ be distinct points outside $S$, with $r\ge1$, such that $A=S\cup\{a_1,\ldots,a_r\}$ is ample, every $\{a_i\}$ is a component of $A\setminus C$, and every $S\cup\{a_i\}$ is corner-peelable. In the component-label expansion, label every component in $S\setminus C$ by zero and label $\{a_i\}$ by $\varepsilon_i$. Then $X_\varepsilon$ is dismantlable ample exactly when at least one $\varepsilon_i$ is zero. For the all-one labeling, the zero section is the nonpeelable family $S$; hence this negative expansion has a proper nonpeelable section and is not a forbidden pc-minor.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Every interpolant $S\cup U$ with $U\subseteq\{a_1,\ldots,a_r\}$ is ample, since it is a section of a component-label expansion. When $U$ is nonempty, delete all but one of its tips and use the assumed peeling of $S\cup\{a_i\}$; thus every such interpolant peels. If some $\varepsilon_i=0$, first delete all tips labeled one. Every intermediate family is an ample expansion over one of these peelable interpolants and the same site $C$. What remains is a peripheral expansion with peelable base and site, so it peels. If all labels are one, conditioning to the zero section gives $S$, and pc-minor closure of dismantlable ampleness rules out a peeling of $X_\varepsilon$.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/component_expansion_signs.tex?#prop:damp-component-label-repair-disjunction

                                                                Witnesses:

                                                                • Nonlinear Peelable Sign Set in a 319-Concept Expansion

                                                                Terminal Edge-Product Attachments Have an Exact Reduction Test

                                                                Name: Terminal Edge-Product Attachments Have an Exact Reduction Test

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Common-Section Gluing
                                                                • Cartesian Product
                                                                • Full Reduction
                                                                • Partial-Cube Minor

                                                                Result Type: Construction

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $(R,0)$ be a rooted factor and let nonempty ample peelable $D\subseteq A$ satisfy the relative-attachment forbiddenness criterion, with $D$ an edge in direction $e$ and $r=\pi_eD$. Put $X=P_R(A,D)=(A\times\{0_F\})\cup(D\times R)$. Then every nonempty coordinate reduction of $X$ is dismantlable ample exactly when $A^e$ peels to $r$. There is a certified $289$-concept choice of $A\subseteq Q_{12}$ with $D=\{0,2\}$ satisfying this condition. For that input, every rooted factor $R$ produces a forbidden pc-minor of order $2|R|+287$ in $12+\dim R$ active coordinates, all of whose nonempty reductions are dismantlable ample. Every output has minimum degree at least three; if the root is the only corner of $R$, the output is cornerless.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                For every old direction other than $e$, the reduction is $A^f\times\{0_F\}$; for every direction of $R$, it is $D\times R^f$. These are positive by reduction and product closure. In direction $e$, the reduction is $(A^e\times\{0_F\})\cup(\{r\}\times R)$, a one-point amalgam of two positive pieces. Since $R$ cannot peel to its root, the vertex-gluing criterion makes this reduction positive exactly when $A^e$ peels to $r$. Forbiddenness follows from the relative-attachment minimality theorem. For the fixed input, stored relative orders verify every required elementary image and a separate order makes $A^e$ peel to $r$. Minimum degree follows because $A$ has minimum degree three and the two-connected rooted factor has minimum degree two; vertices in $D\times R$ gain the edge direction of $D$. When the root is the factor's only corner, all nonroot missing-cube witnesses survive and mixed absent squares destroy the remaining possible corner at the root.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                • Cornerless Terminal Edge-Product Obstruction of Order 865

                                                                Ample-Inclusion-Minimal Negative Classes at a Cut Vertex

                                                                Name: Ample-Inclusion-Minimal Negative Classes at a Cut Vertex

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • One-Point Amalgam
                                                                • Concept Deletion
                                                                • Full Reduction

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $X$ be ample and not dismantlable ample, and suppose every proper ample subfamily of $X$ is dismantlable ample. Then $X$ is cornerless and every coordinate reduction of $X$ is dismantlable ample. If $r$ is a cut vertex, it separates $X$ into exactly two component families and $X=A_1\vee_rA_2$. Conversely, such a vertex gluing is minimal under proper ample subfamilies exactly when each $A_i$ is dismantlable ample but does not peel to $r$, and every proper ample $B\subsetneq A_i$ peels relatively to $B\cap\{r\}$, with an empty target meaning a full peeling. The marked cut vertex uniquely recovers the two coordinate blocks and pieces up to interchange. This criterion does not assert rooted pc-minor minimality of the pieces.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                A corner of $X$ could be deleted to a proper ample positive subfamily and prefixed to its peeling, contradicting negativity. A coordinate reduction has an ample copy inside the corresponding proper section, so it is positive. At a cut vertex, all component families are proper and positive, while at least two fail to peel to the cut vertex by the one-point-amalgam criterion. The union of any two failing pieces is ample and negative, so inclusion-minimality forces exactly two. Replacing either piece by a proper ample subfamily and applying the same gluing criterion gives the required relative peeling property. Conversely, any proper ample subfamily avoiding $r$ lies in one piece and peels; one containing $r$ splits into two positive sections, at least one proper and therefore root-peelable, so the gluing criterion makes their union positive.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#prop:damp-inclusion-minimal-cut-vertex

                                                                Witnesses:

                                                                • Inclusion-Minimal Negative Classes of Orders 527 and 528

                                                                Positive Coordinate Faces Do Not Replace Contraction Tests

                                                                Name: Positive Coordinate Faces Do Not Replace Contraction Tests

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Graph Expansion
                                                                • Coordinate Conditioning
                                                                • Coordinate Projection
                                                                • One-Point Amalgam
                                                                • Partial-Cube Minor

                                                                Result Type: Construction

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $(A,0)$ and $(B,0)$ be rooted factors, on disjoint active coordinate blocks, satisfying the cut-vertex obstruction criterion. For a fresh coordinate $e$, put $X=(A\times\{0\})\cup(B\times\{1\})$, so the two roots are joined by one $e$-edge. Then $X$ is ample and every elementary pc-minor other than the $e$-projection is dismantlable ample, while $\pi_eX=A\vee_0B$ is a forbidden pc-minor. Thus every proper coordinate face of $X$ is positive, but $X$ is negative and is not itself pc-minimal.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The $e$-projection is the ample one-point amalgam $A\vee_0B$ and the $e$-reduction is the common root; the component-label expansion theorem therefore proves ampleness. The two $e$-faces are $A$ and $B$. In a coordinate of one factor, the face away from the root is a proper positive face of that factor, while the root-side face and projection replace it by a proper root-preserving minor that peels to its root. Peel this changed factor to the root, delete the root as the pendant endpoint of the joining edge, and peel the unchanged factor. Hence all those elementary images are positive. The $e$-projection is forbidden by the cut-vertex theorem, so pc-minor closure makes $X$ negative and the negative proper projection rules out forbiddenness of $X$.

                                                                Proof Source:

Joining the two roots by a fresh edge instead gives a cornerless $528$-concept negative ample class with the same proper-ample-subfamily property. It is not a forbidden pc-minor because contracting the new edge produces the negative $527$-concept class. Every coordinate reduction of both examples is dismantlable ample.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The certified rooted input is positive, has $r$ as its only corner, cannot peel to $r$, and every proper ample subfamily $B$ peels relatively to $B\cap\{r\}$. The ample-inclusion cut-vertex criterion therefore proves the $527$ assertion. For the bridge example, attach a new leaf $s$ at $r$. The resulting piece peels ordinarily but cannot peel to $s$; every proper ample subfamily peels relatively to its intersection with $s$, by reducing its old-coordinate part to the corresponding certified subfamily of $A$. Gluing this leaf-rooted piece to the other copy of $A$ gives the $528$ class and the same inclusion-minimality criterion proves its negativity and cornerlessness.                                                                 Edge Attachments Reduce Prescribed Peeling to Central Leaf Constraints

                                                                Name: Edge Attachments Reduce Prescribed Peeling to Central Leaf Constraints

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Common-Section Gluing

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $S$ be ample and attach $P_i\in\mathsf{DAmp}$ along distinct edges $E_i$ of $S$, using pairwise disjoint private coordinate blocks and meeting $S$ exactly in $E_i$. Put $Y=S\cup\bigcup_iP_i$ and let $T$ be a vertex or edge of $S$. Ignore every piece that peels to its attachment edge. For each remaining piece, let $H_i\subseteq E_i$ be its attainable peeling endpoints. Then $Y$ peels to $T$ exactly when $S$ has an acyclic USO with inward boundary at $T$ and, for each remaining piece, an ordering $(u_i,v_i)$ of $E_i$ such that $v_i\in H_i$, $u_i\notin T$, and the central out-map satisfies $r(u_i)=\{e_i\}$, where $e_i$ is the direction of $E_i$. Thus a singleton $H_i$ forces the edge orientation, $H_i=E_i$ allows either orientation, and $H_i=\varnothing$ makes peeling to $T$ impossible.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                If the union peels to $T$, restrict a witnessing acyclic USO to a nonretaining piece. Its sink cannot lie in a private vertex, since that would be a global sink outside $T$, so it is an attainable endpoint $v_i$. At the other endpoint $u_i$, the piece must have an outgoing private direction; otherwise it would have inward boundary on $E_i$ and peel to that edge. The absence of mixed squares forces the central out-map to be exactly $\{e_i\}$ at $u_i$, and the inward target boundary excludes $u_i\in T$. Conversely, choose the asserted central map and endpoint-sink maps on all nonretaining pieces; retaining pieces extend the central edge orientation with inward boundary. Two nonretaining pieces cannot use the same tail because the central out-map there would have to be two distinct singleton directions. The boundary out-maps are therefore compatible, successive edge gluing gives an acyclic USO of $Y$, and its boundary at $T$ is inward.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#prop:damp-edge-attachment-leaf-constraints

                                                                Edge Attachments Cannot Create Endpoint-Retention Failure on the Eleven-Vertex Core

                                                                Name: Edge Attachments Cannot Create Endpoint-Retention Failure on the Eleven-Vertex Core

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Full Reduction

                                                                Result Type: Implication

                                                                Statement:

                                                                In four coordinates of weights $1,2,4,8$, let $S=\{0,1,2,3,7,8,9,11,12,13,15\}$ and $T=\{0,8\}$. Attach arbitrary positive ample pieces to distinct edges of $S$ whose direction is not $8$, using disjoint private coordinates. If the assembled family peels to both $0$ and $8$, then it peels to the edge $T$. Its reduction in direction $8$ remains the path $0-1-3-7$. Hence this entire edge-attachment template cannot produce a both-endpoints retention failure over that path reduction.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                For each acyclic USO of $S$, record at every eligible attachment edge both directed singleton-out-map constraints and the corresponding undirected alternative. Exhaustive enumeration of all $2^{16}$ edge orientations finds $784$ acyclic USOs, independently reproduced from corner deletions: $69$ end at $0$, $69$ end at $8$, and $72$ have inward boundary at $T$. The pairwise intersections of the two endpoint records give $79$ distinct constraint sets, each contained in the record of a map retaining $T$. The general edge-attachment criterion converts endpoint peelings of the assembly into one of these common central constraint sets and converts the covering retaining map back into a peeling to $T$. Since every attachment is constant in coordinate $8$ and private blocks are disjoint, no attachment adds a doubled fiber to that reduction.

                                                                Distinct Central Square Sources Certify Relative Peeling after Attachment

                                                                Name: Distinct Central Square Sources Certify Relative Peeling after Attachment

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Common-Section Gluing

                                                                Result Type: Implication

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $S$ be ample, let $T$ be a vertex or edge of $S$, and attach ample pieces $P_i$ along squares $Q_i$ of $S$, with pairwise disjoint private coordinate blocks. Suppose an acyclic USO $r$ of $S$ has inward boundary at $T$. If there are pairwise distinct vertices $u_i\in Q_i\setminus T$ such that $P_i$ peels to the punctured square $Q_i\setminus\{u_i\}$ and $r(u_i)$ consists exactly of the two directions of $Q_i$, then the assembled family peels to $T$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The central orientation makes $u_i$ the source of $Q_i$. Relative USO extension lifts the orientation on $Q_i\setminus\{u_i\}$ to $P_i$ with inward boundary there, and the two source edges make the orientations agree on the whole square. Only $u_i$ can have outgoing private directions on that boundary; its central outgoing directions are exactly the square directions, so the maps are compatible. Distinct sources prevent conflicts between pieces. A directed excursion through a private block starts at its source and returns, if at all, at another square vertex; replacing it by a directed central square path would turn any global directed cycle into a directed closed walk in the acyclic central map. Thus the glued USO is acyclic, and its boundary at $T$ remains inward.

                                                                Proof Source:
