                                                                Seven Generic and Eight Concrete Square-Attachment Alignments Retain the Target Edge

                                                                Name: Seven Generic and Eight Concrete Square-Attachment Alignments Retain the Target Edge

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Common-Section Gluing

                                                                Result Type: Construction

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For the eleven-vertex core $S$, take $Q_0=(0,1,2,3)$, $Q_1=(8,9,12,13)$, and $Q_2=(9,11,13,15)$, with target edge $T=\{0,8\}$. For each $i$, let $h_i$ select the opposite pair of local hole indices $\{h_i,3\mathbin{\mathrm{xor}}h_i\}$, and suppose the attached piece can peel to the square with either selected member omitted. The square-source criterion certifies peeling to $T$ for every pattern $(h_0,h_1,h_2)$ except $(0,0,1)$; the seven source triples are $(3,13,15),(3,12,15),(3,12,13),(2,13,15),(2,13,11),(2,12,15),(2,12,13)$. Failure of this source condition for $(0,0,1)$ does not decide that generic eighth case. For the concrete $1165$-concept cube-boundary piece, all four punctured squares are attainable, so the fixed sources $(3,13,15)$ work in every alignment. All eight resulting $3494$-concept assemblies peel to $T$, including pattern $(0,0,1)$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The seven displayed central out-maps were checked by corner orders and nonclashing; at their chosen vertices the out-map masks are respectively the two directions of each attachment square, so the square-source theorem applies. In the omitted pattern, avoiding the target forces the first two sources to be $3$ and $13$; choosing source $13$ again for the third square conflicts with distinctness, while choosing $11$ forces the shared edge $3,11$ in the opposite direction from the first source. This proves only failure of the sufficient condition. The concrete boundary piece has certified relative orders for every punctured square, allowing the same first central map in every alignment; replayed orders directly certify the formerly omitted assembly.

                                                                Every Three-Piece Obstruction Has a Component-Reflection Repair

                                                                Name: Every Three-Piece Obstruction Has a Component-Reflection Repair

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Shattered Complex

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Graph Expansion
                                                                • Peripheral Expansion

                                                                Result Type: Construction

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $X=A_1\cup_DA_2\cup_DA_3$ be an ample forbidden pc-minor in its canonical three-piece presentation, let $e$ be the direction of the common edge $D$, and put $r=\pi_eD$. Some piece $A_i$ has both $U=\pi_eA_i$ and $C=A_i^e$ peelable to $r$. For either $b\in\{0,1\}$, replacing $A_i$ by the peripheral expansion $P_b=(U\times\{b\})\cup(C\times\{1-b\})$ produces a dismantlable ample class $X_b$ with the same shattered sets and cardinality as $X$. The replacement reflects only components of $(\pi_eX)\setminus X^e$ lying in the selected piece. If $k_0$ and $k_1$ are the numbers of its components currently labelled zero and one, one of the two repairs uses $\min(k_0,k_1)$ reflections. This is an upper bound; intermediate reflections need not preserve forbiddenness and the bound need not be optimal.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Three-piece boundary necessity supplies a piece admitting an endpoint sink and an endpoint leaf exit, possibly in different acyclic USOs. Contracting the common direction in the sink-ending order makes $U$ peel to $r$. Recording the first lost endpoint of each full fibre in the leaf-exit order gives a corner peeling of $C$ to $r$. In $P_b$, first peel the copy of $C$ in layer $1-b$ to $r$, using the untouched copy of $U$ for mate cubes, and then peel $U\setminus\{r\}$ in layer $b$; this peels the selected piece to $D$. In the full union it leaves an unchanged positive two-piece proper convex minor, so $X_b$ peels. The projected pieces meet only at $r\in X^e$ and have no cross edges, so every complementary component lies in one piece. The component-expansion theorem therefore preserves ampleness, shadow, and cardinality during the relabelling. The two constant labels change respectively $k_1$ and $k_0$ components.

                                                                Exterior Images Decide Rooted Minimality after a Degree-Three Corner Deletion

                                                                Name: Exterior Images Decide Rooted Minimality after a Degree-Three Corner Deletion

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Shattered Complex

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Concept Deletion
                                                                • Coordinate Projection
                                                                • Coordinate Conditioning
                                                                • Partial-Cube Minor

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $(A,a)$ be an irredundantly embedded rooted factor, let $c\ne a$ be a corner with three-coordinate incident support $P$, and put $B=A\setminus\{c\}$. Then $B$ is ample and cannot peel to $a$. Assuming $B$ is dismantlable ample, $(B,a)$ is a rooted factor exactly when every contraction outside $P$ peels to the projected root and every root-containing restriction outside $P$ that retains $c$ peels to the projected root. If one of these exterior tests fails, the corresponding image of $A$ is obtained from the image of $B$ by adding the nonroot image of $c$ with acquired support exactly $P$, and that addition repairs the prescribed endpoint. If $a$ and $c$ are adjacent corners, $B$ is automatically dismantlable ample and the displayed restrictions include all root-containing restrictions outside $P$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Corner deletion preserves ampleness, while a root-ending peeling of $B$ prefixed by $c$ would contradict rooted failure of $A$. The punctured corner cube retains all directions in $P$, and another surviving vertex in its outside-coordinate fibre keeps every other coordinate active. A contraction in $P$ identifies $c$ with a neighbor; a restriction discarding $c$ changes nothing; and a restriction in $P$ retaining $c$ makes only a support-two addition, which cannot change the old prescribed endpoint. Thus only the stated exterior images can fail. In each such image, the shadow difference remains the single support $P$, so the image of $c$ is a nonroot one-concept repair with that exact acquired support. Passing all tests gives every proper root-preserving pc-minor a root-ending peeling and hence gives the rooted-factor criterion. For adjacent corners, deleting both leaves an ample common base with two equal support-two additions; square-pair invariance and corner deletion show that $B$ is dismantlable ample.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#prop:damp-rooted-degree-three-images

                                                                Every Support-Three Endpoint Repair Descends to a Rooted Factor

                                                                Name: Every Support-Three Endpoint Repair Descends to a Rooted Factor

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Shattered Complex

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Concept Deletion
                                                                • Partial-Cube Minor

                                                                Result Type: Implication

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $S$ be ample and ordinarily peelable, let $a\in S$, and suppose that the ample one-concept extension $H=S\cup\{c\}$ acquires a three-coordinate support $P$, peels to $a$, while $S$ does not. There is a root-preserving pc-minor map using only coordinates outside $P$ such that $(T,t)=(\mu S,\mu a)$ is a rooted factor. The paired image $\mu H=T\cup\{\mu c\}$ remains an ample one-concept extension with acquired support $P$, retains the whole punctured $P$-cube at the added concept, and peels to $t$. If $a$ and $c$ are adjacent corners of $H$, their images remain adjacent degree-three corners and $t$ is a degree-two corner of $T$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Every root-preserving operation in a coordinate of $P$ makes the two images equal or leaves a support-two addition at an old root; in either case the smaller image peels to its root. Choose a root-negative pc-minor of $(S,a)$ minimal under root-preserving operations. Operations on distinct coordinates commute, so its map cannot use a coordinate of $P$. Ordinary minor closure and minimality give all rooted-factor conditions. Applying the same outside-coordinate map to $H$, the larger image remains root-positive and cannot merge with the smaller one. The difference therefore stays one concept, the shadow difference stays $P$, and the complete punctured $P$-cube survives. When the original endpoints are adjacent corners, outside restrictions retain their common cube and outside contractions preserve each singleton corner fibre and its support gain. Their images remain adjacent degree-three corners; deleting the added one leaves the root with the other two directions of that cube.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#prop:damp-minimal-rank-three-endpoint-repair

                                                                Adjacent Degree-Three Endpoint Failure Is Equivalent to Repairing a Degree-Two Rooted Factor

                                                                Name: Adjacent Degree-Three Endpoint Failure Is Equivalent to Repairing a Degree-Two Rooted Factor

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes

                                                                • Concept Deletion
                                                                • Partial-Cube Minor

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                The following are equivalent: (1) an ample family $H$ has adjacent degree-three corners $a,c$, peels to $a$, but $H\setminus\{c\}$ does not peel to $a$; (2) a rooted factor $(T,t)$ has a degree-two corner root and admits an adjacent ample one-concept addition with acquired support three that makes peeling to $t$ possible. Both profiles occur in the certified 622-to-621 example. Hence prescribed-endpoint invariance under deleting an adjacent nonroot corner already fails in degree three.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                For (1), delete both adjacent corners. Either single re-addition has the same two-coordinate acquired support; square-pair invariance makes the common base ordinarily peelable, and rank-two extension invariance makes the one-corner deletion ordinarily peelable. The support-three descent theorem then produces the rooted factor in (2), with a degree-two corner root. Conversely, the added concept in (2) is a degree-three corner whose cube contains the neighboring root. The root's two old incident directions together with their new edge are precisely that cube's directions, so the root is also a degree-three corner and deleting the new corner restores endpoint failure. The existing 621-concept factor and its 622-concept repair establish existence.

                                                                A Nonempty Reduction Can Lose a Prescribed Peeling Endpoint

                                                                Name: A Nonempty Reduction Can Lose a Prescribed Peeling Endpoint

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • VC Dimension
                                                                • Isometric Dimension
                                                                • Shattered Complex

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Peripheral Expansion
                                                                • Full Reduction

                                                                Result Type: Construction

                                                                Statement:

                                                                There is an ample family $Y$ with $579$ concepts, isometric dimension $13$, and VC dimension $4$ that peels to a marked root $r$, while its nonempty one-coordinate reduction is the $289$-concept rooted factor $B$ and cannot peel to the projected root $29$. The full fibre through $r$ is present. The only corners of $Y$ are $(157,0)$ and $(29,1)$, and every peeling ending at $r=(29,0)$ starts by deleting $(29,1)$. VC dimension four is the least possible for prescribed-endpoint failure under a nonempty reduction.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Let $M=B\cup\{157\}$ be the certified support-four endpoint repair and set $Y=(M\times\{0\})\cup(B\times\{1\})$. The peripheral-expansion shadow formula gives order $579$, dimension $13$, and VC dimension four. Clearing the upper copy of $B$ and then peeling $M$ to $29$ makes $Y$ peel to $r$, while the reduction is exactly $B$, whose unique corner $29$ must be deleted first and hence cannot be retained as an endpoint. Direct corner-cube inspection leaves only $(157,0)$ and $(29,1)$. Deleting the former produces $B\square Q_1$, whose root-containing restriction is the root-negative $B$, forcing every root-ending order to start with the latter. Finally, a reduction on a nonempty coordinate set lowers VC dimension by at least its size; below VC dimension four the reduction has VC dimension at most two and therefore peels to every prescribed concept.

                                                                Every Rooted Factor Has a Locked Opposite Section in Every Coordinate

                                                                Name: Every Rooted Factor Has a Locked Opposite Section in Every Coordinate

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • VC Dimension
                                                                • Isometric Dimension

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Coordinate Conditioning
                                                                • Full Reduction

                                                                Result Type: Implication

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Write a two-section ample family as $X=(A_0\times\{0\})\cup(A_1\times\{1\})$, with nonempty sections and overlap $C=A_0\cap A_1$. If $A_1$ peels relatively to $C$, then $X$ peels to $(a,0)$ exactly when $A_0$ peels to $a$ and $C$ is dismantlable ample. Consequently, for every active coordinate of a rooted factor, the section opposite the root has no relative peeling to its overlap. That opposite section has VC dimension at least three, uses at least six coordinates, and contains an ample $D\supsetneq C$ all of whose corners lie in $C$. Every rooted factor therefore uses at least seven coordinates.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Necessity follows by restricting a root-ending peeling to the lower section and ordering full fibres by their first deletion to obtain an ordinary peeling of the overlap. Conversely, perform the relative peeling of the upper section outside $C$; its vertices have no lower mates, so their corner cubes are unchanged. The remainder is a lower-root peripheral expansion, which peels to $(a,0)$ exactly under the two stated conditions. In a rooted factor the root-containing section is a positive proper rooted restriction and the overlap is dismantlable ample, so a relative peeling on the opposite side would contradict rooted failure. Known relative-peeling bounds force VC dimension at least three and at least six active coordinates on that side. Greedily delete opposite-side corners outside $C$ until no such deletion remains; failure of a full relative peeling makes the terminal ample family strictly larger than $C$, with all its corners in $C$.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#prop:damp-rooted-section-obstructions

                                                                Corner Cubes Characterize Initial Opposite-Section Locking

                                                                Name: Corner Cubes Characterize Initial Opposite-Section Locking

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Coordinate Conditioning

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $A$ be ample with marked concept $a$, and in every active coordinate call the section containing $a$ lower. Every corner of every opposite section lies in its overlap with the lower section if and only if $a$ belongs to the unique maximal cube of every corner $c$ of $A$. Equivalently, the coordinates on which $c$ differs from $a$ are all incident directions of $c$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                A corner of an opposite section outside the overlap has no mate across the split coordinate. Its lift is therefore a corner of $A$ with the same incident support, and the split coordinate separates it from $a$ without belonging to that support. Conversely, any such separating nonincident coordinate places the entire corner cube in the opposite section and leaves its projection as a corner outside the overlap. Excluding all such coordinates is exactly the condition that $a$ lies in every corner cube.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#lem:damp-root-in-corner-cubes

                                                                Endpoint Peelings Need Not Begin by Clearing a Coordinate Section

                                                                Name: Endpoint Peelings Need Not Begin by Clearing a Coordinate Section

                                                                • Coordinate Conditioning
                                                                • Concept Deletion

                                                                Result Type: Construction

                                                                Statement:

                                                                There is a two-connected, periphery-free, Cartesian-prime ample family $P$ of order $294$, dimension $12$, and VC dimension $3$ that peels to a marked noncorner $a$, although for every active coordinate there is no relative corner peeling to the section containing $a$. In every coordinate the opposite section nevertheless has no corner outside its overlap with the root-containing section. VC dimension three is least possible for this failure in a nontrivial ample family. A second example of order $290$ and VC dimension four has the same failure with the marked endpoint itself a corner.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                For the 294-concept example take $a=1895$; the only corner is its coordinate-zero neighbor $1894$. In every other coordinate that corner already lies in the retained root section, so no relative peeling can start. In coordinate zero, the complete deletion-state graph has six maximal orders: each removes the same seven vertices and stops with 146 opposite-section vertices. The marked endpoint belongs to the unique corner cube, so the corner-cube criterion supplies the asserted overlap condition in every coordinate. For the corner-root example use the 290-concept support-four repair rooted at $29$; its five corners share a four-cube containing the root, while all twelve root-section intervals have complete negative certificates. Below VC dimension three, the relative VC-two peeling theorem clears any chosen coordinate section and then peels it to the prescribed endpoint, proving minimality.

                                                                Original-Cube Pruning Has a Canonical Kernel but Does Not Recognize Peelings

                                                                Name: Original-Cube Pruning Has a Canonical Kernel but Does Not Recognize Peelings

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Concept Deletion

                                                                Result Type: Algorithm

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For a finite family $H$ and protected set $A\subseteq H$, repeatedly delete an unprotected vertex whenever the cube on its current incident directions is contained in the original $H$. The terminal set $K_A(H)$ is independent of all choices. It is the greatest $U$, with $A\subseteq U\subseteq H$, such that every unprotected $v\in U$ has a set $P$ of current incident directions with $v^P\notin H$; $P$ may be chosen inclusion-minimal, so all its proper subfaces occur in $H$. A corner peeling of ample $H$ to $A$ implies $K_A(H)=A$, but the converse fails for a singleton and for the empty set: a $292$-concept rooted factor has singleton kernel at its root, and a $583$-concept ample forbidden pc-minor has empty kernel. Both have VC dimension four, in dimensions twelve and twenty-four.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The deletion predicate persists because later deletions only shrink a vertex's incident support. Any set in which every unprotected vertex has an original missing-cube witness survives every allowed sequence: at its first deletion all witnessing neighbors would still be present, contradicting the predicate. The terminal set itself has such witnesses, proving it is the unique greatest fixed set. If a genuine corner peeling to $A$ existed while the kernel had an extra vertex, the first deleted kernel vertex would still have all witness neighbors, while the completing vertex was absent already in $H$, contradicting its being a corner. In the rooted counterexample the pruning begins by deleting $32$ and then $64$ because the latter's original four-cube is complete, although deleting $32$ has made that cube incomplete; this forgotten new hole explains the false positive. Certified sequences leave the stated kernels, while independent complete deletion graphs prove that the corresponding actual peelings fail.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                Replicated Extensions with Two Core Neighbors Are Two-Connected

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Cartesian Product

                                                                Result Type: Implication

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $S$ be connected with at least two vertices, let $E$ be a nonempty disjoint coordinate set, and let every added base vertex $a$ have at least two neighbors in $S$. For arbitrary row sets $R_a\subseteq Q_E$, the graph of $(S\times Q_E)\cup\bigcup_a(\{a\}\times R_a)$ is two-connected. In particular, this applies when $S$ is ample and nonpeelable and each one-concept extension $S\cup\{a\}$ is ample and peelable.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The product core $S\times Q_E$ remains connected after deleting any vertex: the other cube layers are connected, and every surviving vertex in the deleted layer has a neighbor in another layer. Every added vertex has at least two distinct neighbors in the core, so after any single vertex deletion every surviving added vertex still attaches to the surviving connected core. A resolving ample one-concept extension of a nonpeelable base has at least three base neighbors by low-support endpoint invariance, giving the final application.

                                                                Square Completion Converts Rooted Block Wedges into Two-Connected Forbidden Minors

                                                                Name: Square Completion Converts Rooted Block Wedges into Two-Connected Forbidden Minors

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Shattered Complex

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • One-Point Amalgam
                                                                • Concept Deletion

                                                                Result Type: Construction

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $(A_1,0)$ and $(A_2,0)$ be rooted factors on disjoint coordinate blocks, let $N_i$ be the directions of their root neighbors, and choose a nonempty $\Gamma\subseteq N_1\times N_2$. Starting from the one-point amalgam $A_1\vee A_2$, add $0^{\{e,f\}}$ for every $(e,f)\in\Gamma$. The result is a two-connected ample forbidden pc-minor. Its shattered complex is the union of the two block shadows and the selected cross-block pairs. Every added vertex is a degree-two corner; if each factor has only its root as a corner, these are all the corners. Conversely, if deleting a degree-two corner from a two-connected ample forbidden pc-minor creates a cut vertex, the marked family arises uniquely from this construction with one selected pair, up to interchanging the two recovered rooted factors.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The rooted-factor wedge is forbidden. Each new vertex has exactly the two root-neighbor endpoints of its cross-block square, with the old root opposite; no earlier addition realizes the missing trace. Thus every addition is ample with its selected pair as acquired support, giving the shadow formula. Rank-two extension invariance preserves nonpeelability, and the one-concept atlas preserves pc-minimality at every step. A selected square joins the two rooted blocks after deletion of the common root, and every other vertex or new tip deletion leaves a connected core, proving two-connectivity. For recovery, delete the marked degree-two corner; low-degree descent leaves a forbidden family with a cut vertex. Its two corner neighbors must lie in different cut components and their old two-edge path forces the cut vertex to be the square's opposite vertex. The cut-vertex theorem then recovers the two rooted factors, their root neighbors, and the selected coordinate pair.

                                                                Root-Protected Three-Cores Preserve Adjacent Support-Three Repairs

                                                                Name: Root-Protected Three-Cores Preserve Adjacent Support-Three Repairs

                                                                • Ample Classes

                                                                • Concept Deletion
                                                                • Partial-Cube Minor

                                                                Result Type: Implication

                                                                Statement:

                                                                In a rooted factor $(A,a)$, repeatedly deleting nonroot vertices of degree below three deletes only degree-two corners and preserves rooted-factor status. The terminal family is the unique largest induced subgraph containing $a$ in which every nonroot vertex has degree at least three. If $a$ is a degree-two corner and an adjacent support-three one-concept addition repairs its endpoint, the same addition repairs the terminal factor; its entire punctured three-cube survives and the root is the terminal factor's only degree-two vertex.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Rooted factors are two-connected, so every degree-two vertex is a corner and no smaller degree occurs. Small-corner irreducibility permits every nonroot deletion, and the usual core-containment argument gives uniqueness. For repair persistence, a nonroot degree-two vertex cannot lie in the punctured repair cube: the only candidates would form a second adjacent degree-three corner pair, and square-pair invariance after attaching a fixed bad rooted factor would make the unextended factor peel to its root. Outside the repair cube, the new tip gives such a vertex no new neighbor, so it remains a degree-two corner on both sides. Deleting it preserves both rooted failure and repaired endpoint success, leaves the punctured cube intact, and keeps the acquired support equal to the original triple. Iterating proves the claim.

                                                                Statement:

Then $H$ peels to $a$ if and only if $H\setminus\{c\}$ peels to $a$. Equivalently, for the two remaining projected restrictions $U,V$ meeting in their common edge $E=\{e_0,e_1\}$, both $U$ and $V$ peel to $e_1$ and at least one peels relatively to $E$.

Root-preserving minor closure forces both transverse restrictions to peel to the upper endpoint. Inspecting the first deletion at their four boundary vertices shows that one restriction must peel while retaining the common edge. Conversely, perform that relative peeling, delete the four exposed cube vertices in order, and finish in the other restriction. This constructs a peeling of $H-c$ to $a$; prefixing $c$ gives the forward family.

                                                                Adjacent Rank-Three Repairs Are Two-Square Endpoint Switches

                                                                Name: Adjacent Rank-Three Repairs Are Two-Square Endpoint Switches

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                An adjacent rank-three endpoint repair exists exactly when there are an ample base $G$, distinct coordinates $p,q,r$, and three missing vertices $a,c=a^{\{p\}},z=a^{\{q\}}$ of one three-cube such that $G$ contains its other five vertices, neither $\{p,r\}$ nor $\{q,r\}$ is shattered by $G$, and the two completions $S=G\cup\{z,a\}$ and $T=G\cup\{c,a\}$ have different endpoint behavior at $a$. Both sides are ample, acquire the same two square supports in opposite orders, and have the same shattered complex. The completed union has $a,c,z$ as degree-three corners. A minimum changing switch may be chosen with its bad side a rooted factor whose root is its only degree-two vertex and whose other added neighbor is a degree-three noncorner.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The five old cube vertices provide the two punctured squares, so the distinct-pair attachment theorem proves that both addition orders are ample and acquire exactly the same supports. Completing the three-cube makes the three marked vertices corners and turns unequal endpoint behavior into an adjacent repair. Conversely, minimize an adjacent repair. No successful peeling can start outside the marked cube, at the deleted corner, or at its other cube neighbors. The opposite-edge lemma excludes the remaining antipodal start, forcing a first corner adjacent to the root. Removing that corner, the deleted corner, and the root leaves precisely the required ample five-vertex base. Minimal rooted-factor and three-core reductions give the final normal form.

                                                                Small Lower Supports Cannot Change a Two-Square Endpoint

                                                                Name: Small Lower Supports Cannot Change a Two-Square Endpoint

                                                                Classes:

                                                                Result Type: Implication

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For a normalized two-square switch, write its base across coordinate $r$ as $(D\times\{0\})\cup(U\times\{1\})$, with $E=D\cap U$, $B=D\cup U$, and $d=\{p,q\}$. Then $D,U,E,B$ are ample, $\operatorname{Sh}(E)=\operatorname{Sh}(D)\cap\operatorname{Sh}(U)$, and $\operatorname{Sh}(B)=\operatorname{Sh}(D)\cup\operatorname{Sh}(U)$. If every support in $\operatorname{Sh}(D)\setminus\operatorname{Sh}(E)$ has size at most two, the two switch sides have identical endpoint behavior, equivalent both to $U$ peeling to $0$ with $E$ peeling to $d$ and to $B$ peeling to $0$ with $D$ peeling to $d$. Hence every changing switch needs a lower-exclusive support of size at least three avoiding $p,q,r$; if the bad side is a rooted factor, it also needs an upper-exclusive support of size at least three.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Trace completeness on the two unshattered switch pairs forces the lower section to have $p=q=1$ and gives the claimed square in the upper section. Ampleness converts the two-layer shattering identities into the intersection and union formulas. The relative small-support theorem peels $D\setminus E$ by degree-at-most-two corners, and these deletions lift unchanged to both switch sides. The residual family is peripheral, so its endpoint reduces to the two stated section endpoints. Applying the same theorem to $E\subseteq D$ and $U\subseteq B$ gives the final equivalence. The rooted-section obstruction supplies the symmetric upper-exclusive support requirement.

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Assume a minimum counterexample. Square-pair invariance excludes the two other neighbors of $c$ as corners, and the opposite-edge theorem excludes the remaining opposite corner. Commutation of nonadjacent corner deletions then forces every successful peeling to start with the next two marked path vertices and a uniquely determined third cube vertex. These four vertices form an entire peripheral square restriction. The peripheral endpoint criterion yields a first corner outside that square; it is simultaneously a corner of $H$ and $H-c$, and deleting it produces a smaller counterexample, a contradiction.

                                                                • Coordinate Conditioning

                                                                Result Type: Implication

                                                                Statement:

                                                                In a minimum adjacent rank-three repair, normalize the switch root to $a=0$ and its marked corners to $c=\{p\}$ and $z=\{q\}$. A successful peeling can be chosen to begin $z$, $v=\{q,r\}$, and $x=\{q,r,e\}$. There are nonempty sets $J,F$, disjoint from $\{p,q,r\}$, with $e\in J$ and $F\cap J=\varnothing$, such that the second and third corner supports are $R=\{p,q\}\cup J$ and $R'=\{p,q\}\cup(J\setminus\{e\})\cup F$. Their cubes lie in the original upper section and meet in the $e=1$ facet of the first. Thus the upper section has an exclusive shattered support of size at least three containing $p,q$, while the lower section has an exclusive support of size at least three avoiding $p,q,r$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The switch reduction chooses $z$ first. Minimality and the pointed square-pair argument exclude every next corner except $v$. Its corner cube contains the upper $\{p,q\}$-square and has support $\{p,q\}\cup J$; the four-corner path theorem forces $J$ to be nonempty. After $z,v$ are removed, local cube defects exclude every third corner inside the switch cube. Commutation forces the next corner to neighbor $v$, hence it removes one $e\in J$ and may acquire only new directions $F$ disjoint from $J$. If $F$ were empty, the three deletions could be reordered to contradict minimality. The two cubes and their common facet therefore have the asserted form.

                                                                Statement:

After translating $c$ to zero, existential-universal reductions produce two nonempty disjoint ample classes on the residual directions. For two directions these are disjoint intervals in a three-vertex path, forcing an isolated support and adjacent-marker reversal. For three directions, the exhaustive local two-shore calculation supplies disjoint minimal transversals; their union leaves at most one coordinate, giving the isolated-or-cover dichotomy.

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes

                                                                Result Type: Implication

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $K\subsetneq A$ be ample and put $D=A\setminus K$. If $K\cup\{d\}$ is nonample for every $d\in D$, then every connected component of the graph induced by $D$ has at least nine vertices. In particular, when $|D|\le17$, the residual graph is connected.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The relative Alexander-dual Yang module has a linear presentation whose annihilator and edge relations never cross residual components. It therefore splits as a direct sum over the components, and each summand has a linear resolution. The corresponding exact sequence makes $K$ together with any one component ample. If a component had at most eight concepts, the relative linear-quotient theorem through eight facets would order it with a first concept that can be adjoined amply to $K$, contradicting terminality. Two components therefore require at least eighteen concepts.

                                                                [BousquetYangComplex26]

                                                                A Small Terminal Cut Layer Must Be a Domino Wedge

                                                                Name: A Small Terminal Cut Layer Must Be a Domino Wedge

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $K\subsetneq A$ be ample, put $D=A\setminus K$, and suppose every $d\in D$ is doubly blocked. If the residual graph on $D$ has a cut vertex and $|D|\le11$, then $|D|=11$ and its block-cut tree consists of two six-vertex dominoes sharing one articulation vertex. The articulation has degree two within each domino.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The component-size theorem makes the residual graph connected, and double blocking excludes residual degree below two. Two leaf blocks then satisfy $|D|\ge|L_1|+|L_2|-1$, so one has at most six vertices. Bipartiteness and cube common-neighbor bounds leave only $C_4$, $C_6$, and the domino as possible two-connected induced-cube blocks. The degree-two carrier rules and an exhaustive symbolic passive-coordinate check exclude both cycles and a domino rooted at a degree-three vertex. Thus both leaf blocks are degree-two-rooted dominoes; together they already use eleven vertices, forcing equality and a common articulation.

                                                                Doubly Blocked Terminal Layers Through Eleven Are Two-Connected

                                                                Name: Doubly Blocked Terminal Layers Through Eleven Are Two-Connected

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes

                                                                Result Type: Implication

                                                                Statement:

                                                                If $K\subsetneq A$ are ample, every concept of $D=A\setminus K$ is doubly blocked, and $|D|\le11$, then the residual graph induced by $D$ is two-connected.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Connectivity and minimum degree two follow from the preceding terminal-component arguments. A cut vertex would force the unique eleven-vertex wedge of two degree-two-rooted dominoes. Coordinate labels reduce this wedge to two profiles, according as the middle domino directions coincide or differ. For each profile, a dimension-free passive-coordinate encoding imposes support order, carrier anchors and depths, cross-carrier cubes, marker reversal, and the degree-three dichotomy. Independently checked DRAT cores prove both relaxed formulas unsatisfiable, so no genuine doubly blocked interval has a cut vertex.

                                                                Coordinate Cost of a Two-Connected Cube Subgraph

                                                                Name: Coordinate Cost of a Two-Connected Cube Subgraph

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Active Cube-Coordinate Count

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                If $G$ is a two-connected subgraph of a Boolean cube and $Y$ is the set of coordinates appearing on its edges, then $|V(G)|\ge2|Y|$. The subgraph need not be induced or isometric.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Construct an open-ear decomposition. Every active coordinate on the initial cycle occurs a positive even number of times, so the cycle has at least twice as many vertices as new coordinates. If an ear of length $\ell$ introduces $k$ coordinates, each new coordinate occurs an even positive number of times because the endpoints are old. At least one edge uses an old coordinate, since otherwise the distinct endpoints would agree in every coordinate. Hence $\ell\ge2k+1$, and the ear contributes at least $2k$ new vertices. Summing over all ears proves the bound.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#lem:damp-two-connected-coordinate-cost

                                                                Failed One-Concept Augmentation Localizes to an Antipodal Pair

                                                                Name: Failed One-Concept Augmentation Localizes to an Antipodal Pair

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $K\subseteq Q_X$ be ample and $d\notin K$. Then $K\cup\{d\}$ is nonample if and only if there is a set $T\subseteq X$ with $|T|\ge2$ such that, for $h=d^{\oplus T}$, one has $h\in K$ and $(K\cup\{d\})\cap Q_T(d)=\{d,h\}$. Equivalently, the failed augmentation has a conditioning consisting of the two antipodes of a face of dimension at least two.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The displayed antipodal pair is a nonample conditioning, proving sufficiency. Conversely, condition $K\cup\{d\}$ until reaching a conditioning-minimal nonample class $H$. Every such conditioning contains $d$, and $H\setminus\{d\}$ is an ample conditioning of $K$. If $H$ has $n$ active coordinates and VC dimension $k$, the minimal-nonample structure theorem gives $|H|=2\sum_{i=0}^{k-1}\binom{n-1}{i}$ and all strongly shattered sets of size at most $k-1$. Since deleting $d$ cannot create strongly shattered sets and leaves an ample class, Sauer's inequality yields $\binom{n-1}{k-1}\le1$. With $1\le k\le n-1$, this forces $k=1$, so $H$ consists of two antipodes on all its active coordinates. Restoring the fixed coordinates gives the required face.

                                                                References:

                                                                [BousquetYangComplex26]

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#prop:damp-failed-augmentation-antipodal-localization

                                                                Antipodal Deletion Blockers Descend Along Their Faces

                                                                Name: Antipodal Deletion Blockers Descend Along Their Faces

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Concept Deletion

                                                                Result Type: Implication

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Suppose $v\in A\subseteq Q_X$ and $A\cap Q_J(v)=Q_J(v)\setminus\{h\}$, where $h=v^{\oplus J}$ and $|J|\ge2$. For every proper $S\subset J$, putting $w=v^{\oplus S}$ gives $A\cap Q_{J\setminus S}(w)=Q_{J\setminus S}(w)\setminus\{h\}$. If $|J\setminus S|\ge2$, then $A\setminus\{w\}$ is nonample.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The vertices of $Q_{J\setminus S}(w)$ are $v^{\oplus(S\cup T)}$ for $T\subseteq J\setminus S$; all belong to the original punctured $J$-face except the unique choice $T=J\setminus S$, which gives $h$. After deleting $w$, the complement on this subface is the antipodal pair $\{w,h\}$. In dimension at least two that pair is nonample, and conditioning together with complement duality transfers the failure to $A\setminus\{w\}$.

                                                                Five-Coordinate Passive-Owner Normal Form for Small Terminal Intervals

                                                                Name: Five-Coordinate Passive-Owner Normal Form for Small Terminal Intervals

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Active Cube-Coordinate Count

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $K\subsetneq A\subseteq Q_X$ be ample, put $D=A\setminus K$, and suppose $K\cup\{d\}$ is nonample for every $d\in D$. If the graph induced by $D$ is two-connected and $|D|\le11$, let $Y$ be its active coordinates and $Z=X\setminus Y$. Then $|Y|\le5$, every member of $D$ has one passive restriction $\sigma\in Q_Z$, and the conditioned families $L=\{k|_Y:k\in K,\ k|_Z=\sigma\}$ and $B=L\mathbin{\dot\cup}D$ are ample. The set $R=\{d\in D:L\cup\{d\}\text{ is ample}\}$ is nonempty. For every $d\in R$ there are $z\in Z$ and $c\in D$ such that $c^{\oplus z}\in K$, $d^{\oplus z}\notin K$, and $N_L(d)\cap\operatorname{Diff}(d,c)=\varnothing$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Connectedness makes every coordinate outside $Y$ constant on $D$, and the two-connected coordinate-cost inequality gives $2|Y|\le|D|\le11$. Conditioning $A$ and $K$ at the passive restriction gives the ample pair $L\subseteq B$. If $L$ is empty then $R=D$; otherwise five-coordinate relative peeling ends with an ample singleton extension of $L$, so $R$ is nonempty. For $d\in R$, the one-concept colon criterion makes $d$ teach $L$ but, by terminality, supplies a blocker in $K$. Linear presentation of the relative module gives an interval-exit path from $d$ through $D$ to $K$. Its last edge cannot use an active coordinate, since that would contradict the teaching and blocker conditions. Its passive coordinate and last residual endpoint give $z$ and $c$ with all three asserted properties.

                                                                An Isolated Passive Blocker Forms a Peripheral Active Cell

                                                                Name: An Isolated Passive Blocker Forms a Peripheral Active Cell

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Peripheral Expansion

                                                                Result Type: Construction

                                                                Statement:

                                                                In the passive-owner normal form, let $d\in R$. There are a passive coordinate $z$, a nonempty set $W\subseteq Y\setminus N_L(d)$, and an ample family $C\subseteq D\cap Q_W(d)$ containing $d$ and $d^{\oplus W}$ such that $(d^{\oplus W})^{\oplus z}\in K$. Moreover $C\cap S_z=\{d^{\oplus W}\}$, and the conditioning of $A$ to $Q_{W\cup\{z\}}(d)$ is the peripheral expansion $C\mathbin{\dot\cup}\{(d^{\oplus W})^{\oplus z}\}$ with singleton duplicated site. The cell $C$ lies in the unique minimal active carrier of $d$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Localize the failure of $K\cup\{d\}$ to an antipodal pair $\{d,h\}$ on a face $Q_T(d)$. An interval-exit path inside $D\cap[d,h]$ ends with an edge to $h$. That edge must use a passive coordinate $z$; an active exit would put another member of $K$ in the isolated face. Thus $W=T\setminus\{z\}$ is nonempty and $h^{\oplus z}=d^{\oplus W}$. Isolation also gives $W\cap N_L(d)=\varnothing$. Conditioning $A$ on the active $W$-face produces an ample family $C$ on the residual side and only the mate of $d^{\oplus W}$ on the opposite passive side, proving the peripheral-expansion and unique-owner assertions. Agreement with $d$ on $N_L(d)$ places all of $C$ in its unique minimal carrier.

                                                                Passive Boundary Types Have a Common Owner over an Empty Active Slice

                                                                Name: Passive Boundary Types Have a Common Owner over an Empty Active Slice

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes

                                                                Result Type: Implication

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $K\subsetneq A\subseteq Q_{Y\mathbin{\dot\cup}Z}$ be ample, put $D=A\setminus K$, and suppose all members of $D$ have one passive restriction $\sigma\in Q_Z$, while no member of $K$ has restriction $\sigma$. For $z\in Z$ let $S_z=\{d\in D:d^{\oplus z}\in K\}$ and $Z_0=\{z:S_z\ne\varnothing\}$. If $Z_0$ is nonempty, then $\bigcap_{z\in Z_0}S_z$ is nonempty.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                For every active projection $D\to D|_Q$, label each fiber by the passive boundary types it meets. Boolean differences of the numbers of fibers with each label are sums of fine numerator coefficients of the relative Yang module of $(A,K)$. Since both endpoints are ample, that module is Cohen--Macaulay and all these coefficients are nonnegative. The unique fiber over the empty active projection meets every nonempty $S_z$, so its full-label coefficient is one. Möbius inversion implies that at least one fiber over all of $Y$ still has the full label. Projection to $Y$ is injective because every residual concept has the same passive restriction, so this fiber is a singleton belonging to every $S_z$.

                                                                References:

                                                                [BousquetYangComplex26]

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#lem:damp-empty-active-slice-passive-helly

                                                                Passive Boundary Types Incident with a Minimal Active Carrier Share an Owner

                                                                Name: Passive Boundary Types Incident with a Minimal Active Carrier Share an Owner

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes

                                                                Result Type: Implication

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $K\subsetneq A$ be ample and let $D=A\setminus K$ be connected. In the induced active slice $L\subseteq B=L\mathbin{\dot\cup}D$, let $E_P$ be the carrier of an inclusion-minimal support $P\in\operatorname{Sh}(B)\setminus\operatorname{Sh}(L)$. For passive boundary types $S_z=\{d\in D:d^{\oplus z}\in K\}$, put $Z_P=\{z:E_P\cap S_z\ne\varnothing\}$. If $Z_P$ is nonempty, then $E_P\cap\bigcap_{z\in Z_P}S_z$ is nonempty.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Condition both $A$ and $K$ on the unique active trace on $P$ missed by $L$. Their relative concepts are exactly $E_P$, all with the common passive restriction, and the corresponding lower active slice is empty. The empty-slice passive Helly lemma therefore applies; its nonempty boundary types are precisely the sets $E_P\cap S_z$ for $z\in Z_P$, and it supplies their common owner.

                                                                A Blocked Active Root Transfers to Carrier Depth Two

                                                                Name: A Blocked Active Root Transfers to Carrier Depth Two

                                                                Result Type: Implication

                                                                Statement:

                                                                In a two-connected terminal interval of order at most eleven, let $d$ be an active root for which $L\cup\{d\}$ is ample. The unique minimal active carrier $E_P$ containing $d$ contains a concept $o\ne d$ that belongs to at least two minimal active carriers.

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The one-concept colon criterion identifies $P=N_L(d)$ as the unique minimal support represented by $d$. A passive blocker meets $E_P$ without containing $d$. Choose the common owner $o$ of all passive boundary types incident with $E_P$; then $o\ne d$. If $o$ belonged to only $E_P$, the local one-concept criterion would make $L\cup\{o\}$ ample with unique carrier $E_P$. Applying the passive-root cover to $o$ would produce an incident passive boundary type omitting $o$, contradicting its choice as common owner. Hence $o$ has carrier depth at least two.

                                                                A Passive Coordinate Determines Two Nested Ample Shores

                                                                Name: A Passive Coordinate Determines Two Nested Ample Shores

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Coordinate Conditioning

                                                                Result Type: Construction

                                                                Statement:

                                                                In the active/passive normalization of an ample pair $K\subsetneq A$, fix a passive coordinate $z$ and put $M_z=\{u\in Q_Y:\widehat u^{\oplus z}\in K\}$. Then $S_z=D\cap M_z$. Whenever nonempty, each of $L\cap M_z$, $B\cap M_z$, $L\cup M_z$, and $B\cup M_z$ is ample. Moreover $(B\cap M_z)\setminus(L\cap M_z)=S_z$ and $(B\cup M_z)\setminus(L\cup M_z)=D\setminus S_z$. Thus a passive boundary type and its complement are relative facets of two nested ample pairs on the same active coordinates.

Its two sections are $L$ and $M_z$; the two-layer shadow-intersection lemma makes their union and intersection ample. The same conditioning of $A$ has sections $B$ and $M_z$, because every relative concept lies on the common passive side, so the same lemma handles the two families involving $B$. The shore identities follow from $B=L\mathbin{\dot\cup}D$ and the definition of $M_z$.

                                                                Passive Neighbors Force a Punctured Cube Fiber

                                                                Name: Passive Neighbors Force a Punctured Cube Fiber

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $K\subsetneq A$ be ample, let $D=A\setminus K$ have one passive restriction, and let $L$ be the corresponding active lower slice. For $d\in D$, let $Z(d)=\{z:d^{\oplus z}\in K\}$ and $t(d)=|Z(d)|$. Then $d^{\oplus T}\in K$ for every nonempty $T\subseteq Z(d)$, and $|K|\ge |L|+\sum_{d\in D}(2^{t(d)}-1)$. If $L$ is nonempty and $Z_0=\{z:S_z\ne\varnothing\}$, then every $z\in Z_0$ contributes an additional collar vertex and $|K|\ge |L|+|Z_0|+\sum_{d\in D}(2^{t(d)}-1)$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Condition $K$ on the active word of $d$ and all passive coordinates outside $Z(d)$. The resulting ample family contains every singleton of $Q_{Z(d)}$ but not the empty word. Its ample complement contains the empty word; isometry prevents it from containing any other word because a geodesic would begin with a forbidden singleton. Hence the conditioned family is the punctured cube. Fibers belonging to distinct $d$ have distinct active restrictions, giving the first count. When $L$ is nonempty, the ample two-section class in every nonempty passive direction is connected, so its sections $L$ and $M_z$ intersect. Choosing one intersection point per direction gives pairwise distinct collar vertices outside the punctured fibers and proves the strengthened count.

                                                                Every Nonempty Passive Shore Contains an Active Root

                                                                Name: Every Nonempty Passive Shore Contains an Active Root

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes

                                                                Result Type: Implication

                                                                Statement:

                                                                In a two-connected terminal ample interval of order at most eleven, the active lower slice $L$ is nonempty, and every nonempty passive shore $S_z$ contains some $d$ for which $L\cup\{d\}$ is ample.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                If $L$ were empty, every residual concept would be an active root. The passive Helly theorem would give a common owner of all nonempty shores, while the passive-root cover applied to that owner would require a shore omitting it, a contradiction. Thus $L$ is nonempty. For a nonempty $S_z$, the corresponding opposite active section $M_z$ meets $L$. The nested ample pair $L\cap M_z\subsetneq (B\cap M_z)$ lives on at most five coordinates, so relative peeling supplies a first point $p\in S_z$. The expansion-separator augmentation lemma lifts this first relative addition from the intersection to $L$, proving $L\cup\{p\}$ ample.

                                                                Passive Shores Absorb into Ample Gates and Lower Blocker Rank

                                                                Name: Passive Shores Absorb into Ample Gates and Lower Blocker Rank

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes

                                                                Result Type: Construction

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For every nonempty passive shore $S_z$ in the small terminal normal form, the gate $G_z=L\cup S_z$ is ample. There is a saturated ample chain from $L$ to $B$ that adds every member of $S_z$ before every member of $D\setminus S_z$. If $d\notin S_z$ has a peripheral blocker cell $C$ for the same $z$, with active support $W$ and duplicated endpoint $c=d^{\oplus W}$, then $C\cap G_z=\{c\}$ and $(G_z\cup\{d\})\cap Q_W(d)=\{d,c\}$. Thus the blocker descends to the active face when $|W|\ge2$ and disappears as a named blocker when $|W|=1$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Relative peeling of $L\cap M_z\subsetneq B\cap M_z$ orders the shore. Repeatedly applying the expansion-separator duplication lemma lifts each prefix to an ample family over $L$, ending at $G_z$. A second relative peeling appends the complement shore and gives the two-block saturated chain. The peripheral cell lies in $D$, meets $S_z$ only at $c$, and is otherwise disjoint from $G_z$; restricting $G_z\cup\{d\}$ to its active face therefore leaves exactly the antipodal pair $\{d,c\}$. Antipodal localization proves nonampleness in rank at least two, while rank one is the full edge.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#lem:damp-passive-shore-absorption

                                                                A Terminal Fiber Forces Lower and Upper Directed Root Cycles

                                                                Name: A Terminal Fiber Forces Lower and Upper Directed Root Cycles

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes

                                                                Result Type: Construction

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Assume the small two-connected interval is terminal under both one-concept addition to $K$ and one-concept deletion from $A$. Every nonempty passive shore contains a lower active root, and every nonempty complementary shore contains an upper deletion root. Both root sets have at least two members. On the lower roots there is a loopless directed graph of positive out-degree in which $d\to e$ is separated by a shore containing $e$ but not $d$, together with an isolated peripheral blocker cell, a non-root common owner, and an ample shore gate. The graph contains a directed cycle of length at least two; complement duality gives an analogous upper-root cycle.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The passive-shore root theorem gives the lower assertions, and applying it to the complementary ample pair gives the upper assertions and a two-block chain beginning and ending with the respective roots. Each lower root has a peripheral blocker shore that omits it; choose a different lower root in that shore as its outgoing neighbor. The common-owner theorem supplies a shore owner of carrier depth at least two, hence outside the lower-root set. Every root has a nonloop outgoing edge, so finiteness yields a directed cycle and at least two roots. Applying the same argument to the complementary pair gives the upper cycle.
