                                                                Terminal Root Cycles Couple as Two-Sided Passive-Gate Holonomy

                                                                Name: Terminal Root Cycles Couple as Two-Sided Passive-Gate Holonomy

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes

                                                                Result Type: Construction

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $\mathscr S$ be the distinct nonempty proper passive shores of a two-sided terminal fiber. It is nonempty. For each $S\in\mathscr S$, choose a two-block peeling with first lower root $r_S\in R\cap S$ and last upper root $u_S\in R^+\cap(D\setminus S)$. There are self-maps $\lambda,\mu$ of $\mathscr S$ such that $r_S\in S\setminus\lambda(S)$ and $u_S\in\mu(S)\setminus S$. Neither map has a fixed point, so both contain directed cycles. If there are exactly two shores $S,T$, then $r_S,u_T\in S\setminus T$ and $r_T,u_S\in T\setminus S$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                A lower root has a nonempty proper blocker shore, proving $\mathscr S$ nonempty. Passive-shore absorption supplies the two-block peeling and its endpoint roots. Apply the blocker-cell theorem to $r_S$ and define $\lambda(S)$ to be a shore omitting it; apply the complementary theorem to $u_S$ and define $\mu(S)$ to be a shore containing it while the opposite shore omits it. The asymmetric differences forbid fixed points, and finite fixed-point-free self-maps contain cycles. On a two-element shore set both maps interchange the shores, giving the crossed profile.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#cor:damp-two-sided-passive-gate-holonomy

                                                                Exponential Cost and Equality Form of Passive-Gate Holonomy

                                                                Name: Exponential Cost and Equality Form of Passive-Gate Holonomy

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $S_1,\ldots,S_k$ be a directed cycle of the lower shore map, let $t(d)$ count all passive shores containing $d$, let $t_{\mathcal C}(d)$ count cycle shores containing it, and let $Z_0$ be the active passive directions. With $\eta=|K|-|L|-|Z_0|-\sum_d(2^{t(d)}-1)$, one has $\eta\ge0$, $|K|-|L|\ge |Z_0|+\sum_d(2^{t(d)}-1)\ge3k$, and an exact nonnegative excess decomposition into $\eta$, $|Z_0|-k$, the exponential incidence excesses, and $|S_i|-2$. Equality $|K|=|L|+3k$ forces pairwise disjoint two-concept shores, each realized by one passive coordinate; every shore is an active root--owner edge, its opposite section is a three-vertex path, the corresponding active--passive square lies in $A$, the $k$ squares are vertex-disjoint, and these attached arms exhaust $K\setminus L$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Every cycle shore contains a lower root and a distinct non-root common owner, so its size is at least two and the cycle has at least $2k$ incidences. Also $t(d)\ge t_{\mathcal C}(d)$, $2^{t(d)}-1\ge t(d)$, and at least $k$ passive coordinates realize the distinct cycle shores. The punctured-fiber and collar count gives the bound and, after subtracting $3k$, the exact sum of nonnegative excess terms. Equality forces all inequalities to be equalities: every $t(d)$ is at most one, shores are disjoint pairs with unique coordinates, and no uncounted vertices remain. Shore absorption and the one-concept criterion force each root--owner pair to be an active edge. Equality in the collar count leaves one collar point and a three-vertex opposite path per shore; flipping the root--owner edge yields a full square, and the disjoint active endpoints and passive restrictions make these squares vertex-disjoint and exhaustive.

                                                                An Off-Cycle Passive Shore Costs Its Order Plus One

                                                                Name: An Off-Cycle Passive Shore Costs Its Order Plus One

                                                                • Ample Classes

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For a directed holonomy cycle of length $k$, put $\varepsilon=|K|-|L|-3k$. Every nonempty passive shore satisfies $|S_z|\le\varepsilon+2$ when it is a cycle shore and $|S_z|\le\varepsilon-1$ otherwise. Equivalently, a cycle shore costs at least $|S_z|-2$ units of excess, while a shore outside the cycle costs at least $|S_z|+1$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                A cycle shore contributes its explicit $|S_i|-2$ summand to the holonomy excess decomposition. An off-cycle shore uses an additional passive coordinate, contributing at least one to $|Z_0|-k$. Every concept it contains has one more passive incidence than its cycle incidence, so its exponential incidence term contributes at least one more. These $|S_z|+1$ nonnegative charges give the second bound.

Then $0\le\varepsilon\le2$, and $\varepsilon$ is exactly the sum of the uncounted remainder, $|Z_0|-2$, all exponential incidence excesses, and $(|S_1|-2)+(|S_2|-2)$. Consequently $|Z_0|\le4$ and there are at most four distinct nonempty proper shores. If $|K|=7$, then $|L|=1$, $\varepsilon=0$, and the complete pendant two-arm normal form holds.

Since $k\ge2$, it follows that $k=2$ and the excess lies between zero and two. Substitution into the exact holonomy excess decomposition gives the asserted budget and its bounds on coordinates and shore types. At order seven every inequality is sharp, so the equality classification applies.

The ample gate $L\cup S$ and its first prefix $L\cup\{r\}$ are ample, whereas $L\cup\{o\}$ is not. If $r$ and $o$ were nonadjacent, a blocker in $L$ for adding $o$ would survive after adding $r$, contradicting ampleness of the gate by the one-concept colon criterion.

                                                                One-Unit Holonomy Anomalies Form a Trichotomy

                                                                Name: One-Unit Holonomy Anomalies Form a Trichotomy

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For a two-arm holonomy cycle with excess $\varepsilon=1$, exactly one configuration occurs: two disjoint two-concept shores with one uncounted lower-fiber vertex; two two-concept shores meeting in their common non-root owner; or disjoint shores of orders two and three. No additional nonempty passive coordinate occurs at cost one. If $\varepsilon=2$ and there are three nonempty passive coordinates, the third shore is a singleton disjoint from the two disjoint two-concept cycle shores, and the uncounted remainder is zero.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                In the exact two-arm budget, all terms are nonnegative integers. At excess one, an extra coordinate would itself cost one and every concept in its shore would add another exponential-incidence charge, so exactly the two cycle coordinates occur. The only remaining unit can be the uncounted remainder, one shared incidence of the two shores, or one additional shore member, giving the three cases. Gate holonomy shows that a shared concept cannot be either root, hence is the common owner. At excess two with a third coordinate, its coordinate charge and one concept charge exhaust the budget; overlap with a cycle shore would cost more, forcing the stated singleton profile.

                                                                The Shared-Owner One-Unit Holonomy Anomaly Is Impossible

                                                                Name: The Shared-Owner One-Unit Holonomy Anomaly Is Impossible

                                                                • Ample Classes

                                                                Statement:

                                                                In the two-arm terminal setting with $|K|\le9$ and excess one, two two-concept cycle shores cannot meet in a common non-root owner. Hence the only one-unit profiles are an uncounted remainder of one with two disjoint two-concept shores, or disjoint cycle shores of orders two and three.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Assume the shores are $\{r_1,o\}$ and $\{r_2,o\}$. Each root--owner pair is an active edge in a distinct direction. With zero uncounted remainder, each opposite collar is an ample three-vertex path and the punctured passive fiber over $o$ is forced. Since $|K|\le9$, the active lower slice has at most two vertices. Exhausting whether the collar roots coincide and which endpoint each collar meets shows that the one-inclusion graph of $K$ is a six- or eight-cycle with only tree edges attached and no square. If there are $t$ attached tree edges and the cycle has length $2m$, the isometric dimension is $m+t$, so only the empty set and $m+t$ singletons are strongly shattered. Thus $|\operatorname{SSh}(K)|=1+m+t<2m+t=|K|$, contradicting ampleness.

Two-connectivity invokes the passive-gate normalization and small-lower-family theorem, giving the two-cycle, exact budget, and $|B|\ge|L|+6\ge7$.                                                                 A Crossed Acquired Pair Freezes Its Common Carrier

                                                                Name: A Crossed Acquired Pair Freezes Its Common Carrier

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes

                                                                Result Type: Implication

                                                                Statement:

                                                                In an ample two-layer family with common section $B$, suppose one wing acquires $\{x,y\}$ and the other acquires $\{x,z\}$, while $B$ shatters the three singletons. Then the projections of $B$ to $\{x,y\}$ and $\{x,z\}$ are uniquely punctured squares, the corresponding triples with the layer coordinate are minimal nonfaces with oppositely layered omitted traces, and every $x$-edge of $B$ has the same forced $y$- and $z$-values. Hence distinct distinguished $x$-edges are joined inside the connected $x$-carrier by a path of $\{x,t\}$-squares using neither partner direction.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Projection preserves ampleness. Since $B$ shatters both singletons but not the pair, each two-coordinate projection has three concepts and is a uniquely punctured square by Sandwich equality. Shadow intersection makes the opposite wing omit the same trace, so the three-coordinate projection with the layer bit is a once-punctured cube and the triple is a minimal nonface. An $x$-edge using the omitted $y$- or $z$-value would realize the missing trace, forcing both partner values on every such edge. The anchor set of an $x$-carrier in an ample family is connected; with $y,z$ constant, every transport step uses another coordinate $t$ and corresponds to a full $\{x,t\}$-square.

                                                                An Ample One-Vertex Completion of a Tree Is a Square Fan

                                                                Name: An Ample One-Vertex Completion of a Tree Is a Square Fan

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Trees

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $B$ be ample, let $v\in B$, and suppose $T=G(B)-v$ is a nonempty tree. If $d=\deg_{G(B)}(v)$ and the square link $\Lambda_v$ has the $d$ directions incident with $v$ as vertices, adjacent exactly when their square through $v$ belongs to $B$, then $\Lambda_v$ is a tree. Every cube of dimension at least two is a square through $v$, $B$ has exactly $d-1$ squares, every direction not incident with $v$ labels one edge, and an incident direction $i$ labels $1+\deg_{\Lambda_v}(i)$ edges.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                A square avoiding $v$ would be a cycle in $T$, and a cube of dimension at least three has a square face avoiding $v$. Connectedness of each coordinate carrier in an ample family gives the asserted edge multiplicities and makes the square link a forest: a link cycle would subdivide to a cycle in $T$. If $r$ is the number of active directions and $q=|E(\Lambda_v)|$, carrier counting gives $|E(G(B))|=r+2q$, while the tree completion gives $|E(G(B))|=|B|-2+d$. Ampleness and the absence of larger cubes give $|B|=1+r+q$. Hence $q=d-1$, so the forest on $d$ vertices is a tree.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#lem:damp-ample-one-vertex-tree-square-fan

                                                                An Ample Two-Vertex Completion of a Tree Is a Two-Apex Square Complex

                                                                Name: An Ample Two-Vertex Completion of a Tree Is a Two-Apex Square Complex

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Trees

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $B$ be ample and let distinct $u,v\in B$ satisfy that $G(B)-\{u,v\}$ is a nonempty tree. Every cube of dimension at least two is a square meeting $\{u,v\}$, no two squares have the same direction support, and the number of squares is $q(B)=\deg_B(u)+\deg_B(v)-\mathbf 1_{uv\in E(G(B))}-2$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                A square avoiding both apices would be a cycle in the remaining tree. Every cube of dimension at least four has a square face avoiding two prescribed vertices; a three-cube either has an opposite square avoiding both or, when the apices are antipodal, leaves a six-cycle after their deletion. Thus only squares remain. The connected ample carrier of a fixed square support cannot contain two anchors, since consecutive anchors would create a three-cube, so supports are unique. With $r$ active directions, $n=|B|$, and $q$ squares, ampleness gives $n=1+r+q$ and the edge-shadow identity gives $|E(G(B))|=r+2q$. Restoring the apices to the $(n-2)$-vertex tree gives $|E(G(B))|=n-3+\deg(u)+\deg(v)-\mathbf 1_{uv\in E}$; substitution yields the formula.

                                                                A One-Vertex Completion of a Unicyclic Graph Has a Controlled Square Link

                                                                Name: A One-Vertex Completion of a Unicyclic Graph Has a Controlled Square Link

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $B$ be ample, let $v\in B$, and suppose $T=G(B)-v$ is connected and unicyclic with at most one square. Write $q_0\in\{0,1\}$ for the number of squares in $T$, $d=\deg_B(v)$, and $\Lambda_v$ for the square link at $v$. Then $B$ has no cube of dimension at least three, every square support occurs once, and $B$ has exactly $d$ squares, of which $d-q_0$ contain $v$. If $q_0=0$, $\Lambda_v$ is connected and unicyclic; if $q_0=1$, the unique cycle of $T$ is that square and $\Lambda_v$ is a tree.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                A three-cube avoiding $v$ leaves six squares in $T$, while one containing $v$ leaves three opposite square faces there, contradicting the hypothesis; connected support carriers then make square supports unique. If $r$ is the number of active directions, $q$ the number of squares, and $n=|B|$, ampleness gives $n=1+r+q$ and $|E(G(B))|=r+2q$. Since the unicyclic graph $T$ has $n-1$ edges and restoring $v$ adds $d$, one gets $q=d$ and $|E(\Lambda_v)|=d-q_0$. A cycle in the link subdivides to a cycle in $T$, so its cycle rank is at most one. The two possible edge counts then force respectively a connected unicyclic link or a tree.

                                                                The Pure Two-Unit Holonomy Anomaly Has Two Square Apices

                                                                Name: The Pure Two-Unit Holonomy Anomaly Has Two Square Apices

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                In the small lower-family two-arm setting, suppose $|K|\le9$, a directed two-cycle has excess $\varepsilon=2$, the uncounted remainder is $\eta=2$, there are exactly two passive directions, every carrier-excess term vanishes, and both cycle shores have order two. Then the active slice has order one, $|K|=9$, and the two uncounted vertices $u,v$ satisfy $G(K)-\{u,v\}=P_7$, the path formed by attaching two pendant three-edge arms to the active vertex. All squares of $K$ are uniquely supported and meet an apex, with $q(K)=\deg_K(u)+\deg_K(v)-\mathbf1_{uv\in E(K)}-2$. At most one of the two terminal arm-support pairs is shattered by $K$, so at least one is acquired by the upper family.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Equality in every counted budget term forces disjoint active-edge shores, one passive direction and collar per shore, two pendant three-edge arms, and $|K|=|L|+8$. The shore-root lemma and $|K|\le9$ give $|L|=1$ and $|K|=9$, leaving exactly two apices outside the resulting $P_7$; the two-apex square-complex lemma gives the square structure and count. Any square on a terminal support must contain both apices, because deleting a single apex would leave a forbidden two-edge path in $P_7$. The two terminal directions are distinct, or convexity of their common semicube would identify the disjoint active shores. Thus the terminal supports are disjoint. Two such squares cannot both use the same apex pair, whether the apices are adjacent or opposite, so at most one terminal pair is shattered below; both are shattered above.

                                                                The Two-Unit Holonomy Budget Has Exactly Seven Profiles

                                                                Name: The Two-Unit Holonomy Budget Has Exactly Seven Profiles

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For a directed two-cycle with excess $\varepsilon=2$, and up to interchanging its shores $S_1,S_2$, exactly seven profiles occur: (1) $\eta=2$ with disjoint two-concept shores; (2) $\eta=1$ with two two-concept shores meeting once; (3) $\eta=1$ with disjoint shores of orders two and three; (4) $\eta=0$ with shores of orders two and three meeting once; (5) $\eta=0$ with disjoint shores of orders two and four; (6) $\eta=0$ with disjoint three-concept shores; or (7) $\eta=0$ with disjoint two-concept cycle shores and a third passive coordinate having a singleton shore disjoint from their union. In profiles 1--6 there are exactly two passive directions, each cycle shore has a unique representative, and all other passive shores are empty. Precisely profiles 1--3 have an uncounted lower vertex.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The exact excess identity writes $2$ as the sum of the nonnegative integers $\eta$, the cost of passive directions beyond two, the carrier-incidence excesses, and the two shore-size excesses. Extra passive directions cost at least two units, so there are at most three. Equality with three forces profile 7. With two directions, both cycle shores have unique representatives and the carrier excess equals $a=|S_1\cap S_2|$. Writing $x=|S_1|-2$ and $y=|S_2|-2$ reduces the identity to $\eta+a+x+y=2$. Enumerating its nonnegative solutions, excluding $a=2,x=y=0$ because the two shores must be distinct, gives profiles 1--6 and shows that exactly the first three have $\eta>0$.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#cor:damp-two-unit-holonomy-seven-profiles

                                                                A Disjoint Passive Shore Forces an Acquired Terminal Square

                                                                Name: A Disjoint Passive Shore Forces an Acquired Terminal Square

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes

                                                                Result Type: Implication

                                                                Statement:

                                                                In the active--passive normalization, suppose the active slice is the singleton $L=\{a\}$ and a passive shore $S_z$ is disjoint from every other passive shore. If $S_z$ contains an active edge $xy$ of direction $f$, then $\{z,f\}\in\operatorname{Sh}(A)\setminus\operatorname{Sh}(K)$. Thus the terminal square over that shore edge is genuinely acquired by the upper family, regardless of other vertices of $K$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The vertices $x,y,x^{\oplus z},y^{\oplus z}$ form a full $\{z,f\}$-square in $A$. If $K$ also shattered this pair, ampleness would give a second full square in $K$. The anchors of all such squares form a connected ample carrier, so an anchor path joins the displayed split square to the square in $K$. The first step changing another passive coordinate $w$ starts from a square whose base-layer side contains two vertices; since $L$ is a singleton, one is a lower concept $d$. The adjacent squares then put both $d^{\oplus z}$ and $d^{\oplus w}$ in $K$, implying $d\in S_z\cap S_w$, contrary to shore disjointness.

                                                                At Most One Uncounted Vertex Separates Disjoint Shore Directions

                                                                Name: At Most One Uncounted Vertex Separates Disjoint Shore Directions

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes

                                                                Result Type: Implication

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Suppose the active slice is $L=\{a\}$, the nonempty passive shores are pairwise disjoint, and the uncounted remainder satisfies $\eta\le1$. If distinct shores $S_z,S_w$ contain active edges of directions $f_z,f_w$, then $f_z\ne f_w$. Consequently the active--passive pairs $\{z,f_z\}$ and $\{w,f_w\}$ are disjoint.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                If both shore edges had direction $f$, their passive flips would be two $f$-edges of $K$ in the one-coordinate layers $\sigma\oplus z$ and $\sigma\oplus w$. Their anchor family is ample and connected. At the first anchor-path step that changes the passive restriction, the new edge lies either in the base layer, which contains only the singleton lift and no edge, or in a layer with at least two passive flips. Pairwise shore disjointness puts all forced fibres and collars in one-coordinate layers, so both endpoints in the latter layer would be uncounted, forcing $\eta\ge2$. Both possibilities contradict the assumptions.

                                                                Feasible Uncounted Two-Unit Profiles Are Pair-Rich

                                                                Name: Feasible Uncounted Two-Unit Profiles Are Pair-Rich

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For a two-unit holonomy wing with lower family $K$ of order at most nine, the three profiles having an uncounted lower vertex behave as follows. The $\eta=2$ profile has the two-apex $P_7$ normal form and both terminal pairs are acquired; the $\eta=1$ profile with two two-concept shores meeting in one concept is impossible; and the $\eta=1$ profile with disjoint shores of orders two and three has $|L|=1$, $|K|=9$, and an acquired terminal pair from each shore. In every feasible case the two acquired pairs are disjoint.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                In the $\eta=2$ profile, the terminal pairs from the two-apex normal form are disjoint, so the disjoint-shore terminal-square lemma makes both acquired. In the intersecting $\eta=1$ profile, exact counting gives a singleton active slice and one uncounted vertex; deleting it leaves a square-free shared-owner eight-cycle. The unicyclic square-link theorem forces this cycle to be the subdivision of a four-cycle link, whose direction sequence has no direction on opposite edges, whereas the shore provenance puts every direction on opposite edges. For the disjoint $2$--$3$ profile, exact counting again gives $|L|=1$ and $|K|=9$; each shore contains an active edge, the disjoint-shore lemma makes both terminal pairs acquired, and the one-uncounted direction lemma makes them disjoint.

Hence every feasible two-unit wing is pair-rich.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Exact counting gives $|L|=1$, $|K|=9$, and a complete description by collars and punctured fibres. In each remaining profile, every cycle shore is disjoint from all other nonempty shores and contains an active edge. Below, its collar is the only edge in the passive direction, so the associated active--passive pair is not shattered; above, the shore edge and its flip form the full square. Applying this to both cycle shores gives acquired pairs, and the direction-separation lemma makes them disjoint.

                                                                A Small Three--Four Arm Decomposition Is Intrinsic Except on a Path

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Proof:

The only ambiguous rooted component is a path rooted at an endpoint. Attaching paths of lengths three and four to a one-vertex core gives $P_8$; attaching them to opposite ends of a two-vertex core gives $P_9$; attaching them to the same end creates a unique degree-three vertex with branch lengths $1,3,4$. Comparison with the intrinsic sharp-arm decomposition then identifies the ordinary arm in all remaining cases.

                                                                The Eta-One Holonomy Anomaly Is a Tree of Squares

                                                                Name: The Eta-One Holonomy Anomaly Is a Tree of Squares

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let a one-unit holonomy wing have $|K|\le9$, uncounted remainder $\eta=1$, and two disjoint two-concept cycle shores. Then $|L|\in\{1,2\}$. After choosing one collar vertex for each passive direction, exactly one vertex $v\in K$ remains uncounted, and $G(K)-v$ is obtained from the path $G(L)$ by attaching two pendant paths of length three. The square link of $v$ is a tree, so if $d=\deg_K(v)$, then $K$ contains exactly $d-1$ squares, all through $v$. For arm $i$, the pair $P_i=\{z_i,f_i\}$ of its attachment and terminal directions is not shattered by $K$; the two pairs are disjoint and are exactly the terminal-square supports acquired by the upper family.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The one-unit identity gives $|K|=|L|+7$, and the shore-root lemma gives $1\le|L|\le2$. Connectivity and bipartiteness of each opposite active section allow its collar to be chosen so that the shore edge lifts to a pendant length-three arm. The two arms have disjoint nonbase vertices and no cross edge; together with $L$ they leave exactly the uncounted vertex $v$, so deleting $v$ gives the asserted tree and the one-vertex tree-completion theorem gives the square fan. Each passive arm direction occurs only on its attachment edge below, so a square through it cannot use the terminal direction; ampleness therefore excludes $P_i$ from $\operatorname{Sh}(K)$. Carrier connectivity forces the two terminal directions to differ, and the upper shore squares show that both pairs are acquired.

With at least two squares, any second tree-deletion vertex lies in every square; the link tree is a star, and the block--cut branches recover a common arm unless the competing ordinary arm lies outside both old supports. With one square, comparing the four possible attachment positions leaves one exceptional arrangement: two length-two tails at antipodal square vertices, while the opposite square vertices alternate as core and apex.                                                                 A Pair-Poor Extra-Owner Wing Has a Rooted-Claw Overlap

                                                                Name: A Pair-Poor Extra-Owner Wing Has a Rooted-Claw Overlap

                                                                Statement:

                                                                In the one-unit extra-owner profile with $|K|\le9$, a singleton active slice makes the two disjoint shores supply two disjoint acquired direction pairs. Therefore every pair-poor extra-owner wing has $|L|=2$ and $|K|=9$. Writing $G(L)=ab$ and its ordinary arm as $ap_1p_2p_3$, the graph $G(K)$ is obtained by adding a vertex $c$, three leaves $q_1,q_2,q_3$ adjacent to $c$, and one edge $rc$ with $r\in\{a,b\}$. Thus exactly two rooted overlap graphs occur.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The one-unit identity gives $|K|=|L|+7$. For $|L|=1$, each disjoint shore contains an active edge; the disjoint-shore acquisition lemma makes both active--passive pairs acquired and the direction-separation lemma makes them disjoint. Hence a pair-poor wing has $|L|=2$. Its graph consists of the slice edge, an ordinary length-three arm, and a rooted connected four-vertex component made from the larger shore and its collar. If two shore concepts were adjacent, their active--passive square would be acquired and disjoint from the ordinary-arm pair, whose terminal direction labels a bridge and cannot coincide with the shore-edge direction. Pair-poorness therefore makes the three shore concepts independent; connectivity forces each to meet the collar vertex, so the four-vertex component is a claw rooted at its centre and attached to either endpoint of $ab$.

                                                                The Two Rooted-Claw Overlaps Have Rigid Cuts

                                                                Name: The Two Rooted-Claw Overlaps Have Rigid Cuts

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Trees

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $T^{\parallel}$ and $T^{\times}$ have the common edges $ab,ap_1,p_1p_2,p_2p_3,cq_1,cq_2,cq_3$, with the remaining edge respectively $ac$ or $bc$, and call $ap_1p_2p_3$ the old arm. If deletion of two vertices leaves the seven-vertex path formed by two length-three arms, then the tree is $T^{\times}$, the deleted vertices are two claw leaves, and one surviving arm is the old arm. If one-vertex deletion leaves a one-vertex core with a length-three arm and a rooted four-vertex tree whose three nonattachment vertices contain an edge, that arm is the old arm. The only $(3,5)$ component cut is at $a$ in $T^{\times}$ and isolates the old arm; the only $(4,4)$ cut is at $b$ there and one component is the rooted claw with independent leaves; neither tree has a $(2,3,3)$ cut. In an isometric cube embedding, every recovered old arm retains its original attachment and terminal directions.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                To leave a path after deleting two vertices, the claw centre must remain and two claw leaves must be removed; this fails in $T^{\parallel}$ because $a$ retains degree three, while in $T^{\times}$ it leaves $q_i-c-b-a-p_1-p_2-p_3$. For one-vertex deletion, connectivity forces deletion of a leaf. Checking the leaf orbits and possible core cuts leaves only the cases in which either the four-vertex component is a centre-rooted claw with independent nonattachment vertices or the pendant path is the old arm. Direct vertex deletion gives component profiles $(1,3,4),(2,6),(1,7),(1,1,1,5),(8)$ in $T^{\parallel}$; in $T^{\times}$ only deletion of $a$ and $b$ adds $(3,5)$ and $(4,4)$. Since every edge of a tree partial cube is its own direction class, a repeated arm preserves both relevant directions.

                                                                Passive Layers Can Shield Only Nearby Overlap Corners

                                                                Name: Passive Layers Can Shield Only Nearby Overlap Corners

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Cornerless Ample Classes

                                                                Result Type: Implication

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let a cornerless ample two-layer family have overlap $B$, and suppose every concept exclusive to one wing has the same restriction $\sigma_b$ on a passive coordinate set $Z_b$. Then every corner $v$ of $B$ has passive Hamming distance at most one from $\sigma_b$. If the distance is one with unique differing coordinate $z$, its exclusive shield is forced: $v^{\oplus z}$ belongs to that wing's exclusive part. Thus a corner at passive distance at least two becomes a corner of the full family, while a distance-one corner has only one possible exclusive neighbour.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                At passive distance at least two, $v$ has no exclusive neighbour. All horizontal directions at its copy belong to the unique maximal cube of $B$ through $v$, and the vertical edge joins the two copies, so all incident directions lie in the single product cube over that maximal cube. The copy is therefore a corner of the full family, a contradiction. At distance one the same argument forces an exclusive neighbour. Since every exclusive concept has passive word $\sigma_b$, adjacency can change only the unique differing coordinate $z$; hence the neighbour must be $v^{\oplus z}$.

                                                                A Two-Unit Wing Resolves Every Opposite Profile through Two Units

                                                                Name: A Two-Unit Wing Resolves Every Opposite Profile through Two Units

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Cornerless Ample Classes

                                                                Result Type: Implication

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let a cornerless ample two-layer family have overlap $B$ of order at most nine. If one wing has two-cycle holonomy and excess two while the opposite wing has two-cycle holonomy and excess at most two, then their acquired supports contain three pairwise disjoint direction pairs.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The exact excess classification leaves five feasible two-unit normal forms. Constructing these from a pure $P_7$ completion or wedges of rooted ample gates of orders at most five yields 148 distinct embedded ample overlaps and 960 exact two-unit markers. The audit compares distinct markers against every opposite two-unit, sharp, eta-one, and pair-rich extra-owner marker, while coincident markers immediately repeat both terminal supports and the rooted-claw theorem handles all pair-poor extra-owner markers. All 8395 distinct comparisons end in a repeated acquired support, passive-shielding contradiction, forced-owner conflict, direct terminal matching, or collar-augmented matching; each outcome respectively contradicts the structural identities or yields three independent acquired pairs.

                                                                The One-Unit Central-Square Profile Cannot Be Shielded

                                                                Name: The One-Unit Central-Square Profile Cannot Be Shielded

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Cornerless Ample Classes

                                                                Result Type: Implication

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Under the one-unit opposite-wing hypotheses, a cornerless ample two-layer family has three pairwise disjoint acquired direction pairs. In particular, the exceptional central-square support graph $K_{2,2}$ cannot occur.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Assume the central-square alternative and fix either wing. Its active slice is the singleton $\{c\}$, its uncounted vertex $v$ is opposite $c$ in the central square, and the square directions $z_1,z_2$ are passive attachment directions. Every exclusive concept has the passive word of $c$, so $v$ is at passive distance two from that word. The two pendant paths attach at the other antipodal pair of the square, making $v$ a corner of the overlap $B$. This contradicts passive radius-one shielding in a cornerless family.

                                                                Forced Wing Words Certify Active Coordinates

                                                                Name: Forced Wing Words Certify Active Coordinates

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Cornerless Ample Classes

                                                                Result Type: Implication

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let a cornerless ample two-layer family have overlap $B$ and wing $D_b$, and suppose all members of $D_b$ share one word $\sigma$ on passive coordinates $Z$. Form $W_b$ from any shore concepts whose opposite $Z$-fibres occur in $B$, together with $o_v=v^{\oplus z}$ for every corner $v$ of $B$ whose passive word differs from $\sigma$ only in $z$. Then $W_b\subseteq D_b$. If $D_b$ is connected, every coordinate varying on $W_b$ is active on $D_b$; if $D_b$ is two-connected, then $|D_b|\ge 2|Y(W_b)|$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The shore concepts lie in the wing by definition. Passive radius-one shielding makes $v^{\oplus z}$ the unique possible shield of each distance-one overlap corner, so cornerlessness forces every such owner into $D_b$. A path inside connected $D_b$ between two words differing in coordinate $x$ must traverse an $x$-edge, hence every coordinate varying on $W_b$ is active. The two-connected cube-coordinate cost bound then gives $|D_b|\ge2|Y(W_b)|$.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#lem:damp-forced-wing-words-active-coordinates

                                                                The Terminal Two-Connected Matching Row Closes

                                                                Name: The Terminal Two-Connected Matching Row Closes

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Cornerless Ample Classes

                                                                Result Type: Implication

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let a cornerless ample two-layer family have overlap $B$ with $|B|\le9$. Suppose both proper pairs $B\subsetneq A_b$ are terminal under one-concept addition and deletion, each wing $D_b=A_b\setminus B$ is two-connected, and $|D_b|\in\{10,11\}$. Then the two lower gate-holonomy cycles cannot both have excess at most two. Consequently, no pair of terminal two-connected wings of orders ten or eleven occurs in the below-forty two-wing reduction.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The local profile theorems reduce all excess-at-most-two comparisons to three independent acquired pairs; the sole central-square alternative is excluded by shielding. Adding actual shore concepts and forced distance-one owners to each wing gives sets $W_0,W_1$. Of 2886 two-unit matching comparisons, 302 fail passive-distance or owner-consistency tests; among the remaining 2584, the varying-coordinate counts are 504 of type $(5,5)$, 108 of type $(6,5)$, and 1972 of type $(6,6)$. A two-connected wing with six active coordinates needs at least twelve concepts, excluding the latter two types. In the low-excess comparison, all positioned wings likewise force six coordinates except the $P_8$ equality pattern. The remaining five-cube audit has fourteen two-unit side states and six low-excess side states. For wing orders ten and eleven it finds respectively 504 and 3346 two-connected two-unit completions, of which 238 and 1330 have ample upper families, and 744 and 4176 two-connected $P_8$ completions, of which 198 and 1026 have ample upper families. Every ample upper family has both an addable exclusive concept and a deletable exclusive concept, so none is terminal.

                                                                Nine-Concept Passive-Carrier Exclusion

                                                                Name: Nine-Concept Passive-Carrier Exclusion

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Dismantlable-Ample Relative Corner Threshold

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                There is no nonempty trapped inclusion $K\subsetneq A$ of dismantlable ample families with $\operatorname{Cor}(A)\subseteq K$ and $|A\setminus K|=9$. Consequently, $10\le\rho_{\mathsf{Damp}}\le12$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Choose a maximal proper dismantlable-ample intermediate family. Its nine residual concepts are doubly blocked, induce a connected cube graph of minimum degree two, and satisfy the local passive-carrier rules. Among 160 connected bipartite graph types of order nine, ten admit induced-cube embeddings and yield thirteen coordinate-coloured profiles. The degree-two isolated-marker and cross-carrier checks exclude ten, leaving only active profiles 5.1, 8.1, and 9.1. For each survivor, replace every actual passive support by its down-set in the nine-support inclusion preorder; this preserves exactly all inclusions and equalities needed by a relaxation encoding support distinctness, residual carrier depth, compatible full-cube carriers, isolated degree-two markers, and the degree-three two-shore dichotomy. All three CNFs are unsatisfiable. Their independently checked DRAT cores contain no RAT lemmas and have respectively 9,796,884, 6,854,743, and 7,636,141 resolution steps. Thus no genuine terminal interval realizes a surviving profile. The twelve-concept trapped interval supplies the upper bound.

                                                                Every Sub-Ten Dismantlable-Ample Interval Has a First Concept

                                                                Name: Every Sub-Ten Dismantlable-Ample Interval Has a First Concept

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Result Type: Implication

                                                                Statement:

                                                                If $C\subsetneq H$ are dismantlable ample and $|H\setminus C|\le9$, then some $h\in H\setminus C$ satisfies $C\cup\{h\}\in\mathsf{Damp}$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Otherwise choose a dismantlable-ample $J$ inclusion-minimal with $C\subsetneq J\subseteq H$. No corner of $J$ can lie outside $C$: deleting such a corner either gives the forbidden first extension of $C$ or contradicts minimality of $J$. Hence $\operatorname{Cor}(J)\subseteq C$ and $1\le|J\setminus C|\le9$, producing a trapped pair below the established bound $\rho_{\mathsf{Damp}}\ge10$.

                                                                Small Trapped Wings Need at Most One Marked Synchronization

                                                                Name: Small Trapped Wings Need at Most One Marked Synchronization

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $B\subsetneq A$ be ample with $\operatorname{Cor}(A)\subseteq B$ and $|A\setminus B|\le11$, and suppose every ample intermediate family belongs to $\mathsf{Damp}$. Then there is an ample $C$ with $B\subseteq C\subsetneq A$ and $|C\setminus B|\le1$ such that $R=A\setminus C$ has order ten or eleven, every $r\in R$ is blocked under both addition to $C$ and deletion from $A$, and the graph induced by $R$ is two-connected. Thus an order-ten trapped wing is terminal; an order-eleven wing is terminal or has a terminal ten-concept core above one marked ample addition.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Choose $C$ maximal among proper ample intermediate families. Maximality blocks every one-concept addition $C\cup\{r\}$, while an ample deletion $A\setminus\{r\}$ would make $r$ a corner of $A$ outside $B$, so every residual concept is doubly blocked. Both endpoints lie in $\mathsf{Damp}$ and form a trapped pair. The relative threshold gives $10\le|R|\le11$, hence $|C\setminus B|\le1$. The terminal cut-layer theorem through eleven then makes the residual graph two-connected.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                A Holonomy Shore Has a Contracted Split-Square Marker

                                                                Name: A Holonomy Shore Has a Contracted Split-Square Marker

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Coordinate Projection

                                                                Result Type: Implication

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $K\subsetneq A$ be dismantlable ample, put $D=A\setminus K$, suppose no concept of $D$ can be adjoined amply to $K$, and assume $|D|\le11$. If coordinate $z$ is constant on $D$ and its shore $S_z=\{d\in D:d^{\oplus z}\in K\}$ satisfies $2\le|S_z|<|D|$, then after contracting $z$ some image of $u\in D\setminus S_z$ can be adjoined amply to $\pi_zK$. It cannot lift to $K$; consequently an active edge $uu^{\oplus f}$ crosses into $S_z$ and its opposite square is split, with $(u^{\oplus f})^{\oplus z}\in K$ but $u^{\oplus z}\notin A$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Projection identifies the relative concepts of $\pi_zK\subsetneq\pi_zA$ with the distinct images of $D\setminus S_z$, whose number lies between one and nine. Both projected endpoints are dismantlable ample, so the sub-ten first-concept lemma supplies an addable projected root $u$. Its lift is blocked in $K$. The wrong-side witness theorem applies because the other member of its $z$-fibre lies neither in $D$, where $z$ is constant, nor in $K$. It yields a direction $f$ with $u^{\oplus f}\in D$ and $u^{\oplus\{z,f\}}\in K$, which is exactly the crossing edge and split square.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#prop:damp-holonomy-shore-split-square-marker

                                                                Lower Gate Holonomy Is Carried by Split Squares

                                                                Name: Lower Gate Holonomy Is Carried by Split Squares

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Result Type: Implication

                                                                Statement:

                                                                In a two-sided passive gate-holonomy system from a dismantlable-ample terminal interval of order at most eleven, every shore on a directed lower-gate cycle has at least two concepts and carries a split-square marker. Thus the residual obstruction is a cyclic system of oriented split squares rather than arbitrary boundary subsets.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                For a cyclic shore $S$, its predecessor shore has a lower root blocked by $S$. The shore-root lemma puts one lower root in $S$, while the common-owner theorem puts a distinct non-root owner there, so $|S|\ge2$. Such a shore is proper in the residual set by construction. The contracted split-square marker theorem therefore applies to every cyclic shore.

                                                                Proof Source:
