                                                                Terminal Block-Curvature Tax

                                                                Name: Terminal Block-Curvature Tax

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Shattered Complex
                                                                • Dismantlable-Ample Relative Corner Threshold

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $\varnothing\ne B\subsetneq A$ be dismantlable ample with $\operatorname{Cor}(A)\subseteq B$. Choose a maximal proper dismantlable-ample intermediate $C$ and put $D=A\setminus C$. Define $\tau(D)=e(D)-|D|+\max\{1,|\operatorname{Cor}(D)|\}$. Then $D$ has minimum graph degree at least two, every cube-family corner of $D$ has a neighbor in $C$, the relative Yang module of $(A,C)$ is deletion-minimal Cohen--Macaulay, and $\sum_{S\in\operatorname{Sh}(A)\setminus\operatorname{Sh}(B)}|S|\ge|A\setminus B|+\tau(D)$. In particular $\tau(D)\ge1$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Maximality of $C$ excludes every relative teaching concept. Ampleness makes the relative Yang module Cohen--Macaulay, while deleting any $d\in D$ cannot remain ample because then $d$ would be a corner of $A$ outside $C$; the relative Cohen--Macaulay criterion gives deletion-minimality. An isolated residual vertex would teach $C$ by the first edge of an isometric path, and the relative leaf dichotomy similarly excludes residual degree one, so $e(D)\ge|D|$. Every corner of $D$ needs a boundary neighbor in $C$, or its unique maximal cube in $D$ would also make it a corner of $A$. Hence the boundary has at least $\max\{1,|\operatorname{Cor}(D)|\}$ edges. The ample edge--shadow identity converts internal plus boundary edges into the rank sum of newly shattered supports; the earlier supports from $B$ to $C$ each contribute at least one.

                                                                References:

                                                                [BousquetYangComplex26]

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#prop:damp-terminal-block-curvature-tax

                                                                Wrong-Side Witnesses Localize on Relative Edges

                                                                Name: Wrong-Side Witnesses Localize on Relative Edges

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Partial Cubes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Coordinate Projection

                                                                Result Type: Implication

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $C\subsetneq A\subseteq Q_E$ with $A$ isometric, contract coordinate $e$, and put $D=A\setminus C$. Suppose $d\in D$ is the unique relative member of its $e$-fibre and its image $y$ lies in $\pi_eA\setminus\pi_eC$. If $y$ teaches $\pi_eC$ but $d$ does not teach $C$, then some $c\in C$ has the following property: every contracted teaching direction $f$ that separates $y$ from $c$ satisfies $d^{\oplus f}\in D$ and $d^{\oplus\{e,f\}}\in C$. Thus every witness lost on lifting runs along a relative edge and completes the opposite square into the lower family.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The other lift $d^{\oplus e}$ lies outside $A$. Since $d$ does not teach $C$, choose $c\in C$ with no $C$-neighbor of $d$ in a differing direction. For a contracted teaching direction $f$ separating $y$ from $c$, one lift over $y^{\oplus f}$ lies in $C$; the choice of $c$ rules out $d^{\oplus f}$, so the opposite vertex $d^{\oplus\{e,f\}}$ lies in $C$. Isometry supplies a two-edge path in $A$ from $d$ to that opposite vertex. Its other possible intermediate vertex $d^{\oplus e}$ is absent, forcing $d^{\oplus f}\in A\setminus C=D$.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#prop:damp-contracted-teaching-root-wrong-side

                                                                Algebraic pc-Minor Dictionary

                                                                Name: Algebraic pc-Minor Dictionary

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Partial Cubes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Coordinate Conditioning
                                                                • Coordinate Projection
                                                                • Partial-Cube Minor

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For an isometrically embedded family $X\subseteq Q_E$, its complementary-literal ideal $J_X=(\prod_{e\in E}v_{e,1-x_e}:x\in X)$ has linear quotients exactly when $X$ is dismantlable ample. If a pc-minor $K=\pi_D(X_f)$ conditions coordinates $F$ to a realized word $f$ and contracts disjoint coordinates $D$, then $J_K=\phi_{f,D}(J_X)$, where the conditioned matching literals map to zero, their opposites to one, and both literals of every contracted color to one. Consequently, $X$ is pc-minimal outside dismantlable ampleness exactly when $J_X$ lacks linear quotients but every proper specialization of this form has them.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The monomial-colon formula identifies variable-generated colons with the condition that every earlier concept has a previously inserted cube neighbor of the new concept in their Boolean interval. Induction on Hamming distance makes this equivalent to every prefix being isometric, hence to a reversed corner peeling. Under the displayed specialization, a generator from the wrong conditioned side vanishes, a generator from the retained side loses all conditioned and contracted factors, and its remaining product is exactly the generator of the projected concept; repetitions do not change the ideal. The normal form of a pc-minor as conditioning followed by contractions gives the minimal-obstruction clause.

                                                                References:

                                                                [ChalopiChepoiMoran22]

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#prop:damp-algebraic-minor-dictionary

                                                                Ball Form of Ampleness

                                                                Name: Ball Form of Ampleness

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For every nonempty proper $X\subsetneq Q_E$ and every field $k$, ampleness of $X$, constructible-ball structure of its Yang complex $\Delta_X$, and $k$-homology-ball structure of $\Delta_X$ are equivalent. The ball has dimension $|E|-1$ and boundary $\partial\Delta_X=\Delta_X\cap\Delta_{Q_E\setminus X}$. Moreover, $X$ is corner-peelable exactly when this ball is shellable.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The ample--Cohen--Macaulay dictionary identifies ampleness with Cohen--Macaulayness of $\Delta_X$. A nonempty proper full-dimensional subcomplex of the cross-polytope boundary that is Cohen--Macaulay is a constructible triangulated ball; constructible balls are Cohen--Macaulay over every field, and homology balls are Cohen--Macaulay, giving all three equivalences. The complementary-ball theorem for polarizations identifies the complement Yang complex as the other ball and their intersection as the common boundary. The shelling--corner-peeling correspondence proves the final assertion.

                                                                References:

                                                                [BousquetYangComplex26] [ChalopiChepoiMoran22] [FloystadGabrielsenMafi26]

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#prop:damp-yang-homology-ball

                                                                Colored-Ideal Parametrization of the Dismantlable-Ample Basis

                                                                Name: Colored-Ideal Parametrization of the Dismantlable-Ample Basis

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Coordinate Conditioning
                                                                • Coordinate Projection
                                                                • Partial-Cube Minor

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Up to partial-cube isomorphism, the complete pc-minimal obstruction basis for dismantlable ampleness is the disjoint union of the antipodally punctured cubes $Q_n^{--}$, $n\ge3$, and the hyperoctahedral orbits of full-transversal ideals $J\in\mathfrak B_d^{\mathrm{col}}$: $J$ has a $d$-linear resolution but no linear-quotient order, uses both literals of every color, and all two restriction images and the contraction image in every color have linear quotients. Equivalently, an irredundant ample $X\subseteq Q_d$ is a forbidden pc-minor exactly when $X\notin\mathsf{Damp}$ but all $3d$ elementary pc-minors belong to $\mathsf{Damp}$. Within the ample layer, cornerless obstructions are exactly those whose ideal loses $d$-linearity after deleting any minimal generator.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                A full-transversal ideal recovers an irredundant cube family. Its linear resolution is equivalent to ampleness and failure of linear quotients to failure of dismantlability. The three one-color maps are exactly the ideals of the two elementary restrictions and the elementary contraction. If these images have linear quotients, all elementary pc-minors are dismantlable; pc-minor closure then handles every proper minor. Conversely every ample pc-minimal obstruction satisfies these four ideal conditions. Uniqueness of an irredundant cube embedding gives the quotient by coordinate permutations and reorientations. The nonample-layer theorem supplies precisely the punctured cubes. Finally, deleting a concept preserves ampleness exactly when deleting its ideal generator preserves $d$-linearity, proving the corner criterion.

                                                                References:

                                                                [BousquetYangComplex26] [ChalopiChepoiMoran22]

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#thm:damp-descendant-free-parametrization

                                                                Yang-Ball Parametrization of the Dismantlable-Ample Basis

                                                                Name: Yang-Ball Parametrization of the Dismantlable-Ample Basis

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Coordinate Conditioning
                                                                • Coordinate Projection
                                                                • Partial-Cube Minor

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                An irredundant ample family $X\subseteq Q_d$ is pc-minimal outside dismantlable ampleness exactly when its Yang complex is a nonshellable constructible $(d-1)$-ball, every link at a literal vertex is shellable, and every induced deletion of both literal vertices of one coordinate is shellable. Hence the complete basis consists of the antipodally punctured cubes and these color-minimal nonshellable Yang balls, modulo color permutations and reorientations; no iterated-link or additional pc-minor test is needed.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The Yang complex of a restriction is the link at the retained literal, and the Yang complex of a contraction is the induced deletion of the corresponding literal pair. The ball theorem makes an ample family dismantlable exactly when its Yang ball is shellable. Thus shellability of the $3d$ displayed elementary color minors is precisely the elementary pc-minor condition in the colored-ideal parametrization. Pc-minor closure handles all iterated minors, while the nonample-layer theorem supplies the punctured-cube part.

                                                                References:

                                                                [BousquetYangComplex26] [ChalopiChepoiMoran22] [FloystadGabrielsenMafi26]

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#cor:damp-descendant-free-yang-ball-parametrization

                                                                Critical-Core Extension Normal Form for Ample Dismantlability Obstructions

                                                                Name: Critical-Core Extension Normal Form for Ample Dismantlability Obstructions

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes
                                                                • Cornerless Ample Classes

                                                                Result Type: Construction

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $\mathfrak C_d^{\mathrm{col}}$ consist of full-transversal degree-$d$ ideals with a $d$-linear resolution, no linear-quotient order, and loss of $d$-linearity after deleting any minimal generator. Every ample pc-minimal obstruction to dismantlable ampleness is obtained from some $K\in\mathfrak C_d^{\mathrm{col}}$ by successively adjoining full-transversal generators $u_i$ with $K_{i-1}:u_i$ generated by variables, subject at the endpoint to irredundancy, failure of linear quotients, and linear quotients for all $3d$ elementary one-color images. Conversely every such endpoint is an obstruction. All intermediate ideals retain a $d$-linear resolution, and the extension word is empty exactly for cornerless obstructions.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Adjoining $u_i$ fits into the standard colon exact sequence. A variable-generated colon bounds the quotient regularity by $d-1$, so each enlarged ideal remains $d$-linear. Conversely, delete generators from an obstruction while the remaining ideal stays $d$-linear. Lu's deletion theorem makes every reversed colon variable-generated. The terminal core cannot have linear quotients, since appending the reversed deletions would then give a linear-quotient order for the original obstruction. The ample corner-deletion criterion identifies immediate termination with cornerlessness; the algebraic pc-minor dictionary supplies the endpoint tests.

                                                                References:

                                                                \[DaoDoolittleLyle20minimalCM] [Lu23quasilinear]

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#thm:damp-critical-core-normal-form

                                                                Algebraic and Topological Form of an Ample One-Facet Attachment

                                                                Name: Algebraic and Topological Form of an Ample One-Facet Attachment

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $A=S\cup\{a\}\subseteq Q_F$ be ample and put $I=\{e:a^{\{e\}}\in S\}$. For the complementary-literal generator $m_a$ and new Yang facet $F_a$, one has $J_S:m_a=(v_{e,a_e}:e\in I)$ and $2^{F_a}\cap\Delta_S=\partial2^{\{v_{e,a_e}:e\in I\}}*2^{\{v_{e,a_e}:e\in F\setminus I\}}$. Equivalently, the intersection is the union of the ridges $F_a\setminus\{v_{e,a_e}\}$ for $e\in I$. If $S$ is an ample forbidden pc-minor for dismantlable ampleness, then $\varnothing\ne I\subsetneq F$ and this intersection is a shellable $(|F|-2)$-ball.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Every $a$--$x$ geodesic in the isometric extension starts in a direction $e\in I$, so the monomial quotient for $x$ is divisible by $v_{e,a_e}$; the neighbour in direction $e$ gives the reverse divisibility and the colon formula. A face of $F_a$ lies in the old Yang complex exactly when it omits one of these literals, proving the ridge union. Connectedness gives $I\ne\varnothing$, while $I=F$ would make $S$ a punctured cube and hence corner-peelable. The displayed join is therefore a shellable ball.

                                                                Signed Route Elimination and Exact Elementary-Minor Calculus

                                                                Name: Signed Route Elimination and Exact Elementary-Minor Calculus

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Signed Minimal-Nonface Presentation

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Coordinate Projection
                                                                • Coordinate Conditioning
                                                                • Full Reduction

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                A clutter $\mathcal R$ of consistent literal sets is the full minimally missing-pattern clutter of an ample family exactly when every opposite-literal pair $P,Q\in\mathcal R$ admits $U\in\mathcal R$ contained in $(P\cup Q)$ after deleting both literals of the conflicting coordinate. For an ample $H$, the complete route clutters of projection, conditioning, and full reduction in coordinate $e$ are respectively the routes avoiding both $e$-literals; the inclusion-minimal routes obtained after deleting the fixed literal from routes avoiding its opposite; and the inclusion-minimal routes obtained after deleting both $e$-literals. The formulas include constant coordinates and empty images.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Lawrence's route-system theorem gives the signed elimination equivalence and agrees with cardinality admissibility of the signed minimal-nonface presentation. A visible pattern is missing from a projection exactly when it was already missing without using $e$, and is missing from a conditioning exactly when adjoining the fixed literal contains an old route. For reduction, erase the $e$-literal from every route and minimize. Signed elimination descends to this trimmed clutter, so Lawrence's sufficiency proves that it is the full route clutter of the reduction rather than merely an incomplete clause list.

                                                                References:

                                                                [Lawrence1983]

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                Large Missing-Pattern Conditions Guarantee Every Prescribed Sink

                                                                Name: Large Missing-Pattern Conditions Guarantee Every Prescribed Sink

                                                                • Attainable Sink Set

                                                                Result Type: Implication

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $H\ne\varnothing$ be ample and retain its minimally missing patterns of support at least three. Every vertex of $H$ is the sink of an acyclic unique-sink orientation if there are at most two such patterns, or if every pair agrees wherever their supports overlap. Hence every ample forbidden pc-minor for dismantlable ampleness, and every rooted obstruction factor, has at least three large minimally missing patterns, with two disagreeing on a common coordinate. Binary missing patterns are unrestricted in both sufficient conditions.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The two signed geometric criteria construct a bounded full-dimensional convex polytope whose strict coordinate-sign class is $H$. The coordinate hyperplanes on this polytope give the required realization, and the realizable prescribed-endpoint theorem supplies a peeling, hence an acyclic USO, to every selected vertex. Contraposition gives both necessary conditions for forbidden classes and rooted factors.

                                                                Comments:

                                                                The criteria are sufficient rather than necessary. Failure of both is not a negative certificate for dismantlable ampleness.

                                                                Matching Route Conflicts Give Arbitrary-Coefficient Realizations

                                                                Name: Matching Route Conflicts Give Arbitrary-Coefficient Realizations

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Realizable Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                • Missing-Pattern Conflict Graph
                                                                • Attainable Sink Set

                                                                Result Type: Implication

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $H$ be nonempty and ample. If its full missing-pattern conflict graph has maximum degree at most one, then for every choice of positive coefficients $\lambda_{p,i}$ the signed forms $\ell_p(z)=\sum_i\lambda_{p,i}(2p_i-1)z_i$ realize $H$ as the strict coordinate-sign class of a bounded open convex polyhedron cut out by a box and the inequalities $\ell_p(z)<-\varepsilon$. Consequently every vertex is the sink of an acyclic USO. Thus the conflict graph of every ample forbidden pc-minor or rooted obstruction factor has a vertex of degree at least two.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Reflect a chosen allowed word to zero. A missing pattern with no pure value-one coordinate is paired with at most one conflict, and signed elimination shows that two conflicting patterns cannot both have this property. Increase one private weight for each uncovered pattern, then increase all pure-coordinate weights together; these changes make every signed form negative without undoing earlier inequalities. Repeating for every allowed word, scaling the finitely many witnesses, and adding a bounding box yields one polyhedron with exactly sign class $H$. The realizable endpoint theorem supplies every sink.

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For a nonempty ample family, the full missing-pattern conflict graph of every projection, coordinate conditioning, or full reduction is isomorphic to a subgraph of the original conflict graph. Its maximum degree therefore cannot increase, and the degree-at-most-one realization criterion is preserved under these operations and their compositions.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Use the exact signed-route formulas and choose one parent route for every surviving or trimmed image route. Distinct image routes have distinct parents because every parent has a unique trim. Any conflict at a visible coordinate was already a conflict between the chosen parents, giving an edge-preserving injection. Iteration handles compositions; an empty image has only the empty pattern and no edges.

                                                                Bipartite Route Conflicts Give a Convex-Treelike Construction

                                                                Name: Bipartite Route Conflicts Give a Convex-Treelike Construction

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Convex-Treelike Partial Cubes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                • Missing-Pattern Conflict Graph
                                                                • Attainable Sink Set

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Peripheral Expansion

                                                                Result Type: Construction

                                                                Statement:

                                                                If a nonempty ample family has a bipartite full missing-pattern conflict graph, then it is obtained recursively from singletons by peripheral expansions $(B\times\{0\})\cup(S\times\{1\})$ with $\varnothing\ne S\subseteq B$ and both children constructed by the same rule; constant coordinates may be added freely. Thus it is convex-treelike and every vertex is an attainable acyclic-USO sink. The recursion is recovered from the signed patterns by repeatedly choosing a coordinate at which at most one literal occurs. Consequently every ample forbidden pc-minor for either the convex-treelike or dismantlable ample class, and every rooted obstruction factor, has a nonbipartite conflict graph.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                In a bipartition, if both literal values occurred at every active coordinate, all routes in one part would restrict one common word and all routes in the other its opposite. Signed elimination of a conflicting pair would then produce a route properly contained in one parent, contradicting that routes form a clutter. Hence some coordinate uses at most one polarity, which makes one section contain the other. Conflict-graph monotonicity preserves bipartiteness in both sections, so induction gives the peripheral construction and every endpoint sink. Contraposition gives the obstruction statement.

                                                                Comments:

                                                                Bipartiteness is sufficient, not necessary: path graphs can have nonbipartite missing-pattern conflict graphs while remaining convex-treelike.

                                                                Statement:

In the explicit pair, the feasible set is the union of two equality-partition families and contains 96 of the 128 assignments allowed by the forced equalities.

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The two displayed orders pass the local cube test at every deletion and hence induce acyclic CCMW USOs. Individually incompatible crossings yield seven forced equality blocks. Exhausting their 128 bit assignments gives the exact condition that the central block agree with at least one of two other blocks. Merging it with either block yields a displayed topological order valid for every assignment in that branch. If it agrees with neither, two crossing edges add comparisons completing the directed cycle $1\to3\to14\to15\to1$. The two single-block indicators are feasible, while their mod-two sum is not; a single partition family would be closed under such sums.

                                                                Corners Are Exactly Unique Facet Traces

                                                                Name: Corners Are Exactly Unique Facet Traces

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Shattered Complex

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $H\subseteq Q_F$ be ample with shattered complex $\Sigma$. A concept $x\in H$ is a corner exactly when some facet $T$ of $\Sigma$ has trace $x|_T$ realized by no other member of $H$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Deleting $x$ loses a shattered face precisely when its trace there was unique. The Sandwich inequalities and the ample corner-deletion criterion say that deletion is ample exactly when it loses one shattered face. Uniqueness propagates from a face to every shattered coface, so exactly one face is lost precisely when that face is a facet.

                                                                A Simplicial Maximal Cube Exposes a Corner

                                                                Name: A Simplicial Maximal Cube Exposes a Corner

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Partial Cubes
                                                                • Cornerless Ample Classes

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Maximal-Cube Intersection Graph

                                                                Result Type: Implication

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $X$ be a nonempty cube family. If a maximal cube $C$ is a simplicial vertex of the maximal-cube intersection graph, then $C$ contains a vertex belonging to no other maximal cube, hence a corner. Consequently a cornerless cube family has a maximal-cube intersection graph with no simplicial vertex; that graph is nonchordal and contains an induced cycle of length at least four.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The neighbours of a simplicial cube $C$ meet pairwise, and subcubes of a hypercube have the Helly property, so they share a vertex $z$ of $C$. The antipode of $z$ in $C$ lies in none of their proper traces on $C$, and a nonneighbour is disjoint from $C$. Thus this antipode belongs only to $C$. Every finite chordal graph has a simplicial vertex, giving the final assertions.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                Square-Free Edges of Ample Families Are Bridges

                                                                Name: Square-Free Edges of Ample Families Are Bridges

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Every cycle in the one-inclusion graph of an ample family, viewed as an edge chain over $\mathbb F_2$, is a sum of boundaries of contained squares. Consequently every edge that belongs to no contained square is a bridge.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Induct on the active coordinates. Pair the edges of a cycle in a chosen direction. The projected endpoints lie in the ample and therefore connected intersection of the two sections; paths between each pair lift to square ladders whose boundaries cancel those directional edges. What remains is a sum of cycles inside the two ample sections, handled inductively. An edge on a graph cycle has coefficient one in that cycle, while every square-boundary sum has coefficient zero on an edge lying in no square, proving the bridge claim.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#lem:damp-square-free-edge-bridge

                                                                Inverse Construction from One Relatively Peelable Wing

                                                                Name: Inverse Construction from One Relatively Peelable Wing

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Graph Expansion
                                                                • Full Reduction
                                                                • Concept Deletion
                                                                • Partial-Cube Minor

                                                                Result Type: Construction

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $O$ be an ample forbidden pc-minor for dismantlable ampleness and use every coordinate of $Q_F$. Choose dismantlable ample $B_0,B_1$ with $B_0\cap B_1=O$, ample union $A=B_0\cup B_1$, and no edge between the exclusive wings $B_0\setminus O$ and $B_1\setminus O$. If at least one section peels to $O$, then $X=(B_0\times\{0\})\cup(B_1\times\{1\})$ is an ample forbidden pc-minor. Its sections, contraction, and reduction recover the marked expansion and its inputs. Equivalently, this recovers every ample forbidden expansion with negative reduction and at least one relatively peelable section.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The component-expansion theorem makes $X$ ample, while its negative reduction $O$ and closure of dismantlable ampleness under full reduction make $X$ nonpeelable. Lift a peeling of, say, $B_0$ to $O$ through layer zero. The absent vertical mates and the separation of the exclusive wings preserve each corner cube, reducing $X$ to a peripheral expansion of $O$ and $B_1$; the same order shows the contraction is positive. Apply any old-coordinate elementary operation to this deletion sequence and omit repeated images. Its terminal family is a peripheral expansion of the positive families $\mu O$ and $\mu B_1$, so every proper elementary minor is positive. Pc-minor closure then proves forbiddenness. The sections, union, and intersection recover the construction data.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#thm:damp-one-relative-wing-inverse

                                                                Comments:

                                                                It is enough that every one-concept intermediate $O\cup\{a\}$ in one wing is ample: positivity of the section then forces a relative peeling. No separate tests of old-coordinate minors of $X$ are needed.

The exhaustive verifier branches at the first uncovered cube vertex, retains exactly covers in which every member has a private vertex, and takes the lexicographically least image under all $2^r r!$ cube automorphisms.                                                                 Triangle Carriers Are Maximum Rank-One Trees in VC Dimension Three

                                                                Name: Triangle Carriers Are Maximum Rank-One Trees in VC Dimension Three

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Maximum Classes

                                                                • Shattered Complex

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $H\subseteq Q_E$ be ample of VC dimension at most three and fix a shattered pair $S$. For $L_S=\{e:S\cup\{e\}\in\operatorname{Sh}(H)\}$, the family of placements of contained $S$-cubes, after deleting constants, is a maximum VC-dimension-one class on $L_S$. Its one-inclusion graph is a tree on $|L_S|+1$ vertices with one edge in each direction. The edge in direction $e$ represents the unique cube on $S\cup\{e\}$; either endpoint is nonleaf exactly when its corresponding $S$-facet belongs to another maximal three-cube. For a maximum VC-three class the carrier tree has $|E|-1$ vertices and $|E|-2$ edges.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                A support is shattered or strongly shattered by the carrier exactly when adjoining $S$ gives the corresponding property in $H$. Ampleness and the rank bound make its shattered complex the empty face plus the singletons in $L_S$, so it has $|L_S|+1$ members. Connectedness supplies a spanning tree; every active direction must occur, exhausting its $|L_S|$ edges and excluding additional edges. The definition of the carrier identifies directional edges with the unique three-cubes and adjacency at an endpoint with extension of that facet into another maximal cube.

                                                                Anchored Facet Cubes Reconstruct Ample Families by One Cardinality Test

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Triangle Cap for Rank-Three Ample Families of Order Twenty-Seven

                                                                Name: Triangle Cap for Rank-Three Ample Families of Order Twenty-Seven

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $H$ be an irredundant ample family of VC dimension three and order 27 on $d$ active coordinates. The number of triangular faces in its shattered complex is at most 8 for $d=8$ and at most 7 for $d=9$ or $10$. Thus each candidate minimum-order profile is an anchored-cube union with at most eight maximal three-cubes.

                                                                Writing $f_1,f_2$ for the edge and triangle counts, irredundancy and Sandwich equality give $27=1+d+f_1+f_2$. Kruskal--Katona forces at least ten pairs for eight or nine triples, and at least nine pairs for seven triples. Comparing these shadows with $f_1+f_2=26-d$ excludes nine triangles at $d=8$ and eight triangles at $d=9,10$. Anchored facet-cube reconstruction gives the final formulation.

                                                                Missing Triple Traces Form a Tree on Four Coordinates

                                                                Name: Missing Triple Traces Form a Tree on Four Coordinates

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Shattered Complex
                                                                • Signed Minimal-Nonface Presentation

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $\Sigma$ be a two-dimensional simplicial complex with complete one-skeleton and at most two triangular faces on every four-set, and let an ample $H$ have shadow $\Sigma$. On any four-set $U$, represent each missing triple by the cube edge consisting of the two words extending its omitted trace. These edges have connected union. Hence two missing triples in $U$ have omitted traces agreeing on their overlap; if exactly three missing triples share a coordinate, all three omitted traces take the same value there.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                If $t$ triangles occur in $U$, the projection has $11+t$ concepts, so its complement has $5-t$ vertices and is the union of the $4-t$ missing-triple edges. Their directions are distinct, making the union a forest. A forest with $m$ edges and $m+1$ vertices is connected. Intersecting cube edges have compatible prescribed traces, and connectivity propagates the shared-coordinate value.

                                                                Connected Coordinate Propagation Forces the Canonical Face Family

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $\Sigma$ be a two-dimensional simplicial complex with complete one-skeleton and at most two triangular faces on every four-set. For each coordinate $e$, join two minimal nonfaces containing $e$ when their four-coordinate missing-triple configuration forces their omitted traces to agree at $e$. If each resulting propagation graph is connected whenever nonempty, then every ample family with shattered complex $\Sigma$ is a cube translate of the canonical face family $\{\mathbf1_D:D\in\Sigma\}$.

Connectivity therefore gives one bit $h_e$ shared by every minimal nonface containing $e$. The complete signing is the restriction of the word $h$ to each minimal nonface. Translating by $h+\mathbf1_F$ changes every omitted trace to all ones, whose avoidance family consists exactly of the indicator words of faces of $\Sigma$.

                                                                Cornerlessness Can Be pc-Minimal without Forbiddenness

                                                                Name: Cornerlessness Can Be pc-Minimal without Forbiddenness

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Cornerless Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • One-Point Amalgam
                                                                • Partial-Cube Minor

                                                                Result Type: Construction

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $S$ be an ample forbidden pc-minor whose only corner is a root $0$, and let $P$ be a nontrivial corner-peelable ample family whose only corner is $0$. Assume every proper root-preserving pc-minor of either family peels to its root. On disjoint irredundant coordinate sets, the wedge $X=S\vee P$ is ample and cornerless, every nonempty proper pc-minor of $X$ has a corner, and every nonpeelable pc-minor contains $S$. Thus $S$ is the unique forbidden pc-minor of $X$ up to isomorphism, and $X$ has no cornerless forbidden pc-minor.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Vertex gluing preserves ampleness. Nonroot vertices retain the multiple maximal cubes of their own piece, while neighbours of the root in the two blocks have no mixed completing square, so the root is not a corner. Every minor either lies in one block or retains the root and splits as $S\'\vee P\'$. If $S\'$ is proper, peel it to the root and then peel $P\'$. A nonpeelable minor therefore retains $S$; when it is proper, $P\'$ is proper and supplies a corner, including the root when $P\'=\{0\}$. Forbidden minimality then makes $S$ the unique forbidden minor.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#prop:damp-cornerless-minor-minimal-gluing

                                                                A 580-Concept Cornerless Class with a One-Corner Forbidden Minor

                                                                Name: A 580-Concept Cornerless Class with a One-Corner Forbidden Minor

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes

                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Result Type: Construction

                                                                Statement:

                                                                There is a 580-concept ample class in $Q_{24}$ of VC dimension three and minimum graph degree four that is cornerless and whose every nonempty proper pc-minor has a corner. Its unique forbidden pc-minor has 292 concepts and exactly one corner. Hence pc-minimality among cornerless ample classes is strictly weaker than being a cornerless forbidden pc-minor, even for graph three-cores of VC dimension three.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Translate the verified 292-concept one-corner obstruction and the verified 289-concept one-corner peelable rooted factor so their distinguished corners are zero, then wedge them on disjoint twelve-coordinate blocks. The gluing theorem gives all-minor and uniqueness statements. The checker reconstructs both inputs, verifies their shadows and corners, 48 rooted orders, 36 ordinary proper-minor orders, the order and VC dimension of the wedge, its minimum degree and cornerlessness, and all 72 elementary images.

                                                                Two Largest Supports Force a Permutation Structure in Protected Covers

                                                                Name: Two Largest Supports Force a Permutation Structure in Protected Covers

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Cornerless Ample Classes

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Consider $m$ distinct punctured-cube pieces satisfying the protected-cover equations, and suppose two supports have the largest possible size $m-1$. Their supports are $K\mathbin{\dot\cup}\{a\}$ and $K\mathbin{\dot\cup}\{b\}$ with $|K|=m-2$. The protection labels from the two pieces define a permutation $\pi$ of $K$. If $C$ is its moved set and $c=|C|$, then $c\ge2$; every other support indexed by a moved label has size at least $c$, every fixed-label support has size at least $c+2$, and every such support has size at least three.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The protector equations in both directions force the two supports to differ only in their private labels and make both lists of labels enumerate their common core $K$. Symmetric-difference identities show that a third support contains both private labels and all moved coordinates except its two corresponding labels. This gives the rank bounds and identifies the disagreement set with the moved set of $\pi$, which cannot have size one. The only possible rank-two equality case forces a third missing tip into one of the original punctured cubes, contradicting the cover condition.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#thm:damp-two-largest-supports

                                                                Capacity Bound for Six One-Hole Pieces with Two Largest Supports

                                                                Name: Capacity Bound for Six One-Hole Pieces with Two Largest Supports

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Cornerless Ample Classes

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For a protected cover with six pieces, if two supports have size five, then every other support has size at least three and the sum of the protected-interior sizes is at least 82. In particular the rank multiset $(5,5,4,2,2,2)$ is impossible.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                A rank-$r$ piece protects $f(r)=2^r-r-1$ concepts. The permutation structure on the four-element common core has moved-set size two, three, or four. The corresponding minimum rank profiles give respectively $2f(5)+2f(3)+2f(4)=82$, $3f(5)+3f(3)=90$, and $2f(5)+4f(4)=96$.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#cor:damp-six-piece-two-largest-capacity

                                                                Comments:

                                                                This bounds the sum of protected interior sizes; overlaps mean it is not a lower bound on the order of the union, and it is not a pc-minimality criterion.

                                                                Exact Elementary Images of Oriented One-Hole Covers

                                                                Name: Exact Elementary Images of Oriented One-Hole Covers

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Cornerless Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Coordinate Projection
                                                                • Coordinate Conditioning
                                                                • Partial-Cube Minor

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For $\mathsf P(y,B)=\{y^U:\varnothing\ne U\subseteq B\}$ and a coordinate $e\notin B$, the conditioning at $y_e$ and the projection in $e$ both give $\mathsf P(\bar y,B)$, while the opposite conditioning is empty. If $e\in B$ and $C=B\setminus\{e\}$, conditioning at $y_e$ gives $\mathsf P(\bar y,C)$, while the opposite conditioning and projection both give the full affine cube $\mathsf Q(\bar y,C)$. Images of a finite cover are the unions of these piecewise images, preserving tip and support provenance.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Outside the support, every vertex has the fixed coordinate value. Inside the support, the fixed-tip side corresponds to nonempty flipped subsets of the remaining coordinates, while the opposite side corresponds to arbitrary subsets and hence the full cube. Projection is the union of the two sides, and all three operations commute with unions.

                                                                Canonical Transport and Reconstruction of Local Holes

                                                                Name: Canonical Transport and Reconstruction of Local Holes

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Punctured Expansion Profile

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Coordinate Conditioning
                                                                • Coordinate Projection

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For an ample $H$ and coordinate $e$, conditioning transports the canonical local minimal nonfaces at a retained vertex by discarding exactly those supports containing $e$. A support $A$ is a canonical local hole at a vertex of the contraction exactly when its side data $\varepsilon_{H,e}(z,A;\cdot)$ is a punctured expansion profile. In every switched profile, the double-fibre set $D$ and exclusive sets $Z_0,Z_1$ are nonempty, no punctured-cube edge joins the two exclusive sets, every component outside $D$ is monochromatic, $D$ is ample, and $\operatorname{Sh}(D\cup Z_0)\cap\operatorname{Sh}(D\cup Z_1)=\operatorname{Sh}(D)$. Conversely these conditions construct an ample two-layer family with the prescribed switched contraction hole.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Conditioning takes an induced subcomplex of the local cube-support complex. For contraction, an $A$-cube exists exactly when every profile value is nonempty, giving the minimal-hole equivalence. Oppositely coloured adjacent exclusive vertices would have no length-two path between their lifts, contradicting isometry; connectivity then forces a nonempty separator. Restricting to the profile coordinates gives a two-layer ample family whose union is the punctured cube and whose intersection is $D$. The exact two-layer shadow and order identities force $D$ to be ample and its shadow to equal the intersection of side shadows. Conversely those identities give Sandwich equality for the constructed two-layer family and hence ampleness and the desired canonical hole.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#thm:damp-canonical-hole-transport

                                                                Witnesses:

                                                                • First Switched Local Hole

                                                                Comments:

                                                                The theorem explains why piecewise images of source one-hole covers are insufficient after contraction: switched holes can be assembled jointly by the two sections.

                                                                Yang Two-Cone Decomposition and Gluing Dichotomy

                                                                Name: Yang Two-Cone Decomposition and Gluing Dichotomy

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Coordinate Conditioning
                                                                • Coordinate Projection
                                                                • Full Reduction

                                                                Result Type: Implication

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For an ample family $H$ in an active coordinate $e$, let $B_0,B_1$ be its sections, $A=B_0\cap B_1$ its full reduction, and $C=B_0\cup B_1$ its contraction. All four families are ample, and the Yang complex is the union of the cones $v_{e,0}*\Delta_{B_0}$ and $v_{e,1}*\Delta_{B_1}$ glued along $\Delta_A$. If $A$ and the opposite section are dismantlable ample and one section has an $A$-relative ample chain, then $H$ is dismantlable ample. Hence every active coordinate of an ample forbidden pc-minor has either a nonpeelable inherited site $A$, or a peelable site for which neither side is relatively shellable over $A$; in the latter case all three absolute Yang complexes are shellable.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Facets on the two sides have distinct apex literals, and their intersection is the Yang complex of the section intersection. A relative ample chain deletes the exclusive concepts on one side as corners until only a peripheral expansion with base the opposite section and site A remains; the exact peripheral-expansion test peels it. In a forbidden pc-minor both sections and the contraction are positive proper minors, so if A is also positive, either relative shelling would contradict forbiddenness.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#prop:damp-yang-two-cone-gluing-dichotomy

                                                                A Nonpeelable Overlap of a Forbidden Expansion Is Itself Forbidden

                                                                Name: A Nonpeelable Overlap of a Forbidden Expansion Is Itself Forbidden

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Full Reduction
                                                                • Coordinate Conditioning
                                                                • Coordinate Projection

                                                                Result Type: Construction

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $H$ be an ample forbidden pc-minor and let $A=H^{\{e\}}$ be its full reduction in an active coordinate. If $A$ is not dismantlable ample, then $A$ is itself an ample forbidden pc-minor. Repeating this descent terminates at an obstruction whose full reduction in every active coordinate is dismantlable ample. Each inverse step canonically recovers $H=(A\times\{0,1\})\cup(R_0\times\{0\})\cup(R_1\times\{1\})$, with nonempty signed wings and with both sections and their union dismantlable ample.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Restriction and contraction in any other coordinate commute with full reduction on ample families. Applying full-reduction closure to the corresponding proper pc-minor of H shows that every elementary pc-minor of A is dismantlable ample. Thus a nonpeelable A is forbidden. Each step removes a coordinate, so descent terminates; the two-cone dichotomy makes every terminal coordinate gluing-critical. Periphery-freeness makes both inverse wings nonempty, and the sections and their union are proper pc-minors of H.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#thm:damp-inherited-overlap-descent

                                                                The overlap is a full reduction and need not itself be a pc-minor of the original family.

                                                                Marked Reduction Test for Proper Obstructions in an Expansion

                                                                Name: Marked Reduction Test for Proper Obstructions in an Expansion

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Partial-Cube Minor
                                                                • Full Reduction
                                                                • Coordinate Conditioning
                                                                • Coordinate Projection

                                                                Result Type: Implication

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $X\subseteq Q_{F\cup\{e\}}$ be ample, use all $n+1$ displayed coordinates, and have both $e$-sections and its $e$-contraction dismantlable ample. Put $O=X^{\{e\}}$. Every ample forbidden proper pc-minor $H$ of $X$ can be written $H=\nu X$, where the nonempty minor sequence $\nu$ uses only coordinates in $F$, leaves $e$ active, and satisfies $H^{\{e\}}=\nu O$. If $O$ is forbidden and uses all of $F$, then $\nu O$ is dismantlable ample. If $H$ has $n$ active coordinates, $\nu$ is one elementary operation, so the orders of the coordinate reductions of $H$ and of the elementary pc-minors of $O$ must have a common value.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Any operation deleting $e$ can be commuted to the start of a minor sequence; the result would then be a pc-minor of a positive $e$-section or contraction, contradicting that $H$ is forbidden. The coordinate $e$ cannot become constant for the same reason. Old-coordinate restrictions commute with reduction in $e$. For contraction, isometry supplies an intermediate vertex whenever projected $e$-mates come from opposite shores, giving $(\pi_qX)^{\{e\}}=\pi_qO$; iteration proves $H^{\{e\}}=\nu O$. If $O$ is forbidden and uses every old coordinate, the first operation is proper on $O$, so forbidden-minor minimality makes $\nu O$ positive. Retaining $n$ active coordinates permits exactly one nontrivial elementary operation, which yields the cardinality intersection test.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#prop:damp-inverse-proper-obstruction-reduction-test

                                                                Comments:

                                                                The cardinality intersection is necessary only; it is not an inverse-construction criterion.

                                                                Cube-Dimension Exclusion for Proper Minors of an Expansion

                                                                Name: Cube-Dimension Exclusion for Proper Minors of an Expansion

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Partial-Cube Minor
                                                                • Full Reduction

                                                                Result Type: Implication

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Under the marked-reduction hypotheses, every forbidden proper pc-minor $H$ of $X$ has an active coordinate $f$ such that $\operatorname{VC}(H^{\{f\}})\leq\operatorname{VC}(O)$. Hence, if $\operatorname{VC}(O)\leq d$, no ample forbidden class in which every active coordinate lies in a cube of dimension at least $d+2$ can be a proper pc-minor of $X$. In particular, overlap VC dimension at most three excludes every member of the 1364-vertex maximum-pair rectangular obstruction family.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Choose $f$ to be the surviving marked coordinate. The marked reduction theorem identifies $H^{\{f\}}$ with the pc-minor $\nu O$, so its VC dimension is at most that of $O$. A cube of dimension at least $d+2$ through $f$ would reduce to a cube of dimension at least $d+1$, contradicting this bound. In the rectangular family every coordinate belongs to a five-cube: combine a three-cube in its maximum rank-three factor with a two-cube in the opposite rank-two factor.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#cor:damp-inverse-cube-dimension-exclusion

                                                                Comments:

                                                                The rectangular exclusion uses only the product structure, independently of the signed realization of the factors.

                                                                Statement:

                                                                In the marked-reduction theorem, let the overlap be the recorded twelve-coordinate obstruction $O=Y_{267}$. No proper pc-minor of the expansion is isomorphic to $Y_{267}$ or to any of the 1364-vertex maximum-pair rectangular obstructions.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Every coordinate reduction of $Y_{267}$ has $267-208=59$ concepts, while its nonempty elementary restrictions have orders from 77 through 190 and its contractions have order 208. Thus the necessary one-operation cardinality match fails for a proper minor isomorphic to $Y_{267}$. In a rectangular obstruction $H=(P_1\times O_2)\cup(O_1\times P_2)$, a reduction in either six-coordinate block has order $16\cdot22+6\cdot(42-22)=472$. Since both candidate adversaries use twelve coordinates and 472 exceeds every elementary-minor order of $Y_{267}$, the same test excludes the rectangular family.

Then every vertex of every nonempty proper pc-minor of the forbidden expansion $X$ is an attainable sink. Consequently no pc-minor of $X$ is a rooted factor.

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Each section is all-sinks by hypothesis, and the contraction peels to either section after clearing the opposite wing. For an old-coordinate elementary operation $\mu$, the overlap is the positive family $\mu O$, the sections $\mu B_i$ retain every sink by rooted-minor transport, and both relative wing orders transport. To end in one section, clear the opposite wing, delete the redundant copy of $\mu O$, and finish with the prescribed endpoint order in the retained section. Rooted transport extends the construction to all proper pc-minors. A rooted factor has an unattainable root, while $X$ itself is nonpeelable.

                                                                Small 2-Core Components Force a Relatively Peelable Wing

                                                                Name: Small 2-Core Components Force a Relatively Peelable Wing

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                • Graph Expansion
                                                                • Concept Deletion

                                                                Result Type: Construction

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Under the structural and positive-section hypotheses of the one-relative-wing inverse theorem, suppose that in one exclusive wing every connected component of the graph 2-core has at most eight vertices. Then the expansion is an ample forbidden pc-minor, with no bound on the number of components or on trees attached to their 2-cores. Consequently, if neither section peels relatively to the overlap, each exclusive wing has a 2-core component on at least nine vertices.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                More generally, let $\varnothing\ne H\subseteq A$ have Cohen--Macaulay relative Yang module and put $D=A\setminus H$. Induct on $|D|$. A residual leaf either teaches relative to $H$, so it can be prepended after the teaching lift, or its deletion preserves Cohen--Macaulayness and it can be appended after induction. With no leaf, the relative Alexander-dual presentation splits over residual components. An isolated generator teaches; otherwise every component lies in the 2-core and has at most eight generators, so the eight-facet linear-quotients theorem supplies a teaching generator. Thus the wing has a relative ample chain, and the inverse theorem applies. The lower bound nine is the contrapositive for each wing.
