                                                                Removing a Uniform Inactive Coordinate Preserves Relative Peeling

                                                                Name: Removing a Uniform Inactive Coordinate Preserves Relative Peeling

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Coordinate Conditioning
                                                                • Concept Deletion

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $\varnothing\ne O\subsetneq B\subseteq Q_F$ be ample. Suppose every concept of $B\setminus O$ has value $b$ in coordinate $j$ and $O_j^b$ is nonempty. If $j$ belongs either to every relative shattered support in $\mathcal T=\operatorname{Sh}(B)\setminus\operatorname{Sh}(O)$ or to none of them, then restriction to the $j=b$ section preserves exactly the relative corner-deletion orders. Its relative supports are $\{S\setminus\{j\}:S\in\mathcal T\}$ without repetition, and deleting $j$ preserves the residual graph and all other edge labels.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Write $A=O_j^b$, $D=B_j^b$, and $C=O_j^{1-b}=B_j^{1-b}$. The two-section shadow identity shows that each support in $\operatorname{Sh}(D)\setminus\operatorname{Sh}(A)$ contributes exactly one relative support, containing $j$ precisely when it also lies in $\operatorname{Sh}(C)$. If no relative support contains $j$, cardinality equality shows that no residual concept has a $j$-neighbor, so every section corner lifts. If every support contains $j$, then $D\setminus A\subseteq C$ and $D\cup C=A\cup C$; for every ample intermediate $D'$ in a section order, the shadow union and intersection count proves that the family with sections $D'$ and $C$ remains ample. Thus every section deletion lifts, while restricting any whole-family order gives the converse.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#lem:damp-uniform-inactive-coordinate

                                                                A Corner of Codimension Two Is Not Unique Through Seven Coordinates

                                                                Name: A Corner of Codimension Two Is Not Unique Through Seven Coordinates

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Coordinate Conditioning
                                                                • Full Reduction
                                                                • Concept Deletion

                                                                Result Type: Implication

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $X$ be ample on $q+2$ coordinates with $1\leq q\leq5$. If a corner has degree $q$, then it is not the unique corner of $X$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Translate a hypothetical unique corner to zero, use its $q$ incident directions as $F$, and call the other directions $u,v$. The four fibers are $Q_F,P,Q,C$. Isometry and uniqueness give $P\cup Q=Q_F\setminus\{0\}$ and exclude zero from $P,Q,C$. Relative peeling in at most five coordinates shows $P,Q\subseteq C$, hence $C=P\cup Q=Q_F\setminus\{0\}$ and both $P,Q$ are nonempty. Compare the $u=1$ face with the $u$-reduction. Their relative supports all contain $v$, so uniform inactive-coordinate removal reduces the interval to $Q\subseteq C$, which peels relatively. Lift this peeling to $X$, then peel the retained upper layer, the remaining $Q$-layer, and finally the root cube to zero. The first deletion supplies a corner distinct from the alleged unique corner.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#cor:damp-unique-corner-codimension-two

                                                                A Unique Corner in Seven Coordinates Could Only Have Degree Three

                                                                Name: A Unique Corner in Seven Coordinates Could Only Have Degree Three

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes

                                                                Result Type: Implication

                                                                Statement:

                                                                If an ample class using seven coordinates has a unique corner, that corner has degree three. The exclusion of degree four is computer-assisted.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Existing prescribed-endpoint and overlap results exclude degrees one and two. Full-cube arguments exclude degrees six and seven, and the codimension-two theorem excludes degree five. For degree four, normalize the root cube as $Q_4\times\{0\}$. A symbolic proper-fiber lemma yields a proper nontrivial three-coordinate fiber at a unit root neighbor. The 62 labelled ample possibilities form 17 coordinate-permutation orbits. For each representative, Lawrence's exact total-asymmetry encoding, unique-corner clauses, full coordinate support, the order bound, and fixed fiber literals give a formula with 10,943 variables and 65,378 clauses. All 17 necessary cases have independently checked DRAT refutations; an eighteenth redundant orbit is also certified.

                                                                Comments:

                                                                The database certificate audit verifies all 54 archived files for the 18 DRAT cases against the preserved manifest. The complete CNF, DRAT, and log bytes remain LaTeX-owned.

                                                                Every Ample Class Through Seven Coordinates Peels to Any Prescribed Endpoint

                                                                Name: Every Ample Class Through Seven Coordinates Peels to Any Prescribed Endpoint

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Concept Deletion
                                                                • One-Point Amalgam

                                                                Result Type: Algorithm

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Every nonempty ample class of isometric dimension at most seven has a corner-peeling order ending at any prescribed concept. Consequently every rooted factor has isometric dimension at least eight, and every ample forbidden pc-minor for dismantlable ampleness that has a cut vertex has isometric dimension at least sixteen.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The result is known through six coordinates. In dimension seven, the preceding degree analysis leaves degree three as the only possible unique-corner degree. A proper-fiber reduction enumerates 2,763 labelled nontrivial ample four-coordinate fibers containing zero in 185 coordinate-permutation orbits. Exact total-asymmetry formulas with 10,943 variables and 65,379 clauses have independently checked DRAT refutations for all 185 cases, excluding degree three. Every nontrivial ample class through dimension seven therefore has at least two corners; repeatedly delete a corner different from the prescribed endpoint. A rooted factor cannot admit such an order. A forbidden ample class with a cut vertex decomposes into two rooted factors on disjoint coordinate sets, so their dimensions add to at least $8+8=16$.

                                                                Comments:

                                                                The database certificate audit verifies all 555 archived files for the 185 DRAT cases against the preserved manifest. The complete CNF, DRAT, and log bytes remain LaTeX-owned.

                                                                A Nonpeelable Residual Cycle Requires Uniform Cyclic Support Exchanges

                                                                Name: A Nonpeelable Residual Cycle Requires Uniform Cyclic Support Exchanges

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Concept Deletion
                                                                • Coordinate Conditioning
                                                                • Graph Expansion

                                                                Result Type: Implication

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $\varnothing\ne O\subsetneq B\subseteq Q_F$ be ample and let the residual graph $G(B\setminus O)$ be a cycle of length greater than four. At least as many residual vertices admit an ample addition to $O$ or deletion from $B$ as there are nonisolated relative supports. If $B$ does not peel to $O$, its residual vertices and relative supports admit cyclic bijective listings $c_i,S_i$ with $c_{i+1}=c_i^{\{e_i\}}$, $S_i\setminus S_{i+1}=\{e_i\}$, and $|S_{i+1}\setminus S_i|=1$. All supports have one cardinality and agree off the residual active set $Y$. For $k=|S_i\cap Y|$, restriction to the smallest containing face preserves the interval and $3\leq k\leq|Y|-3$, while $2|Y|\leq m\leq\binom{|Y|}{k}$. Thus failure requires at least six active coordinates and twelve residual vertices. Different support sizes, disagreement outside $Y$, or cycle length at most ten each forces relative peeling and suffices for the one-wing inverse construction.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The degree-two marker theorem injects vertices blocked at both the addition and deletion ends into isolated relative supports; any unblocked vertex breaks the cycle into a path and the relative forest theorem completes a peeling. Under failure the injection is bijective. Carrier duality and exact edge orientation direct the cycle and force consecutive isolated supports to exchange exactly their edge coordinate. Going around the cycle forces equal support sizes and constant coordinates outside the residual active set. Remove those coordinates by uniform inactive-coordinate reduction. Relative small-support peeling, applied also to the complementary ample interval, gives $3\leq k\leq|Y|-3$. Every active coordinate occurs a positive even number of times on the closed cube walk, yielding $m\geq2|Y|$; distinct $k$-subsets give the binomial upper bound. The sufficient conditions follow by contraposition.

                                                                References:

                                                                [BousquetResidualExtension26] [BousquetYangComplex26]

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#cor:damp-marked-cycle-wing-inverse

                                                                Witnesses:

                                                                • A Residual Six-Cycle Whose Designated Vertex Can Be Neither First Nor Last

                                                                Comments:

                                                                The cyclic exchange conditions are necessary for failure, not sufficient. The vertexwise first-or-last dichotomy is false on cycles, as the linked relatively peelable six-cycle shows.

                                                                Simultaneous Extensions Retaining a Negative Reduction Are Forbidden

                                                                Name: Simultaneous Extensions Retaining a Negative Reduction Are Forbidden

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Concept Deletion
                                                                • Full Reduction
                                                                • Partial-Cube Minor

                                                                Result Type: Construction

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $X\subseteq Y\subseteq Q_F$ be ample, with $X$ an irredundant forbidden pc-minor. If an active coordinate $e$ satisfies $X^{\{e\}}=Y^{\{e\}}\notin\mathsf{Damp}$ and $Y$ peels to $X$, then $Y$ is a forbidden pc-minor. It is enough that every connected component of $G(Y\setminus X)$ be a tree or have at most eight vertices; the number of components and the sizes of tree components are unrestricted, and no addition order or proper-minor peeling certificates need be supplied.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Apply any elementary old-coordinate operation $\mu$ to the relative deletion sequence from $Y$ to $X$ and omit repeated images. The remaining singleton changes form a relative peeling from $\mu Y$ to the positive proper minor $\mu X$, so every proper elementary minor of $Y$ is dismantlable ample. The shared negative reduction keeps $Y$ outside that class, proving forbiddenness. Under the graph condition, component expansion makes $X\cup K$ ample for each residual component $K$; the relative forest theorem or the theorem through eight relative facets peels it to $X$. Components are mutually nonadjacent, so their orders concatenate and the first part applies.

                                                                References:

                                                                [BousquetYangComplex26]

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#prop:damp-fixed-negative-reduction-extension

                                                                Comments:

                                                                No converse is claimed: an arbitrary reduction-preserving extension need not have these component graphs, and a reduced obstruction need not contain a suitable smaller forbidden input.

                                                                Opposite Peripheral Completions of Rooted Factors

                                                                Name: Opposite Peripheral Completions of Rooted Factors

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Peripheral Expansion
                                                                • One-Point Amalgam
                                                                • Full Reduction
                                                                • Partial-Cube Minor

                                                                Result Type: Construction

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $(A_i,0)$, $i=0,1$, be rooted factors on disjoint coordinate blocks $F_i$, and choose ample supersets $A_i\subseteq T_i\subseteq Q_{F_i}$. For a fresh coordinate $e$, put $B_0=T_0\vee A_1$, $B_1=A_0\vee T_1$, and $X=(B_0\times\{0\})\cup(B_1\times\{1\})$. Then $X$ is ample, and it is a pc-minimal obstruction to dismantlable ampleness exactly when each $T_i$ admits an acyclic USO with sink $0$, equivalently when both sections $B_i$ are dismantlable ample. In that case the contraction is also positive, while the reduction is the forbidden overlap $A_0\vee A_1$. The marked sections and coordinate blocks recover all four inputs uniquely, and $|X|=|A_0|+|A_1|+|T_0|+|T_1|-2$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The two peripheral pieces meet in one edge and have disjoint private coordinate blocks. Their shadows intersect only in the empty support and the layer singleton, so shadow counting proves ampleness. The layer reduction is the forbidden wedge of the rooted factors. If $X$ is forbidden, positivity of its sections and the vertex-gluing criterion force each $T_i$ to peel to the root. Conversely those endpoint orders make both sections, the contraction, and the two peripheral pieces positive. In every old-coordinate proper minor, rooted minimality and transported endpoint orders clear the changed peripheral piece to the common edge, leaving the unchanged positive piece. Thus every proper pc-minor peels while $X$ does not. Intersecting the marked sections with their two coordinate blocks recovers the inputs.

                                                                References:

                                                                [BousquetYangComplex26]

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#prop:damp-opposite-peripheral-completions

                                                                Witnesses:

                                                                • A 1157-Concept Obstruction with One Edge Wing and One Singleton Wing

                                                                Nested Separating-Edge Pieces Are Exactly Opposite Peripheral Completions

                                                                Name: Nested Separating-Edge Pieces Are Exactly Opposite Peripheral Completions

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Crossing Graph

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Peripheral Expansion
                                                                • One-Point Amalgam
                                                                • Full Reduction

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Opposite peripheral completion generates exactly the ample pc-minimal obstructions to dismantlable ampleness having a separating edge for which the two layer sections of every canonical piece are nested. Such an obstruction has exactly two pieces. Their larger sections lie on opposite sides and attain the projected root as a sink; their smaller sections are the two rooted factors. The separating edge and all four inputs are unique up to exchanging the pieces and reversing the edge. Consequently every three-piece forbidden edge amalgam has a canonical piece with nonnested sections.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                In a nested piece, if both sections attained the root then their endpoint orders would peel the piece to the common edge, which the separator obstruction criterion forbids. Positivity of both global sections and of the contraction permits at most one root failure in each image. Counting those failures forces exactly two pieces, with the smaller root-negative sections on opposite layers and all larger sections root-positive. Their contraction is a forbidden vertex gluing, so the cut-vertex theorem identifies the smaller sections as rooted factors. Conversely, each constructed peripheral piece remains connected after deleting the shared edge, so these are precisely the canonical pieces. Strong descent makes the separating edge unique, after which its components and nested sections recover every input.

                                                                References:

                                                                [BousquetYangComplex26]

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#cor:damp-peripheral-separator-recovery

                                                                Strong Reduction Descent in the Separator Branch

                                                                Name: Strong Reduction Descent in the Separator Branch

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Crossing Graph

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Full Reduction
                                                                • Coordinate Projection
                                                                • Partial-Cube Minor

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $H\subseteq Q_F$ be an irredundantly embedded ample pc-minimal obstruction to dismantlable ampleness. Every nonpeelable reduction $H^D$ is itself an ample pc-minimal obstruction and uses every coordinate in $F\setminus D$; in particular, a coordinate with nonpeelable singleton reduction is universal in the crossing graph. If that graph is not two-connected, then either every nonempty reduction peels, or there is a unique coordinate $e$ and the only nonpeelable reductions are $H$ and $H^{\{e\}}$. In the latter case $e$ is the unique universal vertex and cut vertex of the crossing graph, its deletion has exactly two components, $H$ has a unique separating $e$-edge, and $H^{\{e\}}$ is the uniquely determined cut-vertex obstruction formed by the strong projections of those two pieces. Thus descent in the separator branch has length at most one.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Elementary operations outside $D$ commute with reduction. If a surviving coordinate were inactive, deleting it from $H$ would give a positive proper minor whose reduction is isomorphic to the assumed negative family, a contradiction. Iterated inherited-overlap descent therefore makes every negative reduction forbidden. A singleton negative reduction uses every remaining direction, and each such edge lifts to a square, making its deleted coordinate universal in the crossing graph. A non-two-connected graph of order at least three has at most one universal vertex, so there is at most one negative singleton reduction and no larger negative support. If it exists, deleting that universal coordinate disconnects the crossing graph into exactly the two coordinate blocks of the cut-vertex reduction; crossing-graph separator recovery lifts them to a unique separating edge of $H$ and identifies its strong projections.

                                                                References:

                                                                [BousquetYangComplex26]

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#thm:damp-separator-strong-descent

                                                                Witnesses:

                                                                • Terminal Cut-Vertex Obstruction of Order 1158
                                                                • A Separator-Free Obstruction with a Nonpeelable Strong Reduction

                                                                Comments:

                                                                Universality locates the only possible descent coordinate but does not imply that its reduction is nonpeelable; both outcomes occur among the fixed examples.

                                                                Square Attachments Leave Nonpeelable Strong Carriers Unchanged

                                                                Name: Square Attachments Leave Nonpeelable Strong Carriers Unchanged

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Crossing Graph
                                                                • Shattered Complex

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Concept Deletion
                                                                • Full Reduction
                                                                • Partial-Cube Minor

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $H$ be an irredundantly embedded ample pc-minimal obstruction to dismantlable ampleness, and let $K$ be its canonical graph three-core. For every nonempty coordinate set $D$, the reduction $H^D$ is nonpeelable exactly when $K^D$ is, and then the two embedded reductions are equal. No acquired pair of any square attachment meets a coordinate $e$ with nonpeelable $H^{\{e\}}$. At such an $e$, relative peelability of either section to the common negative overlap is also identical for $H$ and $K$. Consequently, if the crossing graph of $K$ is not two-connected, reduction descent from $H$ has length at most one and the same unique cut-vertex terminal obstruction, even when $H$ itself has no separator.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Reconstruct $H$ from $K$ by ample one-concept additions with acquired coordinate pairs $I$. Under reduction by $D$, one such step either disappears or remains a one-corner addition with acquired support $I\setminus D$. If the earlier reduction is nonpeelable, full-coordinate strong descent says it already shatters every surviving singleton; hence $D\subseteq I$ is impossible and the two reductions are equal. For $D=\{e\}$ this also proves $e\notin I$. The new concept then changes only one $e$-section, by a rank-two addition disjoint from $e$; rank-two relative-extension invariance preserves peelability to the fixed overlap in both directions. Iterating proves all assertions, and applying separator strong descent to $K$ gives the final conclusion.

                                                                Replacing One Coordinate by a Nonempty Block

                                                                Name: Replacing One Coordinate by a Nonempty Block

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Shattered Complex
                                                                • Signed Minimal-Nonface Presentation
                                                                • Crossing Graph

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Full Reduction
                                                                • Coordinate Conditioning
                                                                • Partial-Cube Minor

                                                                Result Type: Construction

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For ample $H\subseteq Q_{G\cup\{z\}}$, write $B_i=\rho_z^iH$, $C=B_0\cup B_1$, and $A=B_0\cap B_1$. Replace $z$ by a nonempty block $E$ of size $m$ and set $W_E(H)=(B_0\times\{0_E\})\cup(B_1\times\{1_E\})\cup(C\times(Q_E\setminus\{0_E,1_E\}))$. Then $W_E(H)$ is ample, $|W_E(H)|=(2^m-1)|C|+|A|$, and its shadow is the disjoint union of $\{D\cup T:D\in\operatorname{Sh}(C),T\subsetneq E\}$ and $\{D\cup E:D\in\operatorname{Sh}(A)\}$. For nonempty $H$, VC dimension rises by $m-1$. Signed minimal nonfaces avoiding $z$ remain unchanged, and each one containing $z$ replaces it by all of $E$ with the old sign repeated. Dismantlable ampleness, pc-minimal obstruction status for active irredundant input, and cornerlessness are each preserved in both directions. For a forbidden input and $m\ge2$, the output has minimum degree at least three, is its own graph three-core, and has a two-connected crossing graph in which every coordinate of $E$ is universal. The marked construction is uniquely recoverable from its two constant sections or its signed clauses.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The nonconstant block rows all carry $C$, while the two constant rows carry $B_0$ and $B_1$. This gives the displayed shadow and order formulas, and Sandwich equality proves ampleness; minimal nonfaces follow from the same decomposition. A binary replacement lifts each corner deletion of $H$: over an overlap word delete its constant lift, and over an exclusive word delete the two nonconstant lifts before the matching constant lift. Reduction along either new coordinate recovers $H$, proving positivity equivalence; iteration handles all block sizes. Old-coordinate elementary minors commute with replacement, while new-coordinate minors are products or peripheral expansions of the positive proper minors $A,B_i,C$, proving obstruction equivalence. Every new vertex gains at least $m-1$ fibre neighbors, cornerlessness projects through a full fibre, and the shadow formula makes every new coordinate universal. Two universal vertices make the crossing graph two-connected. The two constant sections and clause substitution give unique recovery.

                                                                [BousquetYangComplex26]

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#thm:damp-coordinate-block-replacement

                                                                Relative Peeling Is Preserved by Coordinate-Block Replacement

                                                                Name: Relative Peeling Is Preserved by Coordinate-Block Replacement

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Concept Deletion
                                                                • Full Reduction
                                                                • Coordinate Conditioning

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For nonempty ample $T\subseteq H$ with marked coordinate $z$, $W_E(H)$ peels to $W_E(T)$ exactly when $H$ peels to $T$. If $H$ is an ample forbidden class, $|E|\ge2$, and $e\in E$, then the $e=b$ section of $W_E(H)$ peels to its $e$-reduction exactly when the old section $B_b$ peels to the old overlap $A=B_0\cap B_1$. For every coordinate outside the replaced block, relative peelability of either section to its reduction is also unchanged.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The corner-lifting construction for block replacement applies to any deletion prefix and can stop when $T$ remains. Conversely, reduce all but one block coordinate; the images of a relative corner sequence are ample and consecutive images either agree or differ by one concept, so removing repetitions gives a relative sequence from $H$ to $T$. For a new coordinate in a binary block, the deletable vertices are precisely the lifts of $B_b\setminus A$, and their corner cubes correspond term by term to the old section corner cubes. Larger blocks reduce to this binary pair by replacement of the other coordinate. Old-coordinate sections and reductions commute with replacement, so the general equivalence applies directly.

                                                                Name: Protected-Certificate Depth Is Unbounded

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For every $m\ge1$ there is an ample pc-minimal obstruction $K_m$ to dismantlable ampleness with $|K_m|=560\cdot2^m-493$, isometric dimension $m+23$, VC dimension $m+5$, empty protected core, and $d_{\mathrm{prot}}(K_m)\ge2^m$. The family is obtained by replacing one coordinate of a fixed $627$-concept obstruction by a block of size $m$. For $m>1$ it has negative coordinate reductions.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                A fixed $626$-concept root-cube completion has empty protected core, certified by an ordering in which every vertex's later-neighbour directions span a cube in the original family. Adding one compatible tip and replacing a nonincident coordinate by $m$ coordinates expands that tip into a punctured fibre of $2^m-1$ vertices. Block-relative transfer peels this fibre back to the expanded base. Every intermediate family still peels relatively to a target with empty protected core, so it also has empty protected core. Every corner-choice proof tree contains this branch and cannot stop even at the base, giving depth at least $2^m$. Block replacement preserves forbiddenness, and its order, isometric-dimension, and VC-dimension formulas give the stated parameters.

                                                                Rooted Factors and Frozen Missing-Cube Witnesses Survive Block Replacement

                                                                Name: Rooted Factors and Frozen Missing-Cube Witnesses Survive Block Replacement

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Full Reduction
                                                                • Coordinate Conditioning
                                                                • Coordinate Projection

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                If $(A,0)$ is a rooted factor for the cut-vertex obstruction theorem and an active coordinate $z$ is replaced by a nonempty block $E$, then the constant lift of $0$ makes $W_E(A)$ a rooted factor. Suppose additionally that $0^{\{z\}}\in A$ and that each nonroot $x\in A$ has a missing-cube witness $J_x$ whose single-direction neighbours lie in $A$ and whose opposite word lies outside a fixed $C\supseteq A$. Then every nonroot lift in $W_E(A)$ has such a witness missing from $W_E(C)$. In particular, if $0$ is the unique corner of $A$, its constant lift is the unique corner of $W_E(A)$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Block-relative transfer preserves ordinary root attainability and root failure. Root-preserving old-coordinate minors commute with replacement; a new-coordinate contraction is a product and a new-coordinate root restriction is a peripheral expansion of proper rooted minors, so rooted minimality persists. For a lift $v=(y,t)$ choose an old nonroot preimage $x=(y,s)$, using $0^{\{z\}}$ for a nonconstant root fibre. Replace the old witness by its old directions outside $z$ together with block coordinates that move $t$ toward the constant pole opposite the missing trace. Every required neighbour is present in $W_E(A)$, while the opposite vertex is the constant lift of $x^{J_x}\notin C$. Applying this with $C=A$ protects every nonroot lift; the lifted old root cube certifies the remaining root corner.

                                                                Coordinate-Block Replacement Preserves All Prescribed Sinks

                                                                Name: Coordinate-Block Replacement Preserves All Prescribed Sinks

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                If every vertex of a nonempty ample family $H$ is the sink of some acyclic unique-sink orientation, then the same is true of every coordinate-block replacement $W_E(H)$. If $H$ is an irredundant ample pc-minimal obstruction to dismantlable ampleness and every proper pc-minor of $H$ admits every prescribed sink, then $W_E(H)$ is also forbidden and all its proper pc-minors have that prescribed-sink property. Nevertheless, block replacement can create a forbidden expansion whose two positive sections both fail to peel relatively to their negative overlap.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Choose an old preimage $r$ of a desired lifted vertex. An order of $H$ ending at $r$ lifts relatively to the expanded singleton fibre, which is a punctured block cube; every vertex of a punctured cube is an attainable sink, so the order finishes at the chosen lift. For proper minors it is enough to split one coordinate at a time. Old-coordinate minors are replacements of proper minors of $H$. New-coordinate contractions are products, and new-coordinate restrictions are peripheral expansions of the old contraction and sections. Their inputs have every prescribed sink, so the product and rooted peripheral criteria transfer the property. Iteration treats every block size; forbiddenness follows from block replacement.

                                                                Arbitrary Enlargement of One Nonconstant Row

                                                                Name: Arbitrary Enlargement of One Nonconstant Row

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Nonconstant-Row Enlargement
                                                                • Full Reduction
                                                                • Peripheral Expansion
                                                                • Partial-Cube Minor

                                                                Result Type: Construction

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let nonempty ample $H\subseteq Q_{F\cup\{z\}}$ have sections $B_0,B_1$ and contraction $C$, and let ample $D\supseteq C$. The four-row family $V(H,D)=(B_0\times\{00\})\cup(D\times\{01\})\cup(C\times\{10\})\cup(B_1\times\{11\})$ is ample and has first-coordinate reduction $H$. It peels to its $D$-row exactly when $H$ peels, and it is dismantlable ample exactly when both $H$ and $D$ are. If $H$ has full support, then $V(H,D)$ is a pc-minimal obstruction exactly when $H$ is a pc-minimal obstruction and $D$ is dismantlable ample. Marked oriented rows uniquely recover $H$ and $D$; no relative peeling $D\searrow C$ is required.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Completing One Nonconstant Block Row

                                                                Name: Completing One Nonconstant Block Row

Replace $z$ by a binary block and add $(x,0,1)$ to a nonconstant row. The result is an ample forbidden pc-minor with that concept as its unique corner and minimum degree at least three; its reduction in either block coordinate is $H$, and neither section peels to the negative overlap. If the signed-clause columns of $H$ are distinct up to sign, the output also has this property and is fixed by both canonical reductions. Conversely, any irredundant ample forbidden pc-minor with a unique corner of degree at least three whose deletion makes two signed-clause columns agree up to sign, with opposite corner bits in those columns, has exactly this marked presentation. Its cornerless forbidden input, added old word, and acquired support are uniquely recovered for the marked pair.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The added concept completes exactly its acquired support cube, so the local extension criterion proves ampleness. It has no mate in either block direction, leaving a reduction equal to the negative input; reduction closure therefore prevents peeling, and the one-concept extension theorem gives forbiddenness. The corner-lifting argument for block replacement rules out every old corner, while the acquired support gives the new corner degree. Tracking the two new minimal nonfaces distinguishes the block columns and preserves every old signed-column distinction. Conversely, equal signed columns recover the block presentation. The negative reduction and block peeling equivalence recover a forbidden input; any input corner would lift to an old corner surviving the addition, contradicting uniqueness. Contracting both block coordinates recovers the one-concept extension and its support.

                                                                Two Complementary Components Force Antipodal Cube Rows

                                                                Name: Two Complementary Components Force Antipodal Cube Rows

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $A\subseteq C$ be dismantlable ample, suppose $C\setminus A$ has exactly two connected components $K_0,K_1$, and assume the two-layer family $H=(A\times\{0,1\})\cup(K_0\times\{0\})\cup(K_1\times\{1\})$ is an ample forbidden pc-minor. For a nonempty new coordinate block $E$, form $Z$ by retaining every word over $A$ and deleting precisely $q_i\in Q_E$ over each word of $K_i$. Then $Z$ is forbidden exactly when $q_0,q_1$ are antipodal; in that case it is a coordinate-block replacement of $H$ up to reorientation and renaming. If $q_0=q_1$, then $Z$ is dismantlable ample. If they are distinct and nonantipodal, $Z$ has a nonpeelable proper coordinate-face restriction and is not forbidden.

                                                                Proof:

                                                                For antipodal omitted words, reorient the block so they are $1_E,0_E$; the displayed family is exactly the coordinate-block replacement of $H$. For equal words, reorient their common value to $0_E$; the family becomes the block replacement of the peripheral family $(A,C)$, which is dismantlable ample. Otherwise choose block coordinates $e,f$ on which the omitted words respectively agree and disagree. Restrict to their common $e$-value and reduce every remaining block coordinate except $f$. The full fibre over $A$ survives, while the fibres over $K_0,K_1$ retain opposite $f$-values, producing $H$ up to reorientation. This active proper face has a negative reduction, so $Z$ cannot be forbidden.

                                                                One Relative Section Suffices for Mixed-Puncture Retention

                                                                Name: One Relative Section Suffices for Mixed-Puncture Retention

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let an ample family $H$ contain a marked edge with endpoints $a_0,a_1$, and write $A_0,A_1$ for its sections, $D=A_0\cap A_1$, and $C=A_0\cup A_1$. Replace the edge coordinate by a binary block, with root square $T$. If at least one section peels relatively to $D$, then for either mixed word $q$, the block replacement peels to $T\setminus\{q\}$ exactly when $H$ peels to each marked endpoint. The forward implication holds without the relative-section hypothesis. Therefore any counterexample to the reverse implication without that hypothesis must have both relative sections fail, and each exclusive wing must contain a cyclic component of at least nine vertices.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Reducing any proposed block peeling in each new coordinate and deleting repetitions produces rooted peelings of $H$ to both endpoints, proving necessity. For sufficiency, normalize so $A_0$ peels to $D$. Delete its exclusive wing in one nonconstant block row. The absence of edges between opposite exclusive wings makes every lifted deletion valid. One retained block section is now a copy of $H$ and the other is a peripheral family containing it; use the two endpoint orders to delete the copy and then the smaller retained row, followed by the contraction order for $C$. Exactly the three unpunctured root-square vertices remain. If both relative sections fail, the component-expansion theorem says each overlap-plus-component family is ample; the relative forest and eight-facet theorem would peel a wing whose components were all trees or had at most eight vertices, yielding the final necessary condition.

                                                                Exact Relative Criterion for an Adjacent Square Hole

In a forbidden input, the recovered block face and its reduction make the first factor positive; a nonmissing face makes the second factor positive.                                                                 Endpoint Puncture Converse and the Terminal Forbidden Branch

                                                                • Ample Classes

                                                                Statement:

The assertion that every ample marked-edge family $A$ whose two endpoints are attainable has its binary block replacement peel to either mixed-punctured root square is equivalent to the absence of a forbidden mixed-puncture square attachment with every coordinate reduction dismantlable ample. If the assertion fails, a counterexample minimal under pc-minors retaining the marked edge produces such a forbidden attachment with this $B$ and with every other rooted factor on disjoint coordinates. Every counterexample uses at least seven coordinates, fails to retain its full marked edge, and has in each exclusive wing a cyclic component of at least nine vertices. A minor-minimal counterexample has no cut vertex and its marked edge is not separating.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                If all reductions of an attachment are positive, the reduction criterion makes both endpoints attainable; the endpoint assertion would then make the block peel to the punctured square, and the attachment theorem would make the output positive. Conversely, minimize a counterexample among edge-retaining minors. Every private proper image restores puncture retention, while the two endpoint orders give the required section and contraction orders, so the exact adjacent-square criterion makes its attachment forbidden. The reduction theorem makes every coordinate reduction positive. Failure to retain the full edge, the cyclic-wing bounds, and the seven-coordinate lower bound follow from block transport, one-wing retention, and five-coordinate relative peeling. If a cut vertex or separating marked edge existed, all other convex pieces could be peeled away while preserving endpoint attainability, producing a smaller counterexample and contradicting minimality.

                                                                Coordinate Blocks Produce Arbitrarily Many Maximal Descent Supports

                                                                Name: Coordinate Blocks Produce Arbitrarily Many Maximal Descent Supports

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes

                                                                • Coordinate-Block Replacement

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $W_E(H)$ replace a coordinate $z$ of $H$ by a nonempty coordinate block $E$, and let $D$ be a set of old coordinates and $T\subseteq E$. If $T$ is proper in $E$, then the reduction on $D\cup T$ is $W_{E\setminus T}(H^D)$; if $T=E$, it is $H^{D\cup\{z\}}$. Hence the reduction is nonpeelable exactly when the indicated reduction of $H$ is nonpeelable. In particular, if $H$ is an ample forbidden pc-minor whose every nonempty-coordinate reduction peels, then the nonpeelable reductions of $W_E(H)$ are exactly the proper subsets of $E$. For $|E|=m$, there are exactly $m$ maximal descent supports $E\setminus\{e\}$, every maximal one-coordinate negative descent has length $m-1$, and every endpoint is $H$ with its marked coordinate renamed.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Reduction in old coordinates commutes with block replacement. The only nontrivial section identity is $(B_0\cup B_1)^D=B_0^D\cup B_1^D$: any full $D$-cube in the union is shattered by one of the two sections and therefore lies wholly in it. Reducing a proper subset of block coordinates leaves the same constant and nonconstant fibre pattern on the remaining block; reducing all of them requires the old word to lie in the original reduction. The block peeling equivalence transfers nonpeelability. Under the terminal-reduction hypothesis on $H$, only $D=\varnothing$ can remain negative in the proper-block case, while the full-block case is positive. The maximal proper subsets of an $m$-element block give the stated count, lengths, and endpoints.

                                                                Canonical Signed-Column Reduction and Multiplicity Parametrization

                                                                Name: Canonical Signed-Column Reduction and Multiplicity Parametrization

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Coordinate-Block Replacement
                                                                • Full Reduction

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $H\subseteq Q_F$ be an irredundantly embedded ample forbidden pc-minor. For every signed minimal nonface $I$, let the column $v_e(I)$ of coordinate $e$ be $0$ when $e\notin I$ and the signed incidence $2\sigma_I(e)-1$ when $e\in I$. Partition $F$ by $e\sim f$ when $v_e=\pm v_f$. Reorient each class so its columns agree, retain one representative from every class, and fully reduce all other coordinates. The resulting family $R$ is an irredundant ample forbidden pc-minor whose columns are pairwise distinct up to sign. The family $H$ is recovered from $R$ by coordinate-block replacement, using the equivalence-class sizes as positive multiplicities. The reduced family and multiplicities are unique up to coordinate renaming and reorientation, and every sequence of equal-column compressions reaches the same reduced family. Conversely, every such reduced forbidden family and every assignment of positive coordinate multiplicities produces an ample forbidden family and is recovered by this reduction.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                After reorientation, every signed minimal-nonface clause either avoids an equal-column class $E$ or contains all of $E$ with one constant forbidden sign. If $B_0,B_1$ are the constant sections and $C$ is defined by the clauses avoiding $E$, then $B_0\cup B_1\subseteq C$. A word in the difference would induce the face $Q_E\setminus\{0_E,1_E\}$, which has $2^{|E|}-2$ concepts but $2^{|E|}-1$ shattered supports, contradicting closure of ampleness under face restriction. Thus $C=B_0\cup B_1$, exactly the coordinate-block pattern. Reducing all but one coordinate of $E$ therefore recovers a smaller ample nonpeelable family; the strong-descent theorem makes it an irredundant forbidden pc-minor. Compression bijects the signed clauses and leaves every other column unchanged, so distinct equivalence classes never merge. Induction proves canonicity and independence of representatives and compression order. Conversely, coordinate-block replacement preserves forbiddenness and simply repeats the selected signed-clause column; replacements commute, so compression recovers precisely the starting family and its multiplicities.

                                                                Canonical Alternating Graph and Signed-Column Normal Form

                                                                Name: Canonical Alternating Graph and Signed-Column Normal Form

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Concept Deletion
                                                                • Coordinate-Block Replacement
                                                                • Full Reduction

                                                                Result Type: Algorithm

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $H$ be an irredundantly embedded ample forbidden pc-minor of VC dimension $d$. Repeatedly either delete a degree-two vertex or compress two signed minimal-nonface columns that agree up to sign. Every maximal reduction sequence reaches, up to coordinate renaming and reorientation, the same ample forbidden family $H_*$, which has minimum degree at least three and pairwise distinct signed columns up to sign. Maximal runs of one reduction type form canonical alternating phases: graph phases take the full graph three-core and column phases compress every repeated column. If there are $q$ column phases and $s$ graph phases, then $q\le d-\operatorname{VC}(H_*)\le d-3$, $s\le q+1$, and $q+s\le2d-5$; every phase preserves $\operatorname{idim}-\operatorname{VC}$. Conversely, every ample forbidden family is recovered uniquely from such a reduced base by a finite alternating sequence of nonempty admissible square attachments and nontrivial coordinate-block replacements, including the attachment data and coordinate multiplicities. Every minimum-cardinality ample forbidden family is fixed by both reductions.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The two reduction types are mutually exclusive on forbidden families: repeated signed columns express the family as a nontrivial coordinate-block replacement, whose output has minimum degree at least three. Both reductions preserve ample forbidden-minor status and strictly reduce cardinality. Exhausting degree-two deletions gives the choice-independent graph three-core, while exhausting repeated columns gives the choice-independent canonical signed-column reduction; mutual exclusion forces these canonical phases to alternate and proves uniqueness by induction. Graph phases preserve isometric and VC dimensions. A column phase lowers both dimensions by the same positive sum of multiplicity excesses, so $q\le d-\operatorname{VC}(H_*)$; every ample forbidden family has VC dimension at least three, and alternation gives $s\le q+1$. For the inverse direction, a nonempty square attachment is recovered by the graph phase and creates degree-two vertices but no repeated columns, whereas a nontrivial block replacement is recovered by the column phase and creates minimum degree at least three. Induction yields exact phase-by-phase reconstruction and completeness. Either reduction of a minimum-cardinality obstruction would contradict minimality.

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#thm:damp-alternating-reductions

                                                                Witnesses:

                                                                Comments:

                                                                The terminal base is a canonical normal form, but minimum degree at least three and distinct signed columns do not by themselves characterize forbiddenness. The 42-concept weight-at-most-three down-set in $Q_6$ is a peelable ample counterexample to that converse.

                                                                Both Wings of an Overlap-Atomic Obstruction Contain Cycles

                                                                Name: Both Wings of an Overlap-Atomic Obstruction Contain Cycles

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Coordinate Conditioning
                                                                • Full Reduction

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $H$ be an ample forbidden pc-minor whose full reduction in every nonempty coordinate set is dismantlable ample. For any active coordinate $e$, write $B_b=\rho_e^bH$, $A=B_0\cap B_1$, and $R_b=B_b\setminus A$. Then both induced relative-wing graphs $Q[R_0]$ and $Q[R_1]$ contain a cycle. Consequently $|R_0|,|R_1|\ge4$ and $|H|=2|A|+|R_0|+|R_1|\ge2|A|+8$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Overlap atomicity and pc-minimality put the overlap $A$ and both sections $B_0,B_1$ in the dismantlable-ample class, so each relative Yang module for $A\subseteq B_b$ is Cohen--Macaulay. If one relative-wing graph were a forest, the relative Yang forest theorem would give a relative shelling of that section over $A$. The Yang two-cone gluing dichotomy would then make $H$ corner-peelable, contradicting that it is forbidden. Both wings therefore contain cycles. Cube graphs are bipartite, so each cycle uses at least four vertices; the section identity $|H|=|B_0|+|B_1|=2|A|+|R_0|+|R_1|$ gives the order bound.

                                                                [BousquetYangComplex26]

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#prop:damp-atomic-wing-cycle-carriers

                                                                Comments:

                                                                The paired wing cycle spaces are the first nonzero layer of the manuscript's proposed rooted signed cycle invariant. This result supplies a necessary condition, not an intrinsic classification of overlap-atomic seeds.

                                                                The Rooted Signed Graph Presents the Relative Yang Module

                                                                Name: The Rooted Signed Graph Presents the Relative Yang Module

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Concept Deletion

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $A\subsetneq B\subseteq Q_F$ be ample, $D=B\setminus A$, $S_F=k[v_{q,0},v_{q,1}:q\in F]$, $m_x=\prod_{q\in F}v_{q,1-x_q}$, $J_X=(m_x:x\in X)$, and $\mathcal Q(B,A)=J_B/J_A$. The map $\varphi:\bigoplus_{x\in D}S_F\varepsilon_x\to\mathcal Q(B,A)$ sending $\varepsilon_x$ to $\overline{m_x}$ has kernel generated by the root relations $v_{q,x_q}\varepsilon_x$ for $x^{\{q\}}\in A$ and the internal-edge relations $v_{q,x_q}\varepsilon_x-v_{q,y_q}\varepsilon_y$ for $y=x^{\{q\}}\in D$. Hence the coordinate- and sign-labelled rooted graph $\widehat G(B,A)$ determines the relative module with its distinguished generators and all relative shelling orders. More explicitly, put $L_A(x)=\{q:x^{\{q\}}\in A\}$. Delete every internal or root edge whose coordinate label belongs to $L_A(x)$. Then $A\cup\{x\}$ is ample exactly when $x$ and the root lie in different components of the remaining graph.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The relative Yang face module is Cohen--Macaulay, so its squarefree Alexander dual $\mathcal Q(B,A)$ has a linear resolution and is linearly presented. In the general monomial presentation, the linear annihilator relations are exactly cube edges from $D$ into $A$, and the linear pair relations are exactly cube edges within $D$; these generate the full kernel and are read directly from the signed rooted graph. Linear quotients of the distinguished generators are Alexander dual to relative shellings. For the cut test, the colon ideal $J_A:m_x$ is generated by the products over $\operatorname{Diff}(x,a)$ for $a\in A$, with linear generators precisely $v_{q,x_q}$ for $q\in L_A(x)$. A surviving path from $x$ to the root gives an $a$ agreeing with $x$ on all of $L_A(x)$ and obstructs variable generation. Conversely, any such obstructing $a$ gives, in its signed multidegree, an expression of the unit vector at $x$ by edge differences and rooted unit vectors, forcing the component of $x$ to contain a surviving root edge.

                                                                References:

                                                                [BousquetYangComplex26]

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#prop:damp-rooted-relative-presentation

                                                                Comments:

                                                                This makes the full signed rooted graph a complete invariant of an individual relative shelling problem. The graph may still record nearly the whole nested pair, so the manuscript continues to seek smaller intrinsic cut or circuit data.

                                                                Biroot Locking Is a Static Terminal-Pair Certificate

                                                                Name: Biroot Locking Is a Static Terminal-Pair Certificate

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Concept Deletion

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For nested ample $A\subsetneq B$, call the pair lower-root-locked when, for every $x\in B\setminus A$, the root remains connected to $x$ after deleting from $\widehat G(B,A)$ every edge labelled by a coordinate in $L_A(x)$. This finite ordering-free condition certifies that $(\Delta_B,\Delta_A)$ is not relatively shellable. Define upper-root-locking by applying the same condition to the complementary pair $Q_F\setminus B\subsetneq Q_F\setminus A$. It is equivalent to $B\setminus\{x\}$ being nonample for every $x\in B\setminus A$. Therefore a pair locked at both roots admits neither a first nor a last relative shelling facet, and both failures are decided by labelled cut tests in the two rooted graphs.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The rooted cut criterion says that lower-root-locking excludes every ample one-concept extension of $A$ within $B$. A relative shelling would have to begin with such an extension, so none exists. For the upper condition, $B\setminus\{x\}$ is ample exactly when $(Q_F\setminus B)\cup\{x\}$ is ample. Applying the same rooted cut criterion to the complementary nested pair proves the deletion characterization and excludes a final relative shelling facet.
