                                                                [BousquetYangComplex26]

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#cor:damp-biroot-locked-terminal-pair

                                                                Comments:

                                                                Root locking supplies a direct nonshellability certificate without storing a shelling or carrier order. Biroot locking is necessary for relative terminality; this result does not by itself classify all locked presentations.

                                                                Upper-Root-Locked Pairs Have a Canonical One-Hole Normal Form

                                                                Name: Upper-Root-Locked Pairs Have a Canonical One-Hole Normal Form

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Concept Deletion

                                                                Result Type: Construction

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For oriented one-hole data $(y,S)$, let $\mathsf P(y,S)=\{y^T:\varnothing\ne T\subseteq S\}$ be the punctured cube and $\mathsf I(y,S)=\{y^T:T\subseteq S, |T|\ge2\}$ its interior. Given $A$ and a finite family $\mathcal W$ of such data, put $B(A,\mathcal W)=A\cup\bigcup_{(y,S)\in\mathcal W}\mathsf P(y,S)$. If $A$ and $B(A,\mathcal W)$ satisfy Sandwich equality, every tip $y$ is absent, the relative part is nonempty, and every relative concept lies in one of the displayed interiors, then $A\subsetneq B(A,\mathcal W)$ is an upper-root-locked nested ample pair. Conversely, every upper-root-locked nested ample pair $A\subsetneq B$ has this form. It is canonically recovered by taking all absent-tip punctured cubes $\mathsf P(y,S)\subseteq B$ whose interiors meet $B\setminus A$ and whose supports are inclusion-maximal for their fixed tips. Thus upper-root-locked relative Yang presentations have an explicit descendant-free construction and recovery.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The Sandwich equalities make both endpoint families ample. If a relative concept $x=y^T$ lies in a displayed interior, then $|T|\ge2$, every proper flip $x^C$ with $C\subsetneq T$ lies in the punctured cube, and the full flip $x^T=y$ is absent. Hence $T$ is a nontrivial minimal nonface of the local cube-support complex at $x$; $x$ is not a corner, so deleting it makes $B$ nonample. This proves upper-root-locking. Conversely, upper-root-locking makes every relative $x$ a noncorner of $B$. A minimal nonface $S$ of its local cube-support complex supplies an absent tip $y=x^S$ with $\mathsf P(y,S)\subseteq B$ and $x\in\mathsf I(y,S)$. Extending $S$ maximally for its fixed tip yields the canonical family, protects every relative concept, and reconstructs exactly $B$.

                                                                References:

                                                                [BousquetYangComplex26]

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#thm:damp-relative-one-hole-upper-lock

                                                                Comments:

                                                                The admissibility test uses only finite Sandwich equalities, missing tips, and punctured-cube containment; it contains no deletion, corner, shelling, linear-quotient, or rooted-connectivity predicate. This classifies individual upper-locked pairs, while compatibility of two such covers over a common overlap remains separate.

                                                                Punctured-Cube Protection Equals Complementary Root Locking

                                                                Name: Punctured-Cube Protection Equals Complementary Root Locking

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Concept Deletion

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For a nested ample pair $A\subsetneq B$, the following are equivalent: the pair is upper-root-locked; every $x\in B\setminus A$ lies in the interior $\mathsf I(y,S)$ of an absent-tip punctured cube $\mathsf P(y,S)\subseteq B$ with $|S|\ge2$; and, in the rooted signed presentation of the complementary pair, every relative vertex remains joined to the root after deleting all coordinate labels incident with that vertex at the root. Moreover, if $x=y^T$ is protected by such a block, every one-coordinate neighbour $x^{\{q\}}$ with $q\in T$ lies in $B$, so the block induces a root path avoiding all labels deleted by the complementary cut test.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The canonical one-hole normal form identifies upper-root-locking with punctured-cube protection, while the rooted relative presentation identifies upper-root-locking with the complementary labelled cut condition. For a protected word $x=y^T$, removing any $q\in T$ leaves a nonempty subset of the punctured-cube support, so $x^{\{q\}}\in B$. Thus no coordinate of $T$ is removed in the complementary cut test, and the root-cut criterion converts the missing-tip relation into the stated surviving path.

                                                                Paired One-Hole Criterion for Cornerless Two-Layer Gluings

                                                                Name: Paired One-Hole Criterion for Cornerless Two-Layer Gluings

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Cornerless Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Coordinate Conditioning

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $B_0,B_1\subseteq Q_F$ and $H=(B_0\times\{0\})\cup(B_1\times\{1\})$, and suppose the nonempty family $H$ satisfies Sandwich equality. Define $\operatorname{Int}(B_b)$ as the concepts lying in the interior of an absent-tip punctured affine cube contained in $B_b$. Define $\operatorname{Cross}_b(B_0,B_1)$ as the common concepts $a\in B_0\cap B_1$ for which some nonempty support $T$ gives a full $T$-cube through $a$ in $B_b$ and the same cube punctured at $a^T$ in $B_{1-b}$. Then $H$ is cornerless exactly when $B_b=\operatorname{Int}(B_b)\cup\operatorname{Cross}_b(B_0,B_1)$ for both $b=0,1$. All protection sets are computed directly from full and punctured affine cubes in the sections, giving an ordering-free construction and recovery criterion for the nonpeelable root of a two-layer gluing.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Sandwich equality makes $H$ ample. By the local-hole characterization, a lifted concept $(x,b)$ is not a corner exactly when it lies in the interior of a punctured cube with a missing tip. If the punctured-cube support avoids the layer coordinate, the whole block lies in layer $b$ and gives precisely internal protection of $x$. If the support contains the layer coordinate, deleting that coordinate leaves a nonempty support $T$: the layer-$b$ section is the full $T$-cube through $x$, while the opposite section is the same cube punctured at $x^T$. This is exactly cross-layer protection, and either construction reverses to the corresponding punctured cube in $H$. Therefore every concept in both layers is a noncorner exactly when the two displayed protection equalities hold.

                                                                Comments:

                                                                This is the exact nonpeelability compatibility law for the two sections. It does not assert that the elementary pc-minors peel; intrinsic attachment conditions ensuring those positive images remain a separate problem.

                                                                Latent Punctured Faces Characterize Corner-Peeling Words

                                                                Name: Latent Punctured Faces Characterize Corner-Peeling Words

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Concept Deletion

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For $H\subseteq Q_F$, let its latent punctured-face system be all pairs $(y,S)$ with $|S|\ge2$ and $\mathsf P(y,S)\subseteq H$; the tip $y$ may be present, representing a punctured face activated when $y$ is deleted. For an ordering $\mathbf x$ of an ample $H$, assign an absent tip position zero and let $b_{\mathbf x}(y,S)$ be the first displayed member of $\mathsf P(y,S)$. Then $\mathbf x$ is a corner peeling exactly when, for every latent block, whenever the tip occurs before its first displayed vertex, that first vertex is a one-coordinate neighbour $y^{\{q\}}$ of the tip for some $q\in S$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                In a corner peeling, let the first surviving vertex of a latent block be $x=y^T$ after the tip has disappeared. Immediately before deleting $x$, every other displayed block vertex is present. If $|T|\ge2$, the entire punctured subcube $\mathsf P(y,T)$ remains around $x$ while its tip is absent, so the local cube-support complex at $x$ is not a simplex and $x$ is not a corner. Thus $|T|=1$. Conversely, proceed inductively through an ordering satisfying the word rule. Earlier corner deletions preserve ampleness. If the current vertex were not a corner, a minimal nonface $T$ of its local cube-support complex would produce a latent block with missing or earlier tip $y=x^T$, while the current vertex $y^T$ is the block's first displayed member and $|T|\ge2$, contradicting the rule.

                                                                [BousquetYangComplex26]

                                                                Finite Facet-Protector Acyclicity Criterion

                                                                Name: Finite Facet-Protector Acyclicity Criterion

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Concept Deletion

                                                                Result Type: Algorithm

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $H$ be ample. For every latent punctured face $(y,S)$, choose either an escape state, allowed when $y\in H$ and contributing the arc $y^S\to y$, or a facet-protector state marked by $q\in S$ and contributing the arc $y^{S\setminus\{q\}}\to y^S$. Then $H$ is corner-peelable exactly when one can choose one state for every latent block so that the union of all selected arcs is acyclic.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Given a corner peeling, choose the escape state when the block antipode precedes its present tip. Otherwise the tip is absent or earlier. Before the antipode is deleted, at least one support-neighbour must already be gone; if all remained, the antipode's unique maximal corner cube would contain the whole support cube and its tip. Choose that neighbour as protector. Every selected arc points forward, so the union is acyclic. Conversely, topologically order an acyclic selected-arc graph. If the latent word rule failed first at $x=y^T$ with $|T|\ge2$, the latent subblock $(y,T)$ could not use its escape arc because the tip is earlier than $x$. Its chosen protector is another vertex of the original block preceding $x$, contradicting that $x$ was the block's first displayed vertex. The word criterion then makes the topological order a corner peeling.

                                                                References:

                                                                [BousquetYangComplex26]

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#cor:damp-latent-facet-protector-criterion

                                                                Comments:

                                                                This compresses the full word condition to one binary-or-coordinate state per latent block plus an acyclicity test. It is a recognition criterion; later transport results describe how protector states behave under contraction.

                                                                Contraction Transports Facet Protectors by Edge Owners

                                                                Name: Contraction Transports Facet Protectors by Edge Owners

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Coordinate Projection

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $H\subseteq Q_{F\cup\{e\}}$ be ample, let $K=\pi_eH$, and let $L_e(z)\subseteq\{0,1\}$ be the layers in which $z\in K$ lifts to $H$. Every edge $zz^{\{q\}}$ of $K$ has a nonempty owner set $\Omega_e(z,q)=L_e(z)\cap L_e(z^{\{q\}})$. Hence, if a latent block $(y,S)$ of $K$ has antipode $z=y^S$, its facet-protector state $q\in S$ lifts in every layer in $\Omega_e(z,q)$; contraction preserves $q$ and adds only this one- or two-element owner set. In a switched punctured-expansion profile $P_S=D\mathbin{\dot\cup}Z_0\mathbin{\dot\cup}Z_1$, an edge has both owners exactly when both endpoints lie in $D$; otherwise its non-$D$ endpoints lie in one monochromatic $Z_b$ and its owner set is $\{b\}$. Thus the separator and component colors recover every transported protector state without a peeling order.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                If the endpoint lift sets of a projected edge were disjoint, they would be opposite singletons. The two present lifts would then be at Hamming distance two while both possible intermediate cube vertices were absent, contradicting isometry of the ample family. Thus every projected edge has an owner. A facet protector is exactly the edge from a latent block's antipode to the corresponding support neighbour, so its lifting rule follows. In a switched profile, vertices in $D$ have both lifts and vertices in $Z_b$ only their layer-$b$ lift. The canonical profile theorem forbids edges between $Z_0$ and $Z_1$; intersecting endpoint lift sets gives the stated owner formula.

                                                                [BousquetYangComplex26]

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#prop:damp-latent-facet-protector-transport

                                                                Comments:

                                                                Protector transport is canonical and coordinate preserving. Global compatibility of owner choices and escape arcs remains a separate signed-holonomy problem.

                                                                Colored Yang Protector-Atlas Criterion

                                                                Name: Colored Yang Protector-Atlas Criterion

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Concept Deletion

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For an ample $H$, associate to every latent punctured face $(y,S)$ its punctured cross-polytopal chart in the Yang complex, with antipodal facet $A(y,S)=F_{y^S}$, protector facets $P_q(y,S)=F_{y^{S\setminus\{q\}}}$, and, when $y\in H$, escape facet $E(y,S)=F_y$. In every chart choose either the precedence $A(y,S)\prec E(y,S)$ or one precedence $P_q(y,S)\prec A(y,S)$. Then the Yang complex is shellable exactly when the local precedences can be chosen with acyclic union. Whenever they are acyclic, every linear extension is the Yang-facet order corresponding to a corner peeling of $H$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Under the facet--concept bijection, the escape precedence is exactly the latent-block escape arc and each protector precedence is exactly its facet-protector arc. The finite facet-protector acyclicity criterion characterizes corner peelability, and the Yang shellability--corner-peeling dictionary identifies those topological orders with shelling orders.

                                                                Yang Shellability Equals Metric Elimination

                                                                Name: Yang Shellability Equals Metric Elimination

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Partial Cubes
                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Concept Deletion

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let nonempty $H\subseteq Q_F$ be isometric and let $G_H$ be its induced concept graph. The following are equivalent: the Yang complex $\Delta_H$ is shellable; it is strongly shellable; $G_H$ has an elimination order whose every nonempty suffix is isometric in $G_H$; and $G_H$ has an elimination order in which every deleted vertex is weakly $4$-simplicial, meaning that every two of its current neighbours remain at distance at most two after its deletion. Every isometric family satisfying these conditions is ample and corner-peelable. Its distance-preserving elimination orders are exactly its corner-peeling orders, and their reversals are the corresponding Yang shellings.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                For Yang facets, the pure shelling pairwise criterion automatically satisfies the extra containment required for strong shellability because each facet contains exactly one literal of every color. Thus shellability and strong shellability coincide. The codimension-one graph of the Yang complex is $G_H$, facet distance is Hamming distance, and isometry makes this graph harmonious; the strong-shellability graph theorem therefore gives distance-preserving elimination. A vertex deletion preserves all distances exactly when the vertex is weakly $4$-simplicial. Finally, reverse a distance-preserving order from its last singleton. Each successive cube-family extension is isometric, so the one-concept extension criterion preserves ampleness and adds a corner. Conversely every suffix of a corner peeling is ample and therefore isometric.

                                                                References:

                                                                [GuoShenWu19strong] [SmithZahedi25distance] [BousquetYangComplex26]

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#prop:damp-yang-shellability-metric-elimination

                                                                Metric Criterion for Peeling to a Retained Ample Target

                                                                Name: Metric Criterion for Peeling to a Retained Ample Target

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Concept Deletion

                                                                Result Type: Algorithm

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let nonempty $A\subseteq H\subseteq Q_F$ be ample and list $H\setminus A$ as $x_1,\ldots,x_k$. For a distance-two pair $u,v$ in $H$, let $C_H(u,v)$ be its common neighbours. The following are equivalent: the displayed deletions are a relative corner peeling from $H$ to $A$; every prefix-deleted family is isometric in the original concept graph of $H$; and for every distance-two pair, either $C_H(u,v)$ meets $A$, or some endpoint $z\in\{u,v\}\setminus A$ precedes some $w\in C_H(u,v)$ in the deletion list. The target $A$ need not itself be corner-peelable. A complete peeling of $H$ with $A$ as its final block exists exactly when such a relative peeling exists and $A$ is corner-peelable.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                A relative corner peeling leaves ample and hence isometric residual families. Conversely, reverse an isometric residual sequence from the ample target $A$; the one-concept metric extension criterion makes each enlarged family ample and the new concept a corner. For the static original-graph condition, if all residuals are isometric and a distance-two pair has no retained common neighbour, immediately before its first endpoint is deleted some common neighbour must survive later. Conversely, at the first deletion that fails to preserve distances there are two nonadjacent surviving neighbours of the deleted vertex with no surviving common neighbour; all their original common neighbours have already been deleted, contradicting the stated precedence alternative. Concatenating a relative peeling with a peeling of $A$ proves the final-block assertion, and any complete peeling splits into those two parts.

                                                                [CoudertDucoffeNisseSoto18] [BousquetYangComplex26]

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#prop:damp-relative-metric-peeling

                                                                Comments:

                                                                Ampleness of the retained target is essential: deleting $000,111$ from $Q_3$ leaves isometric residuals but the six-cycle target is nonample and the second deletion is not a corner deletion. Peelability of the target is not essential for the relative part: the certified 292-concept extension peels relatively by deleting its added concept to a cornerless ample 291-concept target. The exhaustive replay is archived with migration Batch 162.

                                                                Metric Constraints Separate Across an Ample Overlap

                                                                Name: Metric Constraints Separate Across an Ample Overlap

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Coordinate Conditioning
                                                                • Coordinate Projection
                                                                • Concept Deletion

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let ample $H$ be split in an active coordinate into sections $B_0,B_1$, overlap $A=B_0\cap B_1$, contraction $C=B_0\cup B_1$, and wings $D_b=B_b\setminus A$. The four families are nonempty and ample. For $X\in\{B_0,B_1,C\}$, retain each original-graph distance-two constraint whose common-neighbour set avoids $A$. Then the constraint system for $C$ is the disjoint union of those for $B_0$ and $B_1$, and every exterior vertex in a side constraint lies in that side's wing. Consequently, a partial deletion list in $C\setminus A$ preserves distances after every deletion exactly when its two wing subsequences do so in their sections. A full list peels $C$ relatively to $A$ exactly when both wing subsequences peel their sections relatively to $A$, and every interleaving of two valid wing orders is valid. Moreover, if a same-side distance-two pair acquires a new midpoint under contraction, its old midpoint is unique, the two endpoints and old midpoint lie in $A$, the new midpoint lies in the opposite wing, and their lifted three-face is a cube with exactly the new midpoint's same-side lift missing; every such punctured three-cube gives a new midpoint.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                No contraction edge joins the two exclusive wings, since their exclusive lifts would otherwise be a Hamming-distance-two pair with both intermediate vertices absent. A cross-wing distance-two pair has all common neighbours in $A$, and a pair wholly in $A$ has an $A$-midpoint by isometry. Every constraint avoiding retained midpoints therefore belongs to one section and cannot acquire an opposite-wing midpoint; this proves the disjoint split. A deletion sequence preserves distances exactly while no distance-two pair loses all common neighbours with both endpoints retained. Constraints meeting $A$ are permanently satisfied, and all others split by wing, proving the partial and full order assertions via the relative metric criterion. Finally a cube distance-two pair has only two possible midpoints. Acquiring the second forces the endpoints and old midpoint into $A$ and the new one into the opposite wing; their lifts are precisely the seven vertices of the stated punctured cube, and the construction reverses.

                                                                Comments:

                                                                The result applies to partial exterior deletion lists as well as complete relative peelings. Its exhaustive replay is archived with migration Batch 163.

                                                                Contraction Peelings of Ample Obstructions Must Enter the Overlap

                                                                Name: Contraction Peelings of Ample Obstructions Must Enter the Overlap

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes
                                                                • Cornerless Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Coordinate Conditioning
                                                                • Coordinate Projection
                                                                • Concept Deletion

                                                                Result Type: Implication

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let an ample forbidden pc-minor $H$ be split in an active coordinate into sections $B_0,B_1$, overlap $A$, contraction $C$, and wings $D_0,D_1$. The proper minor $C$ is corner-peelable, but no complete peeling of $C$ has $A$ as its final block. If $A$ is corner-peelable, the first deletion from $A$ occurs while both wings remain nonempty. If $H$ is cornerless, then every corner of $C$ lies in $A$ but is not a corner of $A$. Consequently every peeling of $C$ enters $A$ at its first deletion, and deleting that concept makes the remaining overlap nonample.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The contraction is a proper pc-minor and hence peels. If $A$ does not peel it cannot be a final block. If it does peel, the gluing-critical dichotomy says neither section peels relatively to $A$. Exhausting either wing before entering $A$ would project to a distance-preserving deletion of that section to $A$, which the overlap separation and relative metric criterion turn into the forbidden relative peeling. For cornerless $H$, every cube in $C$ lies in one section. A contraction corner in a wing would therefore lift to a corner of $H$. A contraction corner in $A$ that were also an overlap corner would likewise make one of its two lifts a corner. Thus contraction corners lie in $A\setminus\operatorname{Cor}(A)$, and the ample corner-deletion criterion says their deletion destroys overlap ampleness.

                                                                References:

                                                                [BousquetYangComplex26]

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#cor:damp-contraction-must-enter-overlap

                                                                Comments:

                                                                Retaining the canonical overlap cannot generally produce the required contraction peeling. Attachment rules must justify deletions inside the overlap and their effects on both remaining wings.

                                                                Overlap and Section Deficit Balance

                                                                Name: Overlap and Section Deficit Balance

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Coordinate Conditioning
                                                                • Coordinate Projection
                                                                • Concept Deletion

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Split an ample family $H$ in a coordinate into sections $B_0,B_1$, overlap $A=B_0\cap B_1$, and contraction $C=B_0\cup B_1$. Write $\delta(X)=|\operatorname{Sh}(X)|-|X|$. For every ample $K\subseteq C$, put $B_b^K=B_b\cap K$, $A^K=A\cap K$, and let $H[K]$ be the lift of $K$ in $H$. On every coordinate set, the signed traces of $B_0^K$ and $B_1^K$ intersect exactly in the trace of $A^K$. Hence $\operatorname{Sh}(K)=\operatorname{Sh}(B_0^K)\cup\operatorname{Sh}(B_1^K)$, $\operatorname{Sh}(A^K)=\operatorname{Sh}(B_0^K)\cap\operatorname{Sh}(B_1^K)$, and $\delta(H[K])=\delta(B_0^K)+\delta(B_1^K)=\delta(A^K)$. Thus $H[K]$ is ample exactly when $A^K$ is ample. If a corner $x$ of $K$ is deleted and $L_0,L_1,L_A$ are the shattered supports lost from the two sections and overlap, then the lift-deficit change is $m(x)-|L_0|-|L_1|$: it is zero for $x\notin A$ and is $1-|L_A|$ for $x\in A$. Exterior deletions preserve both side deficits; overlap deletion raises the deficit by at most one and lowers it exactly when at least two overlap supports disappear.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                An isometric path inside $K$ between concepts in opposite wings must pass through $A^K$ without changing any coordinates on which its endpoints agree. This gives the exact trace intersection and therefore the shadow intersection. Every cube of $C$ lies in one section: its intersection with ample $A$ has connected complement when nonempty, and the two wings have no joining edge. Since $K$ is ample, every shattered support of $K$ is represented by a cube, giving the shadow union. The standard two-layer shadow formula, $|H[K]|=|K|+|A^K|$, and $|\operatorname{Sh}(K)|=|K|$ yield the deficit balance and the ampleness equivalence. Finally, deleting $x$ removes $m(x)$ section concepts and exactly the supports in $L_0$ and $L_1$; subtracting the two balance identities gives the transition law. Comparing overlap deficits gives its two cases and the stated consequences.

                                                                [BousquetYangComplex26]

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#prop:damp-contraction-section-deficits

                                                                Comments:

                                                                The formulas also cover the empty residual $K$. They account exactly for scalar shadow loss, but do not by themselves determine which overlap losses are simultaneously compatible. The exhaustive replay is archived with migration Batch 164.

                                                                First Nonample Overlap Has One-Sided Deficit

                                                                Name: First Nonample Overlap Has One-Sided Deficit

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Cornerless Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Coordinate Conditioning
                                                                • Coordinate Projection
                                                                • Concept Deletion

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                In an ample coordinate split with sections $B_0,B_1$, overlap $A$, and contraction $C$, let $x$ be a corner of $C$ that lies in $A$ but is not a corner of $A$. If $Q$ is the unique maximal cube of $C$ through $x$, with support $I$, there is a unique side $B_b$ containing $Q$. Deleting $x$ removes exactly $I$ from $\operatorname{Sh}(B_b)$, changes neither $\operatorname{Sh}(B_{1-b})$ nor $\operatorname{Sh}(A)$, and removes exactly $I$ from the shadow of the lifted family. The owner side remains ample, while the other side, overlap, and lift each have deficit one. Their conditioning-minimal nonample faces agree: for every inclusion-minimal $T$ of size at least two with $x^T\notin A$ and $x^U\in A$ for all proper $U\subset T$, both residuals meet the cube $Q_T(x)$ in $Q_T(x)\setminus\{x,x^T\}$, where $x^T\in B_b\setminus A$; these and only these antipodally twice-punctured faces are conditioning-minimal nonample.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The maximal cube $Q$ lies in at least one section and cannot lie in both, since that would make $x$ an overlap corner. In its unique owner side, $x$ is a corner; in the opposite side and the overlap, the local cube-support complexes at $x$ coincide and $x$ is a noncorner. Deleting a corner from an ample family loses its unique cube support, while deleting a noncorner loses no shattered support. The section-shadow union and two-layer shadow formulas then give the lifted shadow loss and all three unit deficits. The displayed supports $T$ are precisely the minimal nonfaces of the common local support complex. Each lies in $I$, putting $x^T$ in the owner wing, and yields the stated twice-punctured cube. Conversely, any nonample conditioning created by deleting $x$ must contain $x$ and contains such a minimal local nonface; minimality forces it to equal that face.

The same replay also records a 25-concept example showing that adjoining the entire contraction corner cube need not repair an ample overlap.

                                                                Metric Yang Obstruction Characterizes Nonpeelability

                                                                Name: Metric Yang Obstruction Characterizes Nonpeelability

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Metric Yang Obstruction

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For an ample family $H$ of order $m\ge2$, let $\mathscr U_{\mathrm{met}}(H)$ be the union, inside its order sphere $\mathscr O(H)$, of the order-ideal complexes associated with all distance-two endpoint pairs and their common neighbours. Then $H$ is nonpeelable if and only if $\mathscr U_{\mathrm{met}}(H)=\mathscr O(H)$, if and only if $\widetilde H_{m-2}(\mathscr U_{\mathrm{met}}(H);\mathbb F_2)\cong\mathbb F_2$. Consequently $\omega_{\mathrm{met}}(H)\in\{0,1\}$ is an intrinsic invariant of the metric graph and equals one exactly when the Yang complex is nonshellable.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                A total order fails distance-preserving elimination at a distance-two pair $u,v$ exactly when every common neighbour precedes both endpoints. These are precisely the linear extensions, and hence chambers, of the associated failure poset. Thus all orders fail exactly when the metric failure union fills the order sphere. A proper subcomplex of the order sphere has zero top homology over $\mathbb F_2$, whereas the full sphere has its one-dimensional fundamental class. The established equivalence between metric elimination, corner peeling, and Yang shellability completes the characterization.

                                                                Boolean-Prefix Cutset and Exact pc-Minor Transport

                                                                Name: Boolean-Prefix Cutset and Exact pc-Minor Transport

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Coordinate Conditioning
                                                                • Coordinate Projection

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For each distance-two pair $D=\{u,v\}$ of an ample family $H$, let $\mathcal I_D(H)$ be the Boolean interval of prefixes that contain every common neighbour of $u,v$ but neither endpoint. Then $H$ is nonpeelable exactly when $\bigcup_D\mathcal I_D(H)$ meets every maximal chain of $2^H$. This interval system transports exactly under pc-minors. Under restriction to a coordinate section $A$, an interval owned by $D\subseteq A$ becomes $\mathcal I_D(H)\cap2^A$. Under contraction $q:H\to\overline H$, pullback identifies $2^{\overline H}$ with the sublattice of unions of $q$-fibres, and each quotient interval pulls back to the interval from $q^{-1}C_{\overline H}(\overline u,\overline v)$ to $H\setminus q^{-1}\{\overline u,\overline v\}$ inside that sublattice.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                A total order corresponds to its maximal chain of prefixes. It fails at $D$ exactly when one prefix contains every common neighbour before either endpoint, which is exactly membership in $\mathcal I_D(H)$. The static distance-two elimination criterion proves the cutset equivalence. Restriction preserves the common-neighbour set of a retained distance-two pair, so intersecting the interval endpoints with $2^A$ gives the restriction formula. For contraction, inverse image is a lattice isomorphism from the quotient Boolean lattice to the fibre-saturated sublattice; applying it to each quotient interval gives the displayed pullback formula.

                                                                Unique-Midpoint Core and Square Remainder

                                                                Name: Unique-Midpoint Core and Square Remainder

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Partial Cubes
                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Result Type: Algorithm

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For rooted-pair constraints $(w;\{u,v\})$ on a finite set $V$, call nonempty $W\subseteq V$ a core when every $w\in W$ roots a constraint whose two heads lie in $W$. An order satisfying $u\prec w$ or $v\prec w$ for every constraint exists exactly when no core exists. Repeatedly deleting a root with no constraint whose two heads remain computes the unique largest core; if it empties, the deletion order satisfies all constraints. Applied to unique-midpoint constraints of an isometric cube family $H$, a nonempty core proves $H$ nonpeelable. If the core is empty, only full-square constraints remain: an order peels exactly when it satisfies every unique-midpoint constraint and its first two vertices in every square are adjacent. Square constraints alone never obstruct elimination; any order nondecreasing in cube distance from a fixed cube vertex satisfies them. Hence a family with no unique-midpoint constraints is peelable.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                In any order, the first vertex of a core violates the constraint witnessing it. Conversely, unions of cores are cores, so iterative pruning leaves the unique largest one; when it is empty, every deleted root has an already deleted head and the deletion order satisfies all rooted-pair constraints. A distance-two pair has either one common neighbour, giving exactly such a constraint, or two common neighbours forming a square. The two square diagonals are both satisfied precisely when the first two square vertices are adjacent. Finally, relative to any fixed cube vertex, a square has one nearest vertex, two adjacent next-nearest vertices, and one farthest vertex, so every distance-nondecreasing order satisfies all square conditions. The metric elimination criterion translates the resulting orders into peelings.

                                                                References:

                                                                [CoudertDucoffeNisseSoto18] [BousquetYangComplex26]

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#prop:damp-unique-midpoint-core

                                                                Comments:

                                                                The core is a constructive sufficient obstruction. Its emptiness is not sufficient for peelability when full squares are present; the manuscript supplies a certified ample forbidden pc-minor with empty core.

                                                                One-Sided Criterion for Empty Unique-Midpoint Core

                                                                Name: One-Sided Criterion for Empty Unique-Midpoint Core

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Coordinate Conditioning
                                                                • Coordinate Projection
                                                                • Concept Deletion

                                                                Result Type: Algorithm

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For nested ample families $A\subseteq B$, let $\kappa_A(B)$ be the largest $W\subseteq B\setminus A$ such that every $w\in W$ roots a unique-midpoint constraint in $B$ whose two heads lie in $A\cup W$. It is computed by pruning roots with no such witness while retaining $A$ and keeping the original constraint set fixed. Now split ample $H$ in an active coordinate into sections $B_0,B_1$ with overlap $A$. If both ordinary section cores are empty and $\kappa_A(B_i)$ is empty for either side, then the ordinary unique-midpoint core of $H$ is empty. In particular this holds if either section corner-peels to $A$, equivalently if either inclusion $A\subseteq B_i$ admits an $A$-relative ample chain.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Unions of relative cores are relative cores, so the pruning procedure leaves their unique largest member. Assume $\kappa_A(B_0)$ is empty and let $K$ be a core of $H$. A root in the exclusive zero wing has no vertical neighbour, so its witness is horizontal; projection would put it in $\kappa_A(B_0)$, which is impossible. Any remaining zero-section root projects into $A$. A vertical witness for it would require a head in the excluded zero wing, so every witness is again horizontal; the zero section of $K$ would then be an ordinary core of $B_0$ and must be empty. The same argument makes the one section a core of $B_1$, hence empty. Finally, if $B$ corner-peels to $A$, the first deleted member of any nonempty relative core would still have both witness heads present and could not be a corner, a contradiction.

                                                                Comments:

                                                                One side suffices. The archived control has relative-core orders 52 and 0 over its two sections and empty global core, while an empty global core can also coexist with two nonempty relative cores.

                                                                Nonempty Cores Force Two Large Cyclic Wings

                                                                Name: Nonempty Cores Force Two Large Cyclic Wings

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Coordinate Conditioning
                                                                • Coordinate Projection

                                                                Result Type: Implication

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $H$ be an irredundantly embedded ample forbidden pc-minor for the dismantlable ample classes and suppose its unique-midpoint core is nonempty. At every active coordinate, both section cores relative to the overlap are nonempty, neither section admits a relative ample chain down to the overlap, and both induced wing graphs contain cycles. Each wing has at least nine concepts, so $|H|\ge2|A|+18$. These conclusions hold whether or not the overlap $A$ is corner-peelable. If $A$ is nonpeelable, then $|H|\ge2m_{\mathrm{amp}}+18$, where $m_{\mathrm{amp}}$ is the minimum order of an ample forbidden pc-minor.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Both sections are proper pc-minors and therefore corner-peelable, so their ordinary unique-midpoint cores are empty. The one-sided criterion forces both relative cores to be nonempty and excludes a relative ample chain on either side. Irredundancy makes the overlap nonempty, and the gluing dichotomy makes it ample. The relative Yang modules are Cohen--Macaulay; the relative forest and eight-facet linear-quotient theorems would produce a relative ample chain if a wing were a forest or had at most eight concepts. Thus both wings contain cycles and have order at least nine. The section identity gives $|H|=2|A|+|D_0|+|D_1|$. If $A$ is nonpeelable, inherited overlap descent makes it an ample forbidden pc-minor, yielding $|A|\ge m_{\mathrm{amp}}$.

                                                                Empty Unique-Midpoint Core Does Not Imply Peelability

                                                                Name: Empty Unique-Midpoint Core Does Not Imply Peelability

It independently enumerates all 766 unique-midpoint constraints of $H$ and records a complete pruning order, while the same fixed-constraint calculation leaves a witnessed 76-vertex core in $\widehat G$. Finally, it verifies complete corner peelings for every restriction and contraction in all twelve coordinates of both families.                                                                 Local Alphabet and pc-Minor Span Laws for Metric Supports

                                                                Name: Local Alphabet and pc-Minor Span Laws for Metric Supports

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Partial Cubes
                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Coordinate Conditioning
                                                                • Coordinate Projection

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For an isometric cube family $H$, call an inclusion-minimal order-infeasible family of distance-two constraints a metric support, where a constraint on endpoints $u,v$ is satisfied by an order when some common neighbour $w$ follows at least one endpoint. Every distance-two pair has one or two common neighbours, so the local alphabet consists only of a rooted three-vertex constraint and a four-vertex square constraint. Coordinate halfspaces preserve both distance-two pairs and their common-neighbour sets. An ample $H$ is nonpeelable exactly when it contains a metric support. If $H$ is an ample forbidden pc-minor for corner peelability, every metric support meets both halfspaces of every effective coordinate. Moreover every contraction acts nontrivially on every support: it either identifies two support vertices, makes a constrained pair adjacent, or creates a new common neighbour for a same-layer constrained pair.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Isometry makes the endpoints of a distance-two pair differ in exactly two cube coordinates, leaving precisely two possible ambient common neighbours and at least one present neighbour. A coordinate halfspace is convex, and a common neighbour of two distinct same-halfspace vertices cannot lie in the other halfspace, proving exact restriction transport. The static metric elimination criterion makes the whole constraint system order-infeasible exactly when $H$ is nonpeelable; finiteness supplies an inclusion-minimal subsystem. If a support lay in one coordinate halfspace, exact restriction transport would make that proper restriction nonpeelable, contrary to pc-minimality. If a contraction caused none of the three stated changes, projection would identify the support with an order-infeasible subsystem of the proper contraction, giving the same contradiction.

                                                                [CoudertDucoffeNisseSoto18] [BousquetYangComplex26]

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#prop:damp-metric-support-coordinate-span

                                                                Comments:

                                                                These are necessary minimality laws. Order-infeasibility is still the original global peeling obstruction, so the laws do not yet constitute attachment axioms for a generative classification.

                                                                Canonical Yang Order-Sphere Obstruction

                                                                Name: Canonical Yang Order-Sphere Obstruction

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Yang Order-Sphere Obstruction

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For an ample family $H$ of order $m\ge2$, each latent Yang chart $B$ defines a failure poset $P_B$ and a failure region $\mathscr R_B$ in the order sphere $\mathscr O(H)$. The Yang complex is nonshellable exactly when $\mathscr U(H)=\bigcup_B\mathscr R_B$ fills $\mathscr O(H)$, exactly when $\widetilde H_{m-2}(\mathscr U(H);\mathbb F_2)\cong\mathbb F_2$; otherwise this top homology vanishes. For any nonempty chart set $\mathcal I$, generate a preorder from all its failure relations and contract its strongly connected classes to a poset $\overline P_{\mathcal I}$ with $k_{\mathcal I}$ elements. Then $\bigcap_{B\in\mathcal I}\mathscr R_B$ is the proper-ideal order complex of $\overline P_{\mathcal I}$, homotopy equivalent to $S^{k_{\mathcal I}-2}$ when the quotient is an antichain and contractible otherwise. The resulting augmented Mayer--Vietoris spectral sequence converges to the homology of $\mathscr U(H)$, and its only nonzero first-page summands are those one-dimensional antichain-quotient sphere classes.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                A chamber belongs to $\mathscr R_B$ precisely when its order is a linear extension of $P_B$, which is exactly failure of every allowed protector gate in chart $B$. Thus the failure regions cover all chambers exactly when no Yang shelling exists. Chamber adjacency connects the order sphere, so a proper subcomplex has no top-dimensional cycle, whereas the full sphere has its fundamental class. Common ideals of several failure posets are exactly unions of strongly connected classes and hence ideals of the quotient poset. Its proper-ideal complex is a Boolean sphere when the quotient is an antichain; otherwise its atoms have a proper join and the crosscut complex contracts. The standard augmented intersection double complex supplies the stated spectral sequence.

                                                                [BousquetYangComplex26]

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#thm:damp-yang-order-sphere-obstruction

                                                                Balanced Circuit Carriers of Yang Obstructions

                                                                Name: Balanced Circuit Carriers of Yang Obstructions

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Yang Order-Sphere Obstruction

                                                                Result Type: Implication

                                                                Statement:

                                                                If an ample family $H$ is nonpeelable, some nonempty collection $\mathcal I$ of latent charts has every generating failure relation on a directed cycle and satisfies $|\mathcal I|+k_{\mathcal I}=|H|+1$, where $k_{\mathcal I}$ is the number of strongly connected classes of the generated preorder. If $r_{\mathcal I}$ concepts are incident with generating relations and these concepts form $c_{\mathcal I}$ nontrivial strongly connected components, the balance equation is equivalently $|\mathcal I|=r_{\mathcal I}-c_{\mathcal I}+1$. Such balanced circuit collections are necessary carriers of the global obstruction class; their existence alone is not asserted sufficient.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                For a nonpeelable family, the top order-sphere class survives the failure-cover spectral sequence. Some first-page summand of total degree $|H|-2$ supports it. A nonzero summand comes from an antichain strongly connected quotient, has bidegrees $p=|\mathcal I|-1$ and $q=k_{\mathcal I}-2$, and therefore gives the balance equation. An antichain condensation has no arc between distinct components, so every generating relation lies on a directed cycle. Counting the isolated concepts and nontrivial components gives $k_{\mathcal I}=|H|-r_{\mathcal I}+c_{\mathcal I}$ and the equivalent form.

                                                                [BousquetYangComplex26]

                                                                First Yang Cancellation Page Is Cut-Nerve Homology

                                                                Name: First Yang Cancellation Page Is Cut-Nerve Homology

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Yang Order-Sphere Obstruction

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Fix a partition $\pi$ of an ample family $H$ into $k$ parts. Let $\mathcal A_\pi$ be the latent charts whose failure arcs stay within parts, and let $\mathcal N_\pi$ consist of chart sets that fail to make some part strongly connected. The row $q=k-2$ of the first differential of the Yang failure-cover spectral sequence is the direct sum, over all $k$-part partitions, of the relative chain complexes $C_\bullet(2^{\mathcal A_\pi},\mathcal N_\pi;\mathbb F_2)$. Hence $E^2_{p,k-2}\cong\bigoplus_{|\pi|=k}\widetilde H_{p-1}(\mathcal N_\pi;\mathbb F_2)$. Moreover $\mathcal N_\pi$ is homotopy equivalent to the nerve $\mathcal K_\pi$ of the canonical cover indexed by directed cuts within parts, where a cut simplex consists of charts having no arc leaving that cut. Consequently, if $H$ is nonpeelable, then for some $k$-part partition $\pi$, $\widetilde H_{|H|-k-1}(\mathcal K_\pi;\mathbb F_2)\ne0$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                A first-page sphere summand belongs to partition $\pi$ exactly when all arcs stay within parts and strongly connect every part; these are precisely the faces of the simplex $2^{\mathcal A_\pi}$ outside $\mathcal N_\pi$. Removing a chart induces the identity in the same row when all parts remain strongly connected and zero there when a part splits, giving the relative simplicial boundary and the second-page formula. A directed graph is strongly connected exactly when every nontrivial cut has an outgoing arc, so $\mathcal N_\pi$ is the union of the displayed cut simplices. Their intersections are simplices, and the nerve lemma gives $\mathcal N_\pi\simeq\mathcal K_\pi$. A surviving class of total degree $|H|-2$ then yields the final necessary homology class.

                                                                References:

                                                                [BousquetYangComplex26]

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#prop:damp-yang-first-cancellation-cut-nerve

                                                                Metric and Colored Yang Obstructions Agree

                                                                Name: Metric and Colored Yang Obstructions Agree

                                                                • Ample Classes

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Metric Yang Obstruction
                                                                • Yang Order-Sphere Obstruction

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For every finite nonempty ample family $H$, $\omega_{\mathrm{met}}(H)=\omega_{\mathrm{ord}}(H)$. Their common value is zero exactly for dismantlable ample families and one exactly for nonpeelable ample families.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The metric Yang obstruction theorem identifies $\omega_{\mathrm{met}}(H)=1$ exactly with nonpeelability. The colored order-sphere obstruction theorem gives the same characterization for $\omega_{\mathrm{ord}}(H)$. Both invariants are binary, so they agree on every ample family; their singleton normalizations also agree.

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#thm:damp-yang-metric-obstruction-class; PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#thm:damp-yang-order-sphere-obstruction

                                                                Binary Partition Splits Have Canonical Filling Torsors

                                                                Name: Binary Partition Splits Have Canonical Filling Torsors

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Yang Order-Sphere Obstruction

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let a partition $\sigma$ refine $\pi$ by splitting one part $C$ into nonempty parts $C_0,C_1$. The Boolean order sphere $\mathbb S_\pi$ embeds in $\mathbb S_\sigma$. For $b\in\{0,1\}$, take the order complex of proper nonempty subsets of $\sigma$ satisfying $C_{1-b}\in A\Rightarrow C_b\in A$. The two resulting complexes $\mathbb B_0,\mathbb B_1$ are PL balls, their intersection is the embedded old sphere, and their union is the refined sphere. Over $\mathbb F_2$, their top fundamental chains $h_0,h_1$ are exactly the two fillings of the old fundamental cycle: $\partial h_0=\partial h_1=[\mathbb S_\pi]$ and $h_0+h_1=[\mathbb S_\sigma]$. Thus a binary partition split carries a canonical two-element filling torsor indexed by the new parts.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Each hemisphere is the proper-ideal complex of the one-relation poset $C_b

                                                                References:

                                                                [BousquetYangComplex26]
