                                                                Iterated Binary Fillings Factor Through a Permutation

                                                                Name: Iterated Binary Fillings Factor Through a Permutation

                                                                Invariants:

                                                                • Yang Order-Sphere Obstruction

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Suppose $\tau$ refines one part of $\pi$ into nonempty parts indexed by a finite set $L$. An oriented full binary refinement tree orders its leaves by reading each chosen first child before the second. Applying the corresponding hemisphere filling at every split produces the proper-ideal complex of a poset that chains $L$ in this leaf order and leaves all other parts mutually incomparable and incomparable with the chain. This region is a PL ball, depends only on the induced permutation of $L$, and every permutation occurs. Hence coherence changes between binary refinement trees factor through the symmetric group $\mathfrak S_L$. Refinements of distinct parts commute, while interacting refinements of one part have permutation-valued holonomy.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Induct on the refinement tree. A leaf gives a one-element chain; at an internal node the chosen hemisphere orders every leaf of the first child before every leaf of the second, taking the ordinal sum of the two child chains. This yields precisely the recursively read leaf order and the stated ideal complex. Linear extensions of one chain with otherwise incomparable elements form a closed convex region of the Coxeter complex, hence a PL ball. The poset depends only on the final leaf order, and a binary comb realizes every order. Relations from distinct refined parts are disjoint and commute; relations within one part change only its leaf permutation.

                                                                References:

                                                                [BousquetYangComplex26]

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#prop:damp-yang-iterated-filling-permutation

                                                                Comments:

                                                                For a latent chart, the natural finite local coherence group is therefore the symmetric group on its protector labels, together with the escape label when the tip is present. Establishing that the actual Yang cancellation maps factor through this action remains a separate theorem target.

                                                                First-Loss Criterion for a Corner Peeling

                                                                Name: First-Loss Criterion for a Corner Peeling

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Concept Deletion

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let nonempty ample $H$ have shattered complex $\Sigma$ and order $m=|H|=|\Sigma|$. For an ordering $x_1,\ldots,x_m$ and $D\in\Sigma$, define the death time $\delta(D)$ as the minimum, over all traces $q$ on $D$, of the last index at which $q$ occurs. The ordering is a corner-peeling order exactly when $\delta:\Sigma\to[m]$ is a bijection. Thus an order can be checked using only the original trace table, without constructing its descendant families.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                After the first $k$ deletions, a support $D$ remains shattered exactly when every trace on $D$ still has a representative, equivalently when $\delta(D)>k$. If the death map is bijective, exactly $m-k$ supports survive in a suffix of $m-k$ concepts, so equality in the Sandwich bound makes every suffix ample and every deletion a corner deletion. Conversely, a corner peeling has every suffix ample, hence exactly $m-k$ surviving shattered supports after $k$ deletions. These cardinalities force exactly one support to die at each time $1,\ldots,m$.

                                                                References:

                                                                [BousquetYangComplex26]

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#prop:damp-trace-death-peeling

                                                                Acyclic Trace-Carrier Criterion

                                                                Name: Acyclic Trace-Carrier Criterion

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                An ample family has an ordering with bijective first-loss map exactly when it admits an acyclic trace-carrier scheme: a bijection $\kappa$ from shattered supports to concepts, one selected protector in every trace fiber other than the carrier trace, and an acyclic digraph directing all other carrier-trace concepts into the carrier and the carrier into every selected protector. Consequently, existence of such a scheme is equivalent to corner peelability.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                From an order with bijective first-loss map, assign each support to the concept at its death time. In the dying trace all other representatives occur earlier, while the last representative of every other trace occurs later; selecting those last representatives makes every precedence arc point forward. Conversely, topologically order an acyclic scheme. The incoming arcs make the carrier the last representative of its own trace, and each outgoing arc places a representative of every other trace later. Thus the support dies at its carrier's position. Carrier bijectivity makes all death times distinct and exhaustive, and the first-loss criterion yields a corner peeling.

                                                                References:

                                                                [BousquetYangComplex26]

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#thm:damp-acyclic-trace-carrier-criterion

                                                                Comments:

                                                                The criterion is order-free once a scheme is specified, but existence of a scheme remains a recognition problem rather than a generative construction of all obstructions.

                                                                Order-Free Boolean Recognition of the Dismantlable-Ample Forbidden Basis

                                                                Name: Order-Free Boolean Recognition of the Dismantlable-Ample Forbidden Basis

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Coordinate Conditioning
                                                                • Coordinate Projection
                                                                • Partial-Cube Minor

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let an irredundantly embedded binary family $H$ be presented by a signing of the minimal nonfaces of a proposed shattered complex. Then $H$ is an ample forbidden pc-minor for the dismantlable ample classes exactly when the signing is admissible, $H$ admits no acyclic trace-carrier scheme, and each of its $3|F|$ one-coordinate restrictions and contractions admits such a scheme for its own shattered complex. Together with the antipodally twice-punctured cubes $Q_n^{--}$ for $n\ge3$, these signed presentations modulo coordinate permutations and reorientations form the full forbidden basis. The conditions use only finite trace-fiber data of $H$ and its explicit elementary images.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The fixed-shadow signed-clutter theorem identifies admissibility with ampleness and fixes the shattered complex. The first-loss and trace-carrier theorems identify absence of a scheme with nonpeelability and existence of schemes on the elementary images with their peelability. Descendant-free pc-minor reduction makes those elementary tests equivalent to pc-minimality and supplies the quotient by cube symmetries. The nonample-layer theorem supplies exactly the antipodally twice-punctured cubes.

                                                                Exchange Law for Signed Minimal Nonfaces

                                                                Name: Exchange Law for Signed Minimal Nonfaces

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Concept Deletion

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let ample $H=H(\Sigma,\boldsymbol\sigma)$ arise from an admissible signing of the minimal nonfaces of $\Sigma$. For $a\notin H$, let $\mathcal V_H(a)$ be the minimal nonfaces on which $a$ realizes the omitted signed trace. For $c\in H$, let $\mathcal R_H(a,c)$ be those minimal nonfaces on which $a$ and $c$ differ and $c$ is the unique old representative of its trace. Then $(H\setminus\{c\})\cup\{a\}$ is ample with shattered complex $\Sigma$ exactly when $\mathcal V_H(a)=\mathcal R_H(a,c)$. The new signing pivots each violated clause to $c$'s trace and leaves every other clause unchanged. Moreover $H\cup\{a\}$ is ample exactly when $|\mathcal V_H(a)|=1$; in that case its shattered complex is $\Sigma$ together with that unique newly shattered support.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                On each minimal nonface, the old projection omits exactly its signed trace. After exchanging $c$ for $a$, it still omits one trace precisely when either $a$ fills the old omission and $c$ was the sole representative of a different trace, or $a$ does not fill it and removing $c$ creates no second omission. Simultaneous validity is exactly the displayed set equality and gives the signing pivot. The exchanged family has $|\Sigma|$ concepts and shadow contained in $\Sigma$, so Sandwich equality forces ampleness and the exact shadow. For addition, every violated clause becomes shattered. Ampleness allows exactly one new support; conversely, if exactly one clause is violated, any newly shattered support must equal that minimal nonface, so the enlarged family again meets Sandwich equality.

                                                                References:

                                                                [BousquetYangComplex26]

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#prop:damp-signed-clause-exchange

                                                                Fiber Decomposition of Punctured-Face Data

                                                                Name: Fiber Decomposition of Punctured-Face Data

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $S$ be ample. Every minimal nonface $I$ of its shattered complex has a unique omitted trace $\sigma_I$. The punctured-face atlas of $S$ is the disjoint union over such $I$ of outside-assignment fibers: an assignment $y$ on $F\setminus I$ belongs to the $I$-fiber exactly when every nonempty flip of $\sigma_I$ within $I$, paired with $y$, lies in $S$, while the missing tip $(\sigma_I,y)$ has no neighbour in any coordinate outside $I$. Thus all punctured faces with support $I$ share the same missing $I$-trace; the outside assignment alone locates the punctured cube.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                For a punctured face $(a,I)$, all $I$-traces except possibly $a|_I$ occur, while nonshattering says some trace is absent. Hence $a|_I$ is the unique omitted trace $\sigma_I$. Its outside restriction $y$ satisfies the punctured-cube membership conditions, and equality between $I$ and the incident-direction set of $a$ excludes all outside neighbours. Conversely these two fiber conditions put the punctured $I$-cube around $(\sigma_I,y)$ inside $S$, keep its tip outside $S$, and make its incident-direction set exactly $I$, recovering a unique atlas entry.

                                                                References:

                                                                [BousquetYangComplex26]

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#prop:damp-punctured-face-fibers

                                                                Adjacent Square Completions Preserve Dismantlability

                                                                Name: Adjacent Square Completions Preserve Dismantlability

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Concept Deletion

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let nonempty ample $G\subseteq Q_F$ have two absent adjacent concepts $c,u$ such that each individual addition is ample and acquires the same two-coordinate support. Then $H=G\cup\{c,u\}$ is ample, and $H$ is dismantlable ample exactly when $G$ is dismantlable ample.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The two punctured squares and one added tip form a punctured three-cube at the other tip, so the one-concept extension criterion makes the double addition ample. If $G$ peels, delete the two tips and continue in $G$. Conversely take a smallest counterexample and inspect the first deletion of a peeling of $H$. A deletion outside the local three-cube yields a smaller counterexample; a neighbouring local deletion factors the residual through two rank-two additions, which preserve peelability; opposite-face deletions either commute with the second deletion or leave a family isomorphic to $G$. The added tips themselves leave a nonpeelable rank-two completion. Every case contradicts minimality or the assumed peeling of $H$.

                                                                References:

                                                                [BousquetYangComplex26]

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#prop:damp-square-pair-invariance

                                                                Comments:

                                                                The archived verifier exercises every reduction case on three nonminimal ample controls containing the certified 291-concept cornerless family as a proper restriction.

                                                                Resolving Additions under Strong Projection

                                                                Name: Resolving Additions under Strong Projection

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Full Reduction
                                                                • Concept Deletion

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let nonempty ample $S\subseteq Q_F$ have an ample one-concept extension $H=S\cup\{a\}$ with acquired support $I$. For $D\subseteq F$, write $a_D=a|_{F\setminus D}$. Then $H^D=S^D\cup\{a_D\}$ when $D\subseteq I$, while $H^D=S^D$ when $D\not\subseteq I$. In the first case $a_D$ is new and has acquired support $I\setminus D$; if $S^D$ is empty, the extension is a singleton and its support is empty. Consequently, if $H$ is dismantlable ample but $S^D$ is not, then $D\subseteq I$ and $|I\setminus D|\ge 3$. In particular, when $|I|=3$, every reduction of $S$ on a nonempty coordinate set is dismantlable ample.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Only the fibre through $a$ can become a new full $D$-fibre. If $D\subseteq I$, the punctured $I$-cube supplies all its other concepts, so its projection $a_D$ is newly present. If $D$ contains a coordinate outside $I$, the corresponding neighbour of $a$ is absent and the fibre remains incomplete. In the first case the surviving incident directions are exactly $I\setminus D$, giving the asserted acquired support. Strong projections preserve dismantlable ampleness by ordering full fibres according to their completion times in an ample-prefix order. Hence $H^D$ and $S^D$ must differ whenever the former peels and the latter does not, forcing $D\subseteq I$. Their difference is then a resolving one-concept addition, and rank-two extension invariance forces its support to have size at least three. A nonempty $D$ cannot satisfy this when $|I|=3$.

                                                                References:

                                                                [BousquetYangComplex26]

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#prop:damp-repair-strong-projections

                                                                Adjacent Degree-Three Corner-Pair Descent

                                                                Name: Adjacent Degree-Three Corner-Pair Descent

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Concept Deletion
                                                                • Partial-Cube Minor

                                                                Result Type: Implication

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $H\subseteq Q_F$ be an irredundantly embedded ample forbidden pc-minor for the dismantlable ample classes. If $c,u$ are adjacent degree-three corners, then each of $H\setminus\{c\}$, $H\setminus\{u\}$, and $H\setminus\{c,u\}$ is again an ample forbidden pc-minor. Consequently, a degree-three corner of a corner-descent-terminal ample forbidden pc-minor has no corner as a neighbour.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Adjacent corners share their unique maximal three-cube. Deleting both leaves an ample irredundant family $G$, and re-adding either tip has the same acquired two-coordinate support. Adjacent square-completion invariance makes $G$ nonpeelable. For every elementary pc-minor, the image of $H$ equals the image of $G$, or is obtained from it by one addition of support at most two, or by an adjacent pair whose common individual support has size at most two. Rank-two one-concept invariance and adjacent-pair invariance therefore make every proper elementary image of $G$ peelable, proving that $G$ is forbidden. Either single deletion is nonpeelable because a peeling could be prefixed by the deleted corner to peel $H$; the one-concept obstruction atlas then makes both single deletions forbidden. Adjacent corners have the same maximal cube and degree, so the terminality assertion follows.

                                                                References:

                                                                [BousquetYangComplex26]

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#cor:damp-degree-three-corner-pair-descent

                                                                Same-Shadow Exchange at a Punctured Face

                                                                Name: Same-Shadow Exchange at a Punctured Face

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Concept Deletion

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $S$ be a cornerless ample forbidden pc-minor for the dismantlable ample classes, let $(a,I)$ be punctured-face data for $S$, and put $A=S\cup\{a\}$. Define $\mathcal E_S(a,I)$ to consist of the nontrivial $I$-flips $a^U$ that have no neighbour in $S$ in a direction outside $I$. Then the corners of $A$ are exactly the disjoint union of $\{a\}$ and $\mathcal E_S(a,I)$. For every exposed tip $c$, the exchange $T_c=(S\setminus\{c\})\cup\{a\}$ is ample and has the same shattered-set complex as $S$. The datum $(a,I)$ is peelable exactly when $T_c$ is dismantlable ample for some exposed tip $c$. No exposed tip is at Hamming distance one from $a$. If $|I|=2$, every $T_c$ is isomorphic to $S$, so the datum is obstruction-preserving; consequently every peelable punctured-face datum over a cornerless forbidden family has $|I|\ge 3$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The new tip $a$ is a corner of $A$ with completed $I$-cube as its unique maximal cube. Any other corner must have a maximal cube containing $a$, since otherwise it would already be a corner of the cornerless family $S$; this identifies it exactly with an exposed tip. Deleting such a corner removes the unique newly shattered support $I$, so the exchanged family is ample with the same shadow as $S$. A peeling of $A$ cannot start by deleting $a$, because that leaves nonpeelable $S$; its other possible first vertices are precisely the exposed tips, proving the exchange criterion. A distance-one exposed tip would already be a corner of $S$. For $|I|=2$, the only possible exposed tip is opposite $a$ in the completed square, and swapping the two opposite vertices is an automorphism of $A$, so every exchange is isomorphic to $S$ and cannot peel.

                                                                References:

                                                                [BousquetYangComplex26]

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#prop:damp-same-shadow-corner-exchange

                                                                Corner Formula for a Maximum-Class Mutation

                                                                Name: Corner Formula for a Maximum-Class Mutation

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Maximum Classes
                                                                • Cornerless Ample Classes

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let maximum classes $C,C'\subseteq Q_n$ have VC dimension $d$ and differ by the legal exchange $C'=(C\setminus\{r\})\cup\{a\}$. Put $U=(C\setminus\{r\})\cap(N(r)\setminus N(a))$ and $V=(C\setminus\{r\})\cap(N(a)\setminus N(r))$. The incident coordinate sets at $r$ in $C$ and at $a$ in $C'$ agree; writing their common degree as $q$, one has $|\operatorname{Cor}(C')|-|\operatorname{Cor}(C)|=|\{v\in U:\deg_C(v)=d+1\}|-|\{v\in V:\deg_C(v)=d\}|$. Moreover $C'$ is cornerless exactly when $q>d$, every corner of $C$ lies in $V$, and no vertex of $U$ has degree $d+1$. In particular, if $C$ has exactly two corners, a one-mutation move to a cornerless maximum class requires those corners to have Hamming distance two. These conditions evaluate a legal mutation; they do not by themselves prove that the exchanged family is maximum.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Every maximal cube of a maximum VC-$d$ class has dimension $d$, each $d$-support carries exactly one cube, and a vertex is a corner exactly when its degree is $d$. Under the exchange, each $d$-cube through $r$ is replaced by the corresponding cube through $a$ and every other cube survives, so the exchanged vertices have the same incident coordinate set. Among surviving vertices, precisely those in $U$ lose one neighbour and precisely those in $V$ gain one. Thus the new surviving corners are the old degree-$(d+1)$ vertices of $U$, while the lost corners are the old degree-$d$ vertices of $V$; $r$ and $a$ contribute equally. This gives the formula and the cornerless criterion. If two old corners are both lost, they are distinct neighbours of $a$ and therefore differ in exactly two coordinates.

                                                                References:

                                                                [BousquetYangComplex26]

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#prop:damp-maximum-mutation-corner-elimination

                                                                • Hall Reverse-Mutation Corner-Elimination Neighbor

                                                                Two-Corner Mutation Paths from a Hall Projection

                                                                Name: Two-Corner Mutation Paths from a Hall Projection

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Maximum Classes

                                                                Result Type: Construction

                                                                Statement:

                                                                A bounded mutation search from Hall's coordinate-zero projection discovered 505 distinct 232-word maximum VC-three classes in $Q_{11}$, all with exactly two corners; 128 states were processed and 377 remained pending. Two verified three-step paths move the two original corners separately, and their six-step concatenation ends with corner set $\{1537,2023\}$ of Hamming distance six. No zero- or one-corner class occurs among the discovered states.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The archived independent verifier checks maximum VC-three trace conditions and the exact two-corner set for all 505 saved word lists, replays every saved transition from the seed, and verifies the concatenated six exchanges and final word list. It also confirms the final corner distance directly.

                                                                External Section Types around a Marked Four-Cube

                                                                Name: External Section Types around a Marked Four-Cube

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Maximum Classes
                                                                • Cornerless Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Coordinate Conditioning
                                                                • Coordinate Projection
                                                                • Full Reduction

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $X\subseteq Q_{\{1,2,3,4\}\sqcup J}$ be a cornerless maximum class of VC dimension three. Suppose its zero external face is $Q_4\setminus\{7\}$ and the marked vertices $(0,0),(1,0),(8,0)$ have no neighbours in directions from $J$. For each $j\in J$, the first-four-coordinate projection of the section $x_j=1$ is exactly $Q_4\setminus\{0,1,3,7,8\}$ or $Q_4\setminus\{0,1,5,7,8\}$. If $A,B$ are the coordinates of these two types, then $|A|,|B|\ge2$; the fibre over pattern 3 uses only $B$, and that over pattern 5 uses only $A$. Thus for $|J|=7$ the type sizes are $2+5$ or $3+4$, up to symmetry. If $|B|=2$, the pattern-3 fibre is the full $B$-square and the fibres over 2 and 11 contain that square; symmetrically, the same holds for patterns 5, 4, and 13 when $|A|=2$. These are necessary conditions, not an existence or sufficiency result.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Projection to the marked four coordinates is the fifteen-vertex face, since realizing pattern 7 would shatter four coordinates. Each marked fibre is an ample connected coordinate face whose zero vertex is isolated, hence is a singleton. Projecting additionally to an external coordinate gives a 26-word maximum rank-three class; its one-section is therefore an eleven-word maximum rank-two class. Connectivity of its five-word complement forces its extra omitted pattern to be 3 or 5. The type and fibre-support conclusions follow. Minimum degree four at the base vertices over patterns 3 and 5 forces at least two coordinates of each type. When one type has size two, cornerlessness at every nonzero square vertex forces the whole square and its two possible horizontal neighbours, yielding the final containments.

                                                                Hall Double-Reduction Leaves Need Not Lift to Corners

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For all twelve recorded two-corner Hall reverse-mutation controls, reduction in the marked two-coordinate type is an eleven-vertex maximum rank-one class, hence a tree; in fact every such tree is a path with two leaves. At each of the resulting 24 leaves, every external escape profile is a proper subset of the lifted square, yet two profiles cover the entire square, and two is the minimum cover size. Thus a leaf of the double reduction, even when the reduction is a path, does not by itself force a corner in the lifted maximum rank-three class.

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The archived replay reconstructs all twelve marked Hall controls from the Hall word list and their coordinate orders. It recomputes each full-square reduction, its ten distinctly labelled edges, its two leaves, and every proper escape profile. For every leaf it verifies coverage of all four square vertices and exhaustively checks that the minimum profile cover has size two.

                                                                Trace Transport for a Binary Layer System

                                                                Name: Trace Transport for a Binary Layer System

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Coordinate Conditioning
                                                                • Coordinate Projection

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $E,F$ be disjoint and choose an arbitrary section $H_t\subseteq Q_F$ for each $t\in Q_E$, forming $X=\dot\bigcup_{t\in Q_E}(H_t\times\{t\})$. For $L\subseteq E$ and $r\in Q_L$, put $H_{L,r}=\bigcup_{t|_L=r}H_t$. Then for every $D\subseteq F$, $q\in Q_D$, one has $X[D\cup L,(q,r)]=\dot\bigcup_{t|_L=r}(H_t[D,q]\times\{t\})$. Consequently, $D\cup L$ is shattered by $X$ exactly when $D$ belongs to $\bigcap_{r\in Q_L}\operatorname{Sh}(H_{L,r})$. The marked layer coordinates recover every $H_t$ as the projected $t$-section, so this is an exact and canonically recoverable trace table for any finite binary layer system.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                A vertex $(x,t)$ has trace $(q,r)$ on $D\cup L$ exactly when $x|_D=q$ and $t|_L=r$. Partitioning the trace fibre by the full layer word gives the disjoint-union identity. The support is shattered precisely when that fibre is nonempty for every pair $(q,r)$; for fixed $r$, this says exactly that the union $H_{L,r}$ shatters $D$. Sectioning on the marked coordinates gives the recovery statement.

                                                                [BousquetYangComplex26]

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                Independent Repair-Layer Criterion

                                                                Name: Independent Repair-Layer Criterion

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let nonempty layer coordinates $E$ be disjoint from $F$, let $S\subseteq Q_F$ be ample, and choose pairwise distinct absent tips $a_t$ for $t$ in $T\subseteq Q_E$, each making $S\cup\{a_t\}$ ample with unique acquired support $P_t$. The assembly $X_T=(S\times Q_E)\cup\{(a_t,t):t\in T\}$ is ample exactly when $t\mapsto P_t$ is injective. Under this condition, if $\Sigma=\operatorname{Sh}(S)$ and $\Sigma^+=\Sigma\dot\cup\{P_t:t\in T\}$, then $\operatorname{Sh}(X_T)=\{D\cup L:D\in\Sigma,L\subseteq E\}\dot\cup\{P_t:t\in T\}$. Its minimal nonfaces are $\mathcal N(\Sigma^+)\dot\cup\{P_t\cup\{e\}:t\in T,e\in E\}$. Old-coordinate clauses have the signs of $S\cup\{a_t:t\in T\}$, while the clause on $P_t\cup\{e\}$ omits $(a_t|_{P_t},1-t_e)$. These clauses reconstruct the assembly. From the marked layers one recovers $S$ as the intersection of all sections, $T$ as the non-core sections, each singleton tip difference, and each $P_t$ from its neighbours in $S$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Distinct acquired supports give $|S|+|U|$ distinct strongly shattered supports in every union $S\cup\{a_t:t\in U\}$, so Sandwich equality makes each union ample with exactly the expected shadow. Trace transport then shows that a support using a nonempty layer set sees only the core shadow, while the old-coordinate projection gains the $P_t$, proving the formula and ampleness. If two tips share a support, a layer coordinate on which their words differ creates one additional mixed shattered support beyond the Sandwich bound, so the assembly is not ample. Minimality in the displayed shadow gives precisely the stated old and mixed nonfaces. The missing old trace for $P_t$ occurs only at tip $a_t$, so adjoining a layer coordinate changes its missing bit to $1-t_e$. Intersections and section differences give the inverse formulas.

                                                                References:

                                                                [BousquetYangComplex26]

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#prop:damp-independent-repair-layers

                                                                Replicated Repair-Layer Criterion

                                                                Name: Replicated Repair-Layer Criterion

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $S\subseteq Q_F$ be ample, let $\mathcal A$ be finitely many absent tips whose ample one-concept extensions acquire pairwise distinct supports $P_a$, and give each tip a nonempty occurrence family $R_a\subseteq Q_E$ on nonempty disjoint layer coordinates. For $X(\mathbf R)=(S\times Q_E)\cup\bigcup_{a\in\mathcal A}(\{a\}\times R_a)$, one has $\operatorname{Sh}(X(\mathbf R))=\{D\cup L:D\in\operatorname{Sh}(S),L\subseteq E\}\dot\cup\dot\bigcup_{a\in\mathcal A}\{P_a\cup L:L\in\operatorname{Sh}(R_a)\}$. Hence $X(\mathbf R)$ is ample exactly when every occurrence family $R_a$ is ample. In that case, writing $\Sigma^+=\operatorname{Sh}(S)\dot\cup\{P_a\}$ and $\Gamma_a=\operatorname{Sh}(R_a)$, its minimal nonfaces are $\mathcal N(\Sigma^+)\dot\cup\dot\bigcup_a\{P_a\cup J:J\in\mathcal N(\Gamma_a)\}$; the corresponding mixed sign is $(a|_{P_a},\sigma_{R_a}(J))$, with old signs inherited from $S\cup\mathcal A$. Thus old repair clauses and layer clauses compose without another compatibility condition. If every $R_a$ is proper, all parameters are recovered from the marked sections; in general, absorbing every full occurrence row $R_a=Q_E$ into the common core gives the unique normalized presentation.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                For each layer trace, the union of compatible sections is the core together with exactly those tips whose occurrence family realizes that trace. Distinct-support Sandwich equality says this union shatters $P_a$ exactly when it contains $a$. Trace transport therefore makes $P_a\cup L$ shattered exactly when $R_a$ shatters $L$, proving the shadow formula. The global Sandwich defect is the sum over $a$ of $|\operatorname{Sh}(R_a)|-|R_a|$, so it vanishes exactly when every occurrence family is ample. Minimal nonfaces then split into the old minimal nonfaces and a repair support joined to a minimal layer nonface. The unique old missing trace for $P_a$ occurs over precisely $R_a$, which gives the product sign. Proper rows are absent from some section and are separated from the common intersection; full rows lie in every section and are therefore absorbed uniquely into the normalized core.

                                                                References:

                                                                [BousquetYangComplex26]

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#prop:damp-replicated-repair-layers

                                                                Layer-Minor Calculus for Replicated Repairs

                                                                Name: Layer-Minor Calculus for Replicated Repairs

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Coordinate Conditioning
                                                                • Coordinate Projection
                                                                • Partial-Cube Minor

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For a replicated repair assembly $X(\mathbf R)=(S\times Q_E)\cup\bigcup_a(\{a\}\times R_a)$ and a layer coordinate $e\in E$, restriction to $e=i$ replaces every occurrence row by $\rho_e^iR_a=\{t|_{E\setminus\{e\}}:t\in R_a,t_e=i\}$, while contraction of $e$ replaces it by $\pi_eR_a=\{t|_{E\setminus\{e\}}:t\in R_a\}$. Empty rows are discarded and full rows are absorbed into the common core. The normalized images are again replicated repair assemblies with the surviving acquired-support labels $P_a$. Thus all elementary pc-minors in marked layer coordinates are computed inside the finite labelled occurrence cover. In particular, if the assembly is a forbidden pc-minor for the dismantlable ample classes, all $3|E|$ normalized layer-coordinate images are dismantlable ample.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                A word survives the restriction $e=i$ exactly when its layer word has bit $i$ there, and suppressing the coordinate produces $\rho_e^iR_a$. Coordinate contraction is the union of the two restricted sections, hence projects each row to $\pi_eR_a$. The replicated-repair recovery theorem gives the stated normalization and preserves the surviving labels. The final assertion is the elementary-minor condition for forbidden pc-minors.

                                                                [BousquetYangComplex26]

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                Corners and Layer-Minimality of a Replicated Repair Cover

                                                                Name: Corners and Layer-Minimality of a Replicated Repair Cover

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes
                                                                • Cornerless Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Coordinate Conditioning
                                                                • Coordinate Projection
                                                                • Full Reduction

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                In a replicated repair assembly with ample proper occurrence rows, put $C=S\cup\mathcal A$ and let $Q_a$ be the completed cube on the acquired support $P_a$. Then $Q_a$ is the unique maximal cube of $C$ through $a$, and the maximal cubes of the assembly through $(a,t)$ are exactly $Q_a\times K$, where $K$ ranges over maximal cubes of $R_a$ through $t$. If $S$ is cornerless, the corner set is the disjoint union $\dot\bigcup_a(\{a\}\times\operatorname{Cor}(R_a))$. Suppose further that $S$ is nonpeelable, every one-tip repair $S\cup\{a\}$ is dismantlable ample, and every $R_a$ is dismantlable ample. For a layer restriction or contraction $\nu$, the image $\nu X(\mathbf R)$ is dismantlable ample exactly when some image row $\nu R_a$ is the full remaining layer cube. Consequently, all elementary layer-coordinate pc-minors are dismantlable ample exactly when every signed facet $\{t:t_e=i\}$ of $Q_E$ is contained in at least one occurrence row.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Every old-coordinate union obtained by retaining a subset of tips is ample, so each tip is a corner of $C$ with unique cube $Q_a$. A cube through $(a,t)$ projects inside $Q_a$ and uses a layer face contained in $R_a$; conversely the full product with any such layer cube is present, proving the product description. Properness prevents a base cube from extending through a tip in every layer, so a cornerless seed contributes no corners and the exact formula follows. For a layer minor with no full row, strong projection onto the remaining layer block gives the nonpeelable seed, so the image cannot peel. If some rows are full, absorb them into the core, peel all but one absorbed tip to a dismantlable one-tip repair, lift peelings of every remaining proper row, and finish with a Cartesian product. A restricted row is full exactly when its signed facet lies in the original row; either full restriction also makes the contraction full, giving the finite facet-cover test.

                                                                References:

                                                                [BousquetYangComplex26]

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#prop:damp-replicated-repair-corners

                                                                Compatible Repairs Do Not Collide

                                                                Name: Compatible Repairs Do Not Collide

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Coordinate Conditioning
                                                                • Coordinate Projection
                                                                • Concept Deletion

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $S\subseteq Q_F$ be ample and let $\mathcal A\subseteq Q_F\setminus S$ consist of individually ample one-concept extensions with pairwise distinct acquired supports. Then no two tips in $\mathcal A$ are adjacent in the ambient cube. More generally, after restricting or contracting one old coordinate, discard tips that do not survive or whose images enter the image of $S$. The old-coordinate map is injective on all remaining tips. After any subset of those projected tips is retained, every retained tip is a corner of the resulting old-coordinate family.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                If two tips with distinct supports were adjacent in coordinate $f$, neither support would contain $f$. Their simultaneous extension is ample. Contracting $f$ would merge the two tips into one new word, increasing cardinality by one, while both distinct acquired supports survive and increase the shadow by at least two, contradicting cardinality-shadow equality for the ample contracted families. Restrictions are injective on surviving tips, and contractions can identify only adjacent tips, proving image injectivity. For any retained subset, the full and one-tip-deleted old-coordinate families are images of ample simultaneous extensions and differ by exactly that tip; the ample corner-deletion criterion makes it a corner independently of the subset.

                                                                References:

                                                                [BousquetYangComplex26]

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#lem:damp-compatible-repairs-do-not-collide

                                                                Simultaneous Extensions Grouped by Acquired Support

                                                                Name: Simultaneous Extensions Grouped by Acquired Support

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Full Reduction
                                                                • Concept Deletion

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let nonempty ample $S\subseteq Q_F$ and let $U\subseteq Q_F\setminus S$ be finitely many tips such that every one-tip extension $S\cup\{a\}$ is ample, with acquired support $I_a$. For each occurring support $I$, put $U_I=\{a:I_a=I\}$ and $R_I=\{a|_{F\setminus I}:a\in U_I\}$, and let $X=S\cup U$. Then $X$ is ample exactly when every row $R_I$ is ample. Under these conditions, $X^I=R_I$ and $\operatorname{Sh}(X)=\operatorname{Sh}(S)\dot\cup\dot\bigcup_I\{I\cup J:J\in\operatorname{Sh}(R_I)\}$. Moreover, $X$ peels to $S$ exactly when every row $R_I$ is dismantlable ample. The empty tip set is allowed.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                All tips in one group realize the unique trace of $I$ missing from $S$, and no tip from another group can realize that trace without acquiring $I$ as a second support. Thus the full $I$-fibres of $X$ occur exactly over $R_I$, proving $X^I=R_I$ and necessity by reduction closure. Conversely, each cube in $R_I$ lifts through the punctured $I$-fibres in $S$ to a full cube on $I$ together with its row support. Contributions from distinct acquired supports cannot contain one another and are disjoint. If all rows are ample, their shadow sizes sum with $|S|$ to $|X|$, so Sandwich equality proves ampleness and the exact shadow. A tip is a corner exactly when its row projection is a corner, even after arbitrary other tips have been deleted. Row peelings therefore lift and concatenate to a peeling down to $S$, while any relative peeling projects to complete peelings of every row.

                                                                References:

                                                                [BousquetYangComplex26]

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#thm:damp-equal-support-extensions

                                                                Proper-Minor Positivity for Simultaneous Initial Tips

                                                                Name: Proper-Minor Positivity for Simultaneous Initial Tips

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Coordinate Conditioning
                                                                • Partial-Cube Minor
                                                                • Concept Deletion

                                                                Result Type: Implication

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For an ample simultaneous extension $X=S\cup U$ grouped into row families $R_I$ by acquired support, every $R_I$ is a proper coordinate face of $X$. Hence if $X$ is dismantlable ample, or merely if all proper coordinate faces of $X$ are dismantlable ample, then $X$ peels to $S$. If $S$ is additionally an ample forbidden pc-minor using every ambient coordinate, the following are equivalent: every $R_I$ is dismantlable ample; $X$ peels to $S$; every nonempty proper pc-minor of $X$ is dismantlable ample; and $X$ is either dismantlable ample or a forbidden pc-minor. When $X$ is forbidden, every intermediate family in any relative peeling from $X$ to $S$ is also forbidden. Consequently, a corner-descent-terminal forbidden class cannot properly contain such a forbidden $S$ when all additional vertices are individually ample additions to $S$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Fixing the acquired-support coordinates to their unique missing trace leaves precisely $R_I$, and the face is proper because nonempty $S$ realizes no vertex with that trace. Positivity of these faces makes every row peelable, so the simultaneous-extension theorem lifts their peelings to $S$. Over a forbidden seed, transporting a relative peeling through any elementary coordinate operation yields a relative peeling to the corresponding proper image of $S$, which is dismantlable ample because the seed uses every coordinate. This proves positivity of every proper minor and the equivalences. If an intermediate family were peelable, preceding corner deletions would peel $X$; transporting its remaining relative chain to elementary minors shows all of its proper minors are positive, so every intermediate family is forbidden.

                                                                References:

                                                                [BousquetYangComplex26]

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#cor:damp-initial-tip-minor-positivity

                                                                Complete Common-Seed Occurrence-Cover Criterion

                                                                Name: Complete Common-Seed Occurrence-Cover Criterion

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Coordinate Conditioning
                                                                • Coordinate Projection
                                                                • Partial-Cube Minor
                                                                • Full Reduction

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $S$ be an irredundantly embedded ample forbidden pc-minor for the dismantlable ample classes. Choose finitely many distinct-support tips $a$ such that every one-tip repair $S\cup\{a\}$ is dismantlable ample, and assign each tip a nonempty proper ample occurrence row $R_a\subsetneq Q_E$ on nonempty layer coordinates. The replicated repair assembly $X(\mathbf R)$ is a forbidden pc-minor exactly when: (i) every $R_a$ is dismantlable ample; and (ii) every signed facet $\{t:t_e=i\}$ of the layer cube is contained in some occurrence row. No further old-coordinate condition is needed. The normalized marked sections recover $S$ and every labelled triple $(a,P_a,R_a)$, so the criterion is exact within the common-seed class over a fixed forbidden seed. It remains a relative classification because the seed is assumed and row peelability is a recognition condition.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The assembly is ample by the replicated-repair theorem and nonpeelable because strong projection along all proper rows gives the forbidden seed. If it is forbidden, each row is a proper coordinate face and hence peelable, while the layer-minimality theorem forces the signed-facet cover. Conversely, the facet cover makes every elementary layer restriction and contraction peelable. Under an old-coordinate operation, compatible repairs remain distinct and every surviving projected tip stays a corner after arbitrary other tips are removed. Lift a peeling of each occurrence row to remove its whole projected repair row, in any order, leaving the product of the proper seed image with the layer cube. Irredundancy makes that seed image a proper positive minor, and product closure finishes the peeling. Thus all elementary minors are dismantlable ample, while the full assembly is not, proving forbiddenness. Canonical recovery follows from intersecting and comparing the marked sections.

                                                                [BousquetYangComplex26]

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#thm:damp-common-seed-cover-classification

                                                                Layerwise Separation of Unique-Midpoint Cores

                                                                Name: Layerwise Separation of Unique-Midpoint Cores

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For a replicated repair assembly $X(\mathbf R)$ with ample proper occurrence rows, let $H_t=S\cup\{a:t\in R_a\}$ be its old-coordinate section at layer word $t$, and write $\kappa$ for the largest unique-midpoint core. If every row has empty core, then $\kappa(X(\mathbf R))=\dot\bigcup_{t\in Q_E}(\kappa(H_t)\times\{t\})$. In particular, if all occurrence rows and all sections $H_t$ are corner-peelable, the assembled family has empty unique-midpoint core.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                A unique-midpoint constraint rooted at a repair occurrence cannot use two old directions or one old and one layer direction, because the product of its completed repair cube with every layer edge supplies the opposite midpoint. Any constraint rooted there is therefore exactly a lifted constraint of its occurrence row; empty row cores exclude all repair occurrences from a core of the assembly. A remaining root lies in the full product $S\times Q_E$. Two layer directions or one layer and one old direction span a full square, so every surviving witness uses two old directions inside one section $H_t$. This gives one inclusion. Conversely, horizontal distance-two pairs have both candidate midpoints in their own layer, so each section-core constraint is unchanged in the assembly and the union of all lifted section cores is again a core.

                                                                References:

                                                                [BousquetYangComplex26]

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#prop:damp-layer-midpoint-cores

                                                                Successful Layer Sets Force Empty Unique-Midpoint Core

                                                                Name: Successful Layer Sets Force Empty Unique-Midpoint Core

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Result Type: Implication

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Every forbidden pc-minor produced by the complete common-seed occurrence-cover criterion has empty unique-midpoint core. More generally, any ample forbidden pc-minor with a successful layer set has empty core. Hence a nonempty unique-midpoint core excludes every successful layer set. The converse fails: an ample forbidden pc-minor may have empty core without admitting a successful layer set.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The common-seed criterion makes every occurrence row corner-peelable. Each old-coordinate section is a proper pc-minor because the layer set is nonempty and the seed occurs in every layer, so every section is also corner-peelable. The layerwise core formula therefore gives an empty core. The terminal clause-recovery theorem places every successful layer presentation in this common-seed form. For the converse failure, the certified 292-concept obstruction has empty core and exactly one corner. Any successful layer presentation needs at least two nonempty proper rows to own opposite signed facets; each row has a corner that lifts to a distinct occurrence corner, contradicting uniqueness.

                                                                [BousquetYangComplex26]

                                                                Witnesses:

                                                                • One-Corner Forbidden Family with Empty Midpoint Core

                                                                Terminal Empty-Core Obstruction Towers

                                                                Name: Terminal Empty-Core Obstruction Towers

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Result Type: Construction

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For every $r\ge1$, the antipodal repair tower $X_r=(G\times Q_r)\cup(\{91\}\times(Q_r\setminus\{0^r\}))\cup(\{157\}\times(Q_r\setminus\{1^r\}))$ over the certified cornerless 291-concept seed is a corner-descent-terminal ample forbidden pc-minor with empty unique-midpoint core. It has isometric dimension $12+r$, exactly $293\cdot2^r-2$ concepts, and exactly $2r$ corners. For $r=1$, deleting either corner leaves a unique-midpoint core of order 76. Thus terminality restores neither the implication from empty core to peelability nor the existence of a corner whose deletion preserves empty core.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The two tips have certified peelable one-concept extensions and acquire distinct four-coordinate supports. The antipodal repair-tower theorem gives ampleness, forbiddenness, order, and dimension, while the complementary punctured rows partition all signed layer facets and the terminal facet-partition theorem gives corner-descent terminality. Each punctured $r$-cube row has $r$ corners and the seed has none, so the repair-cover corner formula gives $2r$ corners. Successful-layer core separation makes the tower core empty. At $r=1$, deleting either occurrence corner removes its row; the remaining sections are the 76-core seed and an empty-core one-tip repair, so the layerwise formula gives core order 76. The archived checker independently verifies the seed and repair hashes, exact shadows, corners, static pruning orders, and core witnesses for $r=1,2$ and all their corner deletions.

                                                                Universality of Peelable Occurrence Rows

If $K\subseteq Q_D$, add a layer bit $z$, set $E=D\dot\cup\{z\}$, choose $u\in Q_E$, and use occurrence rows $R_0=K\times\{0\}$, $R_+=Q_E\setminus\{u\}$, and $R_-=Q_E\setminus\{\bar u\}$ at the three tips. Fixing the old coordinates to $a_0$ and $z=0$ recovers $K$. Hall's class with tips 183, 315, and 1836 supplies the required seed triple, so the conclusion is unconditional.

The common-seed occurrence-cover criterion therefore makes the assembly an ample forbidden pc-minor independently of the shape of $R_0$. Only $R_0$ occurs at old word $a_0$, and restricting its added bit to zero gives $K$ as a proper face. The certified Hall repair atlas verifies the three distinct-support peelable repairs.

                                                                Universality within Reduced Forbidden Bases

                                                                Name: Universality within Reduced Forbidden Bases

                                                                Classes:

Such bases exist infinitely often with isometric dimension minus VC dimension equal to nine.

                                                                Proof:

                                                                First replace $K$ by its product with an edge and glue a square at zero, obtaining a row $L$ of order $2|K|+3$ that is peelable whenever $K$ is. The replicated-repair theorem gives ampleness, and strong projection to the proper-row core gives Hall's nonpeelable seed, so every output is nonpeelable. The common-seed criterion makes the output forbidden exactly when $K$ peels; conversely, a forbidden output must have its proper face $K$ peelable. The intact seed product supplies minimum degree four and every crossing edge. Old four-support clauses distinguish all seed coordinates, while the square-gluing and constant-coordinate clauses distinguish every layer coordinate, proving signed-column separation. Direct counting and the repair shadow formula give the stated order, dimension, and VC dimension. Hypercube inputs in unbounded dimension yield infinitely many pairwise nonisomorphic forbidden bases with gap nine.

                                                                Clause Transport and Change of pc-Minimality

                                                                Name: Clause Transport and Change of pc-Minimality

The map $K\mapsto X_K$ is injective and preserves both the number of changed clauses and total changed sign-bit distance between two inputs. Every output is nonpeelable, and $X_K$ is a forbidden pc-minor exactly when $K$ is dismantlable ample. The replicated-repair formulas prepend the same seed trace to each input clause and fix all other output clauses, proving the transport and distance assertions. A fixed proper face recovers $K$, giving injectivity. Reduced-base universality gives nonpeelability for every output and forbiddenness exactly for peelable inputs.
