                                                                Ambient-Cube Corner-Descent Criterion

                                                                Name: Ambient-Cube Corner-Descent Criterion

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Concept Deletion
                                                                • Cube Complement

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $A\subsetneq Q_E$ be nonempty and ample. A sequence of corner deletions takes the ambient cube $Q_E$ to $A$ if and only if the cube complement $Q_E\setminus A$ is dismantlable ample.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Write $B=Q_E\setminus A$, which is ample by complement duality. If $b_1,\ldots,b_m$ are deleted from the cube, every residual complement $\{b_1,\ldots,b_j\}$ is ample. Reversing these ample prefixes gives a corner peeling of $B$. Conversely, reverse a peeling of $B$. Its successive prefixes $B_j$ are ample, so their complements are ample; the ample corner-deletion criterion makes each next $b_j$ a corner of $Q_E\setminus B_{j-1}$, producing the descent to $A$.

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#lem:damp-ambient-cube-descent

                                                                Comments:

                                                                This converts generation by deletion from a cube into an ordinary peelability test for the complement.

                                                                Prescribed Sections in Complements of Obstructions

                                                                Name: Prescribed Sections in Complements of Obstructions

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Cartesian Product
                                                                • Coordinate Conditioning
                                                                • Cube Complement
                                                                • Partial-Cube Minor

                                                                Result Type: Construction

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $S$ be an irredundantly embedded ample forbidden pc-minor with three resolving one-concept additions $a_0,a_+,a_-$ having pairwise distinct acquired supports. For nonempty proper $K\in\mathcal D_{\rm amp}$ on a disjoint coordinate set $D$ and $u\in Q_D$, set $X_K=(S\times Q_D)\cup(\{a_0\}\times K)\cup(\{a_+\}\times(Q_D\setminus\{u\}))\cup(\{a_-\}\times(Q_D\setminus\{\bar u\}))$. Then $X_K$ is an ample forbidden pc-minor, and the section of its cube complement at old word $a_0$ is exactly $Q_D\setminus K$. If this complementary section is nonpeelable, both $X_K$ and its cube complement are nonpeelable and $X_K$ cannot be obtained from its ambient cube by corner deletions. Moreover $|X_K|=(|S|+2)2^{|D|}+|K|-2$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The three occurrence rows are nonempty, proper, ample, and peelable. The two punctured cubes own opposite full facets for every coordinate of $D$, so the common-seed occurrence-cover theorem makes $X_K$ an ample forbidden pc-minor. Only the row $K$ occurs at old word $a_0$, giving the asserted complementary section. This is a proper pc-minor of the complement because the complement also contains $(a_+,u)$. A peeling of the complement would induce an ample-prefix order on the section, so a nonpeelable section forces the whole complement to be nonpeelable. The ambient-cube descent criterion then excludes a descent to $X_K$. The four parts are disjoint, and direct counting yields the order formula.

                                                                The theorem prescribes an arbitrary complement section arising as the complement of a nonempty proper dismantlable ample row; it does not claim that the resulting obstruction is terminal under obstruction-preserving corner deletion.

                                                                Common-Seed Obstruction Deletion Test

                                                                Name: Common-Seed Obstruction Deletion Test

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Concept Deletion
                                                                • Partial-Cube Minor

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $X(\mathbf R)$ be a forbidden pc-minor satisfying the common-seed occurrence-cover hypotheses. For $t\in R_a$, replace $R_a$ by $R_a^-=R_a\setminus\{t\}$, discarding the row label if it becomes empty. Then $X(\mathbf R)\setminus\{(a,t)\}$ is again a forbidden pc-minor if and only if $R_a^-$ is empty or dismantlable ample and the modified rows still own every signed layer facet. Whenever these conditions hold, $(a,t)$ is automatically a corner. If the seed is cornerless, the cover is terminal under obstruction-preserving corner deletion exactly when every row deletion either leaves a nonempty nonpeelable row or destroys signed-facet ownership.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                After deleting $(a,t)$ the family remains a replicated repair assembly over the same seed, with only one occurrence row changed. The replicated-layer criterion makes the new assembly ample exactly when the nonempty modified row is ample. After an empty row is discarded, the common-seed classification makes it forbidden exactly when all nonempty rows peel and every signed facet remains owned, giving the stated two conditions. When they hold, both the original and deleted families are ample, so the ample one-concept deletion criterion makes $(a,t)$ a corner. For a cornerless seed all assembly corners lie in the occurrence rows, and negating the test gives the terminality criterion.

                                                                Comments:

                                                                This is an exact test on the row data; the signed-facet partition theorem gives its structural normal form for cornerless seeds.

                                                                Signed-Facet Shell and Residual Core

                                                                Name: Signed-Facet Shell and Residual Core

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Coordinate Conditioning
                                                                • Peripheral Expansion

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For a proper family $R\subsetneq Q_E$, let $\mathcal O(R)$ be the signed facets $F_{e,i}$ contained in $R$, let $F_R$ be the face opposite every member of $\mathcal O(R)$, and put $B_R=R\cap F_R$. At most one sign of each coordinate occurs in $\mathcal O(R)$, and $R=(Q_E\setminus F_R)\mathbin{\dot\cup}B_R$. After suppressing the coordinates fixed on $F_R$, $R$ is ample exactly when $B_R$ is ample, and $R$ is dismantlable ample exactly when $B_R$ is dismantlable ample. The residual core $B_R$ has no full signed facet in its residual cube; the empty core is allowed as a terminal row.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                A proper row cannot contain both facets of one coordinate. The union of all contained facets is exactly the complement of their common opposite face, and the remaining row points form $B_R$. After reorientation, if $K$ is the set of shell coordinates and $L$ the rest, then $R=((Q_K\setminus\{\mathbf1_K\})\times Q_L)\cup(\{\mathbf1_K\}\times B_R)$. Adding the coordinates of $K$ one at a time is an iterated peripheral expansion with one full-cube section, so the exact expansion criterion transfers both ampleness and peelability between $R$ and $B_R$. A full residual facet in $B_R$ would extend through the shell to a full facet of $R$, contradicting its omission from $\mathcal O(R)$.

                                                                The regression certificate exhaustively checks all 65,808 proper rows in dimensions one through four, including the shell decomposition, both equivalences, and the empty-core corner and safe-deletion formulas.

                                                                Terminal Common-Seed Covers as Signed-Facet Partitions

                                                                Name: Terminal Common-Seed Covers as Signed-Facet Partitions

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Concept Deletion
                                                                • Partial-Cube Minor

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                In a terminal forbidden common-seed occurrence cover, the full-signed-facet sets $\mathcal O_a$ of the rows partition $E\times\{0,1\}$, and every row is exactly its facet shell $R_a=\bigcup_{(e,i)\in\mathcal O_a}F_{e,i}$. For a cornerless seed these conditions are also sufficient. Equivalently, every partition of the signed layer facets into nonempty blocks, with no block containing both signs of one coordinate, defines a corner-descent-terminal forbidden pc-minor by taking each occurrence row to be the union of its assigned facets. The marked rows canonically recover the partition.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                If a terminal row had nonempty residual core, peel the first core concept. The shell-core theorem keeps the modified row peelable, and no owned facet is lost, so the deletion test would produce another forbidden pc-minor, a contradiction. Thus every row is its shell. The ownership criterion makes the shell blocks cover all signed facets. If two rows owned one facet, a row corner lying only in that facet could be deleted while the second owner preserved coverage, again contradicting terminality; hence ownership is a partition. Conversely, each partition row has empty residual core and is therefore ample and peelable, while the partition covers all signed facets, so the common-seed theorem gives a forbidden pc-minor. A row corner lies in exactly one maximal owned facet, and deleting it destroys that uniquely owned facet. The deletion test then proves terminality. Full facets of each marked row recover its block.

                                                                This classifies terminal occurrence rows relative to a fixed cornerless forbidden seed and certified repair tips. It is not a classification of every terminal obstruction, nor an intrinsic classification of admissible seeds and repair tips.

                                                                Thickness of Terminal Facet Partitions

                                                                Name: Thickness of Terminal Facet Partitions

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Coordinate Conditioning

                                                                Result Type: Invariant Law

                                                                Statement:

                                                                In a terminal signed-facet partition on $r=|E|$ layer coordinates, let $K_a$ be the layer coordinates represented in owner block $\mathcal O_a$, and let $\lambda(e,i)$ own signed facet $(e,i)$. For the projected $e$-sections $H_i=\rho_e^iX$, one has $|H_i\setminus H_{1-i}|=2^{r-|K_{\lambda(e,i)}|}$. A layer coordinate has symmetric-difference order two exactly when there are two repair tips, in which case every layer coordinate does. With at least three repair tips, every coordinate of $X$, including each seed coordinate, has two nonempty exclusive sections whose total order is at least three.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                For the owner of $(e,i)$, the $i$-section of its row is full and the opposite section misses the face that fixes every other represented coordinate opposite its owned sign. That face has $2^{r-|K_a|}$ words; all nonowners have equal $e$-sections, proving the formula. Both exclusive parts have order one exactly when the two owners represent every coordinate, which exhausts the signed-facet partition and leaves exactly two tips. For an old coordinate, periphery-freeness of the seed supplies one exclusive old word on each side. The product core supplies all layer occurrences of it, and an opposite repair row can fill all but $2^{r-|K_a|}$ occurrences. Both sides remain nonempty; total order two would force two full-support owners and exclude a third tip.

                                                                Terminal Common-Seed Recovery from Signed Clauses

                                                                Name: Terminal Common-Seed Recovery from Signed Clauses

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Coordinate Conditioning
                                                                • Full Reduction
                                                                • Partial-Cube Minor
                                                                • Coordinate Projection

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $X\subseteq Q_V$ be nonempty and ample, and mark a nonempty coordinate set $E$. Let $\mathcal J$ be the minimal nonfaces of $\operatorname{Sh}(X)$ with missing traces $\sigma_J$. Require every $e\in E$ to occur in exactly two members of $\mathcal J$, with opposite missing signs. Put $F=V\setminus E$, let $C_E\subseteq Q_F$ be the family satisfying all clauses supported inside $F$, and for each mixed clause put $P_J=J\cap F$, $K_J=J\cap E$, and $T_J=\{x\in C_E:x|_{P_J}=\sigma_J|_{P_J}\}$. Then $(X,E)$ has a common-seed presentation with a nonempty ample seed, pairwise distinct acquired repair supports, and occurrence rows forming a partition of the signed $E$-facets if and only if all $T_J$ are pairwise distinct singletons $\{a_J\}$. The presentation is unique: $C_E$ is the projection of $X$ onto $F$, the seed is $S_E=C_E\setminus\{a_J\}=X^E$, the repair support is $P_J$, the owner support is $K_J$, and the owner signs are $1-\sigma_J|_{K_J}$. The seed and every one-tip extension $S_E\cup\{a_J\}$ are automatically ample. If $X$ is an irredundantly embedded ample forbidden pc-minor, then $S_E$ is a forbidden pc-minor and every one-tip extension is dismantlable ample; a cornerless recovered seed yields a terminal common-seed obstruction presentation.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                A given facet-partition presentation has one mixed clause per repair, and the missing old trace is supplied in the projection by that repair tip alone, so every trace fibre is its singleton. Conversely, the old clauses reconstruct the ample projection $C_E$. Distinct singleton fibres split it into tips and a seed, and the signed clauses reconstruct $X$ as the seed product together with rows that omit exactly one face on $K_J$; opposite two-clause incidence partitions all signed layer facets. Strong projection identifies the seed with $X^E$ and proves it ample and nonempty. Restricting to an owned facet recovers each ample one-tip extension. Minimal-nonface arguments force its acquired support to equal $P_J$ and make these supports distinct, proving uniqueness. For forbidden $X$, peel the punctured-cube rows down to $S_E\times Q_E$; peelability of the seed would then peel $X$, so the seed is nonpeelable. Its intermediate reductions remain nonpeelable, and inherited descent makes it forbidden. A proper facet minor similarly proves every one-tip extension peelable.

                                                                [BousquetYangComplex26]

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#thm:damp-terminal-clause-recovery

                                                                Witnesses:

                                                                • Hall Thick Terminal Three-Repair Obstruction

                                                                Comments:

                                                                This is an intrinsic recognition and uniqueness theorem for a marked layer set. It does not assert that every terminal forbidden pc-minor has a successful marked layer set. The certificates exhaust all families through dimension three and check fixed two-row and three-row controls, as well as the 1,203-concept Hall reconstruction.

                                                                One-Concept Repairs of a Recovered Facet Partition

                                                                Name: One-Concept Repairs of a Recovered Facet Partition

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Concept Deletion
                                                                • Full Reduction
                                                                • Partial-Cube Minor

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $X$ be an irredundantly embedded ample forbidden pc-minor with a successful recovered layer set $E$, seed $S$, tips $a_J$, repair supports $P_J$, owner supports $K_J$, and mixed missing traces $\sigma_J$. Its one-concept extensions in the dismantlable ample class are exactly the words $(a_J,\sigma_J|_E)$ for which $K_J=E$. Such an addition acquires support $P_J\cup E=J$. Hence there are at most two resolving tips, and there are two exactly when the recovered presentation has two repair tips with oppositely punctured layer-cube rows. If the recovered seed itself has a nonempty successful layer set $D$, then both presentations have exactly two tips and flatten uniquely into one antipodally punctured two-repair presentation on $E\cup D$ with seed $S^D$; in particular $E\cup D$ is successful for $X$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                If $X\cup\{z\}$ peels, its reduction along $E$ must peel although $X^E=S$ does not, so the added word must complete a layer fibre. A single addition can do this only at a repair tip whose omitted face is a singleton, equivalently $K_J=E$, and the missing word is $(a_J,\sigma_J|_E)$. Conversely, completing such a row joins it to the seed product; peel the other punctured rows and then use the certified peeling of $S\cup\{a_J\}$ and the product test. The new word has all layer neighbours and precisely the old neighbours on $P_J$, so its acquired support is $J$. Each layer coordinate has two owners, so at most two blocks can equal $E$; two such blocks exhaust the partition and are antipodal. For nested successful presentations, the outer layer coordinates provide two repairs of the inner seed, forcing both levels to be antipodal two-row presentations. Substitution combines their missing words into the asserted presentation on $E\cup D$.

                                                                [BousquetYangComplex26]

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#thm:damp-recovered-partition-resolving-tips

                                                                Witnesses:

                                                                • Hall Terminal Obstruction without a Resolving Tip
                                                                • Hall Thick Terminal Three-Repair Obstruction

                                                                Comments:

                                                                The archived verifier checks complete repair lists with zero, one, and two resolving tips and explicit peelings of every positive extension. The 2,410-concept example shows that a terminal obstruction need not itself have any resolving tip.

                                                                Forced Enlargement of Candidate Layer Sets

                                                                Name: Forced Enlargement of Candidate Layer Sets

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Coordinate Projection

                                                                Result Type: Algorithm

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $X$ be nonempty and ample, let $\mathcal B(X)$ be the coordinates occurring in exactly two signed minimal-nonface clauses with opposite signs, and start from nonempty $E_0\subseteq\mathcal B(X)$. For a current $E$, form every mixed-clause trace fibre $T_J^E$ in the old-coordinate projection and let $W(E)$ be the union of the coordinates on which words within one fibre vary. Fail if $W(E)\not\subseteq\mathcal B(X)$ or if two distinct mixed-clause fibres intersect; succeed and return $E$ if $W(E)=\varnothing$; otherwise replace $E$ by $E\cup W(E)$ and repeat. The procedure terminates in at most $|\mathcal B(X)|-|E_0|+1$ passes. On success it returns the unique smallest superset of $E_0$ satisfying the distinct-singleton recovery criterion; on failure no such superset exists. Successful layer sets are closed under nonempty intersections. Starting from every singleton in $\mathcal B(X)$ decides whether any successful nonempty layer set exists. Each failure has an explicit two-word outside-coordinate certificate or a two-clause common-word certificate.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                For $E\subseteq D\subseteq\mathcal B(X)$, projection maps every fibre $T_J^E$ into $T_J^D$. Therefore any successful $D$ must contain every coordinate on which a fibre at $E$ varies, and an intersection between two fibres at $E$ persists after projection, contradicting distinct singleton fibres. Inductively, every successful superset of $E_0$ contains every set generated by the procedure, while either failure excludes all such supersets. Each nonterminal successful pass adds a balanced coordinate. At termination every nonempty fibre has no varying coordinate and is therefore a singleton, and the collision test makes the singletons distinct. This proves termination, correctness, minimality, and uniqueness. Running from a member of any successful set must succeed; applying minimality to a nonempty intersection of successful sets proves intersection closure.

                                                                [BousquetYangComplex26]

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#thm:damp-forced-layer-closure

                                                                Comments:

                                                                The exhaustive certificate checks every nonempty ample family through dimension four, including forced growth and both failure-certificate types, and separately checks the Hall control. This theorem recognizes singleton recovery and does not require the recovered seed to be cornerless.

                                                                Largest Recovered Layer Set of an Ample Obstruction

                                                                Name: Largest Recovered Layer Set of an Ample Obstruction

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Full Reduction
                                                                • Partial-Cube Minor
                                                                • Coordinate Projection

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For an irredundantly embedded ample forbidden pc-minor $X$, call nonempty $E\subseteq\mathcal B(X)$ successful when it satisfies the distinct-singleton recovery criterion, without requiring a cornerless seed. Successful sets are closed under union. Thus, whenever recovery is possible, there is a unique largest successful set $E_{\max}(X)$, equal to the set of balanced coordinates whose singleton-start forced-enlargement procedure succeeds. Its recovered seed $X^{E_{\max}(X)}$ is determined by $X$ independently of any presentation choice.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Recover a presentation on one successful set $E$. Its seed is again an irredundant ample forbidden pc-minor, and signed-clause transport shows that balanced coordinates outside $E$ remain balanced in the seed. For a disjoint successful set $D$, singleton fibres force every seed clause meeting $D$ to come from one of two outer repairs whose owner supports equal all of $E$. These two blocks exhaust the signed $E$-facets and have antipodally punctured rows. The induced fibres in the seed are distinct singletons, so nested recovery makes $E\cup D$ successful. For overlapping $E,D$, strongly project their intersection. Their differences become disjoint successful sets in an irredundant forbidden reduction; applying the disjoint argument there and lifting by nested recovery again yields $E\cup D$. Finiteness makes the union of all successful sets successful. A coordinate belongs to this union exactly when its singleton-start closure succeeds, giving the formula and canonical seed.

                                                                [BousquetYangComplex26]

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#thm:damp-obstruction-layer-union

                                                                Comments:

                                                                Union closure uses obstruction minimality and is false for arbitrary ample families; the certificate includes a six-word peelable counterexample. Six certified obstruction models check disjoint and overlapping unions, signed seed-coordinate inheritance, and recovery of the largest set from singleton starts.

                                                                Layer-Recovery and Thin-Coordinate Dichotomy

                                                                Name: Layer-Recovery and Thin-Coordinate Dichotomy

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Coordinate Conditioning
                                                                • Full Reduction

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                For an irredundantly embedded ample forbidden pc-minor $X$, let $\mathcal L(X)$ be its successful layer sets and let $\mathcal T(X)$ be the coordinates whose two projected sections each have exactly one word absent from the other. Exactly one of two alternatives holds. If $\mathcal T(X)\ne\varnothing$, then $E_{\max}(X)=\mathcal T(X)$ and $\mathcal L(X)=2^{\mathcal T(X)}\setminus\{\varnothing\}$; the largest presentation has two repair tips with antipodally punctured rows, and $X$ has exactly two one-concept extensions in the dismantlable ample class. If $\mathcal T(X)=\varnothing$, then either no successful layer set exists or $\mathcal L(X)=\{E_{\max}(X)\}$; in the latter case $|E_{\max}(X)|\ge2$, the presentation has at least three repair tips, and $X$ has at most one dismantlable-ample one-concept extension. Hence a cornered terminal obstruction with every coordinate thick and two distinct resolving extensions has no common-seed presentation.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Inside a recovered presentation on $E$, the fibre for a proper nonempty sublayer set $D$ equals the repair tip times the face that fixes the remaining owner coordinates to their missing signs. Hence $D$ is successful exactly when every owner meeting $D$ contains all of $E\setminus D$. This can occur for a proper sublayer set exactly when there are two owners; then both owner supports are all of $E$ and every nonempty subset is successful. A singleton is successful exactly when its coordinate is thin. If a thin coordinate exists, it lies in the unique largest successful set, forces that presentation to have two owners, and all its nonempty subsets are successful; their singleton members identify the largest set with $\mathcal T(X)$. Without thin coordinates, any largest successful presentation has at least three owners and admits no proper successful subset. The resolving-tip theorem gives exactly two extensions in the first case and at most one in the second.

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#thm:damp-layer-recovery-dichotomy

                                                                Comments:

                                                                The fixed regressions verify the complete successful-set families, thin coordinates, owner counts, repair counts, sublayer fibre formula, and inherited balanced coordinates on six obstruction constructions.

                                                                Cornerless Recovery Requires a Maximal Layer Set

                                                                Name: Cornerless Recovery Requires a Maximal Layer Set

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Full Reduction
                                                                • Coordinate Projection

                                                                Result Type: Implication

                                                                Statement:

                                                                If a nonempty layer set $E$ satisfies the singleton recovery criterion for an ample family $X$ and its recovered seed $X^E$ is cornerless, then no proper superset of $E$ also satisfies that criterion. If $X$ is an irredundantly embedded ample forbidden pc-minor and $E$ is maximal among its successful layer sets, then $X^E$ has no nonempty successful layer set and no thin coordinate; it is a forbidden pc-minor with at least two one-concept repairs in the dismantlable ample class, but it need not be cornerless. Consequently, $X$ has a successful recovery with cornerless seed exactly when $E_{\max}(X)$ exists and $X^{E_{\max}(X)}$ is cornerless.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Suppose a proper successful superset $D$ existed. Recover the signed-facet presentation over $D$ and strongly project its rows along $E$. Every row owning a facet in $D\setminus E$ survives as a product of a singly punctured cube with a cube, and at least one survives because every signed facet outside $E$ has an owner. A corner of such a row lifts to a corner of $X^E$, contradicting cornerlessness. If instead $E$ is maximal for a forbidden obstruction, any successful layer set in $X^E$ would enlarge $E$ by nested recovery. Obstruction descent makes $X^E$ forbidden, while the two distinct owners of either sign at any layer coordinate give two repairs. A thin seed coordinate would itself be a successful singleton. Union closure makes the maximal successful set unique and gives the final equivalence.

                                                                Comments:

                                                                Maximality of the layer set eliminates further recoverable layers, but it does not force the recovered obstruction itself to be cornerless.

                                                                Seed-Corner Deletions in Signed-Facet Assemblies

                                                                Name: Seed-Corner Deletions in Signed-Facet Assemblies

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Concept Deletion
                                                                • Full Reduction
                                                                • Partial-Cube Minor

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $S$ be an ample forbidden pc-minor, let $\mathcal A$ be compatible resolving tips with distinct acquired supports, and let a surjection $\lambda:E\times\{0,1\}\to\mathcal A$ assign opposite facets of every nonempty layer coordinate set $E$ to distinct owners. Put $R_a=\bigcup_{\lambda(e,i)=a}\{t\in Q_E:t_e=i\}$ and $X=(S\times Q_E)\cup\bigcup_{a\in\mathcal A}(\{a\}\times R_a)$. Then $X$ is an ample forbidden pc-minor. For a seed corner $s$, put $G_s=S\setminus\{s\}$ and let $\mathcal A_s$ consist of tips $a$ that are nonadjacent to $s$ and satisfy $G_s\cup\{a\}\in\mathsf{Damp}$. Every obstruction-preserving corner deletion of $X$ deletes a seed concept $(s,t)$, and it does so exactly when $G_s$ is a forbidden pc-minor and $\lambda(e,t_e)\in\mathcal A_s$ for every $e\in E$. For fixed $s$, the allowed layer words form the face $D_s=\prod_{e\in E}\{i:\lambda(e,i)\in\mathcal A_s\}$. Hence $X$ is corner-descent terminal exactly when, for every corner $s$ with forbidden $G_s$, some coordinate $e$ has neither owner in $\mathcal A_s$. In particular, a corner-descent-terminal seed produces terminal signed-facet assemblies even when the seed has corners.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The common-seed theorem gives ampleness and forbiddenness. A seed occurrence $(s,t)$ is a corner precisely when $s$ is a seed corner and no repair tip adjacent to $s$ occurs at $t$. Occurrence-row peelings avoid such a deleted concept and remain valid under every elementary pc-minor. If deleting $(s,t)$ preserves forbiddenness, strong projection gives forbidden $G_s$, and restricting to each selected facet then projecting the remaining layers gives the peelable repair $G_s\cup\{\lambda(e,t_e)\}$; this proves necessity. Conversely, the stated repair conditions make $(s,t)$ a corner, leave the deletion nonpeelable through its reduction $G_s$, and supply explicit row and product peelings for every old-coordinate minor, layer contraction, and layer restriction. Thus all proper elementary minors peel. An occurrence-row corner belongs to one uniquely owned facet, so its deletion cannot preserve forbiddenness. The independent coordinate choices give the product face $D_s$, whose emptiness is exactly the opposite-owner terminality test.

                                                                [BousquetYangComplex26]

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#thm:damp-seed-corner-facet-deletion

                                                                Witnesses:

                                                                • Hall Assembly with a Cornered Maximal Recovered Seed

                                                                Comments:

                                                                This is a complete terminality test within a given signed-facet assembly once the seed-deletion and inherited-repair data are known. It is not an intrinsic characterization of which seeds and repair sets are admissible. The fixed certificate checks the corner formula on 602- and 1,202-concept Hall assemblies and gives peelings for all 78 elementary images of two positive deletions.

                                                                Two-Connected Terminal Towers over Cut-Vertex Seeds

                                                                Name: Two-Connected Terminal Towers over Cut-Vertex Seeds

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Full Reduction
                                                                • Partial-Cube Minor

                                                                Result Type: Construction

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $S\subseteq Q_F$ be an irredundantly embedded, corner-descent-terminal ample forbidden pc-minor with a cut vertex. Suppose $a,b\notin S$ are distinct resolving tips such that $S\cup\{a\}$ and $S\cup\{b\}$ are dismantlable ample and acquire distinct shattered supports. For every nonempty coordinate set $E$ disjoint from $F$, put $X_E=(S\times Q_E)\cup(\{a\}\times(Q_E\setminus\{0^E\}))\cup(\{b\}\times(Q_E\setminus\{1^E\}))$. Then $X_E$ is a two-connected, corner-descent-terminal ample forbidden pc-minor. Its unique largest successful layer set is exactly $E$, and $X_E^E=S$. If $S$ has corners, no successful layer choice for $X_E$ has a cornerless recovered seed. Moreover, $X_E$ has minimum degree at least three and equals its graph three-core.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The two antipodally punctured occurrence rows partition the signed facets, so the common-seed construction and seed-corner deletion criterion make $X_E$ ample, forbidden, and terminal; the replicated construction is two-connected. The displayed presentation makes $E$ successful with reduction $S$. If the largest successful set $D$ satisfied $E\subsetneq D$, strong projection from its recovered presentation along $E$ would retain a nontrivial signed-facet assembly over $D\setminus E$ with at least two distinct resolving tips. This would present $S$ as a two-connected replicated construction, contradicting its cut vertex. Thus $D=E$. Cornerless recovery can only occur at the largest successful set, so a cornered $S$ rules it out. A terminal ample obstruction has no vertex of degree at most two: the low-degree theorem would otherwise provide an obstruction-preserving corner deletion. Hence $X_E$ is its three-core.

                                                                This gives two-connected terminal counterexamples to cornerlessness of the canonical largest recovered seed, even after graph two-core pruning. The construction still has a successful layer set; the following edge-amalgam family removes layer recovery altogether.

                                                                Terminal Obstructions from an Edge Amalgam

                                                                Name: Terminal Obstructions from an Edge Amalgam

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Coordinate Conditioning
                                                                • Partial-Cube Minor

                                                                Result Type: Construction

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $C\subseteq Q_F$ be irredundantly embedded, two-connected, ample, corner-peelable, and have $0$ as its only corner. Fix an edge $D=\{0,0^{\{e\}}\}$. Assume that for every $f\ne e$, the zero restriction and contraction of $C$ peel to their copies of $D$; all three elementary images in coordinate $e$ peel to the singleton image of $D$; and distinct tips $a,b$ give ample extensions $C\cup\{a\},C\cup\{b\}$ that peel to $D$ and acquire distinct supports. Take two copies $C_1,C_2$ whose coordinate sets meet only in $e$ and whose copies of $D$ are identified. With new coordinates $p,q$, put $X=C_2\cup(C_1\times(Q_{\{p,q\}}\setminus\{00\}))\cup\{(a_1,10),(b_1,01)\}$, with $C_2$ in the $00$ section. Then $X$ is a two-connected, corner-descent-terminal ample forbidden pc-minor of order $4|C|+2$ and dimension $2|F|+1$, and its only corners are $(a_1,10)$ and $(b_1,01)$. If $|F|\ge4$ and $e$ lies in at least three minimal nonfaces of $\operatorname{Sh}(C)$, no coordinate of $X$ is balanced, so $X$ has no successful common-seed layer set even when cornered recovered seeds are allowed.

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Shadow decomposition first shows that the punctured three-layer piece is ample; its union with the second copy along $D$ remains ample because mixed supports across the exclusive coordinate blocks are not shattered. The prescribed relative orders combine with product peelings to peel every restriction and contraction of $X$. Away from the two repair tips, the unique-corner property of $C$, the three-layer product, and the two exclusive blocks prevent every candidate corner cube; the two tips remain corners even after either is removed. Thus corner deletion stops at a nonempty cornerless family, so $X$ is nonpeelable, while the elementary-minor peelings make it forbidden. After either tip deletion, one restriction and one contraction expose the cornerless amalgam $C_1\cup_D C_2$ as a proper nonpeelable minor, proving terminality. The punctured product and attachment of the two pieces along an edge preserve two-connectivity. Under the extra hypotheses, every coordinate belongs to at least three minimal nonfaces: exclusive coordinates lie in at least three missing cross-pairs, while the common coordinate retains three minimal nonfaces from $C_2$. Hence no coordinate has the two-clause profile required for a successful recovered layer.

                                                                The construction gives two-connected terminal graph three-cores for which layer recovery does not exist. It assumes relative peeling certificates for the input family and its two repairs; intrinsic admissibility of those inputs remains a separate problem.

                                                                One-Corner Extensions and the Two-Neighbor Falsifier

                                                                Name: One-Corner Extensions and the Two-Neighbor Falsifier

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes
                                                                • Cornerless Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Concept Deletion
                                                                • Coordinate Conditioning
                                                                • Full Reduction

                                                                Result Type: Construction

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $G$ be an irredundantly embedded cornerless ample forbidden pc-minor. If adjacent words $c,h\notin G$ give ample one-concept extensions with the same acquired support, then $S=G\cup\{c\}$ is an ample forbidden pc-minor whose unique corner is $c$; it has no successful layer set and no common-seed cover with nonempty proper rows. More generally, suppose an irredundantly embedded ample forbidden pc-minor $S$ has unique corner $c$, and two distinct words $u,v\notin S$ adjacent to $c$ give dismantlable-ample extensions. On a new coordinate $e$, the two-section family $X=((S\cup\{u\})\times\{0\})\cup((S\cup\{v\})\times\{1\})$ is a corner-descent-terminal ample forbidden pc-minor with exactly two corners. Its only successful layer set is $\{e\}$ and its recovered seed is the cornered family $S$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Write $h=c^{\{f\}}$ and let $I$ be the common acquired support. Then $f\notin I$, and the two punctured $I$-cubes already lie in $G$. The completed $I$-cube makes $c$ a corner of $S$. Any other candidate corner in that cube has an $f$-neighbor supplied by the second punctured cube, while a corner outside it would already be a corner of $G$; hence $c$ is unique. Deleting it returns nonpeelable $G$, so the one-concept atlas makes $S$ forbidden. Every proper-row common-seed cover has at least two occurrence-row corners, excluding such a presentation and therefore any successful layer set. In the general construction, adjacency of the two repairs to different directions at $c$ forces their acquired supports to be distinct. The common-seed theorem makes $X$ forbidden, its two repair occurrences are its only corners, and deleting either exposes $S$ as a proper layer restriction, proving terminality. The new coordinate is thin and successful. The thin-layer dichotomy makes the largest presentation antipodally punctured; its two rows contribute at least twice its layer dimension in distinct corners. Since $X$ has only two corners, that dimension is one and $\{e\}$ is the unique successful set.

                                                                [BousquetYangComplex26]

                                                                The second part is conditional: the required two resolving neighbors are additional hypotheses. The fixed certificate finds adjacent ample additions to a 292-concept one-corner obstruction, but all three tested additions remain nonpeelable and therefore do not realize the falsifier.

                                                                No Resolving Neighbor after a Square Completion

                                                                Name: No Resolving Neighbor after a Square Completion

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                • Concept Deletion

                                                                Result Type: Implication

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $G$ be nonempty, ample, and nonpeelable, and let $S=G\cup\{c\}$ be ample with acquired support $I$ of size at most two. No word adjacent to $c$ is a resolving one-concept addition to $S$. Consequently, the one-corner two-neighbor construction can have its required resolving neighbors only when $|I|\ge3$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                For an adjacent ample addition $u=c^{\{f\}}$, one has $f\notin I$ and its acquired support over $S$ is $P=J\cup\{f\}$ for some $J\subseteq I$. Rank-two extension invariance keeps $S$ nonpeelable and excludes resolution when $|J|\le1$. The only remaining case has $I=J$ of size two. Removing $c$ leaves the punctured $I$-square at $u$ and removes only its $f$-neighbor, so $G\cup\{u\}$ is ample and also acquires $I$. Square-pair invariance then makes $S\cup\{u\}$ nonpeelable.

                                                                Two Forced Deletions at a Rank-Three Neighbor

                                                                Name: Two Forced Deletions at a Rank-Three Neighbor

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Concept Deletion

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $S\subseteq Q_F$ be ample and nonpeelable with unique corner $c$, whose incident-coordinate set $I$ has size at least three. Suppose $u=c^{\{i\}}\notin S$ and $H=S\cup\{u\}$ is ample with a three-coordinate acquired support. Then that support is $P=J\cup\{i\}$ for a two-element proper subset $J\subsetneq I$. Put $x=u^J$ and $y=c^J$. If $H$ peels, every peeling starts by deleting $x$ and then $y$. Thus $x$ has no neighbor outside the completed $P$-cube, and $x$ is the only neighbor of $y$ in a direction outside $I$. Consequently, $u$ is not resolving if another adjacent ample addition $v=c^{\{j\}}$ has acquired support $K\cup\{j\}$ with $J\subseteq K\subseteq I$.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The punctured-cube test gives $i\in P$, $i\notin I$, and $P\setminus\{i\}=J\subsetneq I$. In $H$, the old corner $c$ is blocked by any direction in $I\setminus J$. Any other old corner must lie in the completed $P$-cube and have no neighbor outside it. All candidates except $x$ retain an outside neighbor because $c$ was the unique corner of $S$; hence the only possible first corners are $u$ and $x$. Deleting $u$ returns nonpeelable $S$, so every peeling starts at $x$. Only neighbors of $x$ can become new corners. Two retain incompatible outside neighbors and $u$ loses a required cube vertex, leaving $y$ as the sole possible second deletion. The full $I$-cube at $y$ shows it becomes a corner exactly when its only outside-$I$ neighbor is $x$. A companion addition with $J\subseteq K$ supplies the distinct outside neighbor $v^J=y^{\{j\}}$, contradicting this necessary condition.

                                                                References:

                                                                [BousquetYangComplex26]

                                                                Proof Source:

                                                                PartialCubes:papers/dismantlable-ample/sections/dismantlable_ample_classification.tex?#prop:damp-rank-three-neighbor-first-deletions

                                                                Comments:

                                                                The controls verify both the forced two-deletion case and the companion-blocked case, and replay fifteen recorded rank-three neighbors. The constructed controls have proper nonpeelable minors and are local proof checks rather than forbidden witnesses.

                                                                A Companion Tip Excludes Rank-Three Resolving Neighbors

                                                                Name: A Companion Tip Excludes Rank-Three Resolving Neighbors

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes
                                                                • Cornerless Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Concept Deletion

                                                                Result Type: Implication

                                                                Statement:

                                                                In the adjacent same-support construction that turns a cornerless ample forbidden pc-minor $G$ into the one-corner obstruction $G\cup\{c\}$, every resolving addition adjacent to $c$ has acquired support of size at least four. If the original acquired support $I$ has size three, every such resolving tip $u=c^{\{i\}}$ completes the full $I\cup\{i\}$-cube, while $G\cup\{u\}$ is itself an ample one-corner forbidden pc-minor acquiring $I$. Therefore a two-neighbor falsifier at support three requires three tips $c,u,v$ with the same acquired support over $G$: all individual extensions are nonpeelable, but both pair extensions $G\cup\{c,u\}$ and $G\cup\{c,v\}$ must peel.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The square-completion corollary excludes original support at most two. Let the companion tip be $h=c^{\{f\}}$. Its punctured cube over $G$ shows that adding $h$ to $G\cup\{c\}$ acquires $I\cup\{f\}$, of size at least four. Any resolving neighbor has support at least three by rank-two invariance. If it had size three, the rank-three forced-deletion theorem would apply with companion $h$ and $K=I$, excluding resolution. Thus every resolving neighbor has support at least four. For original support three, the punctured-cube formula bounds an adjacent addition's support by $I\cup\{i\}$, so equality follows. Removing $c$ leaves the punctured $I$-cube at $u$, making $G\cup\{u\}$ ample with acquired support $I$; the adjacent same-support theorem makes it one-corner and forbidden. Applying this to both resolving neighbors yields the three-tip condition.

                                                                Comments:

                                                                This excludes support three only in the companion construction. It does not exclude rank-three resolving neighbors of arbitrary one-corner families or settle cooperation among support-four repairs.

                                                                Strong-Projection Positivity under Adjacent Pair Completions

                                                                Name: Strong-Projection Positivity under Adjacent Pair Completions

Suppose three distinct missing tips $c,u,v$ give ample individual extensions with the same acquired three-coordinate support $I$, with $u=c^{\{i\}}$ and $v=c^{\{j\}}$. If both pair extensions $G\cup\{c,u\}$ and $G\cup\{c,v\}$ are dismantlable ample, then every nonempty strong reduction $G^D$, $\varnothing\ne D\subseteq F$, is dismantlable ample.

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Put $S=G\cup\{c\}$. The additions of $u$ and $v$ to $S$ acquire respectively $I\cup\{i\}$ and $I\cup\{j\}$. If some nonempty $G^D$ were nonpeelable, the strong-projection formula and rank-two extension invariance would make $S^D$ nonpeelable as well. Positivity of both repaired families would then force $D\subseteq(I\cup\{i\})\cap(I\cup\{j\})=I$ and $4-|D|\ge3$, so $D=\{k\}$ for some $k\in I$. In that reduction, the projected tips $c_k,u_k$ remain distinct adjacent ample additions with the same acquired two-coordinate support $I\setminus\{k\}$, and their pair extension is the reduction of the positive family $G\cup\{c,u\}$. Square-pair invariance forces $G^{\{k\}}$ to peel, a contradiction.

                                                                A Third Companion Blocks a Pair in VC Dimension Three

                                                                Name: A Third Companion Blocks a Pair in VC Dimension Three

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes
                                                                • Cornerless Ample Classes

                                                                • Concept Deletion

                                                                Result Type: Implication

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $G$ be a nonempty cornerless ample family of VC dimension at most three. Suppose three distinct missing tips $c,u,v$ give ample individual extensions with the same three-coordinate acquired support $I$, and $u=c^{\{i\}}$, $v=c^{\{j\}}$. Then neither $G\cup\{c,u\}$ nor $G\cup\{c,v\}$ is dismantlable ample.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The punctured cubes at $c,u$ complete the four-cube on $P=I\cup\{i\}$ when both tips are added. The third punctured cube supplies an outside neighbor to every non-corner vertex on the $c$ side. Any old corner of the pair extension must lie in this completed four-cube and have no outside neighbor; the only possible first deletions therefore lie among its upper antipode and the three adjacent upper vertices. Deleting either new tip first leaves a one-corner extension and then the cornerless family, so it cannot start a full peeling. Once an old vertex is deleted, the support $P$ leaves the shadow, and every subsequent ample subfamily has VC dimension at most three. Degree and missing-square arguments protect all twelve vertices on the lower side, the two tips, and their three upper neighbors; only the four candidate upper vertices can ever be deleted. They cannot exhaust the family, so no peeling exists. Interchanging $u$ and $v$ gives the second conclusion.

                                                                A VC-Three One-Corner Family Has at Most One Resolving Neighbor

                                                                Name: A VC-Three One-Corner Family Has at Most One Resolving Neighbor

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                • Concept Deletion

                                                                Result Type: Implication

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $S\subseteq Q_F$ be ample and nonpeelable with unique corner $c$, and let $I$ be the incident-coordinate set of $c$. If $\operatorname{VCdim}(S)\le3$, at most one missing neighbor $u$ of $c$ has $S\cup\{u\}$ dismantlable ample. Hence the one-corner two-neighbor falsifier requires VC dimension at least four. Without a VC bound, if two resolving neighbors have three-coordinate acquired supports $J\cup\{i\}$ and $K\cup\{j\}$ with $J,K\subseteq I$, then $J\cup K\subsetneq I$. In the adjacent same-support companion construction with VC dimension at most three, the specified companion is the only possible resolving neighbor; two distinct companions exclude every resolving neighbor.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                The predecessor $G=S\setminus\{c\}$ is ample and nonpeelable, and adding $c$ acquires $I$. Low-rank invariance excludes resolving supports of size at most two. For two rank-three neighbors, the forced-deletion theorem gives two two-element sets $J,K$ and makes each peeling start with its associated first two old vertices. The only possible third deletion for the first repair uses some direction $r\in I\setminus J$ and forces a cube through an outside-$I$ neighbor. If $r\in K$, that cube either violates the second repair's private-edge condition or gives its first deletion an outside neighbor. Thus $r\notin J\cup K$, proving $J\cup K\subsetneq I$. Under VC dimension three, the corner cube forces $|I|=3$. Two rank-three supports contradict the strict-union condition; a rank-three and rank-four pair are excluded by the companion form of the forced-deletion theorem. If both supports have size four, deleting $c$ leaves a cornerless predecessor and three same-support tips, contradicting the VC-three third-companion theorem. The specialized companion assertions follow by the same rank bounds and that theorem.

All four families are ample. The additions acquire disjoint four-coordinate supports, and their completed cubes have Hamming distance $8+\ell$.                                                                 Translate Hall's 299-concept cornerless family and a certified resolving tip so that the prescribed peeling of the repaired family ends at the attachment word zero. Take two copies on disjoint twelve-coordinate blocks and join their zero words by the monotone path $T_\ell=\{1^k0^{\ell-k}:0\le k\le\ell\}$. No mixed pair of coordinates is shattered, so the shadow is the union of the two block shadows and the $\ell$ bridge singletons. The Sandwich equality proves ampleness before and after either or both tips are added. Every old vertex remains a noncorner and every internal path vertex has two incident directions without a square, so the base is cornerless. Either one-tip extension retains the other Hall copy as a proper signed restriction and is nonpeelable. After both tips are added, peel each repaired Hall copy to its attachment and then peel the remaining path. The two completed four-cubes lie four steps from their respective attachments and differ across every bridge coordinate, giving distance $4+\ell+4$.

                                                                Terminal Iterated Common-Seed Covers Are Antipodal Two-Repair Towers

                                                                Name: Terminal Iterated Common-Seed Covers Are Antipodal Two-Repair Towers

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Coordinate Conditioning
                                                                • Coordinate Projection
                                                                • Partial-Cube Minor
                                                                • Full Reduction

                                                                Result Type: Recognition

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $G\subseteq Q_F$ be an irredundantly embedded ample forbidden pc-minor. Let $S$ be a forbidden common-seed cover over $G$ on a nonempty layer set $D$, with distinct-support resolving tips and nonempty proper occurrence rows, and let $X$ be a second such cover over $S$ on a disjoint nonempty set $E$. If $X$ is corner-descent-terminal, then both stages have exactly two repair tips and antipodally punctured rows. For distinct tips $a,b$, words $u\in Q_D$ and $v\in Q_E$, one has $S=(G\times Q_D)\cup(\{a\}\times(Q_D\setminus\{u\}))\cup(\{b\}\times(Q_D\setminus\{\bar u\}))$ and $X=(G\times Q_{D\cup E})\cup(\{a\}\times(Q_{D\cup E}\setminus\{(u,v)\}))\cup(\{b\}\times(Q_{D\cup E}\setminus\{(\bar u,\bar v)\}))$. Thus $D\cup E$ is successful for $X$. A terminal chain of two or more such covers is a single antipodal two-repair tower over its initial seed.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                A resolving addition to the inner cover must change its full reduction along $D$, which equals the nonpeelable seed $G$. It must therefore fill the unique missing word of an occurrence row $R_a=Q_D\setminus\{u_a\}$; conversely each such completion peels by the common-seed criterion. Flatten the outer cover over $G$: a selected row becomes $(R_a\times Q_E)\cup(\{u_a\}\times T_a)$ and an unselected row becomes $R_a\times Q_E$. Every flattened row is nonempty, proper, and ample. Terminality forces these flattened rows to partition the signed facets of $D\cup E$. Reducing along $E$ recovers the inner rows and shows that they partition the signed facets of $D$; the outer rows likewise partition those of $E$. The nested-recovery theorem then forces two owners at each stage, opposite punctures, the displayed flattening, and success of $D\cup E$. Applying the two-stage argument repeatedly flattens any longer terminal chain.

                                                                Witnesses:

                                                                Comments:

                                                                The inner rows need not be facet shells and may have overlapping facet ownership. Applied to the canonical largest recovered layer set of a terminal obstruction, the theorem prevents a further nontrivial common-seed cover satisfying these hypotheses.

                                                                Repair Growth after Extending a Recovered Obstruction

                                                                Name: Repair Growth after Extending a Recovered Obstruction

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes
                                                                • Dismantlable Ample Classes

                                                                Operations:

                                                                • Concept Deletion
                                                                • Coordinate Projection
                                                                • Full Reduction

                                                                Result Type: Implication

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $H\subseteq Q_V$ be an irredundantly embedded ample forbidden pc-minor with a successful nonempty layer set $E$, and let $S=H\cup\{c\}$ be ample and nonpeelable. If $\mathcal R(Y)=\{a\notin Y:Y\cup\{a\}\text{ is dismantlable ample}\}$, then $\mathcal R(H)\subseteq\mathcal R(S)$, $|\mathcal R(S)\setminus\mathcal R(H)|\le1$, and $|\mathcal R(S)|\le3$. Every inherited repair is nonadjacent to $c$ and keeps its acquired support. A new repair, if present, has the same old-coordinate projection as $c$; their two missing layer words form an edge, so the new repair is adjacent to $c$. No signed-facet assembly over $S$ using compatible resolving tips is corner-descent terminal. Consequently, if a terminal facet assembly has a cornered seed, every obstruction-preserving corner deletion of that seed has no successful layer presentation.

                                                                Status: Established

                                                                Proof:

                                                                Recover $H$ from its successful layer set, with nonpeelable seed $K=H^E$. Since $S$ is nonpeelable, adding $c$ completes no full $E$-fibre, so $S^E=K$ and the acquired support of $c$ does not contain $E$. Every old repair has a different support; compatible-repair union makes $H\cup\{a,c\}$ ample, and deleting $c$ leaves a peelable family, so it is a repair of $S$ with unchanged support and is nonadjacent to $c$. Any new repair of $S$ must change the nonpeelable strong $E$-projection and therefore complete an $E$-fibre. Its old projection must equal that of $c$, or it would already repair $H$. The original fibre has exactly these two missing words; the recovered-row geometry makes them an edge. Hence there is at most one new repair, while the recovered-obstruction theorem bounds the inherited set by two. Finally, for the seed corner $c$, exactly the inherited repairs satisfy the seed-corner deletion criterion. At most one owner is ineligible, whereas opposite signed facets require distinct owners, so every compatible facet assembly retains an obstruction-preserving copy of $c$ and cannot be terminal.

                                                                The bound of three repairs and the single-new-repair bound are both sharp. The theorem also explains why a cornered seed inside a terminal facet assembly cannot itself arise by an obstruction-preserving corner extension from an obstruction with successful layers.

                                                                Inherited Repair Fibres Admit Complete Obstruction Descent

                                                                Name: Inherited Repair Fibres Admit Complete Obstruction Descent

                                                                Classes:

                                                                • Ample Classes

                                                                Statement:

                                                                Let $G\subseteq Q_F$ be an irredundantly embedded cornerless ample forbidden pc-minor, and suppose $S=G\cup\{c\}$ is ample and nonpeelable. Let $\mathcal A$ be compatible resolving tips of $G$ whose acquired supports, together with the acquired support of $c$, are pairwise distinct. Assign the tips rows $R_a$ forming a partition of the signed facets of a nonempty layer cube $Q_E$, set $Y=(G\times Q_E)\cup\bigcup_{a\in\mathcal A}(\{a\}\times R_a)$, and put $X=Y\cup(\{c\}\times Q_E)$. Then $X$ is an ample forbidden pc-minor and admits $2^{|E|}$ obstruction-preserving corner deletions that remove exactly the full fibre $\{c\}\times Q_E$ and end at $Y$.                                                                 Proof:

                                                                The signed-facet partition theorem makes $Y$ a terminal ample forbidden pc-minor. Choose a corner peeling of $Q_E$, with ample suffixes $T_0=Q_E,T_1,\ldots,T_m=\varnothing$. Compatible-repair union and the replicated-layer theorem make every $Y_i=Y\cup(\{c\}\times T_i)$ ample. Its strong reduction along $E$ is $S$ when $i=0$ and $G$ thereafter, so every $Y_i$ is nonpeelable. Traversed from $Y_m$ to $Y_0$, each step is an ample one-concept extension in the same irredundant ambient cube and remains nonpeelable; the one-concept atlas therefore makes every intermediate family a forbidden pc-minor. Reversing the sequence gives the required corner deletions. Since every $R_a$ is proper, $X^E=S$, and compatible-repair union preserves the distinct acquired supports, so the marked presentation is exactly the recovered-layer presentation claimed.
